# Rust Port of the Phase 0 Analysers Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Move the fifteen Python analysers of `scripts/phase0/` into Rust (seven into `lazymkv-core`, eight as `lazymkv-dev` commands), prove with goldens and ported tests that the Rust gives the recorded verdicts, and delete every Python file and `python3` call from the repository, in one pull request.

**Architecture:** `crates/core` gains `lang`, `recording` (an in-memory tree handed in by the caller; no I/O in core), `robot`, `reconcile`, `audio::{levels, measures, rule, reference, titles, report, labels, dataset}` and `subtitle::{align, text}`. A new crate `crates/dev` builds the binary `lazymkv-dev`, which owns all I/O: it builds the tree from a recording or the evidence clone, runs `ffprobe` and `ffmpeg` through a runner trait, writes files with a Python-compatible JSON writer, and exposes one command per Python entry point plus `decide` and `golden`. Goldens written once by the Python (kept in the evidence repository beside the goldens) and the 213 Python test cases ported one for one are the acceptance.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.99.0 (`rust-toolchain.toml`, edition 2021); crates `serde` (derive), `serde_json` with `preserve_order` and `float_roundtrip`, `regex`, `fancy-regex`, `unicode-normalization`, `md-5`, `sha1`; `cargo test --workspace` on the Mac and on the mini PC (`scripts/box.sh cargo test --workspace`); Python 3.9.6 on the Mac only to write the goldens before it is deleted; the private evidence repository `lazymkv-evidence` cloned at `corpus/owner/`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-rust-port-design.md` (the port design; binding), which argues from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-lazymkv-design.md` (the design spec; its decisions D1 to D23 bind too).

**Branch:** `rust-port`, created from `main` after pull request krcm0209/lazymkv#1 (`phase-0-evidence`) has merged. The port design and this plan are on that pull request, so `main` holds them when work starts. Nothing in this plan runs on the mini PC except `cargo test --workspace` through `scripts/box.sh` where a task says so.

## Global Constraints

- The port reproduces the Python of commit `75fa76a`'s tree, written by Python 3.9.6 on the Mac: verdicts, markers, classes, roles, counts, orders, review reasons, exit codes and the decision-carrying report lines of spec section 3.4 are identical; floating-point measures agree within 1e-9 absolute, SMI within 1e-6; the Rust computes in `f64` in the Python's loop order. Deliberate deviations are only those the spec lists (exit 3 for a missing evidence directory; exit 2 where the Python crashed; `compare-scans`'s tuple reprs; `proxy.txt`'s unresolved path; the snapshot's v3 keys).
- `core` has no I/O and nothing OS-specific: every function takes parsed inputs or a `Tree` and returns values or typed errors; a missing file is `Missing(path)`, never a silent default. Directory walking, file reading and writing, process running, printing and exit codes live in `crates/dev`.
- Text files are decoded as UTF-8 with an optional byte-order mark, lossily where the Python read with `errors="replace"`; each reader splits lines as its Python does (`robot.parse` on `\n` only with a trailing `\r` stripped; the others with the boundaries of Python's `str.splitlines`).
- The tree is ordered as Python sorts `Path` objects: component by component, each name by code point. Walkers skip a folder named `golden/`.
- Every file the Rust writes that the Python wrote is byte-identical from the same inputs: the Python-compatible JSON writer (indent `n`, `": "` and `","` separators, insertion order, `ensure_ascii` as a flag, Python float `repr` spelling, ints and floats distinct, `NaN` as `null`), level files rounded half away from zero on the decimal string with `CRLF`, `manifest.txt` with `LF`.
- No subtitle text, no token, no unit-key content, no drive serial, no machine user name in any tracked file of either repository, in a golden, in a test fixture or in a commit message; `scripts/phase0/check-names.sh` and the evidence repository's README checks print nothing before every commit.
- Decisions D1 to D23 of the design spec stay byte-identical; the port changes no measure, threshold or verdict; the design spec's 6.2 step 7 improvements are not in this pull request (RP6).
- Dependencies: only the crates named in the tech stack; nothing downloaded at run time (D17); no network in any test.
- Commits: every commit signed with the owner's SSH key as `krcm0209 <17315774+krcm0209@users.noreply.github.com>` through the global git config (never `--no-gpg-sign`, `--no-verify`, or overrides of `user.name`, `user.email`, `commit.gpgsign`; never amend or re-date), with NO attribution trailer or line of any kind; after each commit `git log -1 --format='%G? %an <%ae> %cn <%ce>%n%B'` shows `G`, that identity and a clean body. One commit per module in dependency order, each with its ported tests and golden comparisons; then the dev commands; then deletions and documents.
- PowerShell scripts are edited only where the spec's section 6 says (comments and printed commands): ASCII only, no global `$ErrorActionPreference`, `-ErrorAction Stop` per cmdlet, the `RESULT ok|FAILED:` convention kept; parse-checked on the mini PC before the commit.
- The evidence clone at `corpus/owner/` is a separate repository: nothing under it is ever staged in `lazymkv`; its commits (goldens, the v3 snapshot) are signed the same way and pushed to `lazymkv-evidence`.
- Tests that need the evidence clone, the level series, the OCR text or `ffmpeg` pass with a printed `skipped: <reason>` when their input is absent; they never fail for a missing input and never pass silently.
- An expected-output mismatch that comes from plan text about the environment (an extra git-status line for the task's own files, a path spelling, a skip line) is recorded in the task report and the step continues; a mismatch in a test result, a verdict, a count, a measure or file content stops the task.

## Review Focus

Input classes the spec implies but the ported tests would not exercise; each line's test is added to the task that owns the code, in that task's own step style:

1. A `scan.txt` recorded on the mini PC with a byte-order mark and `CRLF` line ends, fed to `robot::parse`: every line parses, no line is skipped for its `\r`. (Task 2)
2. A label folder named `golden` (or any file under `golden/`) inside a recording: every walker skips it; `labels auto`, `levels-args`, `retune` and `decide` never treat it as a rip label. (Task 1, Task 8)
3. A recording with two level folders for one label (as `pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd/all-tracks` has) and a title measured only for the dataset (main stream, no candidate): the harness judges in each folder, uses the folder with the most candidates for the table, and the dataset-only folder adds nothing to the counts. (Task 8)
4. A labels file with non-ASCII in a note and an unknown key: `labels check` reports the Python's sentence, an edit keeps the unknown key and the note's characters, and the file is written with `ensure_ascii` off. (Task 7)
5. An evidence clone without the level series and without OCR text (a fresh clone): `retune` exits 3 with the Python's "its level files are not here" line, `golden check` reports every affected comparison as `skipped` with its reason and exits 3 when nothing could run, and `cargo test` passes with the skip lines printed. (Task 8, Task 14)

## Shared interfaces

Every item below crosses a task boundary: one task defines it, later tasks call it. A task that needs an item not listed here keeps it private to its own file. Signatures are exact; bodies are left out (`;` in place of a body). Each item carries a one-line doc, its Python origin (`Py:`), the task that defines it (`Def:`) and the tasks that use it (`Use:`). Where a later task adds to a file an earlier task created (the test generators in `testsupport`), the item says so.

### Conventions every task follows

- **Names.** Rust names are the Python names in snake_case. Every field of the audio `Measures`, the audio `Rule`, the audio `Constants`, the subtitle `Rule` and the subtitle `Measures` keeps the Python key spelling exactly (`MATCH_R`, `CUE`, `rev_tenths`), with `#[allow(non_snake_case)]` on the struct. A Python key that is a Rust keyword is a raw identifier (`r#type`); `serde` writes it as `type`.
- **Python strings stay strings.** A closed set of Python strings (verdicts, roles, classes) is a Rust enum whose `as_str()` returns the Python spelling, whose `serde` form is that spelling, and whose `FromStr` accepts only it.
- **Numbers.** A Python `int` is `i64` (or `u32` where spec 3.3 binds it), a Python `float` is `f64`. A value that is an int in one place and a float in another is `Num`. `NaN` is the Python `float("nan")`; every serialiser writes it as `null` and every deserialiser reads `null` back as `NaN` (`nan_to_none` / `none_to_nan`).
- **Python dicts.** A dict whose order is ever printed or written is `Ordered<V>` (insertion order, a repeated key keeps its first place and takes the last value). A dict whose keys are only looked up or always sorted is a `BTreeMap`.
- **Errors.** Where the Python raised and its caller caught (`except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError)`), the Rust returns `Err(String)` holding the Python's `str(e)` text where the spec names it, so the caller prints the same line. A file that is not there is `ReadError::Missing`, never a silent default. Where the Python crashed with a traceback, the Rust returns `Err` and the dev command exits 2 (spec 3.4). JSON syntax errors carry `serde_json`'s message, not Python's `JSONDecodeError` text (no recorded input is malformed JSON; see Open points).
- **No I/O in `core`.** Every `core` function takes text, parsed values, or a `&dyn Tree`. Writing, running programs, printing and exit codes are in `crates/dev`.
- **Test support.** `crates/core/src/lib.rs` declares `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "testsupport"))] pub mod testsupport;`. `crates/core/Cargo.toml` gets `[features] testsupport = []`; `crates/dev/Cargo.toml` lists `lazymkv-core = { path = "../core", features = ["testsupport"] }` under `[dev-dependencies]`, so the dev crate's integration tests (Tasks 8, 11, 12) use the same `PyRandom` and level generators as the core tests. This adds no dependency.

### `core::lang` (Task 1)

```rust
/// ISO 639-2 bibliographic code -> terminology code: the 20 pairs of the Python, in its order ("alb" -> "sqi" ... "wel" -> "cym").
/// Py: compare_tracks.B_TO_T. Def: T1. Use: T3, T12.
pub const B_TO_T: [(&str, &str); 20];

/// `(code or "und").lower()`, then mapped through `B_TO_T` (None and "" are "und"). Py: compare_tracks.norm_lang. Def: T1. Use: T3, T12.
pub fn norm_lang(code: Option<&str>) -> String;

/// The codes that name no language (spec 8.6). Py: audio_similarity.NO_LANGUAGE. Def: T1. Use: T5, T6, T8.
pub const NO_LANGUAGE: [&str; 6] = ["", "-", "und", "zxx", "mul", "mis"];

/// TMDb's original_language of a work without speech. Py: audio_similarity.TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE. Def: T1. Use: T5.
pub const TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE: &str = "xx";

/// TMDb's two-letter original_language -> the three-letter stream codes, every entry of the Python's table in its order.
/// Py: audio_similarity.ISO639. Def: T1. Use: T5, T6, T8.
pub const ISO639: &[(&str, &[&str])];

/// The three-letter codes of one two-letter code, or None when the table lacks it. Py: `ISO639.get(code)`. Def: T1. Use: T5, T6.
pub fn iso639(code: &str) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]>;
```

### `core::recording` (`recording/mod.rs`, Task 1)

#### The tree

```rust
/// A path inside a tree: '/'-separated components below the tree's root. Ordered component by component, each
/// name by code point (derived `Ord` over `Vec<String>`), which is how Python sorts `PurePosixPath` objects:
/// `all-tracks/x` < `all-tracks-2/x` and `audio-levels-20ms-1-2/x` < `audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3/x`.
/// Py: pathlib.PurePosixPath ordering. Def: T1. Use: every later task.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct PathKey(Vec<String>);

impl PathKey {
    /// The tree's root (no component).
    pub fn root() -> PathKey;
    /// A key from "a/b/c"; empty and "." components are dropped, as pathlib drops them.
    pub fn new(path: &str) -> PathKey;
    /// This key with `name` appended ("x/y" appends two components). Py: `path / name`.
    pub fn join(&self, name: &str) -> PathKey;
    /// The key without its last component (the root's parent is the root). Py: Path.parent.
    pub fn parent(&self) -> PathKey;
    /// The last component, "" for the root. Py: Path.name.
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str;
    /// The components in order.
    pub fn components(&self) -> &[String];
}
/// '/'-joined components, "" for the root.
impl std::fmt::Display for PathKey;

/// What a path names. Py: Path.is_file / Path.is_dir.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind { File, Dir }

/// A file the tree does not have. Its Display is Python's FileNotFoundError text,
/// `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<shown>'`, with `shown` the path as `Tree::display` prints it. Def: T1.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Missing { pub path: PathKey, pub shown: String }

/// Why a read failed: the file is not there, or the OS refused it (the message is the OSError text). Def: T1.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ReadError { Missing(Missing), Io { path: PathKey, message: String } }
impl std::fmt::Display for ReadError;

/// A recording directory or the whole evidence directory, in memory. Every walker of the Python is a function over
/// it. `list` and `glob` never return a folder named `golden` or anything under one (section 5 of the spec reserves
/// the name); `read`, `kind` and `exists` do not filter, so the golden code reads its files through the same tree.
/// Py: the pathlib calls of every module. Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub trait Tree {
    /// File, folder, or None when absent. Py: Path.exists / is_file / is_dir.
    fn kind(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Option<Kind>;
    /// `self.kind(path).is_some()`. Py: Path.exists.
    fn exists(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool;
    /// Py: Path.is_file.
    fn is_file(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool;
    /// Py: Path.is_dir.
    fn is_dir(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool;
    /// The entries directly in `dir`, files and folders, in `PathKey` order. Py: sorted(dir.iterdir()).
    fn list(&self, dir: &PathKey) -> Vec<PathKey>;
    /// The paths below `base` matching `pattern`: '/'-separated, each component an fnmatch pattern (`*`, `?`,
    /// `[seq]`, `[!seq]`, case-sensitive, a leading dot matched like any character, as pathlib's glob), in
    /// `PathKey` order. Py: sorted(base.glob(pattern)).
    fn glob(&self, base: &PathKey, pattern: &str) -> Vec<PathKey>;
    /// The file's bytes; a lazy entry is loaded on its first read and kept. Py: Path.read_bytes.
    fn read(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Result<std::sync::Arc<[u8]>, ReadError>;
    /// The path as the Python printed it: the tree's display root joined with `path` as pathlib joins
    /// (a display root of "." adds nothing). Py: str(Path).
    fn display(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String;
    /// The last component of the path's resolved absolute form; for the root, the resolved root's own name.
    /// Py: Path.resolve().name (audio_similarity.report's label, audio_labels' new slug, levels_args' slug).
    fn resolved_name(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String;
}

/// Loads a lazy file's bytes once; `Err` holds the OSError text. Def: T1.
pub type Loader = std::sync::Arc<dyn Fn() -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> + Send + Sync>;

/// The in-memory `Tree`: `BTreeMap<PathKey, Node>` with folders explicit (an empty folder exists, as on disk),
/// files as bytes or as a `Loader`. Tests build it directly; `crates/dev` fills it from a directory. Def: T1. Use: all.
pub struct MemTree { /* entries, display_root, resolved_root */ }

impl MemTree {
    /// An empty tree printed under `display_root` ("corpus/owner", ".", or a path as the user gave it) whose root
    /// resolves to a folder named `resolved_root_name`.
    pub fn new(display_root: &str, resolved_root_name: &str) -> MemTree;
    /// Adds a file (its parent folders too).
    pub fn insert_file(&mut self, path: &str, bytes: impl Into<Vec<u8>>);
    /// Adds a file read on first use.
    pub fn insert_lazy(&mut self, path: &str, load: Loader);
    /// Adds a folder (its parents too).
    pub fn insert_dir(&mut self, path: &str);
}
impl Tree for MemTree;
```

#### Decoding and line splitting

```rust
/// Python's "utf-8" (a byte-order mark stays as U+FEFF) and "utf-8-sig" (one leading mark removed). Def: T1.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Encoding { Utf8, Utf8Sig }

/// Python's errors="strict" and errors="replace" (U+FFFD per maximal invalid subpart, as `from_utf8_lossy`). Def: T1.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Errors { Strict, Replace }

/// Bytes to text as `bytes.decode(encoding, errors)`; Err is Python's UnicodeDecodeError text
/// ("'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte"). Py: Path.read_text. Def: T1. Use: all readers.
pub fn decode_text(bytes: &[u8], encoding: Encoding, errors: Errors) -> Result<String, String>;

/// `tree.read` then `decode_text`; Err is the ReadError or decode text. Py: Path.read_text(encoding, errors). Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub fn read_text(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey, encoding: Encoding, errors: Errors) -> Result<String, String>;

/// A JSON file read as "utf-8-sig", strict, into `T`. Py: json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")). Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub fn read_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey) -> Result<T, String>;

/// Lines on Python's `str.splitlines` boundaries: \n, \r, \r\n, \v, \f, \x1c, \x1d, \x1e, \x85, \u2028, \u2029; no
/// terminators; no final empty line. Py: str.splitlines. Def: T1. Use: T4 (levels, manifest, refusal), T7 (row 13),
/// T10 (ocr_records), T12 (hit-rate statuses, ocr-compare).
pub fn py_splitlines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>;

/// Lines as Python's text-mode file iteration gives them (universal newlines: \n, \r, \r\n only), without
/// terminators. Py: `for line in open(path)`. Def: T1. Use: T4 (frame_ms_of), T1 pyjson (convert_levels).
pub fn universal_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>;

/// `text.split("\n")`, each line with its trailing "\r"s removed (rstrip("\r")); a final empty piece kept, as
/// split keeps it. Py: robot.parse's loop. Def: T1. Use: T2.
pub fn strip_cr_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>;

/// Lines of bytes on `bytes.splitlines` boundaries (\n, \r, \r\n only). Py: check_encoding's data.splitlines().
/// Def: T1. Use: T12 (encoding).
pub fn py_bytes_splitlines(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<&[u8]>;
```

#### Python spellings

```rust
/// Python's str.isspace for one character: Unicode White_Space plus the bidi classes B, S and WS, so \x1c to \x1f
/// count (Rust's char::is_whitespace does not). Def: T1. Use: the helpers below.
pub fn py_is_space(c: char) -> bool;
/// str.split() with no argument (runs of py_is_space, no empty pieces). Def: T1. Use: T4 (manifest), T10, T12.
pub fn py_split(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>;
/// str.strip() with no argument. Def: T1. Use: T4, T10, T12.
pub fn py_strip(text: &str) -> &str;
/// str.isdigit(), ASCII digits only (see Open points). Def: T1. Use: T3, T6, T12.
pub fn py_isdigit(text: &str) -> bool;
/// int() of a str: surrounding whitespace, one sign, ASCII digits with single underscores between them; None where
/// Python raises ValueError. Def: T1. Use: T2, T3, T6, T7, T9, T10, T12.
pub fn py_int(text: &str) -> Option<i64>;
/// float() of a str: whitespace, sign, digits with underscores, exponent, "inf"/"infinity"/"nan" in any case;
/// None where Python raises ValueError. Def: T1. Use: T4, T8 (--set), T9, T10.
pub fn py_float(text: &str) -> Option<f64>;
/// int() of a JSON value: an int as is, a float truncated, a str by py_int, a bool as 0 or 1; Err is Python's
/// TypeError or ValueError text. Def: T1. Use: T9, T10 (packet sizes), T11.
pub fn py_int_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<i64, String>;
/// float() of a JSON value: an int or float as f64, a str by py_float; Err as above. Def: T1. Use: T9, T10.
pub fn py_float_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<f64, String>;
/// repr(float): the shortest round-trip digits, exponent form below 1e-4 and from 1e16 ("1e-05", "1e+16"), ".0" on
/// whole numbers, "nan", "inf", "-inf". Def: T1. Use: T1 pyjson, T5/T8 (Num's Display, canonical constants JSON).
pub fn py_float_repr(x: f64) -> String;
/// '%.Nf' % x (round half to even on the exact binary value; "nan", "inf", "-0.0" spelt as Python spells them).
/// Def: T1. Use: T3, T4 testsupport, T6, T8, T9, T10, T12.
pub fn py_fixed(x: f64, digits: usize) -> String;
/// format(x, "g") (6 significant digits, trailing zeros dropped). Def: T1. Use: T4 (refusal), T11 (volume=).
pub fn py_g(x: f64) -> String;
/// repr() of a str: single quotes unless the text holds ' and no ", backslash escapes for \\ \n \r \t and the
/// quote, \xNN / \uNNNN / \UNNNNNNNN for characters Python does not print. Def: T1. Use: T7, T9, T11, T12.
pub fn py_repr_str(text: &str) -> String;
/// repr() of the Python value json.loads gives: None, True, False, ints, py_float_repr, py_repr_str,
/// "[a, b]", "{'k': v}". Def: T1. Use: T7 (problem sentences), T8 (fitted order), T11, T12.
pub fn py_repr(value: &serde_json::Value) -> String;
/// str() of that value: a str as is, otherwise py_repr. Def: T1. Use: T3 (channel counts), T12.
pub fn py_str(value: &serde_json::Value) -> String;
/// bool() of that value: false for null, false, 0, 0.0, "", [] and {}. Def: T1. Use: T7, T8, T12.
pub fn py_truthy(value: &serde_json::Value) -> bool;
```

#### `Ordered`

```rust
/// A Python dict whose order is printed or written: entries in insertion order; `insert` of a present key replaces
/// its value in place. Serialised as a JSON object in that order; deserialised keeping the file's order. `==`
/// compares in order (Python's dict == does not: sort first where order may differ). Def: T1. Use: T4 (Fields),
/// T8 (overrides, unlabelled verdicts), T10 (shares, corrections), T12.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Ordered<V>(pub Vec<(String, V)>);
/// Empty; written by hand so that V needs no Default (Ordered<Verdict> has one).
impl<V> Default for Ordered<V>;

impl<V> Ordered<V> {
    pub fn new() -> Ordered<V>;
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&V>;
    pub fn contains_key(&self, key: &str) -> bool;
    pub fn insert(&mut self, key: String, value: V);
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &V)>;
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize;
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool;
}
impl<V: serde::Serialize> serde::Serialize for Ordered<V>;
impl<'de, V: serde::Deserialize<'de>> serde::Deserialize<'de> for Ordered<V>;
```

Types of the recorder's files. Unknown keys are ignored (`serde` default); every field the Python reads with `.get()` is an `Option` with `#[serde(default)]`. ### `core::testsupport` (`testsupport/mod.rs`; Task 1, generators added by Task 4)

```rust
/// Python's random.Random: MT19937 seeded as random.seed(int) (init_by_array over the 32-bit words of the seed),
/// with the methods the tests call, giving the same values as Python 3.9. `cfg(any(test, feature = "testsupport"))`.
/// Checked against crates/core/tests/fixtures/pyrandom.json (values Python printed once). Py: random.Random.
/// Def: T1. Use: T4, T5, T6, T8, T10, T11.
pub struct PyRandom { /* state: [u32; 624], index: usize */ }
impl PyRandom {
    /// random.Random(seed) for a non-negative int seed.
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> PyRandom;
    /// random(): 53 bits, (a >> 5) * 67108864 + (b >> 6), over 2**53.
    pub fn random(&mut self) -> f64;
    /// getrandbits(k), 1 <= k <= 64 (words taken little-end first, as CPython).
    pub fn getrandbits(&mut self, k: u32) -> u64;
    /// randint(a, b) = a + _randbelow(b - a + 1), _randbelow by rejection on getrandbits(n.bit_length()).
    pub fn randint(&mut self, a: i64, b: i64) -> i64;
    /// uniform(a, b) = a + (b - a) * random().
    pub fn uniform(&mut self, a: f64, b: f64) -> f64;
    /// choice(seq) = seq[_randbelow(len(seq))]; panics on an empty slice (Python's IndexError).
    pub fn choice<'a, T>(&mut self, seq: &'a [T]) -> &'a T;
}

// Added by Task 4: the synthetic level series of test_audio_similarity.py and test_audio_dataset.py (one copy,
// both test files define them identically). Def: T4. Use: T5, T6, T8, T11.
/// 20 ms frames per second.
pub const FPS: usize = 50;
/// Syllables: loud for randint(4, 7) frames, quiet for randint(4, 8), each level plus uniform(-1, 1). Py: speech.
pub fn speech(rnd: &mut PyRandom, frames: usize, loud: f64, quiet: f64) -> Vec<f64>;
/// (mix, centre) of a dialogue-driven programme. Py: programme(seconds=420, seed=1).
pub fn programme(seconds: usize, seed: u64) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>);
/// 10 * log10(10 ** (a / 10) + 10 ** (b / 10)). Py: power_sum.
pub fn power_sum(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64;
/// Two voices talking through `mix` ducked by 30 dB. Py: commentary(mix, seed=7).
pub fn commentary(mix: &[f64], seed: u64) -> Vec<f64>;
/// A compact level file as audio-levels.ps1 writes it: the header line, then py_fixed(v, 1) per line, "\n" ends. Py: level_file.
pub fn level_file_text(values: &[f64]) -> String;
/// ffmpeg's ametadata output, one frame every `step_s` seconds. Py: test_audio_similarity.raw_file.
pub fn raw_file_text(values: &[f64], step_s: f64) -> String;
```

```rust
/// How json.dumps was called. Def: T1. Use: T7, T8, T9, T11, T12, T13, T14.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Style {
    /// None: one line with Python's default separators ", " and ": "; Some(n): n spaces per level with "," and ": ".
    pub indent: Option<usize>,
    /// true: every non-ASCII character as \uXXXX (lowercase hex, surrogate pairs above U+FFFF); false: kept.
    /// Both escape \" \\ \n \r \t \b \f and other controls below 0x20 as \u00XX, as json.dumps does.
    pub ensure_ascii: bool,
    /// json.dumps(sort_keys=True): object keys by code point.
    pub sort_keys: bool,
}
impl Style {
    /// json.dumps(x): indent None, ASCII, insertion order.
    pub const PY_DEFAULT: Style;
    /// The snapshot and streams.json: indent 1, ASCII.
    pub const INDENT1_ASCII: Style;
    /// The labels and fitted files: indent 2, non-ASCII kept.
    pub const INDENT2_UTF8: Style;
}

/// json.dumps(value, ...) byte for byte: insertion order (serde_json `preserve_order`), ints and floats distinct
/// (`Number::is_f64` floats spelt by core's py_float_repr), true/false/null, empty containers as [] and {}.
/// A NaN never reaches it: serde_json::Value holds none (nan_to_none). Py: json.dumps. Def: T1. Use: as Style.
```

```rust
/// Every command, in every cmd/<name>.rs:
///     pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32;
/// `args` excludes the command name; the return value is the exit code of spec 3.4; stdout lines go to `out`,
/// error lines to `err`. Def: T1 (the type and dispatch). Use: T2 to T14 (one file each).
pub type Command = fn(&Ctx, &[String], &mut dyn std::io::Write, &mut dyn std::io::Write) -> i32;

/// (name as typed, the command, its one-line synopsis for --help), in spec 3.4's order. A task adds its row.
/// Def: T1 (empty table and `--help`). Use: T2 to T14.
pub const COMMANDS: &[(&str, Command, &str)];

/// `argv[0]` picks the command; `--help`, no argument or an unknown name print the table (exit 0 for --help,
/// 2 otherwise). Def: T1.
pub fn dispatch(ctx: &Ctx, argv: &[String], out: &mut dyn std::io::Write, err: &mut dyn std::io::Write) -> i32;

/// Hand-written argument parsing with argparse's spellings: `--name VALUE`, `--name=VALUE`, a unique prefix of a
/// declared long flag (argparse's allow_abbrev), repeatable flags, switches, positionals. Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub struct Args { /* remaining words, declared flags */ }
impl Args {
    /// The words after the command name; `flags` declares the long flags the command knows (with "--").
    pub fn new(args: &[String], flags: &[&str]) -> Args;
    /// The value of a single-use flag; Err("argument --name: expected one argument") when it has none.
    pub fn flag(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, String>;
    /// Every value of a repeatable flag (--set), in order.
    pub fn flags(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
    /// Whether a switch (--allow-unmeasured) was given.
    pub fn switch(&mut self, name: &str) -> bool;
    /// The words left; Err("unrecognized arguments: ...") for an undeclared "--" word.
    pub fn positionals(self) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
}
/// Prints "usage: lazymkv-dev <usage>" and "lazymkv-dev <cmd>: error: <message>" to `err`, returns 2 (argparse's
/// exit). Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
```

### `core::audio::labels` (Task 7)

The labels file and the fitted file are `serde_json::Value` (insertion order kept, unknown keys kept); validation runs over the value and gives the Python's sentences verbatim (`{x!r}` through `py_repr`); typed views exist only after validation. Edits are functions from a value to the new value; `crates/dev` writes the result with `pyjson::write_labels`.

```rust
}
```

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum HarnessError { Labels(Vec<String>) }
/// The tuning harness over the evidence (Python main's body from loading the labels to the change blocks).
/// Py: audio_dataset.main. Def: T8. Use: T14.
pub fn harness(input: &HarnessInput) -> Result<Harness, HarnessError>;

/// Where the snapshot goes. Py: main's choice of `out`. Def: T8.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Destination { Given, Trial, Unchecked, Baseline }
/// --snapshot given; else overrides: Trial; else something unchecked other than "not measured": Unchecked; else
/// Baseline. Def: T8.
pub fn destination(given: bool, overrides: bool, unchecked: &[String]) -> Destination;
/// The phrase after the path (" (a trial: the baseline is not replaced)", " (the baseline <baseline_shown> was NOT
/// replaced: ...; to replace it on purpose, run again with --snapshot <baseline_shown>)", or ""). Def: T8.
pub fn why_phrase(dest: Destination, baseline_shown: &str, unchecked: &[String]) -> String;
/// "snapshot: <out><why>" plus " (unchanged but for its time: not rewritten)" when not written. Def: T8.
pub fn snapshot_line(out_shown: &str, why: &str, written: bool) -> String;
/// The RESULT line and the exit code (1 failures; 3 unchecked without --allow-unmeasured; 0). Def: T8. Use: T14.
pub fn result_line(failures: &[String], unchecked: &[String], allow_unmeasured: bool) -> (String, i32);
```

The dev side of `retune` (Task 8): read the spec (exit 2), `parse_sets` (exit 2), `resolve_evidence` (exit 3), `DiskTree::open`, read `audio-dataset.json` with `read_snapshot`, run `harness`, pick the destination, compare `pyjson::dumps(old with "created": null, INDENT1_ASCII)` with the same of the new snapshot (text comparison, as the Python's `timeless`), write with `pyjson::write_snapshot` unless equal, append "", the snapshot line and the RESULT line, print, exit.

### Golden files (Tasks 13 and 14)

Every golden is written once by `write_goldens.py` (evidence repository, Task 14) into `corpus/owner/<slug>/golden/` (and `corpus/owner/golden/` for the corpus-wide ones), with exactly the serde form of the Rust type named here, so `golden check` and Task 13's `decide` tests compare by `pyjson::structural_diff` with `Tolerance::spec()` (text files: line by line). The JSON writer for goldens is `json.dumps(x, indent=1) + "\n"` (ASCII); NaN is written as null (`nan_to_none` applied by the writer at every level). No golden holds subtitle text, a drive serial, a machine user name, a token or unit-key content: the types below carry none (`Scan.drives` and `messages`, `Track.events[].lines`, `Features.words` and `Measured.bigrams` are never serialised; `proxy.txt` and `ffmpeg.txt` are left out of the proxy golden).

| Golden file | Rust type (serde form) | Produced by | Def | Compared by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<slug>/golden/scan.json` | `robot::ScanJson` | `robot::scan_json(&parse(scan.txt))` | T2 | T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/titles.txt` | lines | `audio::titles::titles_report` | T6 | T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/<label>/reconcile.json` | `reconcile::Report` | `reconcile::reconcile` (selection and title from `rip_label`) | T3 | T13, T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/<label>/audio-<folder>.json` | `audio::report::FolderJson` | `results` (default rule, `Plain`) then `folder_json` | T6 | T13, T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/<label>/audio-<folder>.txt` | lines | `audio::report::report_lines` | T6 | T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/<label>/subs.json` | `subtitle::text::SubsJson` | `subs_run` then `subs_json` | T10 | T13, T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/<label>/subs.txt` | lines | `SubsRun.stdout` then `SubsRun.stderr` | T10 | T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/<label>/align.json` | `subtitle::align::AlignJson` | `align_subs_dir(<label>/subs, 64, 300)` | T9 | T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/labels.json` | `audio::labels::LabelsJson` | `labels_json` | T7 | T14 |
| `<slug>/golden/proxy-<folder>/` | `manifest.txt`, the level files, `streams.json` (byte for byte) and `golden.json` (`ProxyGolden`) | `levels_from_proxy::build` | T11 | T14 |
| `golden/retune-report.txt` | lines | `harness` + the snapshot and RESULT lines | T8 | T14 |
| `golden/README.md` | the schema of each file above, and a fenced code block whose info string is `json written_by` (`WrittenBy`) | by hand, Task 14 | T14 | T14 |

```rust
    /// The lazymkv pull request and the branch commit write_goldens.py ran beside.

}
/// The written_by block of golden/README.md. Def: T14.
pub fn read_written_by(readme: &str) -> Result<WrittenBy, String>;

/// proxy-<folder>/golden.json: what was rebuilt and with which ffmpeg. Def: T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ProxyGolden {
    pub slug: String, pub label: String,

    pub proxy_sha1: String,
}

/// How one comparison ended. Display: "pass", "fail: <first differences>", "skipped: <reason>". Def: T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Outcome { Pass, Fail(String), Skipped(String) }
/// One comparison: its name is the golden's path below corpus/owner ("<slug>/golden/<label>/subs.json").
/// Def: T14.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Comparison { pub name: String, pub outcome: Outcome }
/// Every comparison of the table above for every recording with a golden/ folder, in PathKey order, plus a
/// "not covered" line per recording or rip label without one. Skip reasons, verbatim: "no evidence clone at
/// <dir>", "no golden/ folder for <slug>", the Python's "its level files are not here ..." line, "no OCR text:
/// <path> (give --text DIR or LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT)", "ffmpeg is not on PATH", "ffmpeg is <v>, the golden was
/// written by <v>", "the proxy is not fetched: <path>". Def: T14.
pub fn check(ctx: &Ctx, evidence: &std::path::Path, text: Option<&std::path::Path>) -> Vec<Comparison>;
/// The summary line ("golden check: <p> pass, <f> fail, <s> skipped") and the exit code: 1 on any fail, 3 when
/// nothing could run, 0 otherwise. Def: T14.
pub fn summary(comparisons: &[Comparison]) -> (String, i32);
/// `golden write`: the same files from the Rust (for a named re-recording commit only). Def: T14.
pub fn write(ctx: &Ctx, evidence: &std::path::Path, text: Option<&std::path::Path>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
/// The round trip of spec section 5: the committed v2 baseline against the first v3 snapshot, structurally, with
/// "/format", "/created", "/code", "/tracks/*/key" and "/tracks/*/peer/key" ignored and "measures_cache" compared
/// as a multiset of values (its keys changed with the formula). Def: T14.
pub fn snapshot_diff(baseline: &serde_json::Value, ours: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<String>;
/// retune-report.txt against the Rust's lines: byte for byte, except the lines whose content depends on the
/// cache and the baseline's state rather than on the rule: "measures: ...", "snapshot: ...", and the parenthesis
/// of "Changes since the previous snapshot (...):" (see Open points). Def: T14.
pub fn retune_diff(golden: &[String], ours: &[String]) -> Vec<String>;
```

### Open points found while fixing the interfaces

Each needs a decision in the task named, or a line in the spec's list of deliberate deviations; none changes a verdict.

1. **retune-report.txt has state-dependent lines (Task 14).** Spec 3.4 says `golden check` compares every line but the five rewritten ones byte for byte. Three more depend on the cache and the baseline, not on the rule: `measures: <a> analysed now, <b> taken from the cache` (the Python ran against a warm v2 cache; the first Rust run computes everything), `snapshot: <path>...` (the Python's "unchanged but for its time"), and the parenthesis of `Changes since the previous snapshot (<created>, code <sha> | rule version <n>):`. `retune_diff` exempts exactly these; `golden check` runs the harness with `--snapshot` into the temporary folder so a check never replaces the baseline.
2. **The round trip also differs in `format` (Task 14).** Spec section 4 lists `created`, `code`, `tracks[].key`, peer `key` and the `measures_cache` keys as the only differences between the v2 baseline and the first v3 snapshot; `format` differs too (v2 to v3). `snapshot_diff` ignores it.
3. **`cfg(test)` does not reach `crates/dev`'s tests (Task 1).** `PyRandom` and the level generators are needed by the dev crate's integration tests (ProxyStreams, the retune tests); the `testsupport` cargo feature above provides them without a new dependency.
4. **Skip lines and the test harness (Task 1).** `cargo test` captures `println!` and `eprintln!` of passing tests, so "skipped: <reason>" would not show; `evidence::skip` writes to `std::io::stderr()` directly, which is not captured.
5. **Local time without a date crate (Task 1).** `datetime.now()` and `date.today()` are local; `std` has no time-zone offset, and only the named crates are allowed. `Ctx::now` should run `date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'` (macOS, Linux) or `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Date -Format s"` (the mini PC) through `RealRunner`, falling back to UTC with a stderr warning; tests set `clock`. A UTC `today()` would date a label set in the evening (US time) a day late in `audio-labels.json`. Confirmed by the owner, 2026-10-14 (RP9).
6. **Error texts on malformed JSON (all tasks).** `serde_json`'s messages differ from Python's `JSONDecodeError` ("Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"). No recorded file is malformed, so no golden line holds one; the spec's deviation list should name it.
7. **`encoding` splits bytes (Task 12).** Spec 3.2 lists `encoding` among the `str.splitlines` readers; the Python splits the raw bytes with `bytes.splitlines` (\n, \r, \r\n only). The interface follows the Python (`py_bytes_splitlines`).
8. **Two more line splitters (Tasks 4 and 11).** `frame_ms_of` and `convert_levels` iterate a text-mode file (universal newlines: \n, \r, \r\n), not `str.splitlines`; `universal_lines` covers them.
9. **`str.isdigit` and `int()` on non-ASCII digits (Tasks 1, 3, 6, 12).** Python accepts other Unicode digits (`isdigit` true, then `int` may raise); `py_isdigit` and `py_int` take ASCII only. The planner of Task 1 confirms no recorded or pinned scan holds a non-ASCII digit (`grep -P '[^\x00-\x7f]'` over the robot logs, digits only).
10. **Typed recorder files (Task 1).** A summary or index field of an unexpected type fails the whole `serde` parse where the Python's `isinstance` skipped only that field. Every recorded `rip-summary.json` has `ok` bool, `title` int, `bytes` int (checked while writing this part); a broken file becomes "unreadable" rather than partly read.
11. **Where the proxy golden's input comes from (Task 14).** The spec's skip list has no "proxy absent", but the `.mka` lives only on the dataset share. `tuning-fetch.ps1` copies it to `<DIR>/<slug>/<label>/audio-proxy.mka`, the same layout as the OCR text, so `golden check --text DIR` finds both; absent, the comparison is `skipped: the proxy is not fetched: <path>`. The golden's level files are committed in the evidence repository (`<slug>/golden/proxy-<folder>/` does not match the `*/*/audio-levels-*/*.txt` ignore rule): about 2 MB per series.
12. **Two OCR text layouts (Tasks 10, 13, 14).** `subs --text DIR` reads `DIR/sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl` (the Python's); the goldens' layout is `<DIR>/<slug>/<label>/<reading>/`. `decide_doc` tries `<DIR>/<slug>/<label>/subs-ocr/` first, then `DIR` itself.
13. **Two more lines name a Python script (Tasks 7, 8).** Besides spec 3.4's five: the harness's "RESULT FAILED: a labels file does not validate (audio_labels.py check)" (written above as `lazymkv-dev labels check`; not in the golden report) and `exp13_requirements`' "...; update audio_labels.py" (should name `core::audio::labels`). The `--compare` header "Changes against <file> (<created>, code <sha>):" maps as the "Changes since" one does.
14. **`labels auto` writes once (Task 7).** The Python saved after each label; the Rust applies the same edits in order to one value and writes once. Same final file; after a mid-run refusal nothing is written instead of the earlier labels.
15. **`decide` and the golden audio check recompute every measure (Tasks 13, 14).** `Plain` over full series (about 357,000 frames per series on the UHD recording) is the slow path; the per-recording `decide` tests take minutes. A `Measurer` seeded from the committed v3 snapshot would make them fast but would no longer exercise `analyse`. Settled: recompute (owner, 2026-10-14, RP8).
16. **`--evidence`'s default (Task 1).** The Python's default `corpus/owner` was relative to the current directory; `resolve_evidence` takes it under `repo_root` when one is found, so `cargo test` (which runs in `crates/dev`) and a subdirectory both find the clone. Paths are printed as `corpus/owner/...` either way.
17. **argparse abbreviations (Task 1).** argparse accepts a unique prefix of a long flag (`--allow` for `--allow-unmeasured`); `Args` does too, so every command line the Python accepted still works.
18. **Audio verdicts to review reasons (Task 13).** Spec 3.4 says `reviews` is "the union of the review reasons of the audio verdicts", but neither the spec nor the Python maps verdicts to reasons. `audio_reviews` takes the mapping from MEANING and spec 8.8: reference-unclear raises `audio_reference_unclear`; commentary and commentary-cross-language raise `commentary_detected` (MEANING names it for the cross-language case; for a same-language commentary, spec 8.6 leaves whether it goes to review open under D15); ad-pattern, note-commentary and note-ad are notes, not reasons. Confirmed by the owner, 2026-10-14 (RP7): a same-language commentary goes to review.

**`core::recording` (`recording/mod.rs`, Task 1)**

*The tree*

```rust
/// A path inside a tree: '/'-separated components below the tree's root. Ordered component by component, each
/// name by code point (derived `Ord` over `Vec<String>`), which is how Python sorts `PurePosixPath` objects:
/// `all-tracks/x` < `all-tracks-2/x` and `audio-levels-20ms-1-2/x` < `audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3/x`.
/// Py: pathlib.PurePosixPath ordering. Def: T1. Use: every later task.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct PathKey(Vec<String>);

impl PathKey {
    /// The tree's root (no component).
    pub fn root() -> PathKey;
    /// A key from "a/b/c"; empty and "." components are dropped, as pathlib drops them.
    pub fn new(path: &str) -> PathKey;
    /// This key with `name` appended ("x/y" appends two components). Py: `path / name`.
    pub fn join(&self, name: &str) -> PathKey;
    /// The key without its last component (the root's parent is the root). Py: Path.parent.
    pub fn parent(&self) -> PathKey;
    /// The last component, "" for the root. Py: Path.name.
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str;
    /// The components in order.
    pub fn components(&self) -> &[String];
}
/// '/'-joined components, "" for the root.
impl std::fmt::Display for PathKey;

/// What a path names. Py: Path.is_file / Path.is_dir.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind { File, Dir }

/// A file the tree does not have. Its Display is Python's FileNotFoundError text,
/// `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<shown>'`, with `shown` the path as `Tree::display` prints it. Def: T1.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Missing { pub path: PathKey, pub shown: String }

/// Why a read failed: the file is not there, or the OS refused it (the message is the OSError text). Def: T1.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ReadError { Missing(Missing), Io { path: PathKey, message: String } }
impl std::fmt::Display for ReadError;

/// A recording directory or the whole evidence directory, in memory. Every walker of the Python is a function over
/// it. `list` and `glob` never return a folder named `golden` or anything under one (section 5 of the spec reserves
/// the name); `read`, `kind` and `exists` do not filter, so the golden code reads its files through the same tree.
/// Py: the pathlib calls of every module. Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub trait Tree {
    /// File, folder, or None when absent. Py: Path.exists / is_file / is_dir.
    fn kind(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Option<Kind>;
    /// `self.kind(path).is_some()`. Py: Path.exists.
    fn exists(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool;
    /// Py: Path.is_file.
    fn is_file(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool;
    /// Py: Path.is_dir.
    fn is_dir(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool;
    /// The entries directly in `dir`, files and folders, in `PathKey` order. Py: sorted(dir.iterdir()).
    fn list(&self, dir: &PathKey) -> Vec<PathKey>;
    /// The paths below `base` matching `pattern`: '/'-separated, each component an fnmatch pattern (`*`, `?`,
    /// `[seq]`, `[!seq]`, case-sensitive, a leading dot matched like any character, as pathlib's glob), in
    /// `PathKey` order. Py: sorted(base.glob(pattern)).
    fn glob(&self, base: &PathKey, pattern: &str) -> Vec<PathKey>;
    /// The file's bytes; a lazy entry is loaded on its first read and kept. Py: Path.read_bytes.
    fn read(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Result<std::sync::Arc<[u8]>, ReadError>;
    /// The path as the Python printed it: the tree's display root joined with `path` as pathlib joins
    /// (a display root of "." adds nothing). Py: str(Path).
    fn display(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String;
    /// The last component of the path's resolved absolute form; for the root, the resolved root's own name.
    /// Py: Path.resolve().name (audio_similarity.report's label, audio_labels' new slug, levels_args' slug).
    fn resolved_name(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String;
}

/// Loads a lazy file's bytes once; `Err` holds the OSError text. Def: T1.
pub type Loader = std::sync::Arc<dyn Fn() -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> + Send + Sync>;

/// The in-memory `Tree`: `BTreeMap<PathKey, Node>` with folders explicit (an empty folder exists, as on disk),
/// files as bytes or as a `Loader`. Tests build it directly; `crates/dev` fills it from a directory. Def: T1. Use: all.
pub struct MemTree { /* entries, display_root, resolved_root */ }

impl MemTree {
    /// An empty tree printed under `display_root` ("corpus/owner", ".", or a path as the user gave it) whose root
    /// resolves to a folder named `resolved_root_name`.
    pub fn new(display_root: &str, resolved_root_name: &str) -> MemTree;
    /// Adds a file (its parent folders too).
    pub fn insert_file(&mut self, path: &str, bytes: impl Into<Vec<u8>>);
    /// Adds a file read on first use.
    pub fn insert_lazy(&mut self, path: &str, load: Loader);
    /// Adds a folder (its parents too).
    pub fn insert_dir(&mut self, path: &str);
}
impl Tree for MemTree;
```

*Decoding and line splitting*

```rust
/// Python's "utf-8" (a byte-order mark stays as U+FEFF) and "utf-8-sig" (one leading mark removed). Def: T1.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Encoding { Utf8, Utf8Sig }

/// Python's errors="strict" and errors="replace" (U+FFFD per maximal invalid subpart, as `from_utf8_lossy`). Def: T1.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Errors { Strict, Replace }

/// Bytes to text as `bytes.decode(encoding, errors)`; Err is Python's UnicodeDecodeError text
/// ("'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte"). Py: Path.read_text. Def: T1. Use: all readers.
pub fn decode_text(bytes: &[u8], encoding: Encoding, errors: Errors) -> Result<String, String>;

/// `tree.read` then `decode_text`; Err is the ReadError or decode text. Py: Path.read_text(encoding, errors). Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub fn read_text(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey, encoding: Encoding, errors: Errors) -> Result<String, String>;

/// A JSON file read as "utf-8-sig", strict, into `T`. Py: json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")). Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub fn read_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey) -> Result<T, String>;

/// Lines on Python's `str.splitlines` boundaries: \n, \r, \r\n, \v, \f, \x1c, \x1d, \x1e, \x85, \u2028, \u2029; no
/// terminators; no final empty line. Py: str.splitlines. Def: T1. Use: T4 (levels, manifest, refusal), T7 (row 13),
/// T10 (ocr_records), T12 (hit-rate statuses, ocr-compare).
pub fn py_splitlines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>;

/// Lines as Python's text-mode file iteration gives them (universal newlines: \n, \r, \r\n only), without
/// terminators. Py: `for line in open(path)`. Def: T1. Use: T4 (frame_ms_of), T1 pyjson (convert_levels).
pub fn universal_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>;

/// `text.split("\n")`, each line with its trailing "\r"s removed (rstrip("\r")); a final empty piece kept, as
/// split keeps it. Py: robot.parse's loop. Def: T1. Use: T2.
pub fn strip_cr_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>;

/// Lines of bytes on `bytes.splitlines` boundaries (\n, \r, \r\n only). Py: check_encoding's data.splitlines().
/// Def: T1. Use: T12 (encoding).
pub fn py_bytes_splitlines(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<&[u8]>;
```

*Python spellings*

```rust
/// Python's str.isspace for one character: Unicode White_Space plus the bidi classes B, S and WS, so \x1c to \x1f
/// count (Rust's char::is_whitespace does not). Def: T1. Use: the helpers below.
pub fn py_is_space(c: char) -> bool;
/// str.split() with no argument (runs of py_is_space, no empty pieces). Def: T1. Use: T4 (manifest), T10, T12.
pub fn py_split(text: &str) -> Vec<&str>;
/// str.strip() with no argument. Def: T1. Use: T4, T10, T12.
pub fn py_strip(text: &str) -> &str;
/// str.isdigit(), ASCII digits only (see Open points). Def: T1. Use: T3, T6, T12.
pub fn py_isdigit(text: &str) -> bool;
/// int() of a str: surrounding whitespace, one sign, ASCII digits with single underscores between them; None where
/// Python raises ValueError. Def: T1. Use: T2, T3, T6, T7, T9, T10, T12.
pub fn py_int(text: &str) -> Option<i64>;
/// float() of a str: whitespace, sign, digits with underscores, exponent, "inf"/"infinity"/"nan" in any case;
/// None where Python raises ValueError. Def: T1. Use: T4, T8 (--set), T9, T10.
pub fn py_float(text: &str) -> Option<f64>;
/// int() of a JSON value: an int as is, a float truncated, a str by py_int, a bool as 0 or 1; Err is Python's
/// TypeError or ValueError text. Def: T1. Use: T9, T10 (packet sizes), T11.
pub fn py_int_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<i64, String>;
/// float() of a JSON value: an int or float as f64, a str by py_float; Err as above. Def: T1. Use: T9, T10.
pub fn py_float_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<f64, String>;
/// repr(float): the shortest round-trip digits, exponent form below 1e-4 and from 1e16 ("1e-05", "1e+16"), ".0" on
/// whole numbers, "nan", "inf", "-inf". Def: T1. Use: T1 pyjson, T5/T8 (Num's Display, canonical constants JSON).
pub fn py_float_repr(x: f64) -> String;
/// '%.Nf' % x (round half to even on the exact binary value; "nan", "inf", "-0.0" spelt as Python spells them).
/// Def: T1. Use: T3, T4 testsupport, T6, T8, T9, T10, T12.
pub fn py_fixed(x: f64, digits: usize) -> String;
/// format(x, "g") (6 significant digits, trailing zeros dropped). Def: T1. Use: T4 (refusal), T11 (volume=).
pub fn py_g(x: f64) -> String;
/// repr() of a str: single quotes unless the text holds ' and no ", backslash escapes for \\ \n \r \t and the
/// quote, \xNN / \uNNNN / \UNNNNNNNN for characters Python does not print. Def: T1. Use: T7, T9, T11, T12.
pub fn py_repr_str(text: &str) -> String;
/// repr() of the Python value json.loads gives: None, True, False, ints, py_float_repr, py_repr_str,
/// "[a, b]", "{'k': v}". Def: T1. Use: T7 (problem sentences), T8 (fitted order), T11, T12.
pub fn py_repr(value: &serde_json::Value) -> String;
/// str() of that value: a str as is, otherwise py_repr. Def: T1. Use: T3 (channel counts), T12.
pub fn py_str(value: &serde_json::Value) -> String;
/// bool() of that value: false for null, false, 0, 0.0, "", [] and {}. Def: T1. Use: T7, T8, T12.
pub fn py_truthy(value: &serde_json::Value) -> bool;
```

*`Ordered`*

```rust
/// A Python dict whose order is printed or written: entries in insertion order; `insert` of a present key replaces
/// its value in place. Serialised as a JSON object in that order; deserialised keeping the file's order. `==`
/// compares in order (Python's dict == does not: sort first where order may differ). Def: T1. Use: T4 (Fields),
/// T8 (overrides, unlabelled verdicts), T10 (shares, corrections), T12.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Ordered<V>(pub Vec<(String, V)>);
/// Empty; written by hand so that V needs no Default (Ordered<Verdict> has one).
impl<V> Default for Ordered<V>;

impl<V> Ordered<V> {
    pub fn new() -> Ordered<V>;
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&V>;
    pub fn contains_key(&self, key: &str) -> bool;
    pub fn insert(&mut self, key: String, value: V);
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &V)>;
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize;
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool;
}
impl<V: serde::Serialize> serde::Serialize for Ordered<V>;
impl<'de, V: serde::Deserialize<'de>> serde::Deserialize<'de> for Ordered<V>;
```

**`core::recording::files` (`recording/files.rs`, Task 1)**

Types of the recorder's files. Unknown keys are ignored (`serde` default); every field the Python reads with `.get()` is an `Option` with `#[serde(default)]`. **`core::testsupport` (`testsupport/mod.rs`; Task 1, generators added by Task 4)**

```rust
/// Python's random.Random: MT19937 seeded as random.seed(int) (init_by_array over the 32-bit words of the seed),
/// with the methods the tests call, giving the same values as Python 3.9. `cfg(any(test, feature = "testsupport"))`.
/// Checked against crates/core/tests/fixtures/pyrandom.json (values Python printed once). Py: random.Random.
/// Def: T1. Use: T4, T5, T6, T8, T10, T11.
pub struct PyRandom { /* state: [u32; 624], index: usize */ }
impl PyRandom {
    /// random.Random(seed) for a non-negative int seed.
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> PyRandom;
    /// random(): 53 bits, (a >> 5) * 67108864 + (b >> 6), over 2**53.
    pub fn random(&mut self) -> f64;
    /// getrandbits(k), 1 <= k <= 64 (words taken little-end first, as CPython).
    pub fn getrandbits(&mut self, k: u32) -> u64;
    /// randint(a, b) = a + _randbelow(b - a + 1), _randbelow by rejection on getrandbits(n.bit_length()).
    pub fn randint(&mut self, a: i64, b: i64) -> i64;
    /// uniform(a, b) = a + (b - a) * random().
    pub fn uniform(&mut self, a: f64, b: f64) -> f64;
    /// choice(seq) = seq[_randbelow(len(seq))]; panics on an empty slice (Python's IndexError).
    pub fn choice<'a, T>(&mut self, seq: &'a [T]) -> &'a T;
}
```

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Style {
    /// None: one line with Python's default separators ", " and ": "; Some(n): n spaces per level with "," and ": ".
    pub indent: Option<usize>,
    /// true: every non-ASCII character as \uXXXX (lowercase hex, surrogate pairs above U+FFFF); false: kept.
    /// Both escape \" \\ \n \r \t \b \f and other controls below 0x20 as \u00XX, as json.dumps does.
    pub ensure_ascii: bool,
```

```rust
/// Every command, in every cmd/<name>.rs:
///     pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32;
/// `args` excludes the command name; the return value is the exit code of spec 3.4; stdout lines go to `out`,
/// error lines to `err`. Def: T1 (the type and dispatch). Use: T2 to T14 (one file each).
pub type Command = fn(&Ctx, &[String], &mut dyn std::io::Write, &mut dyn std::io::Write) -> i32;

/// (name as typed, the command, its one-line synopsis for --help), in spec 3.4's order. A task adds its row.
/// Def: T1 (empty table and `--help`). Use: T2 to T14.
pub const COMMANDS: &[(&str, Command, &str)];

/// `argv[0]` picks the command; `--help`, no argument or an unknown name print the table (exit 0 for --help,
/// 2 otherwise). Def: T1.
pub fn dispatch(ctx: &Ctx, argv: &[String], out: &mut dyn std::io::Write, err: &mut dyn std::io::Write) -> i32;

/// Hand-written argument parsing with argparse's spellings: `--name VALUE`, `--name=VALUE`, a unique prefix of a
/// declared long flag (argparse's allow_abbrev), repeatable flags, switches, positionals. Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub struct Args { /* remaining words, declared flags */ }
impl Args {
    /// The words after the command name; `flags` declares the long flags the command knows (with "--").
    pub fn new(args: &[String], flags: &[&str]) -> Args;
    /// The value of a single-use flag; Err("argument --name: expected one argument") when it has none.
    pub fn flag(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, String>;
    /// Every value of a repeatable flag (--set), in order.
    pub fn flags(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
    /// Whether a switch (--allow-unmeasured) was given.
    pub fn switch(&mut self, name: &str) -> bool;
    /// The words left; Err("unrecognized arguments: ...") for an undeclared "--" word.
    pub fn positionals(self) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
}
/// Prints "usage: lazymkv-dev <usage>" and "lazymkv-dev <cmd>: error: <message>" to `err`, returns 2 (argparse's
/// exit). Def: T1. Use: T2 to T14.
pub fn usage_error(err: &mut dyn std::io::Write, cmd: &str, usage: &str, message: &str) -> i32;
```

Where this task's code differs from those entries (each change is additive, or needed for the entry to compile; later tasks may rely on it):

1. `Command`, `COMMANDS`, `dispatch`, `Args` and `usage_error` live in `crates/dev/src/lib.rs`, not in `main.rs`: items of a binary cannot be reached from `cmd/*.rs` modules shared with the integration tests under `crates/dev/tests/`. Paths: `lazymkv_dev::{Command, COMMANDS, dispatch, Args, usage_error}`, `lazymkv_dev::evidence::*`, `lazymkv_dev::pyjson::*`, `lazymkv_dev::runner::*`, `lazymkv_dev::cmd::<name>::run`. `main.rs` only calls `dispatch`.
2. `Summary` also derives `PartialEq` (`RipLabel` derives `PartialEq` and holds a `Summary`).
3. Every `Option` field of `FfprobeStream` carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`: a stream is written back as ffprobe and `proxy_streams` write it, with an absent key left out.
4. `Tree::exists`, `Tree::is_file` and `Tree::is_dir` have default bodies over `kind`; an implementation writes `kind`, `list`, `glob`, `read`, `display` and `resolved_name`.
5. Added: `FakeRunner::scripted(outputs: Vec<Output>) -> FakeRunner` (the k-th call gets the k-th output; a call past the end panics) and `DiskTree::open_sub(root: &Path, display_root: &str, sub: &str) -> std::io::Result<DiskTree>` (a tree rooted at `root` that holds only the folder `sub`, so that a recording named by path or slug does not walk its whole parent).
6. `rip_label` also refuses a folder named `golden`: "golden: the folder name golden is reserved for goldens; it is not a rip label" (Review Focus 2).
7. `disc_format` returns `meta.json`'s `format` as `crates/capture` writes it: `"bluray"` or `"dvd"` (the entry's "UHD", "BD", "DVD" are not what the recorder writes; every recorded `meta.json` says `bluray` or `dvd`).
8. `COMMANDS`' third column is the command's arguments as spec 3.4 writes them after the name (for example `"<slug|dir> [--title N] [--label L]"`); `--help` prints each row as `  <name> <arguments>`. A task may write its row as `("scan", cmd::scan::run as Command, "...")`.
9. A recording named as a slug that is not a folder under the evidence is `Refused { code: 2, line: "corpus/owner/<slug>: no such recording (neither a recording folder nor a slug under corpus/owner)" }`.
10. `--evidence`'s default is shown relative to the current directory in the exit-3 line (`corpus/owner` from the repository root, `../../corpus/owner` from `crates/dev`), as the Python showed its relative default.
11. `Output.stdout` and `Output.stderr` are read with universal newlines ("\r\n" and "\r" become "\n"), as `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` reads them, besides the entry's lossy UTF-8.
12. `Ctx::from_process` copies the whole process environment into `Ctx.env` (lossily decoded); the commands read only the five variables the entry names.
13. Known reader limits, none met by a recorded file: `py_int` gives None beyond i64 (Python gives a big int); `py_isdigit`, `py_int`, `py_float` and `round_level` take ASCII digits only (Python also takes other Unicode digits; the 41 robot logs under `corpus/` hold none); serde_json reads the JSON integer `-0` as the float `-0.0` where Python reads the int `0`.

```rust
//! The language code tables of the phase 0 analysers, as the Python has them (port spec section 3.1): the
//! reconciler's bibliographic-to-terminology mapping (compare_tracks.B_TO_T) and the audio rule's tables
//! (audio_similarity.ISO639, NO_LANGUAGE, TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE; spec 8.6 "Languages").

/// ISO 639-2 bibliographic code -> terminology code: the 20 pairs of the Python, in its order.
/// Py: compare_tracks.B_TO_T.
pub const B_TO_T: [(&str, &str); 20] = [
    ("alb", "sqi"), ("arm", "hye"), ("baq", "eus"), ("bur", "mya"), ("chi", "zho"), ("cze", "ces"),
    ("dut", "nld"), ("fre", "fra"), ("geo", "kat"), ("ger", "deu"), ("gre", "ell"), ("ice", "isl"),
    ("mac", "mkd"), ("mao", "mri"), ("may", "msa"), ("per", "fas"), ("rum", "ron"), ("slo", "slk"),
    ("tib", "bod"), ("wel", "cym"),
];

/// `(code or "und").lower()`, then mapped through `B_TO_T` (None and "" are "und"). Py: compare_tracks.norm_lang.
pub fn norm_lang(code: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let code = match code {
        Some(text) if !text.is_empty() => text.to_lowercase(),
        _ => "und".to_string(),
    };
    match B_TO_T.iter().find(|(bibliographic, _)| *bibliographic == code) {
        Some((_, terminology)) => terminology.to_string(),
        None => code,
    }
}

/// The codes that name no language (spec 8.6). Py: audio_similarity.NO_LANGUAGE.
pub const NO_LANGUAGE: [&str; 6] = ["", "-", "und", "zxx", "mul", "mis"];

/// TMDb's original_language of a work without speech: English is then the reference language.
/// Py: audio_similarity.TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE.
pub const TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE: &str = "xx";

/// TMDb's two-letter original_language -> the three-letter codes a stream may carry: every entry of the Python's
/// table in its order (191 entries, 223 codes). Py: audio_similarity.ISO639.

/// The three-letter codes of one two-letter code, or None when the table lacks it. Py: `ISO639.get(code)`.
pub fn iso639(code: &str) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]> {
    ISO639.iter().find(|(two, _)| *two == code).map(|(_, three)| *three)
}
```

Insert at the top of `crates/core/src/recording/text.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
//! Bytes to text and text to lines, as the Python's readers do it (port spec 3.2): `bytes.decode` with "utf-8" or
//! "utf-8-sig" and errors="strict" or "replace", `str.splitlines`, text-mode file iteration, `robot.parse`'s
//! `split("\n")`, and `bytes.splitlines`.

/// Python's "utf-8" (a byte-order mark stays as U+FEFF) and "utf-8-sig" (one leading mark removed).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Encoding {
    Utf8,
    Utf8Sig,
}

/// Python's errors="strict" and errors="replace" (U+FFFD per maximal invalid subpart, as `from_utf8_lossy`).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Errors {
    Strict,
    Replace,
}

const BOM: &[u8] = b"\xef\xbb\xbf";

/// Bytes to text as `bytes.decode(encoding, errors)`. Err is Python's UnicodeDecodeError text ("'utf-8' codec can't
/// decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte"), positions counted after a removed byte-order mark, as
/// Python counts them. Py: Path.read_text.
pub fn decode_text(bytes: &[u8], encoding: Encoding, errors: Errors) -> Result<String, String> {
    let body = match encoding {
        Encoding::Utf8Sig => bytes.strip_prefix(BOM).unwrap_or(bytes),
        Encoding::Utf8 => bytes,
    };
    match errors {
        Errors::Replace => Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(body).into_owned()),
        Errors::Strict => match std::str::from_utf8(body) {
            Ok(text) => Ok(text.to_string()),
            Err(error) => Err(decode_error(body, &error)),
        },
    }
}

/// CPython's UnicodeDecodeError text for the first invalid sequence: one byte is "byte 0x.. in position n", more are
/// "bytes in position n-m"; a lead byte C2 to F4 makes the reason "invalid continuation byte", any other "invalid
/// start byte"; a sequence cut by the end of the input is "unexpected end of data".
fn decode_error(body: &[u8], error: &std::str::Utf8Error) -> String {
    let start = error.valid_up_to();
    let (count, reason) = match error.error_len() {
        None => (body.len() - start, "unexpected end of data"),
        Some(count) if (0xc2..=0xf4).contains(&body[start]) => (count, "invalid continuation byte"),
        Some(count) => (count, "invalid start byte"),
    };
    if count == 1 {
        format!("'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x{:02x} in position {}: {}", body[start], start, reason)
    } else {
        format!("'utf-8' codec can't decode bytes in position {}-{}: {}", start, start + count - 1, reason)
    }
}

/// Splits `text` after every character `is_boundary` accepts ("\r\n" counts as one), without the terminators and
/// without a final empty line.
fn split_lines(text: &str, is_boundary: fn(char) -> bool) -> Vec<&str> {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    let mut start = 0;
    let mut chars = text.char_indices().peekable();
    while let Some((at, c)) = chars.next() {
        if !is_boundary(c) {
            continue;
        }
        lines.push(&text[start..at]);
        start = at + c.len_utf8();
        if c == '\r' {
            if let Some(&(next_at, '\n')) = chars.peek() {
                chars.next();
                start = next_at + 1;
            }
        }
    }
    if start < text.len() {
        lines.push(&text[start..]);
    }
    lines
}

/// Lines on Python's `str.splitlines` boundaries: \n, \r, \r\n, \v, \f, \x1c, \x1d, \x1e, \x85, \u{2028}, \u{2029}; no
/// terminators; no final empty line. Py: str.splitlines.
pub fn py_splitlines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    split_lines(text, |c| {
        matches!(c, '\n' | '\r' | '\x0b' | '\x0c' | '\x1c' | '\x1d' | '\x1e' | '\u{85}' | '\u{2028}' | '\u{2029}')
    })
}

/// Lines as Python's text-mode file iteration gives them (universal newlines: \n, \r, \r\n only), without
/// terminators. Py: `for line in open(path)`.
pub fn universal_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    split_lines(text, |c| c == '\n' || c == '\r')
}

/// `text.split("\n")`, each line with its trailing "\r"s removed (rstrip("\r")); a final empty piece kept, as split
/// keeps it. Py: robot.parse's loop.
pub fn strip_cr_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    text.split('\n').map(|line| line.trim_end_matches('\r')).collect()
}

/// Lines of bytes on `bytes.splitlines` boundaries (\n, \r, \r\n only), without terminators and without a final
/// empty line. Py: check_encoding's data.splitlines().
pub fn py_bytes_splitlines(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<&[u8]> {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    let mut start = 0;
    let mut at = 0;
    while at < data.len() {
        match data[at] {
            b'\n' => {
                lines.push(&data[start..at]);
                at += 1;
                start = at;
            }
            b'\r' => {
                lines.push(&data[start..at]);
                at += if data.get(at + 1) == Some(&b'\n') { 2 } else { 1 };
                start = at;
            }
            _ => at += 1,
        }
    }
    if start < data.len() {
        lines.push(&data[start..]);
    }
    lines
}
```

```rust
    fn string_repr_is_python_repr() {
        let cases = [
            ("abc", "'abc'"),
            ("it's", "\"it's\""),
            ("say \"hi\"", "'say \"hi\"'"),
            ("both ' and \"", "'both \\' and \"'"),
            ("tab\there", "'tab\\there'"),
            ("nl\n", "'nl\\n'"),
            ("cr\r", "'cr\\r'"),
            ("back\\slash", "'back\\\\slash'"),
            ("\x00\x1f\x7f", "'\\x00\\x1f\\x7f'"),
            ("caf\u{e9}", "'caf\u{e9}'"),
            ("\u{a0}", "'\\xa0'"),
            ("\u{ad}", "'\\xad'"),
            ("\u{200b}", "'\\u200b'"),
            ("\u{feff}", "'\\ufeff'"),
            ("\u{2028}", "'\\u2028'"),
            ("\u{1f600}", "'\u{1f600}'"),
            ("\u{e0001}", "'\\U000e0001'"),
            ("\u{e000}", "'\\ue000'"),
            ("\u{f0000}", "'\\U000f0000'"),
            ("\u{378}", "'\\u0378'"),
            ("\u{85}", "'\\x85'"),
            ("\u{ff}", "'\u{ff}'"),
            ("\u{3000}", "'\\u3000'"),
            ("\u{fffe}", "'\\ufffe'"),
        ];
        for (text, repr) in cases {
            assert_eq!(py_repr_str(text), repr, "{:?}", text);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn repr_str_and_truth_of_json_values_follow_python() {
        let value = json!({"a": [1, 2.5, null, true, false], "b": "x'y", "c": {}, "d": -0.0, "e": 1e16});
        assert_eq!(py_repr(&value), "{'a': [1, 2.5, None, True, False], 'b': \"x'y\", 'c': {}, 'd': -0.0, 'e': 1e+16}");
        assert_eq!(py_str(&json!("plain")), "plain");
        assert_eq!(py_str(&json!(6)), "6");
        assert_eq!(py_str(&json!(6.0)), "6.0");
        assert_eq!(py_str(&json!(null)), "None");
        for falsy in [json!(null), json!(false), json!(0), json!(0.0), json!(""), json!([]), json!({})] {
            assert!(!py_truthy(&falsy), "{}", falsy);
        }
        for truthy in [json!(true), json!(1), json!(-0.5), json!("0"), json!([0]), json!({"k": null})] {
            assert!(py_truthy(&truthy), "{}", truthy);
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
    fn not_printable_ranges_are_sorted_disjoint_and_python_3_9s() {
        assert_eq!(NOT_PRINTABLE.len(), 678);
        assert_eq!(NOT_PRINTABLE[0], (0x80, 0xa0));
        assert_eq!(NOT_PRINTABLE[677], (0xe01f0, 0x10ffff));

        assert!(!is_printable('\u{378}'));
        assert!(is_printable('\u{e9}'));
        assert!(is_printable('\u{1f600}'));
        assert!(!is_printable('\u{10ffff}'));
```

```rust
//! Which characters Python 3.9's repr() keeps as they are: `str.isprintable` of Unicode 13.0. The table holds the
//! code points from U+0080 up that are NOT printable (categories Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, and Zs other than the
//! space), as 678 sorted, disjoint ranges.

use std::cmp::Ordering;

/// Whether repr() keeps `c` as it is (asked only for characters from U+0080 up).
pub(super) fn is_printable(c: char) -> bool {
    let code = c as u32;
    NOT_PRINTABLE
        .binary_search_by(|&(low, high)| {
            if high < code {
                Ordering::Less
            } else if low > code {
                Ordering::Greater
            } else {
                Ordering::Equal
            }
        })
        .is_err()
}
```
