Insert at the top of `crates/core/src/recording/python.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
//! Python's spellings of strings and numbers (port spec section 4), so that every printed or written value reads as
//! the Python's did: str.isspace, str.split(), str.strip(), str.isdigit(), int() and float() of a str or of a JSON
//! value, repr() of a float, a str and a JSON value, '%.Nf' % x, format(x, "g"), str() and bool().

use super::printable::is_printable;
use serde_json::Value;

/// Python's str.isspace for one character: Unicode White_Space plus the bidi classes B, S and WS, so U+001C to
/// U+001F count (char::is_whitespace does not count them): 29 characters in Python 3.9.
pub fn py_is_space(c: char) -> bool {
    matches!(
        c,
        '\t'..='\r'
            | '\x1c'..=' '
            | '\u{85}'
            | '\u{a0}'
            | '\u{1680}'
            | '\u{2000}'..='\u{200a}'
            | '\u{2028}'
            | '\u{2029}'
            | '\u{202f}'
            | '\u{205f}'
            | '\u{3000}'
    )
}

/// str.split() with no argument: runs of py_is_space separate, no empty pieces.
pub fn py_split(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    text.split(py_is_space).filter(|piece| !piece.is_empty()).collect()
}

/// str.strip() with no argument.
pub fn py_strip(text: &str) -> &str {
    text.trim_matches(py_is_space)
}

/// str.isdigit(), ASCII digits only. Python's isdigit also accepts other Unicode digits; no recorded or pinned robot
/// log holds one (checked while planning: the 41 robot logs under corpus/ hold no non-ASCII digit), so no verdict
/// depends on the difference (02-interfaces.md, open point 9).
pub fn py_isdigit(text: &str) -> bool {
    !text.is_empty() && text.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit())
}

/// A leading '-' or '+' taken off: (negative, the rest).
fn split_sign(text: &str) -> (bool, &str) {
    match text.as_bytes().first() {
        Some(b'-') => (true, &text[1..]),
        Some(b'+') => (false, &text[1..]),
        _ => (false, text),
    }
}

/// ASCII digits with single underscores between digits (PEP 515), at least one digit.
fn valid_digits(text: &str) -> bool {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    match (bytes.first(), bytes.last()) {
        (Some(first), Some(last)) => {
            first.is_ascii_digit()
                && last.is_ascii_digit()
                && bytes.iter().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit() || *b == b'_')
                && !text.contains("__")
        }
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// int() of a str: surrounding whitespace, one sign, ASCII digits with single underscores between them; None where
/// Python raises ValueError. A value beyond i64 is None too (Python would give a big int; no recorded value is near).
pub fn py_int(text: &str) -> Option<i64> {
    let (negative, digits) = split_sign(py_strip(text));
    if !valid_digits(digits) {
        return None;
    }
    let cleaned: String = digits.chars().filter(|c| *c != '_').collect();
    let signed = if negative { format!("-{}", cleaned) } else { cleaned };
    signed.parse().ok()
}

/// The decimal form float() accepts: digits [. [digits]] or . digits, then optionally e or E, a sign and digits;
/// every digit run as valid_digits.
fn valid_float(text: &str) -> bool {
    let (mantissa, exponent) = match text.find(|c: char| c == 'e' || c == 'E') {
        Some(at) => (&text[..at], Some(&text[at + 1..])),
        None => (text, None),
    };
    let mantissa_ok = match mantissa.split_once('.') {
        Some((whole, fraction)) => {
            (!whole.is_empty() || !fraction.is_empty())
                && (whole.is_empty() || valid_digits(whole))
                && (fraction.is_empty() || valid_digits(fraction))
        }
        None => valid_digits(mantissa),
    };
    let exponent_ok = match exponent {
        None => true,
        Some(digits) => valid_digits(split_sign(digits).1),
    };
    mantissa_ok && exponent_ok
}

/// float() of a str: whitespace, sign, digits with underscores, exponent, "inf"/"infinity"/"nan" in any case; None
/// where Python raises ValueError. Non-ASCII digits are refused (Python accepts them; no recorded value has one).
pub fn py_float(text: &str) -> Option<f64> {
    let (negative, rest) = split_sign(py_strip(text));
    let magnitude = match rest.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
        "inf" | "infinity" => f64::INFINITY,
        "nan" => f64::NAN,
        _ => {
            if !valid_float(rest) {
                return None;
            }
            let cleaned: String = rest.chars().filter(|c| *c != '_').collect();
            cleaned.parse::<f64>().ok()?
        }
    };
    Some(if negative { -magnitude } else { magnitude })
}

/// type(value).__name__ of the Python value json.loads gives.
fn type_name(value: &Value) -> &'static str {
    match value {
        Value::Null => "NoneType",
        Value::Bool(_) => "bool",
        Value::Number(number) if number.is_f64() => "float",
        Value::Number(_) => "int",
        Value::String(_) => "str",
        Value::Array(_) => "list",
        Value::Object(_) => "dict",
    }
}

/// int() of a JSON value: an int as is, a float truncated, a str by py_int, a bool as 0 or 1; Err is Python's
/// TypeError or ValueError text (Python 3.9's wording).
pub fn py_int_value(value: &Value) -> Result<i64, String> {
    match value {
        Value::Bool(flag) => Ok(i64::from(*flag)),
        Value::Number(number) => {
            if let Some(int) = number.as_i64() {
                Ok(int)
            } else if number.is_u64() {
                Err(format!("int too large for 64 bits: {}", number))
            } else {
                let truncated = number.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN).trunc();
                if (-9.223_372_036_854_776e18..9.223_372_036_854_776e18).contains(&truncated) {
                    Ok(truncated as i64)
                } else {
                    Err(format!("float too large for 64 bits: {}", number))
                }
            }
        }
        Value::String(text) => {
            py_int(text).ok_or_else(|| format!("invalid literal for int() with base 10: {}", py_repr_str(text)))
        }
        other => Err(format!(
            "int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a number, not '{}'",
            type_name(other)
        )),
    }
}

/// float() of a JSON value: an int or float as f64, a str by py_float, a bool as 0.0 or 1.0; Err as py_int_value.
pub fn py_float_value(value: &Value) -> Result<f64, String> {
    match value {
        Value::Bool(flag) => Ok(if *flag { 1.0 } else { 0.0 }),
        Value::Number(number) => Ok(number.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN)),
        Value::String(text) => {
            py_float(text).ok_or_else(|| format!("could not convert string to float: {}", py_repr_str(text)))
        }
        other => Err(format!("float() argument must be a string or a number, not '{}'", type_name(other))),
    }
}

/// Python's spelling of a NaN or an infinity; None for a finite number.
fn non_finite(x: f64) -> Option<String> {
    if x.is_nan() {
        Some("nan".to_string())
    } else if x == f64::INFINITY {
        Some("inf".to_string())
    } else if x == f64::NEG_INFINITY {
        Some("-inf".to_string())
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// repr(float): the shortest digits that read back as x, in exponent form below 1e-4 and from 1e16 ("1e-05",
/// "1e+16", at least two exponent digits), else positional with ".0" on whole numbers; "nan", "inf", "-inf".
pub fn py_float_repr(x: f64) -> String {
    if let Some(text) = non_finite(x) {
        return text;
    }
    if x == 0.0 {
        let text = if x.is_sign_negative() { "-0.0" } else { "0.0" };
        return text.to_string();
    }
    // {:e} without a precision writes the shortest digits that read back as x, the digits Python's repr chooses.
    let scientific = format!("{:e}", x.abs());
    let (mantissa, exponent) = scientific.split_once('e').expect("{:e} writes an exponent");
    let exponent: i32 = exponent.parse().expect("{:e} writes a whole exponent");
    let digits: String = mantissa.chars().filter(|c| *c != '.').collect();
    let sign = if x < 0.0 { "-" } else { "" };
    let point = exponent + 1;
    let body = if !(-4..16).contains(&exponent) {
        let head = if digits.len() > 1 { format!("{}.{}", &digits[..1], &digits[1..]) } else { digits.clone() };
        format!("{}e{}{:02}", head, if exponent < 0 { '-' } else { '+' }, exponent.abs())
    } else if point <= 0 {
        format!("0.{}{}", "0".repeat((-point) as usize), digits)
    } else if (point as usize) < digits.len() {
        format!("{}.{}", &digits[..point as usize], &digits[point as usize..])
    } else {
        format!("{}{}.0", digits, "0".repeat(point as usize - digits.len()))
    };
    format!("{}{}", sign, body)
}

/// '%.Nf' % x: rounded half to even on the exact binary value (Rust's {:.N} rounds the same way), "-0.0" kept,
/// "nan", "inf", "-inf".
pub fn py_fixed(x: f64, digits: usize) -> String {
    match non_finite(x) {
        Some(text) => text,
        None => format!("{:.*}", digits, x),
    }
}

/// The text without trailing zeros after a decimal point, and without the point when nothing follows it.
fn without_trailing_zeros(text: &str) -> String {
    if text.contains('.') {
        text.trim_end_matches('0').trim_end_matches('.').to_string()
    } else {
        text.to_string()
    }
}

/// format(x, "g"): six significant digits; positional when the exponent of the rounded value is from -4 to 5, else
/// exponent form with at least two exponent digits; trailing zeros dropped; "-0", "nan", "inf", "-inf".
pub fn py_g(x: f64) -> String {
    if let Some(text) = non_finite(x) {
        return text;
    }
    if x == 0.0 {
        let text = if x.is_sign_negative() { "-0" } else { "0" };
        return text.to_string();
    }
    let scientific = format!("{:.5e}", x);
    let (mantissa, exponent) = scientific.split_once('e').expect("{:e} writes an exponent");
    let exponent: i32 = exponent.parse().expect("{:e} writes a whole exponent");
    if (-4..6).contains(&exponent) {
        without_trailing_zeros(&format!("{:.*}", (5 - exponent) as usize, x))
    } else {
        format!("{}e{}{:02}", without_trailing_zeros(mantissa), if exponent < 0 { '-' } else { '+' }, exponent.abs())
    }
}

/// repr() of a str: single quotes unless the text holds ' and no ", backslash escapes for \\ \t \n \r and the quote,
/// \xNN for the other controls and DEL, the characters str.isprintable accepts as they are, and \xNN / \uNNNN /
/// \UNNNNNNNN (lowercase hex) for the rest. Py: unicode_repr.
pub fn py_repr_str(text: &str) -> String {
    let quote = if text.contains('\'') && !text.contains('"') { '"' } else { '\'' };
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len() + 2);
    out.push(quote);
    for c in text.chars() {
        let code = c as u32;
        match c {
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            _ if c == quote => {
                out.push('\\');
                out.push(c);
            }
            _ if code < 0x20 || code == 0x7f => out.push_str(&format!("\\x{:02x}", code)),
            _ if code < 0x7f => out.push(c),
            _ if is_printable(c) => out.push(c),
            _ if code <= 0xff => out.push_str(&format!("\\x{:02x}", code)),
            _ if code <= 0xffff => out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", code)),
            _ => out.push_str(&format!("\\U{:08x}", code)),
        }
    }
    out.push(quote);
    out
}

/// repr() of the Python value json.loads gives: None, True, False, ints, py_float_repr, py_repr_str, "[a, b]",
/// "{'k': v}" in the object's order.
pub fn py_repr(value: &Value) -> String {
    match value {
        Value::Null => "None".to_string(),
        Value::Bool(true) => "True".to_string(),
        Value::Bool(false) => "False".to_string(),
        Value::Number(number) => {
            if let Some(int) = number.as_i64() {
                int.to_string()
            } else if let Some(int) = number.as_u64() {
                int.to_string()
            } else {
                py_float_repr(number.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN))
            }
        }
        Value::String(text) => py_repr_str(text),
        Value::Array(items) => format!("[{}]", items.iter().map(py_repr).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
        Value::Object(map) => format!(
            "{{{}}}",
            map.iter().map(|(key, item)| format!("{}: {}", py_repr_str(key), py_repr(item))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
        ),
    }
}

/// str() of that value: a str as it is, anything else as py_repr.
pub fn py_str(value: &Value) -> String {
    match value {
        Value::String(text) => text.clone(),
        other => py_repr(other),
    }
}

/// bool() of that value: false for None, False, 0, 0.0, "", [] and {}.
pub fn py_truthy(value: &Value) -> bool {
    match value {
        Value::Null => false,
        Value::Bool(flag) => *flag,
        Value::Number(number) => number.as_f64().map_or(false, |x| x != 0.0),
        Value::String(text) => !text.is_empty(),
        Value::Array(items) => !items.is_empty(),
        Value::Object(map) => !map.is_empty(),
    }
}
```

```rust
//! A Python dict whose order is printed or written (02-interfaces.md, "Python dicts").

use serde::de::{MapAccess, Visitor};
use serde::ser::SerializeMap;
use std::fmt;
use std::marker::PhantomData;

/// A Python dict whose order is printed or written: entries in insertion order; `insert` of a present key replaces
/// its value in place. Serialised as a JSON object in that order; deserialised keeping the file's order, a repeated
/// key keeping its first place and taking the last value (as json.loads builds a dict). `==` compares in order
/// (Python's dict == does not: sort first where order may differ).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Ordered<V>(pub Vec<(String, V)>);

/// Empty; written by hand so that V needs no Default.
impl<V> Default for Ordered<V> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Ordered(Vec::new())
    }
}

impl<V> Ordered<V> {
    pub fn new() -> Ordered<V> {
        Ordered(Vec::new())
    }

    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&V> {
        self.0.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == key).map(|(_, value)| value)
    }

    pub fn contains_key(&self, key: &str) -> bool {
        self.get(key).is_some()
    }

    pub fn insert(&mut self, key: String, value: V) {
        match self.0.iter().position(|(name, _)| *name == key) {
            Some(at) => self.0[at].1 = value,
            None => self.0.push((key, value)),
        }
    }

    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &V)> {
        self.0.iter().map(|(name, value)| (name.as_str(), value))
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.0.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.is_empty()
    }
}

impl<V: serde::Serialize> serde::Serialize for Ordered<V> {
    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        let mut map = serializer.serialize_map(Some(self.0.len()))?;
        for (name, value) in &self.0 {
            map.serialize_entry(name, value)?;
        }
        map.end()
    }
}

impl<'de, V: serde::Deserialize<'de>> serde::Deserialize<'de> for Ordered<V> {
    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        struct OrderedVisitor<V>(PhantomData<V>);

        impl<'de, V: serde::Deserialize<'de>> Visitor<'de> for OrderedVisitor<V> {
            type Value = Ordered<V>;

            fn expecting(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
                formatter.write_str("a JSON object")
            }

            fn visit_map<A: MapAccess<'de>>(self, mut access: A) -> Result<Ordered<V>, A::Error> {
                let mut out = Ordered::new();
                while let Some((name, value)) = access.next_entry::<String, V>()? {
                    out.insert(name, value);
                }
                Ok(out)
            }
        }

        deserializer.deserialize_map(OrderedVisitor(PhantomData))
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The recording as the analysers see it (port spec 3.2): an in-memory tree of a recording directory or of the
//! whole evidence directory, ordered as Python sorts `Path` objects, whose `list` and `glob` never return a folder
//! named `golden` (spec section 5 reserves the name); the decoders and line splitters of the Python's readers; the
//! Python spellings of strings and numbers; `Ordered`; and the recorder's file types (`files`). No I/O: `crates/dev`

mod ordered;
mod printable;
mod python;
mod text;

pub use python::{
    py_fixed, py_float, py_float_repr, py_float_value, py_g, py_int, py_int_value, py_is_space, py_isdigit, py_repr,

    fn keys(paths: &[&str]) -> Vec<PathKey> {
        paths.iter().map(|path| PathKey::new(path)).collect()
    }

    /// A recording with the two pairs of names that sort differently as paths and as strings, an empty folder, and
    /// golden folders at two depths.
    fn sample() -> MemTree {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("corpus/owner", "owner");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/scan.txt", "MSG:1005,0,1,\"made-up line\"\n");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/all-tracks/rip-summary.json", "{}");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/all-tracks-2/rip-summary.json", "{}");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/all-tracks/audio-levels-20ms-1-2/main-mix.txt", "x");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/all-tracks/audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3/main-mix.txt", "x");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/exp02/title-10.txt", "");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/exp02/title-2.txt", "");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/exp02/titles.txt", "");
        tree.insert_dir("disc-a/empty");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/golden/rip-summary.json", "{}");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/golden/scan.json", "{}");
        tree.insert_file("disc-a/all-tracks/golden/audio-x.json", "{}");
        tree
    }

    #[test]
    fn path_keys_order_component_by_component_as_python_sorts_paths() {
        let pairs = [
            ("all-tracks/x", "all-tracks-2/x"),
            ("audio-levels-20ms-1-2/main-mix.txt", "audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3/main-mix.txt"),
        ];
        for (first, second) in pairs {
            assert!(PathKey::new(first) < PathKey::new(second), "{} sorts before {}", first, second);
            assert!(first > second, "as one string {} would sort after {}", first, second);
        }
        assert!(PathKey::new("B") < PathKey::new("a"), "by code point, capitals first");
        assert!(PathKey::new("a") < PathKey::new("a/b"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn path_key_new_join_parent_and_name_behave_as_pathlib() {
        assert_eq!(PathKey::new("./a//b/"), PathKey::new("a/b"));
        assert_eq!(PathKey::new("a/b").components(), &["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()]);
        assert_eq!(PathKey::new("a").join("b/c").to_string(), "a/b/c");
        assert_eq!(PathKey::new("a/b").parent(), PathKey::new("a"));
        assert_eq!(PathKey::root().parent(), PathKey::root());
        assert_eq!(PathKey::new("a/b.txt").name(), "b.txt");
        assert_eq!(PathKey::root().name(), "");
        assert_eq!(PathKey::root().to_string(), "");
        assert_eq!(PathKey::new("."), PathKey::root());

    #[test]
    fn list_gives_entries_in_python_order_with_empty_folders() {
        let tree = sample();

        assert!(!tree.exists(&PathKey::new("disc-a/nothing")));
        assert!(tree.is_dir(&PathKey::root()));
        assert_eq!(tree.list(&PathKey::root()), keys(&["disc-a"]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn golden_folders_are_skipped_by_list_and_glob_but_still_readable() {
        let tree = sample();
        assert!(!tree.list(&PathKey::new("disc-a")).contains(&PathKey::new("disc-a/golden")));
        assert_eq!(
            tree.glob(&PathKey::new("disc-a"), "*/rip-summary.json"),
            keys(&["disc-a/all-tracks/rip-summary.json", "disc-a/all-tracks-2/rip-summary.json"])

            keys(&["disc-a/all-tracks/rip-summary.json", "disc-a/all-tracks-2/rip-summary.json"])

            tree.glob(&PathKey::new("disc-a/all-tracks"), "*"),

                "disc-a/all-tracks/audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3",

        assert!(tree.glob(&PathKey::new("disc-a/golden"), "*").is_empty());
        assert!(tree.is_dir(&PathKey::new("disc-a/golden")));
        assert_eq!(&*tree.read(&PathKey::new("disc-a/golden/scan.json")).unwrap(), b"{}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn glob_matches_each_component_as_fnmatch() {
        let tree = sample();
        let exp = PathKey::new("disc-a/exp02");
        assert_eq!(tree.glob(&exp, "title-[0-9]*.txt"), keys(&["disc-a/exp02/title-10.txt", "disc-a/exp02/title-2.txt"]));
        assert_eq!(tree.glob(&exp, "title?.txt"), keys(&["disc-a/exp02/titles.txt"]));
        assert_eq!(tree.glob(&exp, "[!t]*"), Vec::<PathKey>::new());
        assert_eq!(
            tree.glob(&PathKey::new("disc-a"), "all-tracks/audio-levels-20ms-*"),
            keys(&["disc-a/all-tracks/audio-levels-20ms-1-2", "disc-a/all-tracks/audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3"])

        assert_eq!(tree.glob(&PathKey::new("disc-a"), "scan.txt"), keys(&["disc-a/scan.txt"]));

    #[test]
    fn fnmatch_handles_sets_ranges_negation_and_literal_brackets() {
        assert!(fnmatch("abc", "a*"));
        assert!(fnmatch("abc", "*c"));
        assert!(fnmatch("", "*"));
        assert!(!fnmatch("abc", "a?"));
        assert!(fnmatch("a]", "a[]]"));
        assert!(fnmatch("ab", "a[!]]"));
        assert!(!fnmatch("a]", "a[!]]"));
        assert!(fnmatch("a-", "a[x-]"));
        assert!(fnmatch("a[b", "a[b"));
        assert!(fnmatch("a[!", "a[!"));
        assert!(!fnmatch("a[", "a[!"));
        assert!(!fnmatch("ABC", "abc"));
        assert!(fnmatch(".hidden", "*"));
        assert!(fnmatch("b", "[a-c]"));
        assert!(!fnmatch("d", "[a-c]"));
        assert!(fnmatch("-", "[a-c-e]"));
        assert!(fnmatch("e", "[a-c-e]"));
        assert!(!fnmatch("d", "[a-c-e]"));
        assert!(fnmatch("a\\b", "a\\b"));

    #[test]
    fn display_joins_the_display_root_as_pathlib_does() {
        let tree = MemTree::new("corpus/owner", "owner");

        assert_eq!(MemTree::new("", "recs").display(&PathKey::new("x")), "x");

        assert_eq!(here.resolved_name(&PathKey::root()), "recordings");
        assert_eq!(here.resolved_name(&PathKey::new("disc-a")), "disc-a");
    }

    #[test]
    fn reading_a_missing_file_or_a_folder_gives_the_python_errors() {
        let tree = sample();
        let missing = tree.read(&PathKey::new("disc-a/nothing.json")).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            missing,
            ReadError::Missing(Missing {
                path: PathKey::new("disc-a/nothing.json"),
                shown: "corpus/owner/disc-a/nothing.json".to_string(),
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(missing.to_string(), "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'corpus/owner/disc-a/nothing.json'");
        assert_eq!(
            tree.read(&PathKey::new("disc-a/exp02")).unwrap_err().to_string(),
            "[Errno 21] Is a directory: 'corpus/owner/disc-a/exp02'"

    }

    #[test]
    fn lazy_files_are_loaded_once_and_report_their_error() {
        let calls = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let counter = calls.clone();
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "rec");
        tree.insert_lazy(
            "levels/main-mix.txt",
            Arc::new(move || -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
                counter.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                Ok(b"-23.5\r\n".to_vec())
            }),
        );
        tree.insert_lazy(
            "levels/cand-2.txt",
            Arc::new(|| -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> { Err("[Errno 13] Permission denied: 'levels/cand-2.txt'".to_string()) }),
        );
        assert!(tree.is_dir(&PathKey::new("levels")));
        assert!(tree.is_file(&PathKey::new("levels/main-mix.txt")));
        assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
        for _ in 0..2 {
            assert_eq!(&*tree.read(&PathKey::new("levels/main-mix.txt")).unwrap(), b"-23.5\r\n");
        }
        assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            tree.read(&PathKey::new("levels/cand-2.txt")).unwrap_err().to_string(),
            "[Errno 13] Permission denied: 'levels/cand-2.txt'"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn read_text_and_read_json_decode_as_python_does() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "rec");
        tree.insert_file("a.json", b"\xef\xbb\xbf{\"ok\": true}".to_vec());
        tree.insert_file("bad.txt", b"x\xff".to_vec());
        assert_eq!(
            read_text(&tree, &PathKey::new("a.json"), Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict),
            Ok("{\"ok\": true}".to_string())
        );
        let value: serde_json::Value = read_json(&tree, &PathKey::new("a.json")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(value, serde_json::json!({"ok": true}));
        assert_eq!(
            read_text(&tree, &PathKey::new("bad.txt"), Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Strict),
            Err("'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 1: invalid start byte".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            read_text(&tree, &PathKey::new("bad.txt"), Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace),
            Ok("x\u{fffd}".to_string())
        );
        assert_eq!(
            read_json::<serde_json::Value>(&tree, &PathKey::new("none.json")),
            Err("[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'none.json'".to_string())
        );
    }
}
```

```rust

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fmt;
use std::ops::Bound;
use std::sync::{Arc, OnceLock};

/// The folder name the port spec (section 5) reserves for goldens: `list` and `glob` never return one, nor anything
/// under one.
const GOLDEN: &str = "golden";

/// A path inside a tree: '/'-separated components below the tree's root. Ordered component by component, each
/// name by code point (derived `Ord` over `Vec<String>`), which is how Python sorts `PurePosixPath` objects:
/// `all-tracks/x` < `all-tracks-2/x` and `audio-levels-20ms-1-2/x` < `audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3/x`.
/// Py: pathlib.PurePosixPath ordering.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct PathKey(Vec<String>);

impl PathKey {
    /// The tree's root (no component).
    pub fn root() -> PathKey {
        PathKey(Vec::new())
    }

    /// A key from "a/b/c"; empty and "." components are dropped, as pathlib drops them.
    pub fn new(path: &str) -> PathKey {
        PathKey(path.split('/').filter(|part| !part.is_empty() && *part != ".").map(str::to_string).collect())
    }

    /// This key with `name` appended ("x/y" appends two components). Py: `path / name`.
    pub fn join(&self, name: &str) -> PathKey {
        let mut parts = self.0.clone();
        parts.extend(PathKey::new(name).0);
        PathKey(parts)
    }

    /// The key without its last component (the root's parent is the root). Py: Path.parent.
    pub fn parent(&self) -> PathKey {
        let mut parts = self.0.clone();
        parts.pop();
        PathKey(parts)
    }

    /// The last component, "" for the root. Py: Path.name.
    pub fn name(&self) -> &str {
        self.0.last().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("")
    }

    /// The components in order.
    pub fn components(&self) -> &[String] {
        &self.0
    }

    /// Whether this key lies at or below `prefix`.
    fn starts_with(&self, prefix: &PathKey) -> bool {
        self.0.len() >= prefix.0.len() && self.0[..prefix.0.len()] == prefix.0[..]
    }
}

/// '/'-joined components, "" for the root.
impl fmt::Display for PathKey {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(&self.0.join("/"))
    }
}

/// What a path names. Py: Path.is_file / Path.is_dir.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Kind {
    File,
    Dir,
}

/// A file the tree does not have. Its Display is Python's FileNotFoundError text,
/// `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<shown>'`, with `shown` the path as `Tree::display` prints it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Missing {
    pub path: PathKey,
    pub shown: String,
}

impl fmt::Display for Missing {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: {}", py_repr_str(&self.shown))
    }
}

/// Why a read failed: the file is not there, or the OS refused it (the message is the OSError text).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ReadError {
    Missing(Missing),
    Io { path: PathKey, message: String },
}

impl fmt::Display for ReadError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            ReadError::Missing(missing) => fmt::Display::fmt(missing, f),
            ReadError::Io { message, .. } => f.write_str(message),
        }
    }
}

/// A recording directory or the whole evidence directory, in memory. Every walker of the Python is a function over
/// it. `list` and `glob` never return a folder named `golden` or anything under one; `read`, `kind` and `exists` do
/// not filter, so the golden code reads its files through the same tree. Py: the pathlib calls of every module.
pub trait Tree {
    /// File, folder, or None when absent; the root is always a folder. Py: Path.exists / is_file / is_dir.
    fn kind(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Option<Kind>;

    /// `self.kind(path).is_some()`. Py: Path.exists.
    fn exists(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool {
        self.kind(path).is_some()
    }

    /// Py: Path.is_file.
    fn is_file(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool {
        self.kind(path) == Some(Kind::File)
    }

    /// Py: Path.is_dir.
    fn is_dir(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool {
        self.kind(path) == Some(Kind::Dir)
    }

    /// The entries directly in `dir`, files and folders, in `PathKey` order; empty for a file or an absent path.
    /// Py: sorted(dir.iterdir()).
    fn list(&self, dir: &PathKey) -> Vec<PathKey>;

    /// The paths below `base` matching `pattern`: '/'-separated, each component an fnmatch pattern (`*`, `?`,
    /// `[seq]`, `[!seq]`, case-sensitive, a leading dot matched like any character, as pathlib's glob), every
    /// component but the last naming a folder, in `PathKey` order. Py: sorted(base.glob(pattern)).
    fn glob(&self, base: &PathKey, pattern: &str) -> Vec<PathKey>;

    /// The file's bytes; a lazy entry is loaded on its first read and kept. Py: Path.read_bytes.
    fn read(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Result<Arc<[u8]>, ReadError>;

    /// The path as the Python printed it: the tree's display root joined with `path` as pathlib joins (a display
    /// root of "." adds nothing). Py: str(Path).
    fn display(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String;

    /// The last component of the path's resolved absolute form; for the root, the resolved root's own name.
    /// Py: Path.resolve().name.
    fn resolved_name(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String;
}

/// Loads a lazy file's bytes once; `Err` holds the OSError text.
pub type Loader = Arc<dyn Fn() -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> + Send + Sync>;

enum Node {
    Dir,
    File(Arc<[u8]>),
    Lazy(Loader, OnceLock<Arc<[u8]>>),
}

/// The in-memory `Tree`: a `BTreeMap<PathKey, Node>` with folders explicit (an empty folder exists, as on disk),
/// files as bytes or as a `Loader`. Tests build it directly; `crates/dev` fills it from a directory.
pub struct MemTree {
    entries: BTreeMap<PathKey, Node>,
    display_root: String,
    resolved_root: String,
}

impl MemTree {
    /// An empty tree printed under `display_root` ("corpus/owner", ".", or a path as the user gave it) whose root
    /// resolves to a folder named `resolved_root_name`.
    pub fn new(display_root: &str, resolved_root_name: &str) -> MemTree {
        MemTree {
            entries: BTreeMap::new(),
            display_root: pathlib_str(display_root),
            resolved_root: resolved_root_name.to_string(),
        }
    }

    /// Adds a file (its parent folders too).
    pub fn insert_file(&mut self, path: &str, bytes: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) {
        let key = PathKey::new(path);
        self.insert_parents(&key);
        let bytes: Vec<u8> = bytes.into();
        self.entries.insert(key, Node::File(Arc::from(bytes)));
    }

    /// Adds a file read on first use.
    pub fn insert_lazy(&mut self, path: &str, load: Loader) {
        let key = PathKey::new(path);
        self.insert_parents(&key);
        self.entries.insert(key, Node::Lazy(load, OnceLock::new()));
    }

    /// Adds a folder (its parents too).
    pub fn insert_dir(&mut self, path: &str) {
        let key = PathKey::new(path);
        if key.0.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        self.insert_parents(&key);
        self.entries.entry(key).or_insert(Node::Dir);
    }

    fn insert_parents(&mut self, key: &PathKey) {
        for end in 1..key.0.len() {
            self.entries.entry(PathKey(key.0[..end].to_vec())).or_insert(Node::Dir);
        }
    }

    /// Every entry directly in `dir`, golden folders included, in `PathKey` order.
    fn children(&self, dir: &PathKey) -> Vec<PathKey> {
        self.entries
            .range((Bound::Excluded(dir.clone()), Bound::Unbounded))
            .map(|(key, _)| key)
            .take_while(|key| key.starts_with(dir))
            .filter(|key| key.0.len() == dir.0.len() + 1)
            .cloned()
            .collect()
    }

    /// Whether `path` is a folder named golden or lies under one.
    fn hidden(&self, path: &PathKey) -> bool {
        (1..=path.0.len()).any(|end| path.0[end - 1] == GOLDEN && self.is_dir(&PathKey(path.0[..end].to_vec())))
    }

    fn is_a_directory(&self, path: &PathKey) -> ReadError {
        ReadError::Io {
            path: path.clone(),
            message: format!("[Errno 21] Is a directory: {}", py_repr_str(&self.display(path))),
        }
    }
}

impl Tree for MemTree {
    fn kind(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Option<Kind> {
        if path.0.is_empty() {
            return Some(Kind::Dir);
        }
        self.entries.get(path).map(|node| match node {
            Node::Dir => Kind::Dir,
            Node::File(_) | Node::Lazy(..) => Kind::File,
        })
    }

    fn list(&self, dir: &PathKey) -> Vec<PathKey> {
        if !self.is_dir(dir) {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        self.children(dir).into_iter().filter(|key| !self.hidden(key)).collect()
    }

    fn glob(&self, base: &PathKey, pattern: &str) -> Vec<PathKey> {
        let parts: Vec<&str> = pattern.split('/').filter(|part| !part.is_empty() && *part != ".").collect();
        if parts.is_empty() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let mut current = vec![base.clone()];
        for (at, part) in parts.iter().enumerate() {
            let last = at + 1 == parts.len();
            let mut next = Vec::new();
            for dir in &current {
                if !self.is_dir(dir) {
                    continue;
                }
                if has_magic(part) {
                    for child in self.children(dir) {
                        if fnmatch(child.name(), part) && (last || self.is_dir(&child)) {
                            next.push(child);
                        }
                    }
                } else {
                    let child = dir.join(part);
                    let wanted = if last { self.exists(&child) } else { self.is_dir(&child) };
                    if wanted {
                        next.push(child);
                    }
                }
            }
            current = next;
        }
        let mut found: Vec<PathKey> = current.into_iter().filter(|path| !self.hidden(path)).collect();
        found.sort();
        found.dedup();
        found
    }

    fn read(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Result<Arc<[u8]>, ReadError> {
        match self.entries.get(path) {
            Some(Node::File(bytes)) => Ok(bytes.clone()),
            Some(Node::Lazy(load, cell)) => {
                if let Some(bytes) = cell.get() {
                    return Ok(bytes.clone());
                }
                let loaded = (**load)().map_err(|message| ReadError::Io { path: path.clone(), message })?;
                let bytes: Arc<[u8]> = Arc::from(loaded);
                Ok(cell.get_or_init(|| bytes).clone())
            }
            Some(Node::Dir) => Err(self.is_a_directory(path)),
            None if path.0.is_empty() => Err(self.is_a_directory(path)),
            None => Err(ReadError::Missing(Missing { path: path.clone(), shown: self.display(path) })),
        }
    }

    fn display(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String {
        if path.0.is_empty() {
            return self.display_root.clone();
        }
        match self.display_root.as_str() {
            "." => path.to_string(),
            "/" => format!("/{}", path),
            root => format!("{}/{}", root, path),
        }
    }

    fn resolved_name(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String {
        if path.0.is_empty() {
            self.resolved_root.clone()
        } else {
            path.name().to_string()
        }
    }
}

/// `str(PurePosixPath(text))`: empty and "." components dropped, a leading "/" kept, "." for nothing.
fn pathlib_str(text: &str) -> String {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = text.split('/').filter(|part| !part.is_empty() && *part != ".").collect();
    if text.starts_with('/') {
        format!("/{}", parts.join("/"))
    } else if parts.is_empty() {
        ".".to_string()
    } else {
        parts.join("/")
    }
}

/// Whether a glob component holds a wildcard (pathlib then lists the folder instead of testing one name).
fn has_magic(part: &str) -> bool {
    part.chars().any(|c| matches!(c, '*' | '?' | '['))
}

/// fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern): `*` any run, `?` one character, `[seq]` and `[!seq]` a set (a `]` first in
/// the set is literal, `a-z` a range, an unclosed `[` a literal), every other character literal, case-sensitive.
/// A range whose ends are reversed matches nothing (Python's re would refuse the pattern; none is used).
fn fnmatch(name: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool {
    let name: Vec<char> = name.chars().collect();
    let pattern: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();
    match_from(&name, &pattern)
}

fn match_from(name: &[char], pattern: &[char]) -> bool {
    match pattern.first() {
        None => name.is_empty(),
        Some('*') => (0..=name.len()).any(|skip| match_from(&name[skip..], &pattern[1..])),
        Some('?') => !name.is_empty() && match_from(&name[1..], &pattern[1..]),
        Some('[') => match parse_set(&pattern[1..]) {
            Some((negated, items, used)) => {
                !name.is_empty()
                    && items.iter().any(|&(low, high)| low <= name[0] && name[0] <= high) != negated
                    && match_from(&name[1..], &pattern[1 + used..])
            }
            None => name.first() == Some(&'[') && match_from(&name[1..], &pattern[1..]),
        },
        Some(c) => name.first() == Some(c) && match_from(&name[1..], &pattern[1..]),
    }
}

/// The set that starts after a '[': (negated, its ranges, the pattern characters used through the closing ']'), or
/// None when no ']' closes it. The scan is fnmatch.translate's: a '!' then a ']' right after the '[' belong to the set.
fn parse_set(rest: &[char]) -> Option<(bool, Vec<(char, char)>, usize)> {
    let mut end = 0;
    if rest.get(end) == Some(&'!') {
        end += 1;
    }
    if rest.get(end) == Some(&']') {
        end += 1;
    }
    while end < rest.len() && rest[end] != ']' {
        end += 1;
    }
    if end >= rest.len() {
        return None;
    }
    let (negated, body) = match rest[..end].split_first() {
        Some(('!', body)) => (true, body),
        _ => (false, &rest[..end]),
    };
    let mut items = Vec::new();
    let mut at = 0;
    while at < body.len() {
        if at + 2 < body.len() && body[at + 1] == '-' {
            items.push((body[at], body[at + 2]));
            at += 3;
        } else {
            items.push((body[at], body[at]));
            at += 1;
        }
    }
    Some((negated, items, end + 1))
}

/// `tree.read` then `decode_text`; Err is the ReadError's or the decode error's text.
/// Py: Path.read_text(encoding, errors).
pub fn read_text(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey, encoding: Encoding, errors: Errors) -> Result<String, String> {
    let bytes = tree.read(path).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
    decode_text(&bytes, encoding, errors)
}

/// A JSON file read as "utf-8-sig", strict, into `T`; Err is the read, decode or serde_json text.
/// Py: json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")).
pub fn read_json<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey) -> Result<T, String> {
    let text = read_text(tree, path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)?;
    serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
}
```

```rust
//! The recorder's files as the PowerShell jobs and crates/capture write them (port spec 3.3, `core::recording`), and
//! what makes a folder a rip label. Unknown keys are ignored; every field the Python reads with .get() is an Option.
//! A file whose field has another type fails to parse, and its reader reports it unreadable (02-interfaces.md, open
//! point 10: every recorded rip-summary.json has `ok` a bool, `title` and `bytes` ints).

use super::{py_split, py_splitlines, py_strip, py_truthy, read_json, Ordered, PathKey, Tree};
use serde_json::Value;

/// The rip's track selection, from the profile's file name. Py: compare_tracks --selection.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Selection {
    All,
    Eng,
}

impl Selection {
    /// "all" or "eng".
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Selection::All => "all",
            Selection::Eng => "eng",
        }
    }

    /// The selection a --selection value names, spelt exactly; None for anything else.
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<Selection> {
        match text {
            "all" => Some(Selection::All),
            "eng" => Some(Selection::Eng),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// meta.json (crates/capture): the disc's volume label, format ("bluray" or "dvd"), fingerprint and size.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Meta {
    pub volume_label: Option<String>,
    pub format: Option<String>,
    pub fingerprint: Option<String>,
    pub disc_id: Option<String>,
    pub file_count: Option<i64>,
    pub total_bytes: Option<i64>,
    pub captured_unix: Option<f64>,
}

/// One entry of files.json (a list of these).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FilesEntry {
    pub path: String,
    pub size: i64,
}

/// rip-summary.json (rip-title.ps1) and extract-summary.json (extract-from-copy.ps1): the fields the Python reads.
/// Py: titles_report, ripped, same_rip, _scan_flags, exp11 match.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Summary {
    pub ok: Option<bool>,
    pub result: Option<String>,
    pub slug: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<String>,
    pub title: Option<i64>,
    pub profile: Option<String>,
    pub bytes: Option<i64>,
}

/// probe-summary.json (probe-title.ps1).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ProbeSummary {
    pub ok: Option<bool>,
    pub result: Option<String>,
    pub file: Option<String>,
    pub file_bytes: Option<i64>,
    pub subtitle_tracks: Option<i64>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct MkvmergeIdent {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tracks: Vec<MkvTrack>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub chapters: Vec<MkvChapters>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub container: MkvContainer,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct MkvTrack {
    pub id: i64,

    pub r#type: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub codec: String,
    /// Every property as mkvmerge wrote it (language, audio_channels, tag_*, forced_track, track_name, ...).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub properties: serde_json::Map<String, Value>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct MkvChapters {

    pub num_entries: i64,

/// mkvmerge -J's container.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct MkvContainer {

/// duration in nanoseconds (0 when absent, as `.get("duration", 0)`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]

/// ffprobe-streams.json and a level folder's streams.json. Py: ffprobe_audio, read_streams, _scan_flags,
/// audio_positions, no_audio, levels_args.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FfprobeStreams {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub streams: Vec<FfprobeStream>,
}

/// One ffprobe stream. An absent key stays absent when the stream is written again, as ffprobe and proxy_streams
/// leave it out.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FfprobeStream {
    pub index: i64,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub codec_type: Option<String>,

    /// ffprobe's tags (language, title, ...), in file order.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub tags: Option<Ordered<String>>,
}

/// One entry of subs/index.json (a list). Py: subtitle_alignment.index_streams, subtitle_text.load_title.

/// One packet of sub-<n>.packets.json; ffprobe writes the three as strings. Py: events, packet_events, buckets.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Packet {
    pub pts_time: Option<Value>,
    pub duration_time: Option<Value>,
    pub size: Option<Value>,
}

/// sub-<n>.packets.json: `{"packets": [...]}`, or a bare list (packet_events accepts both).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum PacketsFile {
    Object {
        #[serde(default)]
        packets: Vec<Packet>,
    },
    List(Vec<Packet>),
}

impl PacketsFile {
    /// The packets, whichever form the file has.
    pub fn packets(&self) -> &[Packet] {
        match self {
            PacketsFile::Object { packets } => packets,
            PacketsFile::List(packets) => packets,
        }
    }
}

/// subs-ocr/summary.json (ocr-subs.ps1) and ocrs-summary.json (ocrs-trial.ps1): their stream entries.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct OcrSummary {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub streams: Vec<serde_json::Map<String, Value>>,
}

/// One entry of subs-ocr/sub-<n>.frames.json (a list): the frame number and its OCR line count.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FrameEntry {
    pub frame: i64,
    pub lines: Option<i64>,
}

/// One record of sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl or ocrs-s<n>[-crop<pad>].jsonl. Holds subtitle text: in memory only, never
/// written, printed or hashed field by field. Py: ocr_records, ocr_compare.read_frames.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct OcrLine {
    pub frame: Option<i64>,
    pub file: Option<String>,
    pub t: Option<f64>,
    pub pts: Option<f64>,
    /// A list in the final format; anything else means "use `text`" (isinstance(r.get('lines'), list)).
    pub lines: Option<Value>,
    pub text: Option<String>,
    /// ocrs-trial's `{"summary": {...}}` line.
    pub summary: Option<serde_json::Map<String, Value>>,
    /// The other keys (ms, decode_ms, detect_ms, rec_ms, crop, crop_ms), presence kept.
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub rest: serde_json::Map<String, Value>,
}

/// Every non-blank line (py_strip) of a JSON-lines text, parsed; lines split by py_splitlines. Err is serde_json's
/// text for the first line that is not a record. Py: the two jsonl readers.
pub fn read_jsonl(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<OcrLine>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for line in py_splitlines(text) {
        if py_strip(line).is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        out.push(serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// tmdb.json, slimmed (original_language, fetched_at).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Tmdb {
    pub original_language: Option<String>,
    pub fetched_at: Option<String>,
}

/// What thediscdb-hash.json / thediscdb-discid.json says.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DiscDbAnswer {
    Hit,
    Miss,
    NotADisc,
}

/// A non-empty list or an object with a truthy "titles" is a hit, an empty list a miss, anything else not a disc
/// record. Py: hit_rate.lookup.
pub fn thediscdb_answer(value: &Value) -> DiscDbAnswer {
    match value {
        Value::Array(items) if items.is_empty() => DiscDbAnswer::Miss,
        Value::Array(_) => DiscDbAnswer::Hit,
        Value::Object(map) if map.get("titles").map_or(false, py_truthy) => DiscDbAnswer::Hit,
        _ => DiscDbAnswer::NotADisc,
    }
}

/// lookup-status.txt: `{parts[0]: parts[-1]}` for every line (py_splitlines) with two or more py_split parts.
/// Py: hit_rate.statuses.
pub fn lookup_statuses(text: &str) -> Ordered<String> {
    let mut out = Ordered::new();
    for line in py_splitlines(text) {
        let parts = py_split(line);
        if parts.len() >= 2 {
            out.insert(parts[0].to_string(), parts[parts.len() - 1].to_string());
        }
    }
    out
}

/// A rip label of a recording.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct RipLabel {
    pub label: String,
    /// "rip-summary.json" or "extract-summary.json", whichever says ok (rip-summary.json first, as same_rip).
    pub summary_file: &'static str,
    pub summary: Summary,
    pub title: i64,
    pub selection: Selection,
}

/// The summaries that make a rip label, in the order same_rip reads them.
const SUMMARY_FILES: [&str; 2] = ["rip-summary.json", "extract-summary.json"];

/// Every rip label of the recording at `slug_dir`, in PathKey order: a folder (never `golden`) with an ok-saying
/// summary and an mkvmerge.json.
pub fn rip_labels(tree: &dyn Tree, slug_dir: &PathKey) -> Vec<RipLabel> {
    tree.list(slug_dir)
        .iter()
        .filter(|path| tree.is_dir(path))
        .filter_map(|path| rip_label(tree, slug_dir, path.name()).ok())
        .collect()
}

/// The rip label `label` of `slug_dir`, or why it is not one: "<label>: no rip-summary.json or extract-summary.json
/// saying ok" (a summary that cannot be read counts as not saying ok, as same_rip skips it), "<label>: no
/// mkvmerge.json", "<label>: the summary names no title", or, for a folder named golden, "golden: the folder name
/// golden is reserved for goldens; it is not a rip label".
pub fn rip_label(tree: &dyn Tree, slug_dir: &PathKey, label: &str) -> Result<RipLabel, String> {
    if label == "golden" {
        return Err(format!("{}: the folder name golden is reserved for goldens; it is not a rip label", label));
    }
    let dir = slug_dir.join(label);
    let mut found = None;
    for name in SUMMARY_FILES {
        if let Ok(summary) = read_json::<Summary>(tree, &dir.join(name)) {
            if summary.ok == Some(true) {
                found = Some((name, summary));
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    let (summary_file, summary) =
        found.ok_or_else(|| format!("{}: no rip-summary.json or extract-summary.json saying ok", label))?;
    if !tree.is_file(&dir.join("mkvmerge.json")) {
        return Err(format!("{}: no mkvmerge.json", label));
    }
    let title = title_of(&summary).ok_or_else(|| format!("{}: the summary names no title", label))?;
    let selection = selection_of(summary.profile.as_deref());
    Ok(RipLabel { label: label.to_string(), summary_file, summary, title, selection })
}

/// The title number a summary names.
pub fn title_of(summary: &Summary) -> Option<i64> {
    summary.title
}

/// `eng` when the profile's file name (the part after the last '\\', never Path::file_name: it is a Windows path)
/// is `eng-only.mmcp.xml`, else `all` (also for no profile: extract-summary.json names none).
pub fn selection_of(profile_path: Option<&str>) -> Selection {
    match profile_path {
        Some(path) if path.rsplit('\\').next() == Some("eng-only.mmcp.xml") => Selection::Eng,
        _ => Selection::All,
    }
}

/// The disc format meta.json states, as crates/capture writes it ("bluray" or "dvd").
pub fn disc_format(meta: &Meta) -> Option<&str> {
    meta.format.as_deref()
}
```

- [ ] **Step 31: Write `PyRandom`**

Insert at the top of `crates/core/src/testsupport/mod.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]` (CPython 3.9's `_randommodule.c` and `random.py`, in their order of operations):

```rust
//! Test support (port spec section 5, "Ported tests"): Python's random.Random, so that the ported tests draw the same
//! synthetic signals as the Python tests. Compiled for this crate's tests and, through the `testsupport` feature,
//! for lazymkv-dev's integration tests. Task 4 adds the synthetic level series here.

const N: usize = 624;
const M: usize = 397;

/// Python's random.Random: MT19937 seeded as random.seed(int) (init_by_array over the 32-bit words of the seed,
/// least significant first), with the methods the tests call, giving the same values as Python 3.9. Checked against
/// crates/core/tests/fixtures/pyrandom.json (values Python printed once). Py: random.Random.
pub struct PyRandom {
    state: [u32; N],
    index: usize,
}

impl PyRandom {
    /// random.Random(seed) for a non-negative int seed.
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> PyRandom {
        let key: Vec<u32> = if seed >> 32 == 0 { vec![seed as u32] } else { vec![seed as u32, (seed >> 32) as u32] };
        let mut mt = [0u32; N];
        mt[0] = 19_650_218;
        for i in 1..N {
            mt[i] = 1_812_433_253u32.wrapping_mul(mt[i - 1] ^ (mt[i - 1] >> 30)).wrapping_add(i as u32);
        }
        let (mut i, mut j) = (1usize, 0usize);
        for _ in 0..N.max(key.len()) {
            mt[i] = (mt[i] ^ (mt[i - 1] ^ (mt[i - 1] >> 30)).wrapping_mul(1_664_525))
                .wrapping_add(key[j])
                .wrapping_add(j as u32);
            i += 1;
            j += 1;
            if i >= N {
                mt[0] = mt[N - 1];
                i = 1;
            }
            if j >= key.len() {
                j = 0;
            }
        }
        for _ in 0..N - 1 {
            mt[i] = (mt[i] ^ (mt[i - 1] ^ (mt[i - 1] >> 30)).wrapping_mul(1_566_083_941)).wrapping_sub(i as u32);
            i += 1;
            if i >= N {
                mt[0] = mt[N - 1];
                i = 1;
            }
        }
        mt[0] = 0x8000_0000;
        PyRandom { state: mt, index: N }
    }

    /// genrand_uint32: the next 32-bit output, regenerating the 624 words when they are used up.
    fn next_u32(&mut self) -> u32 {
        if self.index >= N {
            for k in 0..N {
                let y = (self.state[k] & 0x8000_0000) | (self.state[(k + 1) % N] & 0x7fff_ffff);
                let mut next = self.state[(k + M) % N] ^ (y >> 1);
                if y & 1 == 1 {
                    next ^= 0x9908_b0df;
                }
                self.state[k] = next;
            }
            self.index = 0;
        }
        let mut y = self.state[self.index];
        self.index += 1;
        y ^= y >> 11;
        y ^= (y << 7) & 0x9d2c_5680;
        y ^= (y << 15) & 0xefc6_0000;
        y ^= y >> 18;
        y
    }

    /// random(): 53 bits, (a >> 5) * 67108864 + (b >> 6), over 2**53.
    pub fn random(&mut self) -> f64 {
        let a = f64::from(self.next_u32() >> 5);
        let b = f64::from(self.next_u32() >> 6);
        (a * 67_108_864.0 + b) * (1.0 / 9_007_199_254_740_992.0)
    }

    /// getrandbits(k), 1 <= k <= 64: one word shifted right for k <= 32; else the low word whole, then the next
    /// word's top k - 32 bits as the high word (CPython fills the words least significant first).
    pub fn getrandbits(&mut self, k: u32) -> u64 {
        assert!((1..=64).contains(&k), "getrandbits: k must be 1 to 64, not {}", k);
        if k <= 32 {
            return u64::from(self.next_u32() >> (32 - k));
        }
        let low = u64::from(self.next_u32());
        let high = u64::from(self.next_u32() >> (64 - k));
        low | (high << 32)
    }

    /// _randbelow_with_getrandbits(n) of Python 3.9: k = n.bit_length(), getrandbits(k) until it is below n.
    fn randbelow(&mut self, n: u64) -> u64 {
        if n == 0 {
            return 0;
        }
        let k = 64 - n.leading_zeros();
        let mut r = self.getrandbits(k);
        while r >= n {
            r = self.getrandbits(k);
        }
        r
    }

    /// randint(a, b) = a + _randbelow(b - a + 1); panics when b < a (Python's ValueError).
    pub fn randint(&mut self, a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 {
        assert!(b >= a, "empty range for randrange() ({}, {}, {})", a, b + 1, b + 1 - a);
        let width = (i128::from(b) - i128::from(a) + 1) as u64;
        (i128::from(a) + i128::from(self.randbelow(width))) as i64
    }

    /// uniform(a, b) = a + (b - a) * random().
    pub fn uniform(&mut self, a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
        a + (b - a) * self.random()
    }

    /// choice(seq) = seq[_randbelow(len(seq))]; panics on an empty slice (Python's IndexError).
    pub fn choice<'a, T>(&mut self, seq: &'a [T]) -> &'a T {
        let at = self.randbelow(seq.len() as u64) as usize;
        seq.get(at).expect("Cannot choose from an empty sequence")
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Running ffprobe and ffmpeg (port spec 3.1): the trait the commands call, the real programs, and a fake for tests,
//! so that the Python's mocked subprocess tests port as they are.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::io;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// What a finished program gave: exit status (negative signal number when killed, as subprocess), and its output
/// decoded as UTF-8 (lossily) with universal newlines, as subprocess.run(..., text=True) reads it.
/// Py: subprocess.CompletedProcess.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Output {
    pub status: i32,
    pub stdout: String,
    pub stderr: String,
}

/// Runs ffprobe and ffmpeg. Py: subprocess.run(args, cwd=..., capture_output=True, text=True).
pub trait Runner {
    /// Runs `program` with `args` in `cwd` (None: the current directory); Err when it cannot be started
    /// (io::ErrorKind::NotFound when it is not on PATH).
    fn run(&self, program: &str, args: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>) -> io::Result<Output>;
}

/// std::process::Command.
pub struct RealRunner;

impl Runner for RealRunner {
    fn run(&self, program: &str, args: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>) -> io::Result<Output> {
        let mut command = std::process::Command::new(program);
        command.args(args);
        if let Some(dir) = cwd {
            command.current_dir(dir);
        }
        let output = command.output()?;
        Ok(Output { status: exit_status(&output.status), stdout: text_of(&output.stdout), stderr: text_of(&output.stderr) })
    }
}

/// The exit code, or minus the signal number when a signal ended the program (subprocess's returncode).
#[cfg(unix)]
fn exit_status(status: &std::process::ExitStatus) -> i32 {
    use std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt;
    status.code().or_else(|| status.signal().map(|signal| -signal)).unwrap_or(-1)
}

/// The exit code (Windows has no signals).
#[cfg(not(unix))]
fn exit_status(status: &std::process::ExitStatus) -> i32 {
    status.code().unwrap_or(-1)
}

/// text=True: UTF-8 (here lossily, where Python would raise) with "\r\n" and "\r" read as "\n".
fn text_of(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    String::from_utf8_lossy(bytes).replace("\r\n", "\n").replace('\r', "\n")
}

/// One call a FakeRunner received.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Call {
    pub program: String,
    pub args: Vec<String>,
    pub cwd: Option<PathBuf>,
}

/// The handler a FakeRunner answers with: it may write files into `cwd` (as the Python test's fake ffmpeg writes
/// raw-<series>.txt).
pub type Handler = Box<dyn Fn(&str, &[String], Option<&Path>) -> io::Result<Output>>;

/// A Runner for tests (the mocked `subprocess.run` and `proxy_tracks` of ProxyStreams port through it).
pub struct FakeRunner {
    handler: Handler,
    calls: RefCell<Vec<Call>>,
}

impl FakeRunner {
    pub fn new(handler: Handler) -> FakeRunner {
        FakeRunner { handler, calls: RefCell::new(Vec::new()) }
    }

    /// Every program is missing (NotFound): the "ffmpeg absent" skip path.
    pub fn absent() -> FakeRunner {
        FakeRunner::new(Box::new(|program: &str, _args: &[String], _cwd: Option<&Path>| -> io::Result<Output> {
            Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, format!("{}: not found (FakeRunner::absent)", program)))
        }))
    }

    /// Answers the k-th call with the k-th output; a call past the end panics.
    pub fn scripted(outputs: Vec<Output>) -> FakeRunner {
        let queue = RefCell::new(VecDeque::from(outputs));
        FakeRunner::new(Box::new(move |program: &str, _args: &[String], _cwd: Option<&Path>| -> io::Result<Output> {
            match queue.borrow_mut().pop_front() {
                Some(output) => Ok(output),
                None => panic!("FakeRunner::scripted has no output left for {}", program),
            }
        }))
    }

    /// The calls so far, in order.
    pub fn calls(&self) -> Vec<Call> {
        self.calls.borrow().clone()
    }
}

impl Runner for FakeRunner {
    fn run(&self, program: &str, args: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>) -> io::Result<Output> {
        self.calls.borrow_mut().push(Call {
            program: program.to_string(),
            args: args.to_vec(),
            cwd: cwd.map(Path::to_path_buf),
        });
        (self.handler)(program, args, cwd)
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Where the commands find their inputs (port spec 3.4): the context of a run (cwd, environment, the program runner,
//! the clock), the evidence clone and its exit-3 refusal, the repository root and --spec's default, the OCR text
//! folder, a directory on disk as a `Tree`, and a recording named as a slug or a path.

use crate::runner::{FakeRunner, RealRunner, Runner};
use lazymkv_core::recording::{py_repr_str, Kind, Loader, MemTree, PathKey, ReadError, Tree};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;

/// The fixed clock of `Ctx::for_test`.
const TEST_CLOCK: &str = "2026-10-13T12:00:00";
/// --spec's default below the repository root. Py: audio_labels.SPEC.
const SPEC: &str = "docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-lazymkv-design.md";

/// Everything a command reads from its surroundings, so that tests set all of it.
pub struct Ctx {
    /// The directory relative paths are taken against.
    pub cwd: PathBuf,
    /// The environment variables the commands read: LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT, TMPDIR, TEMP, TMP.
    pub env: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// ffprobe and ffmpeg (and, for `now`, the clock programs).
    pub runner: Box<dyn Runner>,
    /// A fixed local time "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS" for tests; None reads the system clock.
    pub clock: Option<String>,
}

impl Ctx {
    /// The process's cwd, environment, RealRunner, no fixed clock.
    pub fn from_process() -> Ctx {
        Ctx {
            cwd: std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from(".")),
            env: std::env::vars_os()
                .map(|(name, value)| (name.to_string_lossy().into_owned(), value.to_string_lossy().into_owned()))
                .collect(),
            runner: Box::new(RealRunner),
            clock: None,
        }
    }

    /// A context for tests: `cwd`, an empty environment, FakeRunner::absent(), clock "2026-10-13T12:00:00".
    pub fn for_test(cwd: &Path) -> Ctx {
        Ctx {
            cwd: cwd.to_path_buf(),
            env: BTreeMap::new(),
            runner: Box::new(FakeRunner::absent()),
            clock: Some(TEST_CLOCK.to_string()),
        }
    }

    /// Local time to the second, as datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"). std has no time zones and no date
    /// crate is allowed, so the clock program says it: `date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'` (macOS, Linux) or `powershell
    /// -NoProfile -Command "Get-Date -Format s"` (the mini PC), through the runner; when that fails, UTC with a
    /// warning on stderr (02-interfaces.md, open point 5).
    pub fn now(&self) -> String {
        if let Some(clock) = &self.clock {
            return clock.clone();
        }
        let (program, args): (&str, Vec<String>) = if cfg!(windows) {
            ("powershell", vec!["-NoProfile".to_string(), "-Command".to_string(), "Get-Date -Format s".to_string()])
        } else {
            ("date", vec!["+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S".to_string()])
        };
        if let Ok(output) = self.runner.run(program, &args, None) {
            let text = output.stdout.trim();
            if output.status == 0 && is_local_time(text) {
                return text.to_string();
            }
        }
        let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr(), "warning: {} did not give the local time; the time is given in UTC", program);
        utc_now()
    }

    /// The local date, YYYY-MM-DD (the first 10 characters of now()). Py: datetime.date.today().isoformat().
    pub fn today(&self) -> String {
        self.now().chars().take(10).collect()
    }

    /// tempfile.gettempdir(): TMPDIR, TEMP, TMP from `env` (made absolute against cwd), else std::env::temp_dir().
    pub fn temp_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        for name in ["TMPDIR", "TEMP", "TMP"] {
            if let Some(value) = self.env.get(name).filter(|value| !value.is_empty()) {
                return self.abs(value).components().collect();
            }
        }
        std::env::temp_dir()
    }

    /// `path` taken against `cwd` when relative.
    pub fn abs(&self, path: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let path = Path::new(path);
        if path.is_absolute() {
            path.to_path_buf()
        } else {
            self.cwd.join(path)
        }
    }
}

/// "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS", digits where digits belong.
fn is_local_time(text: &str) -> bool {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    bytes.len() == 19
        && bytes.iter().enumerate().all(|(at, b)| match at {
            4 | 7 => *b == b'-',
            10 => *b == b'T',
            13 | 16 => *b == b':',
            _ => b.is_ascii_digit(),
        })
}

/// The time now in UTC, "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS".
fn utc_now() -> String {
    let seconds = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|elapsed| elapsed.as_secs())
        .unwrap_or(0);
    civil_time(seconds)
}

/// "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS" of a count of seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00, by the days-to-civil algorithm of the
/// proleptic Gregorian calendar.
fn civil_time(seconds: u64) -> String {
    let days = (seconds / 86_400) as i64;
    let rest = seconds % 86_400;
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let day_of_era = z - era * 146_097;
    let year_of_era = (day_of_era - day_of_era / 1460 + day_of_era / 36_524 - day_of_era / 146_096) / 365;
    let day_of_year = day_of_era - (365 * year_of_era + year_of_era / 4 - year_of_era / 100);
    let month_index = (5 * day_of_year + 2) / 153;
    let day = day_of_year - (153 * month_index + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let month = if month_index < 10 { month_index + 3 } else { month_index - 9 };
    let year = year_of_era + era * 400 + if month <= 2 { 1 } else { 0 };
    format!("{:04}-{:02}-{:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}", year, month, day, rest / 3600, rest % 3600 / 60, rest % 60)
}

/// The private evidence repository's URL. Py: audio_dataset.EVIDENCE.
pub const EVIDENCE_URL: &str = "https://github.com/krcm0209/lazymkv-evidence";
/// How every report prints the evidence root, whatever --evidence says (spec 3.4).
pub const EVIDENCE_SHOWN: &str = "corpus/owner";

/// Why a slug command cannot run: the line it prints (to stderr) and its exit code.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Refused {
    pub code: i32,
    pub line: String,
}

/// The evidence directory: `flag` (--evidence), else LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE, else "corpus/owner" under the repository
/// root (else under cwd). Refused { code: 3, "<dir>: no such folder; the evidence repository lazymkv-evidence is not
/// cloned there (git clone <EVIDENCE_URL> <dir>)" } when it does not exist, code 2 "<dir>: not a folder" when it is
/// a file; <dir> is the path as given, or the default relative to cwd. Py: audio_dataset.main's corpus check.
pub fn resolve_evidence(ctx: &Ctx, flag: Option<&str>) -> Result<PathBuf, Refused> {
    let given = flag
        .map(str::to_string)
        .or_else(|| ctx.env.get("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE").filter(|value| !value.is_empty()).cloned());
    let (path, shown) = match given {
        Some(given) => (ctx.abs(&given), given),
        None => evidence_default(&ctx.cwd, repo_root(&ctx.cwd).as_deref()),
    };
    if !path.exists() {
        return Err(Refused {
            code: 3,
            line: format!(
                "{}: no such folder; the evidence repository lazymkv-evidence is not cloned there (git clone {} {})",
                shown, EVIDENCE_URL, shown
            ),
        });
    }
    if !path.is_dir() {
        return Err(Refused { code: 2, line: format!("{}: not a folder", shown) });
    }
    Ok(path)
}

/// The default evidence folder and how it is shown: corpus/owner under the repository root, shown relative to cwd
/// ("corpus/owner" from the root, "../../corpus/owner" from crates/dev); without a root, corpus/owner under cwd.
fn evidence_default(cwd: &Path, root: Option<&Path>) -> (PathBuf, String) {
    match root {
        Some(root) => {
            let depth = cwd.strip_prefix(root).map(|rest| rest.components().count()).unwrap_or(0);
            (root.join(EVIDENCE_SHOWN), format!("{}{}", "../".repeat(depth), EVIDENCE_SHOWN))
        }
        None => (cwd.join(EVIDENCE_SHOWN), EVIDENCE_SHOWN.to_string()),
    }
}

/// The repository root: the nearest ancestor of `start` (itself included) whose Cargo.toml holds a `[workspace]`
/// table (a `[workspace]` or `[workspace.<key>]` header line).
pub fn repo_root(start: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    start
        .ancestors()
        .find(|dir| {
            std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("Cargo.toml"))
                .map(|text| {
                    text.lines().any(|line| {
                        let line = line.trim();
                        line == "[workspace]" || line.starts_with("[workspace.")
                    })
                })
                .unwrap_or(false)
        })
        .map(Path::to_path_buf)
}

/// --spec's default: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-lazymkv-design.md under repo_root; None when there is no
/// root (--spec is then required). Py: audio_labels.SPEC.
pub fn default_spec(ctx: &Ctx) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    repo_root(&ctx.cwd).map(|root| root.join(SPEC))
}

/// The OCR text folder: `flag` (--text), else LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT, else None.
pub fn ocr_text_dir(ctx: &Ctx, flag: Option<&str>) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    match flag {
        Some(given) => Some(ctx.abs(given)),
        None => ctx.env.get("LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT").filter(|value| !value.is_empty()).map(|value| ctx.abs(value)),
    }
}

/// A directory on disk as a Tree: walked once on open (folders and file names; `.git` left out), file bytes read on
/// first use.
pub struct DiskTree {
    root: PathBuf,
    tree: MemTree,
}

impl DiskTree {
    /// Opens `root`, printed under `display_root` (EVIDENCE_SHOWN, or the path as the user gave it).
    pub fn open(root: &Path, display_root: &str) -> std::io::Result<DiskTree> {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(display_root, &resolved_name_of(root));
        walk(root, "", &mut tree)?;
        Ok(DiskTree { root: root.to_path_buf(), tree })
    }

    /// Like `open`, but the tree holds only the folder `sub` of `root` (one name, no '/'): a recording named by
    /// slug or path is read without walking the rest of its parent.
    pub fn open_sub(root: &Path, display_root: &str, sub: &str) -> std::io::Result<DiskTree> {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(display_root, &resolved_name_of(root));
        tree.insert_dir(sub);
        walk(&root.join(sub), sub, &mut tree)?;
        Ok(DiskTree { root: root.to_path_buf(), tree })
    }

    /// The file system path of a key, for writing.
    pub fn path(&self, key: &PathKey) -> PathBuf {
        let mut path = self.root.clone();
        for part in key.components() {
            path.push(part);
        }
        path
    }
}

/// Adds every folder and file under `dir` to `tree`, below `prefix` ("" for the root), files as lazy loaders.
fn walk(dir: &Path, prefix: &str, tree: &mut MemTree) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir)? {
        let entry = entry?;
        let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        if name == ".git" {
            continue;
        }
        let key = if prefix.is_empty() { name } else { format!("{}/{}", prefix, name) };
        let path = entry.path();
        if path.is_dir() {
            tree.insert_dir(&key);
            walk(&path, &key, tree)?;
        } else {
            let shown = tree.display(&PathKey::new(&key));
            let load: Loader = Arc::new(move || std::fs::read(&path).map_err(|error| os_error_text(&error, &shown)));
            tree.insert_lazy(&key, load);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Python's OSError text: "[Errno <n>] <strerror>: '<path>'" (Rust's message without its " (os error n)").
fn os_error_text(error: &std::io::Error, shown: &str) -> String {
    match error.raw_os_error() {
        Some(code) => {
            let text = error.to_string();
            let description = match text.rfind(" (os error ") {
                Some(at) => text[..at].to_string(),
                None => text,
            };
            format!("[Errno {}] {}: {}", code, description, py_repr_str(shown))
        }
        None => error.to_string(),
    }
}

/// The name of `root`'s resolved absolute path ("" when it cannot be resolved). Py: Path.resolve().name.
fn resolved_name_of(root: &Path) -> String {
    std::fs::canonicalize(root)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|path| path.file_name().map(|name| name.to_string_lossy().into_owned()))
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

impl Tree for DiskTree {
    fn kind(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Option<Kind> {
        self.tree.kind(path)
    }

    fn list(&self, dir: &PathKey) -> Vec<PathKey> {
        self.tree.list(dir)
    }

    fn glob(&self, base: &PathKey, pattern: &str) -> Vec<PathKey> {
        self.tree.glob(base, pattern)
    }

    fn read(&self, path: &PathKey) -> Result<Arc<[u8]>, ReadError> {
        self.tree.read(path)
    }

    fn display(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String {
        self.tree.display(path)
    }

    fn resolved_name(&self, path: &PathKey) -> String {
        self.tree.resolved_name(path)
    }
}

/// A recording named on the command line, as a slug under the evidence or as a directory path.
pub struct Recording {
    /// The evidence root (slug form) or the recording's parent directory (path form).
    pub tree: DiskTree,
    /// The recording folder inside `tree`.
    pub dir: PathKey,
    /// Its folder name.
    pub slug: String,
}

/// `arg` is a path when it names an existing directory (relative to cwd), else a slug under
/// resolve_evidence(flag) (exit 3 as there; code 2 "corpus/owner/<arg>: no such recording (neither a recording
/// folder nor a slug under corpus/owner)" when the slug is not a folder there). The path form prints paths as given
/// and makes no evidence check (spec 3.4).
pub fn resolve_recording(ctx: &Ctx, evidence_flag: Option<&str>, arg: &str) -> Result<Recording, Refused> {
    let given = ctx.abs(arg);
    if given.is_dir() {
        let (parent, parent_shown, name) = match split_recording_path(ctx, arg) {
            Some(parts) => parts,
            None => {
                let canonical = std::fs::canonicalize(&given)
                    .map_err(|error| Refused { code: 2, line: format!("{}: {}", arg, error) })?;
                let parent = canonical
                    .parent()
                    .map(Path::to_path_buf)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Refused { code: 2, line: format!("{}: not a recording folder", arg) })?;
                let name = canonical.file_name().map(|name| name.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default();
                let shown = parent.display().to_string();
                (parent, shown, name)
            }
        };
        let tree = DiskTree::open_sub(&parent, &parent_shown, &name)
            .map_err(|error| Refused { code: 2, line: format!("{}: {}", arg, error) })?;
        return Ok(Recording { tree, dir: PathKey::new(&name), slug: name });
    }
    let evidence = resolve_evidence(ctx, evidence_flag)?;
    let simple = !arg.is_empty() && arg != "." && arg != ".." && !arg.contains('/') && !arg.contains('\\');
    if !simple || !evidence.join(arg).is_dir() {
        return Err(Refused {
            code: 2,
            line: format!(
                "{}/{}: no such recording (neither a recording folder nor a slug under {})",
                EVIDENCE_SHOWN, arg, EVIDENCE_SHOWN
            ),
        });
    }
    let tree = DiskTree::open_sub(&evidence, EVIDENCE_SHOWN, arg)
        .map_err(|error| Refused { code: 2, line: format!("{}/{}: {}", EVIDENCE_SHOWN, arg, error) })?;
    Ok(Recording { tree, dir: PathKey::new(arg), slug: arg.to_string() })
}

/// (the parent folder on disk, the parent as the user wrote it, the recording's name) for a recording path, split
/// as pathlib splits str(Path(arg)); None for ".", "..", "/" or a path ending in "..", which are resolved instead.
fn split_recording_path(ctx: &Ctx, arg: &str) -> Option<(PathBuf, String, String)> {
    let normal = if cfg!(windows) { arg.replace('\\', "/") } else { arg.to_string() };
    let shown = pathlib_str(&normal);
    let (head, name) = match shown.rsplit_once('/') {
        Some(("", name)) => ("/".to_string(), name.to_string()),
        Some((head, name)) => (head.to_string(), name.to_string()),
        None => (".".to_string(), shown.clone()),
    };
    if name.is_empty() || name == "." || name == ".." {
        return None;
    }
    let parent = ctx.abs(arg).parent()?.to_path_buf();
    Some((parent, head, name))
}

/// `str(PurePosixPath(text))`: empty and "." components dropped, a leading "/" kept, "." for nothing.
fn pathlib_str(text: &str) -> String {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = text.split('/').filter(|part| !part.is_empty() && *part != ".").collect();
    if text.starts_with('/') {
        format!("/{}", parts.join("/"))
    } else if parts.is_empty() {
        ".".to_string()
    } else {
        parts.join("/")
    }
}

/// A test whose input is absent: writes "skipped: <reason>" straight to std::io::stderr() (not through eprintln!,
/// which the test harness captures), so `cargo test` shows it; the test then returns and passes.
pub fn skip(reason: &str) {
    let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr(), "skipped: {}", reason);
}
```
