```rust
//! Python's json.dumps byte for byte, the files the Python wrote with it, the level files of
//! proxy_levels.convert_levels, and the structural comparison the goldens use (port spec 3.3 "Writers", section 4).

use lazymkv_core::recording::{py_float_repr, py_is_space, universal_lines};
use serde_json::{Number, Value};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

/// How json.dumps was called.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Style {
    /// None: one line with Python's default separators ", " and ": "; Some(n): n spaces per level with "," and ": ".
    pub indent: Option<usize>,
    /// true: every character outside ' ' to '~' as \uXXXX (lowercase hex, surrogate pairs above U+FFFF); false:
    /// kept. Both escape \" \\ \n \r \t \b \f by name and the other controls below 0x20 as \u00XX, as json.dumps does.
    pub ensure_ascii: bool,
    /// json.dumps(sort_keys=True): object keys by code point.
    pub sort_keys: bool,
}

impl Style {
    /// json.dumps(x): indent None, ASCII, insertion order.
    pub const PY_DEFAULT: Style = Style { indent: None, ensure_ascii: true, sort_keys: false };
    /// The snapshot and streams.json: indent 1, ASCII.
    pub const INDENT1_ASCII: Style = Style { indent: Some(1), ensure_ascii: true, sort_keys: false };
    /// The labels and fitted files: indent 2, non-ASCII kept.
    pub const INDENT2_UTF8: Style = Style { indent: Some(2), ensure_ascii: false, sort_keys: false };
}

/// json.dumps(value, ...) byte for byte: insertion order (serde_json `preserve_order`), ints and floats distinct
/// (floats spelt by py_float_repr), true/false/null, empty containers as [] and {}. A NaN never reaches it:
/// serde_json::Value holds none (serde_json turns a NaN f64 into null, which is nan_to_none).
pub fn dumps(value: &Value, style: Style) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    write_value(&mut out, value, style, 0);
    out
}

fn write_value(out: &mut String, value: &Value, style: Style, level: usize) {
    match value {
        Value::Null => out.push_str("null"),
        Value::Bool(true) => out.push_str("true"),
        Value::Bool(false) => out.push_str("false"),
        Value::Number(number) => out.push_str(&number_text(number)),
        Value::String(text) => write_string(out, text, style.ensure_ascii),
        Value::Array(items) => {
            if items.is_empty() {
                out.push_str("[]");
                return;
            }
            out.push('[');
            for (at, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                if at > 0 {
                    out.push_str(item_separator(style));
                }
                newline(out, style, level + 1);
                write_value(out, item, style, level + 1);
            }
            newline(out, style, level);
            out.push(']');
        }
        Value::Object(map) => {
            if map.is_empty() {
                out.push_str("{}");
                return;
            }
            let mut entries: Vec<(&String, &Value)> = map.iter().collect();
            if style.sort_keys {
                entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(b.0));
            }
            out.push('{');
            for (at, (key, item)) in entries.into_iter().enumerate() {
                if at > 0 {
                    out.push_str(item_separator(style));
                }
                newline(out, style, level + 1);
                write_string(out, key, style.ensure_ascii);
                out.push_str(": ");
                write_value(out, item, style, level + 1);
            }
            newline(out, style, level);
            out.push('}');
        }
    }
}

/// ", " on one line, "," when indented (json.dumps' default separators).
fn item_separator(style: Style) -> &'static str {
    if style.indent.is_some() {
        ","
    } else {
        ", "
    }
}

/// "\n" and indent * level spaces when indented; nothing on one line.
fn newline(out: &mut String, style: Style, level: usize) {
    if let Some(indent) = style.indent {
        out.push('\n');
        out.push_str(&" ".repeat(indent * level));
    }
}

/// An int as its digits, a float as Python's repr.
fn number_text(number: &Number) -> String {
    if let Some(int) = number.as_i64() {
        int.to_string()
    } else if let Some(int) = number.as_u64() {
        int.to_string()
    } else {
        py_float_repr(number.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN))
    }
}

fn write_string(out: &mut String, text: &str, ensure_ascii: bool) {
    out.push('"');
    for c in text.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            '\u{8}' => out.push_str("\\b"),
            '\u{c}' => out.push_str("\\f"),
            _ if (c as u32) < 0x20 => out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
            _ if ensure_ascii && (c as u32) > 0x7e => {
                let mut units = [0u16; 2];
                for unit in c.encode_utf16(&mut units).iter() {
                    out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", unit));
                }
            }
            _ => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
}

/// Writes `text` to `<path>.tmp`, then renames it over `path` (os.replace).
pub fn write_atomic(path: &Path, text: &str) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut tmp = path.as_os_str().to_os_string();
    tmp.push(".tmp");
    let tmp = PathBuf::from(tmp);
    std::fs::write(&tmp, text)?;
    std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)
}

/// The snapshot: dumps(INDENT1_ASCII) + "\n", through `.tmp` and a rename. Py: audio_dataset.write_snapshot (whose
/// "unchanged but for its time" check stays with the caller, Task 8).
pub fn write_snapshot(path: &Path, value: &Value) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    write_atomic(path, &format!("{}\n", dumps(value, Style::INDENT1_ASCII)))
}

/// A labels or fitted file: dumps(INDENT2_UTF8) + "\n", UTF-8, through `.tmp` and a rename. Py: audio_labels.write_json.
pub fn write_labels(path: &Path, value: &Value) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    write_atomic(path, &format!("{}\n", dumps(value, Style::INDENT2_UTF8)))
}

/// streams.json: dumps(INDENT1_ASCII) + "\n", written in place. Py: proxy_levels.build.
pub fn write_streams_json(path: &Path, value: &Value) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::write(path, format!("{}\n", dumps(value, Style::INDENT1_ASCII)))
}

/// The ametadata key of a level line. Py: proxy_levels.KEY.
pub const KEY: &str = "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=";

const FLOOR: &str = "-100.0";
const CONVERSION_SYNTAX: &str = "[<class 'decimal.ConversionSyntax'>]";
const INVALID_OPERATION: &str = "[<class 'decimal.InvalidOperation'>]";

/// A number as Python's decimal module reads it.
enum Decimal {
    NaN,
    Infinity { negative: bool },
    /// The value is (-1 if negative) * digits * 10**exponent; `digits` holds ASCII digits, leading zeros allowed.
    Finite { negative: bool, digits: String, exponent: i64 },
}

/// One level as audio-levels.ps1 and proxy_levels write it: Decimal("-100.0") when the text holds "inf" or "nan",
/// else max(Decimal("-100.0"), Decimal(text)) (the first wins a tie), quantized to 0.1 with ROUND_HALF_UP (half away
/// from zero), spelt as str(Decimal) ("-23.5", "-0.0", "-100.0"). Err is str() of the decimal exception the Python
/// would raise: "[<class 'decimal.ConversionSyntax'>]" for text Decimal() refuses, "[<class
/// 'decimal.InvalidOperation'>]" for +Infinity, a NaN (max() compares with it) or a result of more than 28 digits.
/// Non-ASCII digits are refused (Decimal() accepts them; ffmpeg never writes one). Py: convert_levels' loop body.
pub fn round_level(text: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if text.contains("inf") || text.contains("nan") {
        return Ok(FLOOR.to_string());
    }
    match parse_decimal(text).ok_or_else(|| CONVERSION_SYNTAX.to_string())? {
        Decimal::NaN => Err(INVALID_OPERATION.to_string()),
        Decimal::Infinity { negative: true } => Ok(FLOOR.to_string()),
        Decimal::Infinity { negative: false } => Err(INVALID_OPERATION.to_string()),
        Decimal::Finite { negative, digits, exponent } => {
            if negative && !below_hundred(&digits, exponent) {
                return Ok(FLOOR.to_string());
            }
            quantize_tenth(negative, &digits, exponent)
        }
    }
}

/// Decimal(text) of Python 3.9's C decimal: underscores dropped anywhere, surrounding whitespace stripped, then
/// [sign] (digits [. [digits]] | . digits) [e|E [sign] digits], or [sign] Inf / Infinity, or [sign] NaN / sNaN with
/// optional digits (letters in any case). None where Decimal() raises ConversionSyntax.
fn parse_decimal(text: &str) -> Option<Decimal> {
    let cleaned: String = text
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| *c != '_')
        .map(|c| if !c.is_ascii() && py_is_space(c) { ' ' } else { c })
        .collect();
    let body = cleaned.trim_matches(|c: char| matches!(c, ' ' | '\t' | '\n' | '\x0b' | '\x0c' | '\r'));
    let (negative, rest) = match body.as_bytes().first() {
        Some(b'-') => (true, &body[1..]),
        Some(b'+') => (false, &body[1..]),
        _ => (false, body),
    };
    let lower = rest.to_ascii_lowercase();
    if lower == "inf" || lower == "infinity" {
        return Some(Decimal::Infinity { negative });
    }
    if let Some(payload) = lower.strip_prefix("nan").or_else(|| lower.strip_prefix("snan")) {
        return if payload.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) { Some(Decimal::NaN) } else { None };
    }
    let (mantissa, exponent_text) = match rest.find(|c: char| c == 'e' || c == 'E') {
        Some(at) => (&rest[..at], Some(&rest[at + 1..])),
        None => (rest, None),
    };
    let (whole, fraction) = match mantissa.split_once('.') {
        Some((whole, fraction)) => (whole, fraction),
        None => (mantissa, ""),
    };
    if whole.is_empty() && fraction.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    if !whole.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) || !fraction.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return None;
    }
    let exponent = match exponent_text {
        None => 0,
        Some(text) => {
            let (sign, digits) = match text.as_bytes().first() {
                Some(b'-') => (-1, &text[1..]),
                Some(b'+') => (1, &text[1..]),
                _ => (1, text),
            };
            if digits.is_empty() || !digits.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) {
                return None;
            }
            let significant = digits.trim_start_matches('0');
            let magnitude: i64 = if significant.is_empty() {
                0
            } else if significant.len() > 15 {
                1_000_000_000_000_000
            } else {
                significant.parse().unwrap_or(0)
            };
            sign * magnitude
        }
    };
    Some(Decimal::Finite { negative, digits: format!("{}{}", whole, fraction), exponent: exponent - fraction.len() as i64 })
}

/// Whether digits * 10**exponent is below 100 (so that a negative value is above the floor of -100).
fn below_hundred(digits: &str, exponent: i64) -> bool {
    let significant = digits.trim_start_matches('0');
    significant.is_empty() || (significant.len() as i64 - 1 + exponent) < 2
}

/// Decimal.quantize(Decimal("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP) and str() of the result.
fn quantize_tenth(negative: bool, digits: &str, exponent: i64) -> Result<String, String> {
    let digits = digits.trim_start_matches('0');
    let kept: String = if exponent >= -1 {
        if digits.is_empty() {
            "0".to_string()
        } else {
            if digits.len() as i64 + exponent + 1 > 28 {
                return Err(INVALID_OPERATION.to_string());
            }
            format!("{}{}", digits, "0".repeat((exponent + 1) as usize))
        }
    } else {
        let dropped = (-1 - exponent) as usize;
        let (head, first_dropped) = if digits.len() > dropped {
            (digits[..digits.len() - dropped].to_string(), digits.as_bytes()[digits.len() - dropped])
        } else if digits.len() == dropped {
            ("0".to_string(), digits.as_bytes()[0])
        } else {
            ("0".to_string(), b'0')
        };
        if first_dropped >= b'5' {
            increment(&head)
        } else {
            head
        }
    };
    let kept = kept.trim_start_matches('0');
    let kept = if kept.is_empty() { "0" } else { kept };
    if kept.len() > 28 {
        return Err(INVALID_OPERATION.to_string());
    }
    let (whole, tenth) = kept.split_at(kept.len() - 1);
    Ok(format!("{}{}.{}", if negative { "-" } else { "" }, if whole.is_empty() { "0" } else { whole }, tenth))
}

/// A string of ASCII digits plus one.
fn increment(digits: &str) -> String {
    let mut bytes = digits.as_bytes().to_vec();
    let mut at = bytes.len();
    loop {
        if at == 0 {
            bytes.insert(0, b'1');
            break;
        }
        at -= 1;
        if bytes[at] == b'9' {
            bytes[at] = b'0';
        } else {
            bytes[at] += 1;
            break;
        }
    }
    String::from_utf8(bytes).expect("ASCII digits")
}

/// A level file's text from ffmpeg's raw ametadata output: `header`, then one round_level per line starting with KEY
/// (lines from universal_lines, which already drops the "\r\n" convert_levels strips), every line ended by "\r\n";
/// and the number of frames. Py: proxy_levels.convert_levels.
pub fn level_file_text(raw: &str, header: &str) -> Result<(String, usize), String> {
    let mut text = header.replace('\n', "\r\n");
    text.push_str("\r\n");
    let mut frames = 0;
    for line in universal_lines(raw) {
        if let Some(value) = line.strip_prefix(KEY) {
            text.push_str(&round_level(value)?);
            text.push_str("\r\n");
            frames += 1;
        }
    }
    Ok((text, frames))
}

/// Writes level_file_text(raw, header) to `path` (CRLF line ends, UTF-8) and returns the frame count; Err with the
/// I/O or decimal text (nothing is written when a level is refused). Py: proxy_levels.convert_levels.
pub fn write_level_file(path: &Path, raw: &str, header: &str) -> Result<usize, String> {
    let (text, frames) = level_file_text(raw, header)?;
    std::fs::write(path, text).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
    Ok(frames)
}

/// manifest.txt: the lines joined with "\n" plus a final "\n", UTF-8. Py: proxy_levels.build.
pub fn write_manifest(path: &Path, lines: &[String]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::write(path, format!("{}\n", lines.join("\n")))
}

/// How two parsed JSON documents may differ and still be equal: floats within `abs` (1e-9), keys named in
/// `loose_keys` ("smi", "rev_smi") within `loose` (1e-6), null equal to null (NaN as null), ints equal to equal floats
/// never (1 and 1.0 differ, as Python's text does); paths in `ignore` are JSON pointers with `*` for any key or
/// index ("/created", "/tracks/*/key").
pub struct Tolerance {
    pub abs: f64,
    pub loose: f64,
    pub loose_keys: &'static [&'static str],
    pub ignore: Vec<String>,
}

impl Tolerance {
    /// abs 1e-9, loose 1e-6 for "smi" and "rev_smi", nothing ignored (spec section 4).
    pub fn spec() -> Tolerance {
        Tolerance { abs: 1e-9, loose: 1e-6, loose_keys: &["smi", "rev_smi"], ignore: Vec::new() }
    }
}

/// Every difference between `expected` and `actual`, one line each ("<pointer>: <expected> != <actual>", values as
/// dumps(PY_DEFAULT), "(absent)" for a missing key or element, "(root)" for the whole document); empty when they are
/// equal under `tol`. Object keys are compared as sets (expected's keys first, in its order, then actual's own),
/// arrays in order. A float inside an array takes the tolerance of the key that holds the array.
pub fn structural_diff(expected: &Value, actual: &Value, tol: &Tolerance) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    diff_at(&mut Vec::new(), None, Some(expected), Some(actual), tol, &mut out);
    out
}

fn diff_at(
    pointer: &mut Vec<String>,
    key: Option<&str>,
    expected: Option<&Value>,
    actual: Option<&Value>,
    tol: &Tolerance,
    out: &mut Vec<String>,
) {
    if tol.ignore.iter().any(|pattern| pointer_matches(pattern, pointer.as_slice())) {
        return;
    }
    match (expected, actual) {
        (Some(Value::Object(left)), Some(Value::Object(right))) => {
            let mut names: Vec<&String> = left.keys().collect();
            names.extend(right.keys().filter(|name| !left.contains_key(name.as_str())));
            for name in names {
                pointer.push(name.clone());
                diff_at(pointer, Some(name.as_str()), left.get(name.as_str()), right.get(name.as_str()), tol, out);
                pointer.pop();
            }
        }
        (Some(Value::Array(left)), Some(Value::Array(right))) => {
            for at in 0..left.len().max(right.len()) {
                pointer.push(at.to_string());
                diff_at(pointer, key, left.get(at), right.get(at), tol, out);
                pointer.pop();
            }
        }
        (Some(left), Some(right)) if same(left, right, key, tol) => {}
        _ => out.push(format!("{}: {} != {}", pointer_text(pointer), shown(expected), shown(actual))),
    }
}

/// Equal under `tol`: numbers of the same kind (int or float), floats within the key's tolerance; anything else
/// exactly.
fn same(expected: &Value, actual: &Value, key: Option<&str>, tol: &Tolerance) -> bool {
    match (expected, actual) {
        (Value::Number(left), Value::Number(right)) => {
            if left.is_f64() != right.is_f64() {
                return false;
            }
            if !left.is_f64() {
                return left == right;
            }
            let (left, right) = (left.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN), right.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN));
            let loose = key.map_or(false, |name| tol.loose_keys.iter().any(|loose_key| *loose_key == name));
            let limit = if loose { tol.loose } else { tol.abs };
            left == right || (left - right).abs() <= limit
        }
        _ => expected == actual,
    }
}

fn shown(value: Option<&Value>) -> String {
    match value {
        Some(value) => dumps(value, Style::PY_DEFAULT),
        None => "(absent)".to_string(),
    }
}

/// A JSON pointer ("/a~1b/0"), or "(root)" for the whole document.
fn pointer_text(pointer: &[String]) -> String {
    if pointer.is_empty() {
        return "(root)".to_string();
    }
    pointer.iter().map(|part| format!("/{}", part.replace('~', "~0").replace('/', "~1"))).collect()
}

/// Whether `pattern` ("/tracks/*/key") names `pointer`: as many parts, each equal or "*".
fn pointer_matches(pattern: &str, pointer: &[String]) -> bool {
    let parts: Vec<String> = pattern.split('/').skip(1).map(|part| part.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~")).collect();
    parts.len() == pointer.len() && parts.iter().zip(pointer).all(|(part, name)| part == "*" || part == name)
}
```

```rust

use evidence::Ctx;
use lazymkv_core::recording::py_repr_str;
use std::io::Write;

/// Every command, in every cmd/<name>.rs: `pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut
/// dyn Write) -> i32`. `args` excludes the command name; the return value is the exit code of spec 3.4; stdout lines
/// go to `out`, error lines to `err`.
pub type Command = fn(&Ctx, &[String], &mut dyn Write, &mut dyn Write) -> i32;

/// (name as typed, the command, its arguments as spec 3.4 writes them after the name), in spec 3.4's order. Each of
/// Tasks 2 to 14 adds its row, for example `("scan", cmd::scan::run as Command, "<slug|dir> [--title N] [--label L]")`.
pub const COMMANDS: &[(&str, Command, &str)] = &[];

const USAGE: &str = "usage: lazymkv-dev <command> [arguments]";

/// `argv[0]` picks the command (`argv` excludes the program name); `--help` or `-h` prints the table to `out` and
/// returns 0; no argument prints it to `err` and returns 2; an unknown name prints "lazymkv-dev: unknown command
/// '<name>'" and the table to `err` and returns 2.
pub fn dispatch(ctx: &Ctx, argv: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    let Some(name) = argv.first() else {
        help(err);
        return 2;
    };
    if name == "--help" || name == "-h" {
        help(out);
        return 0;
    }
    match COMMANDS.iter().find(|(command, _, _)| *command == name.as_str()) {
        Some((_, run, _)) => run(ctx, &argv[1..], out, err),
        None => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev: unknown command {}", py_repr_str(name));
            help(err);
            2
        }
    }
}

/// The usage line, a blank line, "commands:" and one "  <name> <arguments>" line per command.
fn help(w: &mut dyn Write) {
    let _ = writeln!(w, "{}", USAGE);
    let _ = writeln!(w);
    let _ = writeln!(w, "commands:");
    if COMMANDS.is_empty() {
        let _ = writeln!(w, "  (none yet)");
    }
    for (name, _, synopsis) in COMMANDS {
        let _ = writeln!(w, "  {} {}", name, synopsis);
    }
}

/// Hand-written argument parsing with argparse's spellings: `--name VALUE`, `--name=VALUE`, a unique prefix of a
/// declared long flag (argparse's allow_abbrev), repeatable flags, switches, positionals, and `--` before words that
/// would look like flags. A command declares its flags, takes each with `flag`, `flags` or `switch`, then the rest
/// with `positionals`. A value may be a negative number ("-5", "-2.5") or "-", as argparse allows.
pub struct Args {
    words: Vec<String>,
    declared: Vec<String>,
}

/// What one word is to the parser.
enum Resolved {
    /// A positional word (or a flag-like word no declared flag matches).
    Word,
    /// A declared flag (its full name) and the value written after '=', if any.
    Flag(String, Option<String>),
    /// A prefix of several declared flags (the word as written and the flags it matches).
    Ambiguous(String, Vec<String>),
}

impl Args {
    /// The words after the command name; `flags` declares the long flags the command knows (with "--").
    pub fn new(args: &[String], flags: &[&str]) -> Args {
        Args { words: args.to_vec(), declared: flags.iter().map(|flag| flag.to_string()).collect() }
    }

    /// The value of a single-use flag (the last one given wins, as argparse's store); Err("argument --name: expected
    /// one argument") when it has none.
    pub fn flag(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, String> {
        Ok(self.take(name)?.pop())
    }

    /// Every value of a repeatable flag (--set), in order.
    pub fn flags(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
        self.take(name)
    }

    /// Whether a switch (--allow-unmeasured) was given.
    pub fn switch(&mut self, name: &str) -> bool {
        let mut found = false;
        let mut at = 0;
        while at < self.words.len() && self.words[at] != "--" {
            match self.resolve(&self.words[at]) {
                Resolved::Flag(flag, None) if flag == name => {
                    self.words.remove(at);
                    found = true;
                }
                _ => at += 1,
            }
        }
        found
    }

    /// The words left, in order; a lone "--" is dropped and every word after it is positional. Err("ambiguous
    /// option: --s could match --set, --snapshot") for an ambiguous prefix, else Err("unrecognized arguments: ...")
    /// for flag-like words no call took.
    pub fn positionals(self) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        let mut unknown = Vec::new();
        let mut after_dashes = false;
        for word in &self.words {
            if after_dashes {
                out.push(word.clone());
            } else if word == "--" {
                after_dashes = true;
            } else if is_value(word) {
                out.push(word.clone());
            } else if let Resolved::Ambiguous(option, matches) = self.resolve(word) {
                return Err(format!("ambiguous option: {} could match {}", option, matches.join(", ")));
            } else {
                unknown.push(word.clone());
            }
        }
        if unknown.is_empty() {
            Ok(out)
        } else {
            Err(format!("unrecognized arguments: {}", unknown.join(" ")))
        }
    }

    /// Removes every occurrence of flag `name` before a "--", with its value, and returns the values in order.
    fn take(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
        let mut values = Vec::new();
        let mut at = 0;
        while at < self.words.len() && self.words[at] != "--" {
            match self.resolve(&self.words[at]) {
                Resolved::Flag(flag, inline) if flag == name => {
                    self.words.remove(at);
                    match inline {
                        Some(value) => values.push(value),
                        None if at < self.words.len() && is_value(&self.words[at]) => values.push(self.words.remove(at)),
                        None => return Err(format!("argument {}: expected one argument", name)),
                    }
                }
                _ => at += 1,
            }
        }
        Ok(values)
    }

    fn resolve(&self, word: &str) -> Resolved {
        if !word.starts_with("--") || word == "--" {
            return Resolved::Word;
        }
        let (option, inline) = match word.split_once('=') {
            Some((option, value)) => (option, Some(value.to_string())),
            None => (word, None),
        };
        if self.declared.iter().any(|flag| flag == option) {
            return Resolved::Flag(option.to_string(), inline);
        }
        let matches: Vec<String> = self.declared.iter().filter(|flag| flag.starts_with(option)).cloned().collect();
        match matches.len() {
            0 => Resolved::Word,
            1 => Resolved::Flag(matches[0].clone(), inline),
            _ => Resolved::Ambiguous(option.to_string(), matches),
        }
    }
}

/// Whether argparse takes `word` as a value: it does not start with '-', is "-" alone, or is a negative number
/// ("-5", "-.5", "-2.5").
fn is_value(word: &str) -> bool {
    if !word.starts_with('-') || word == "-" {
        return true;
    }
    let rest = &word[1..];
    match rest.split_once('.') {
        None => !rest.is_empty() && rest.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()),
        Some((whole, fraction)) => {
            !fraction.is_empty() && whole.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) && fraction.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit())
        }
    }
}

/// Prints "usage: lazymkv-dev <usage>" and "lazymkv-dev <cmd>: error: <message>" to `err`, returns 2 (argparse's
/// exit). `usage` starts with the command name, as argparse's usage line does.
pub fn usage_error(err: &mut dyn Write, cmd: &str, usage: &str, message: &str) -> i32 {
    let _ = writeln!(err, "usage: lazymkv-dev {}", usage);
    let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {}: error: {}", cmd, message);
    2
}
```

```rust
//! The lazymkv-dev binary: the process's arguments, environment and standard streams handed to `dispatch`.

use std::io::Write;

fn main() {
    let argv: Vec<String> = std::env::args_os().skip(1).map(|arg| arg.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).collect();
    let ctx = lazymkv_dev::evidence::Ctx::from_process();
    let mut out = std::io::stdout().lock();
    let mut err = std::io::stderr().lock();
    let code = lazymkv_dev::dispatch(&ctx, &argv, &mut out, &mut err);
    let _ = out.flush();
    let _ = err.flush();
    std::process::exit(code);
}
```

And in `crates/dev` (not a cross-task item): `lazymkv_dev::cmd::scan::run`, of type `Command`, registered in `COMMANDS` (`crates/dev/src/lib.rs`) as `("scan", cmd::scan::run as Command, "<slug|dir> [--title N] [--label L]")`; the third column is the arguments after the name (Task 1's note 8), so `--help` prints `  scan <slug|dir> [--title N] [--label L]`.

**What `scan` does (spec 3.4), and the decisions this task takes:**

- `scan <slug|dir>` prints `summarize_scan.py`'s lines byte for byte: `MakeMKV: <MSG:1005's first parameter, or ?>`, `Java in use: <MSG:3344's first parameter, or no (MSG:3344 absent)>`, `Disc: type=<CINFO 1> name=<CINFO 2> volume=<CINFO 32>` (`None` when absent), `Message codes seen: [<sorted codes>]`, an empty line, the table header and one row per title in numeric order. `scan.txt` is read as the Python read it: UTF-8, `errors="replace"`, and Python's text-mode newline translation (`\r\n` and a lone `\r` become `\n`), which `read_text` does not do, so `cmd/scan.rs` applies it (`text_mode`) before `robot::parse`. No recorded or pinned scan holds a lone `\r` (checked 2026-10-13), so this changes no output; it keeps the port exact.
- `scan <slug|dir> --title N` prints the Step 5 listing of title N (the phase 0 plan, Task 12 Step 5: attributes 3, 6, 22 and 42 of every subtitle stream of the title in scan order, the derived forced-only note, the count, and, when `<recording>/all-tracks/probe-summary.json` exists, the two totals; the heredoc read that `all-tracks` file whatever the title, and so does the port). N is read as Python's `int()` (`py_int`); argparse's "invalid int value" message otherwise. The heredoc's first line named `subtitle_alignment.py`; it now names `lazymkv-dev align` (spec 3.4 rewrites lines that name a script, and after Task 15 no `.py` reference may remain). The heredoc's form without a title (the title from `all-tracks/rip-summary.json`) is not a separate form: Task 15 rewrites Step 5 to pass `--title` with that number.
- `scan <slug|dir> --label L` prints the Step 15 listing: `<slug>/<L>: title <t>, <a> audio streams in the file, <b> in the scan`, then one line per audio stream of `L/ffprobe-streams.json` with the k-th audio stream's scan flags (attribute 22) and their names. The title comes from `L/rip-summary.json` read directly, as the heredoc did (not through `rip_label`, which would also take `extract-summary.json` and require `mkvmerge.json`).
- `--title` and `--label` together: argparse's mutually-exclusive error, exit 2.
- Comments in the Rust name the Python modules without their extension (`summarize_scan`, `robot`), so Task 15's `git grep -n 'python3\|\.py\b'` finds nothing in the files this task adds; the only `python3` call is the one-off comparison of Step 12, which is run, not committed.
- Exit codes: 0; 2 for an argument error or an unreadable input (a missing or undecodable file, a summary without `title`, a flag `int()` refused; the Python crashed with 1 there, a deliberate change spec 3.4 lists); 3 from `resolve_recording` when a slug is given and the evidence clone is absent. On exit 2 for an input, stderr has one line `lazymkv-dev scan: error: <message>` and stdout nothing (the Python had printed the lines before its traceback; the port prints nothing it cannot finish).

The parsed form: `corpus/thediscdb/README.md` describes the folder as real `makemkvcon` robot-mode scan logs "with TheDiscDB's parsed form". Each log `discNN.txt` has `discNN.json` beside it, whose `Titles` list gives every title's `Index` and `Duration` (MakeMKV's attribute 9, `H:MM:SS`); `discNN-summary.txt` is TheDiscDB's prose summary, not a log. The folder holds nine logs; the pinned numbers below (title count, sum of the titles' durations in seconds) are what `robot.parse` and `robot.duration_seconds` gave on 2026-10-13, and every title's attribute 9 equalled the parsed form's `Duration`.

Create `crates/dev/tests/thediscdb_scans.rs`:

```rust
//! The robot-mode parser over the pinned public scan logs of `corpus/thediscdb` (spec section 5: "title count and
//! the duration of every title against their parsed forms"). Each log `discNN.txt` has TheDiscDB's parsed form
//! beside it, `discNN.json`, whose `Titles` list gives every title's `Index` and `Duration` ("H:MM:SS", MakeMKV's
//! attribute 9). The `discNN-summary.txt` files are TheDiscDB's prose summaries, not logs. Needs no evidence clone.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use lazymkv_core::recording::{decode_text, Encoding, Errors};
use lazymkv_core::robot::{duration_seconds, parse};

/// Every pinned log in Python's `Path` order, with its title count and the sum of its titles' durations in
/// seconds, as `robot.parse` and `robot.duration_seconds` gave them on 2026-10-13.
const LOGS: [(&str, usize, u32); 9] = [
    ("movie/John Wick (2014)/4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray/disc01.txt", 10, 15287),
    ("movie/John Wick (2014)/4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray/disc02.txt", 9, 9214),
    ("movie/Knowing (2009)/2010-dvd/disc01.txt", 7, 9454),
    ("movie/Smile (2022)/2022-4k/disc01.txt", 236, 20514),
    ("movie/The Expendables 3 (2014)/the-expendables-3-film-collection/disc01.txt", 64, 77981),
    ("series/Chernobyl (2019)/2020-4k-US/disc01.txt", 33, 24875),
    ("series/Chernobyl (2019)/2020-4k-US/disc02.txt", 31, 18509),
    ("series/Firefly (2002)/2003-dvd-the-complete-series/disc01.txt", 5, 10385),
    ("series/Firefly (2002)/2003-dvd-the-complete-series/disc02.txt", 6, 10465),
];

fn corpus() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus/thediscdb")
}

/// Every `*.txt` below `dir` that is not a `-summary.txt`, as its path components below the corpus.
fn scan_logs(dir: &Path, prefix: &[String], found: &mut Vec<Vec<String>>) {
    for entry in fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap() {
        let entry = entry.unwrap();
        let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let mut components = prefix.to_vec();
        components.push(name.clone());
        if entry.path().is_dir() {
            scan_logs(&entry.path(), &components, found);
        } else if name.ends_with(".txt") && !name.ends_with("-summary.txt") {
            found.push(components);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_nine_pinned_logs_are_here() {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    scan_logs(&corpus(), &[], &mut found);
    // Component by component, each name by code point: the order Python gives Path objects.
    found.sort();
    let found: Vec<String> = found.iter().map(|components| components.join("/")).collect();
    let pinned: Vec<&str> = LOGS.iter().map(|(path, _, _)| *path).collect();
    assert_eq!(found, pinned);
}

#[test]
fn every_log_gives_its_parsed_forms_titles_and_durations() {
    for (log, titles_pinned, seconds_pinned) in LOGS {
        let path = corpus().join(log);
        let text = decode_text(&fs::read(&path).unwrap(), Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace).unwrap();
        let scan = parse(&text);
        assert!(scan.skipped.is_empty(), "{log}: skipped {:?}", scan.skipped);
        let parsed: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(path.with_extension("json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let titles = parsed["Titles"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(scan.titles.len(), titles.len(), "{log}: title count against the parsed form");
        assert_eq!(scan.titles.len(), titles_pinned, "{log}: pinned title count");
        let mut seconds = 0;
        for title in titles {
            let index = u32::try_from(title["Index"].as_u64().unwrap()).unwrap();
            let duration = title["Duration"].as_str().unwrap();
            let attrs = scan
                .titles
                .get(&index)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{log}: title {index} of the parsed form is not in the scan"));
            assert_eq!(attrs.get(&9).map(String::as_str), Some(duration), "{log}: title {index}");
            let expected = duration_seconds(duration)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{log}: title {index}: {duration} is not H:MM:SS"));
            assert_eq!(duration_seconds(&attrs[&9]), Some(expected), "{log}: title {index}");
            seconds += expected;
        }
        assert_eq!(seconds, seconds_pinned, "{log}: pinned sum of the title durations");
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Write `core::robot`**

Replace the contents of `crates/core/src/robot.rs` with the code below, followed by the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` block of Step 3, unchanged. The translation keeps `robot.py`'s loop and its evaluation order: each line is `text.split("\n")` with trailing `\r`s stripped (`strip_cr_lines`) and leading U+FEFF removed (`lstrip`); `partition(":")` is `split_once(':')`; in `d[k] = v` Python evaluates `v` first, then `d` (so `setdefault` has created the title or stream before the attribute number is converted), then `k`. Numbers are read with `py_int` (Python's `int()` on a `str`); a number that is not a `u32` (negative or too large) skips the line, as `02-interfaces.md` binds (no recorded or pinned scan has one).

```rust
//! The parser for makemkvcon's robot-mode output (spec 9.4), the port of phase 0's Python module `robot`:
//! `split_fields`, `parse` and `duration_seconds`, with the flag read every caller of the Python repeated
//! (`int_attr`) and the `scan.json` golden form (`scan_json`). No I/O: callers hand in the decoded text.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use crate::recording::{py_int, py_repr_str, strip_cr_lines, Ordered};

/// A title's or stream's attributes: attribute number -> value (the last line wins). Py: the inner dicts of Scan.
pub type Attrs = BTreeMap<u32, String>;

/// One MSG line: (code, text, params) = (int(f[0]), f[3], f[5:]).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Message {
    pub code: u32,
    pub text: String,
    pub params: Vec<String>,
}

/// One DRV line's fields. Never written to a golden (it can carry a drive serial).
pub type Drive = Vec<String>;

/// A parsed robot-mode log. Sparse title numbering kept. Py: robot.Scan.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Scan {
    pub messages: Vec<Message>,
    pub drives: Vec<Drive>,
    /// CINFO: attribute -> value.
    pub disc: BTreeMap<u32, String>,
    /// TINFO: title -> attributes.
    pub titles: BTreeMap<u32, Attrs>,
    /// SINFO: (title, stream) -> attributes.
    pub streams: BTreeMap<(u32, u32), Attrs>,
    /// Lines the parser skipped and why ("field <i> is missing", "field <i> is not a number: '<text>'"); a line
    /// without ':' is not recorded. For diagnostics only: never printed by a report, never written.
    pub skipped: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

/// The fields after "KIND:": quoted fields keep commas, a backslash takes the next character, "" is a quote.
/// Py: robot.split_fields (indexing by character, as Python indexes a str).
pub fn split_fields(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let n = chars.len();
    let mut fields = Vec::new();
    let mut current = String::new();
    let mut quoted = false;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < n {
        let c = chars[i];
        if quoted {
            if c == '\\' && i + 1 < n {
                current.push(chars[i + 1]);
                i += 2;
                continue;
            }
            if c == '"' {
                if i + 1 < n && chars[i + 1] == '"' {
                    current.push('"');
                    i += 2;
                    continue;
                }
                quoted = false;
            } else {
                current.push(c);
            }
        } else if c == '"' {
            quoted = true;
        } else if c == ',' {
            fields.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
        } else {
            current.push(c);
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    fields.push(current);
    fields
}

/// Parses a robot-mode log, never failing. Py: robot.parse.
pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Scan {
    let mut scan = Scan::default();
    for raw in strip_cr_lines(text) {
        let line = raw.trim_start_matches('\u{feff}');
        let Some((kind, rest)) = line.split_once(':') else {
            continue;
        };
        let fields = split_fields(rest);
        let outcome = match kind {
            "MSG" => message(&mut scan, &fields),
            "DRV" => {
                scan.drives.push(fields);
                Ok(())
            }
            "CINFO" => disc_attribute(&mut scan, &fields),
            "TINFO" => title_attribute(&mut scan, &fields),
            "SINFO" => stream_attribute(&mut scan, &fields),
            _ => Ok(()),
        };
        if let Err(reason) = outcome {
            scan.skipped.push((line.to_string(), reason));
        }
    }
    scan
}

/// `f[i]`, or why the Python's f[i] raised IndexError.
fn field(fields: &[String], i: usize) -> Result<&str, String> {
    fields.get(i).map(String::as_str).ok_or_else(|| format!("field {i} is missing"))
}

/// `int(f[i])` as a u32, or why not (ValueError in the Python; a negative or too large number here too).
fn number(fields: &[String], i: usize) -> Result<u32, String> {
    let text = field(fields, i)?;
    py_int(text)
        .and_then(|n| u32::try_from(n).ok())
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("field {i} is not a number: {}", py_repr_str(text)))
}

/// `scan.messages.append((int(f[0]), f[3], f[5:]))`: the tuple is built left to right.
fn message(scan: &mut Scan, fields: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let code = number(fields, 0)?;
    let text = field(fields, 3)?.to_string();
    let params = fields.get(5..).unwrap_or_default().to_vec();
    scan.messages.push(Message { code, text, params });
    Ok(())
}

/// `scan.disc[int(f[0])] = f[2]`: the value is evaluated first.
fn disc_attribute(scan: &mut Scan, fields: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let value = field(fields, 2)?.to_string();
    let attribute = number(fields, 0)?;
    scan.disc.insert(attribute, value);
    Ok(())
}

/// `scan.titles.setdefault(int(f[0]), {})[int(f[1])] = f[3]`: the value, then the title (created here and kept
/// when the attribute number then fails, as setdefault kept it), then the attribute.
fn title_attribute(scan: &mut Scan, fields: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let value = field(fields, 3)?.to_string();
    let title = number(fields, 0)?;
    let attrs = scan.titles.entry(title).or_default();
    let attribute = number(fields, 1)?;
    attrs.insert(attribute, value);
    Ok(())
}

/// `scan.streams.setdefault((int(f[0]), int(f[1])), {})[int(f[2])] = f[4]`, in the same order.
fn stream_attribute(scan: &mut Scan, fields: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let value = field(fields, 4)?.to_string();
    let key = (number(fields, 0)?, number(fields, 1)?);
    let attrs = scan.streams.entry(key).or_default();
    let attribute = number(fields, 2)?;
    attrs.insert(attribute, value);
    Ok(())
}

/// "H:MM:SS" to seconds; None where the Python raised ValueError (not three parts, a part not an int) and for a
/// negative total (which the Python returned; no recorded or pinned scan has one). Py: robot.duration_seconds.
pub fn duration_seconds(text: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = text.split(':').collect();
    let [hours, minutes, seconds] = parts.as_slice() else {
        return None;
    };
    let total = py_int(hours)?
        .checked_mul(3600)?
        .checked_add(py_int(minutes)?.checked_mul(60)?)?
        .checked_add(py_int(seconds)?)?;
    u32::try_from(total).ok()
}

/// `int(a.get(id, "0") or 0)`: 0 for an absent or empty attribute; Err with Python's ValueError text (its repr of
/// the text cut at 200 characters, as `%.200R`) where int() raised.
pub fn int_attr(a: &Attrs, id: u32) -> Result<i64, String> {
    match a.get(&id).map(String::as_str) {
        None | Some("") => Ok(0),
        Some(text) => py_int(text).ok_or_else(|| {
            let shown: String = py_repr_str(text).chars().take(200).collect();
            format!("invalid literal for int() with base 10: {shown}")
        }),
    }
}

/// scan.json's content (section 5): titles, streams and disc with decimal-string keys in numeric order (a stream's
/// key is "<title>,<stream>"), and duration_seconds of every title's attribute 9 (null when absent or unreadable).
/// No drives, no messages.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ScanJson {
    pub titles: Ordered<Ordered<String>>,
    pub streams: Ordered<Ordered<String>>,
    pub disc: Ordered<String>,
    pub duration_seconds: Ordered<Option<u32>>,
}

/// Builds ScanJson from a Scan.
pub fn scan_json(scan: &Scan) -> ScanJson {
    let mut titles = Ordered::new();
    let mut durations = Ordered::new();
    for (title, attrs) in &scan.titles {
        titles.insert(title.to_string(), attrs_json(attrs));
        durations.insert(title.to_string(), attrs.get(&9).and_then(|text| duration_seconds(text)));
    }
    let mut streams = Ordered::new();
    for ((title, stream), attrs) in &scan.streams {
        streams.insert(format!("{title},{stream}"), attrs_json(attrs));
    }
    ScanJson { titles, streams, disc: attrs_json(&scan.disc), duration_seconds: durations }
}

/// Attribute numbers as decimal strings, in numeric order.
fn attrs_json(attrs: &BTreeMap<u32, String>) -> Ordered<String> {
    let mut out = Ordered::new();
    for (attribute, value) in attrs {
        out.insert(attribute.to_string(), value.clone());
    }
    out
}
```

```rust
fn repo_root() -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..")
}

/// The built lazymkv-dev, run from the repository root: (exit code, stdout, stderr).
fn lazymkv_dev(args: &[&str]) -> (Option<i32>, String, String) {
    let output = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_lazymkv-dev"))
        .args(args)
        .current_dir(repo_root())
        .env_remove("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE")
        .output()
        .unwrap();
    (output.status.code(), String::from_utf8(output.stdout).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(output.stderr).unwrap())
}

#[test]

    assert_eq!(out, DISC_A_SUMMARY);
}

#[test]
fn every_recorded_scan_parses_with_a_byte_order_mark_and_crlf() {
    let root = match std::env::var("LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE") {
        Ok(dir) if !dir.is_empty() => PathBuf::from(dir),
        _ => repo_root().join("corpus/owner"),
    };
    if !root.is_dir() {
        skip(&format!("no evidence clone at {}", root.display()));
        return;
    }
    let mut logs = Vec::new();
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&root).unwrap() {
        let dir = entry.unwrap().path();
        let log = dir.join("scan.txt");
        if dir.file_name().is_some_and(|name| name != "golden") && log.is_file() {
            logs.push(log);
        }
    }
    logs.sort();
    if logs.is_empty() {
        skip(&format!("no recording with a scan.txt under {}", root.display()));
        return;
    }
    let mut with_crlf = 0;
    for log in &logs {
        let mut bytes = b"\xef\xbb\xbf".to_vec();
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&std::fs::read(log).unwrap());
        let text = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace).unwrap();
        if text.contains("\r\n") {
            with_crlf += 1;
        }
        let scan = parse(&text);
        // Never print the scan itself: its DRV lines can carry a drive serial.
        assert!(scan.skipped.is_empty(), "{}: {} lines skipped", log.display(), scan.skipped.len());
        let lines = |kind: &str| text.split('\n').filter(|l| l.trim_start_matches('\u{feff}').starts_with(kind)).count();
        assert_eq!(scan.messages.len(), lines("MSG:"), "{}: MSG lines", log.display());
        assert_eq!(scan.drives.len(), lines("DRV:"), "{}: DRV lines", log.display());
        let unix = text.trim_start_matches('\u{feff}').replace("\r\n", "\n");
        assert!(scan == parse(&unix), "{}: a CRLF line parsed differently from its LF form", log.display());
    }
    if with_crlf == 0 {
        skip("no recorded scan.txt has CRLF line ends; the byte-order mark alone was checked");
    }
}
```

```rust
    );

    /// Lines as print() writes them.
    fn text(lines: Vec<String>) -> String {
        lines.iter().map(|line| format!("{line}\n")).collect()
    }

    /// A folder under the system's temporary directory, removed when dropped.
    struct TempDir(PathBuf);

    impl TempDir {
        fn new(name: &str) -> TempDir {
            let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lazymkv-dev-scan-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&path);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).unwrap();
            TempDir(path)
        }

        fn write(&self, rel: &str, bytes: &[u8]) {
            let path = self.0.join(rel);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(path, bytes).unwrap();
        }
    }

    impl Drop for TempDir {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
        }
    }

    /// The fixture recordings on disk, as the mini PC writes them.
    fn fixture(name: &str) -> TempDir {
        let tmp = TempDir::new(name);
        let mut scan = b"\xef\xbb\xbf".to_vec();
        scan.extend_from_slice(SCAN.replace('\n', "\r\n").as_bytes());
        tmp.write("test-disc-2000-bluray/scan.txt", &scan);
        tmp.write(
            "test-disc-2000-bluray/all-tracks/probe-summary.json",
            "\u{feff}{\"ok\": true, \"result\": \"ok\", \"subtitle_tracks\": 4}\r\n".as_bytes(),
        );
        tmp.write(
            "test-disc-2000-bluray/all-tracks/rip-summary.json",
            "\u{feff}{\"ok\": true, \"result\": \"ok\", \"title\": 0}\r\n".as_bytes(),
        );
        tmp.write("test-disc-2000-bluray/all-tracks/ffprobe-streams.json", FFPROBE.as_bytes());
        tmp.write("test-disc-2000-bluray/eng-only/notes.txt", b"no summary here\n");
        tmp.write("bare-disc/scan.txt", BARE_SCAN.as_bytes());
        tmp
    }

    /// `run` with `dir` as the current directory: (exit code, stdout, stderr).
    fn run_in(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> (i32, String, String) {
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(dir);
        let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect();
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = run(&ctx, &args, &mut out, &mut err);
        (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
    }

    #[test]
    fn summary_lines_match_summarize_scan() {
        let scan = parse(&SCAN.replace('\n', "\r\n"));
        assert_eq!(text(summary_lines(&scan)), SUMMARY);
    }

    #[test]
    fn summary_lines_of_a_scan_without_disc_facts() {
        assert_eq!(text(summary_lines(&parse(BARE_SCAN))), BARE_SUMMARY);
    }

    #[test]
    fn subtitle_lines_match_the_step_5_listing() {
        let lines = subtitle_lines("test-disc-2000-bluray", 0, &parse(SCAN), Some(Some(4))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(text(lines), TITLE_0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn subtitle_lines_of_another_title_and_without_a_probe_summary() {
        let lines = subtitle_lines("test-disc-2000-bluray", 2, &parse(SCAN), Some(Some(4))).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(text(lines), TITLE_2);
        let lines = subtitle_lines("bare-disc", 0, &parse(BARE_SCAN), None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(text(lines), BARE_TITLE_0);

    #[test]
    fn run_prints_the_summary_from_disk() {

    #[test]
    fn run_prints_both_listings_from_disk() {

        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));

    #[test]
    fn run_refuses_without_the_evidence_clone() {

        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (3, ""));

        let (code, _, err) = run_in(&tmp.0, &[]);

        let (code, _, err) = run_in(&tmp.0, &["test-disc-2000-bluray", "bare-disc"]);
        assert_eq!(code, 2);

    #[test]
    fn run_exits_2_on_a_flag_python_could_not_read() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("bad-flag");
        tmp.write("bad-flags/scan.txt", b"SINFO:0,1,1,6203,\"Subtitles\"\nSINFO:0,1,22,0,\"x\"\n");
        let (code, out, err) = run_in(&tmp.0, &["bad-flags", "--title", "0"]);
        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (2, ""));

    }

    #[test]
    fn scan_is_in_the_command_table() {
        assert!(crate::COMMANDS.iter().any(|(name, _, _)| *name == "scan"));
    }
}
```

Replace the contents of `crates/dev/src/cmd/scan.rs` with the code below, followed by the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` block of Step 9, unchanged. Each listing keeps its Python's loop: titles in numeric order and, per title, every stream counted (`summarize_scan.py`); streams in `sorted(scan.streams.items())` order, which is the `BTreeMap<(u32, u32), _>` order (Steps 5 and 15). Python's f-string padding (`{x:>3}`, `{x:<14}`) pads by characters, as Rust's `{:>3}` and `{:<14}` do; `None` prints as `None`; `{x!r}` is `py_repr_str`; `a.get(26, '')[:60]` is the first 60 characters.

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev scan <slug|dir> [--title N | --label L]` (spec 3.4): what a recorded scan says about a disc, line
//! for line as the Python `summarize_scan` printed it; with `--title N`, the subtitle streams of title N as the scan lists
//! them (the phase 0 plan's Task 12 Step 5 listing); with `--label L`, the audio streams of rip L's file against
//! the scan's flags (Task 12 Step 15). Exit 0; 2 for an argument error or an unreadable input (the Python crashed
//! with 1); 3 when a slug is given and the evidence clone is absent.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::io::Write;

use lazymkv_core::recording::files::{FfprobeStream, FfprobeStreams, ProbeSummary, Summary};
use lazymkv_core::recording::{py_int, py_repr_str, read_json, read_text, Encoding, Errors, Tree};
use lazymkv_core::robot::{int_attr, parse, Attrs, Scan};

use crate::evidence::{resolve_recording, Ctx, Recording};
use crate::{usage_error, Args};

/// The usage line, after "usage: lazymkv-dev ".
pub const USAGE: &str = "scan [--evidence DIR] [--title N | --label L] <slug|dir>";
/// summarize_scan's Java line when no MSG:3344 names a runtime.
pub const JAVA_ABSENT: &str = "no (MSG:3344 absent)";
/// summarize_scan's table header, as its f-string padded it.
pub const TABLE_HEADER: &str =
    "  # source          duration chap         bytes segs aud sub  comment / segment map";
/// The Step 5 listing's first line after "<slug> title <n>". The Python named the alignment script, whose
/// command is now `lazymkv-dev align` (spec 3.4 rewrites lines that name a script).
pub const SUBTITLE_HEADER: &str = ": subtitle streams in scan order; s<k> in lazymkv-dev align is line s<k>";
/// Appended to the line of a derived forced-only stream (flags 4096 and 2048 together, spec 8.7).
pub const DERIVED_FORCED_NOTE: &str = "  derived forced-only: set aside, not counted";
/// The Step 5 count line, before its number.
pub const COUNTED_LINE: &str =
    "English or no-language subtitle streams, derived forced-only streams not counted:";
/// The Step 15 names of the scan's audio flags (attribute 22), in the Python's order.
pub const AUDIO_FLAG_NAMES: [(i64, &str); 5] = [
    (1, "director-comments"),
    (2, "alt-director-comments"),
    (4, "visually-impaired"),
    (512, "secondary"),
    (2048, "derived"),
];

/// The command, registered in COMMANDS as "scan".
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    let mut parsed = Args::new(args, &["--evidence", "--title", "--label"]);
    let evidence = match parsed.flag("--evidence") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, "scan", USAGE, &message),
    };
    let title = match parsed.flag("--title") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, "scan", USAGE, &message),
    };
    let label = match parsed.flag("--label") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, "scan", USAGE, &message),
    };
    let words = match parsed.positionals() {
        Ok(words) => words,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, "scan", USAGE, &message),
    };
    let recording = match words.as_slice() {
        [] => return usage_error(err, "scan", USAGE, "the following arguments are required: recording"),
        [one] => one.clone(),
        [_, rest @ ..] => {
            return usage_error(err, "scan", USAGE, &format!("unrecognized arguments: {}", rest.join(" ")))
        }
    };
    if title.is_some() && label.is_some() {
        return usage_error(err, "scan", USAGE, "argument --label: not allowed with argument --title");
    }
    let title = match title {
        None => None,
        Some(text) => match py_int(&text) {
            Some(number) => Some(number),
            None => {
                let message = format!("argument --title: invalid int value: {}", py_repr_str(&text));
                return usage_error(err, "scan", USAGE, &message);
            }
        },
    };
    let rec = match resolve_recording(ctx, evidence.as_deref(), &recording) {
        Ok(rec) => rec,
        Err(refused) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "{}", refused.line);
            return refused.code;
        }
    };
    let lines = match (title, label) {
        (Some(title), _) => title_listing(&rec, title),
        (None, Some(label)) => label_listing(&rec, &label),
        (None, None) => summary(&rec),
    };
    match lines {
        Ok(lines) => {
            for line in lines {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "{line}");
            }
            0
        }
        Err(message) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev scan: error: {message}");
            2
        }
    }
}

/// summarize_scan's lines for a parsed scan.
pub fn summary_lines(scan: &Scan) -> Vec<String> {
    let version = first_param(scan, 1005).unwrap_or("?");
    let java = match first_param(scan, 3344) {
        Some(java) if !java.is_empty() => java,
        _ => JAVA_ABSENT,
    };
    let codes: BTreeSet<u32> = scan.messages.iter().map(|m| m.code).collect();
    let codes: Vec<String> = codes.iter().map(|code| code.to_string()).collect();
    let mut lines = vec![
        format!("MakeMKV: {version}"),
        format!("Java in use: {java}"),
        format!(
            "Disc: type={} name={} volume={}",
            or_none(scan.disc.get(&1)),
            or_none(scan.disc.get(&2)),
            or_none(scan.disc.get(&32))
        ),
        format!("Message codes seen: [{}]", codes.join(", ")),
        String::new(),
        TABLE_HEADER.to_string(),
    ];
    for (title, a) in &scan.titles {
        let (mut audio, mut subtitles) = (0usize, 0usize);
        for ((t, _), stream) in &scan.streams {
            if t != title {
                continue;
            }
            match stream.get(&1).map(String::as_str) {
                Some("Audio") => audio += 1,
                Some("Subtitles") => subtitles += 1,
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        let segment_map: String = attr(a, 26, "").chars().take(60).collect();
        lines.push(format!(
            "{:>3} {:<14} {:>9} {:>4} {:>13} {:>4} {:>3} {:>3}  {} [{}]",
            title,
            attr(a, 16, ""),
            attr(a, 9, ""),
            attr(a, 8, "0"),
            attr(a, 11, ""),
            attr(a, 25, ""),
            audio,
            subtitles,
            attr(a, 49, ""),
            segment_map
        ));
    }
    lines
}

/// The Step 5 listing of `title`; `probe` is None when all-tracks/probe-summary.json does not exist, else its
/// "subtitle_tracks" (None when the key is absent). Err with Python's int() text when a flag is not a number.
pub fn subtitle_lines(slug: &str, title: i64, scan: &Scan, probe: Option<Option<i64>>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let mut lines = vec![format!("{slug} title {title}{SUBTITLE_HEADER}")];
    let (mut k, mut counted) = (0usize, 0usize);
    for ((t, s), a) in &scan.streams {
        if i64::from(*t) != title || a.get(&1).map(String::as_str) != Some("Subtitles") {
            continue;
        }
        let flags = int_attr(a, 22)?;
        let lang = match a.get(&3) {
            Some(lang) if !lang.is_empty() => lang.as_str(),
            _ => "und",
        };
        let derived_forced = (flags & 4096) != 0 && (flags & 2048) != 0;
        if (lang == "eng" || lang == "und") && !derived_forced {
            counted += 1;
        }
        let note = if derived_forced { DERIVED_FORCED_NOTE } else { "" };
        lines.push(format!(
            "s{:<3} stream {:>2}  lang={:<4} codec={:<10} flags={:<5} conversion={}{}",
            k,
            s,
            lang,
            attr(a, 6, ""),
            flags,
            attr(a, 42, ""),
            note
        ));
        k += 1;
    }
    lines.push(format!("{COUNTED_LINE} {counted}"));
    if let Some(in_file) = probe {
        lines.push(format!(
            "subtitle streams in the scan: {k}; subtitle tracks in the ripped file (probe-summary.json): {}",
            or_none(in_file)
        ));
    }
    Ok(lines)
}

/// The Step 15 listing: the audio streams of `probe` (the label's ffprobe-streams.json), the k-th against the scan's
/// k-th audio stream of `title`. Err with Python's int() text when a flag is not a number.
pub fn audio_lines(slug: &str, label: &str, title: i64, scan: &Scan, probe: &FfprobeStreams) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let mut flags = Vec::new();
    for ((t, _), a) in &scan.streams {
        if i64::from(*t) == title && a.get(&1).map(String::as_str) == Some("Audio") {
            flags.push(int_attr(a, 22)?);
        }
    }
    let audio: Vec<&FfprobeStream> =
        probe.streams.iter().filter(|s| s.codec_type.as_deref() == Some("audio")).collect();
    let mut lines = vec![format!(
        "{slug}/{label}: title {title}, {} audio streams in the file, {} in the scan",
        audio.len(),
        flags.len()
    )];
    for (k, s) in audio.iter().enumerate() {
        let f = flags.get(k).copied();
        let marks: Vec<&str> = match f {
            Some(f) => AUDIO_FLAG_NAMES.iter().filter(|(bit, _)| (f & *bit) != 0).map(|(_, name)| *name).collect(),
            None => Vec::new(),
        };
        let track_title = match tag(s, "title") {
            Some(title) => py_repr_str(title),
            None => "None".to_string(),
        };
        lines.push(format!(
            "  stream {}: {} profile={} {} ch {} lang={} title={} scan_flags={} {}",
            s.index,
            or_none(s.codec_name.as_deref()),
            or_none(s.profile.as_deref()),
            or_none(s.channels),
            or_none(s.channel_layout.as_deref()),
            tag(s, "language").map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("und"),
            track_title,
            or_none(f),
            marks.join(" ")
        ));
    }
    Ok(lines)
}

/// The first parameter of the first `code` message that has one.
/// Py: next((p[0] for code, _, p in scan.messages if code == c and p), default).
fn first_param(scan: &Scan, code: u32) -> Option<&str> {
    scan.messages.iter().find(|m| m.code == code && !m.params.is_empty()).map(|m| m.params[0].as_str())
}

/// `a.get(id, default)` of a title's or stream's attributes.
fn attr<'a>(a: &'a Attrs, id: u32, default: &'a str) -> &'a str {
    a.get(&id).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or(default)
}

/// `s.get("tags", {}).get(key)` of an ffprobe stream.
fn tag<'a>(stream: &'a FfprobeStream, key: &str) -> Option<&'a String> {
    stream.tags.as_ref().and_then(|tags| tags.get(key))
}

/// An f-string of a value that may be None: the value, or "None".
fn or_none<T: std::fmt::Display>(value: Option<T>) -> String {
    value.map_or_else(|| "None".to_string(), |value| value.to_string())
}

/// Python's text-mode read (universal newlines): "\r\n" and a lone "\r" become "\n", as Path.read_text gave them.
fn text_mode(text: &str) -> String {
    text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace('\r', "\n")
}

/// The recording's scan.txt, decoded with errors="replace" in `encoding` (summarize_scan: utf-8; the heredocs:
/// utf-8-sig), newlines as text mode gives them, parsed.
fn read_scan(rec: &Recording, encoding: Encoding) -> Result<Scan, String> {
    let text = read_text(&rec.tree, &rec.dir.join("scan.txt"), encoding, Errors::Replace)?;
    Ok(parse(&text_mode(&text)))
}

/// summarize_scan's main.
fn summary(rec: &Recording) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    Ok(summary_lines(&read_scan(rec, Encoding::Utf8)?))
}

/// The Step 5 heredoc with a title argument: the scan, then all-tracks/probe-summary.json when it exists.
fn title_listing(rec: &Recording, title: i64) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let scan = read_scan(rec, Encoding::Utf8Sig)?;
    let probe_path = rec.dir.join("all-tracks").join("probe-summary.json");
    let probe = if rec.tree.exists(&probe_path) {
        Some(read_json::<ProbeSummary>(&rec.tree, &probe_path)?.subtitle_tracks)
    } else {
        None
    };
    subtitle_lines(&rec.slug, title, &scan, probe)
}

/// The Step 15 heredoc: <label>/rip-summary.json, <label>/ffprobe-streams.json, scan.txt, in the Python's order.
fn label_listing(rec: &Recording, label: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let folder = rec.dir.join(label);
    let summary_path = folder.join("rip-summary.json");
    let rip: Summary = read_json(&rec.tree, &summary_path)?;
    let probe: FfprobeStreams = read_json(&rec.tree, &folder.join("ffprobe-streams.json"))?;
    let scan = read_scan(rec, Encoding::Utf8Sig)?;
    let title = rip
        .title
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("{}: the summary names no title", rec.tree.display(&summary_path)))?;
    audio_lines(&rec.slug, label, title, &scan, &probe)
}
```

Behaviour fixed by this task (spec 3.3, 3.4, RP6): exactly the Python of commit `75fa76a`'s tree (`scripts/phase0` is unchanged since). Five verdicts `count`, `order`, `video`, `chapters`, `duration`; the symmetric `DURATION_TOLERANCE_S = 2` for every format; no closed-caption exception (a caption stream is compared position by position like any other); codecs are not compared; exit 1 when any verdict is no. Where the Python crashed with a traceback (exit 1), the Rust prints one error line to stderr, nothing to stdout, and exits 2 (deliberate, spec 3.4): a file missing or unreadable, `mkvmerge.json` not JSON, a title the scan does not list (also a negative title), attribute 22 or 8 not an int, attribute 9 not `H:MM:SS`, a kept stream without attribute 1 (the table's `:<9` raised on `None`), a track language that is not a string. Paths print as Python 3.9's `PurePosixPath` prints them.

```rust
//! The scan-against-file reconciler of phase 0: `scripts/phase0/compare_tracks.py` (commit 75fa76a's tree) ported
//! line for line (port spec 3.3; RP6: the Python's rule, not the design spec's 6.2 step 7). Five verdicts (count,
//! order, video, chapters, duration), the symmetric 2-second duration band for every format, no closed-caption
//! exception, codecs not compared. No I/O: `lazymkv-dev reconcile` reads the files and prints the lines.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;

use crate::lang::norm_lang;
use crate::recording::files::{MkvmergeIdent, Selection};
use crate::recording::{py_isdigit, py_int, py_repr, py_repr_str, py_str};
use crate::robot::{duration_seconds, int_attr, parse, Attrs, Scan};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    /// One title: video, then two audio tracks of the same language with 8 and 2 channels. Py: TRACK_SCAN.
    const TRACK_SCAN: &str = r#"TINFO:0,8,0,"2"
TINFO:0,9,0,"0:10:00"
SINFO:0,0,1,6201,"Video"
SINFO:0,0,6,0,"MpegH"
SINFO:0,1,1,6202,"Audio"
SINFO:0,1,3,0,"{lang}"
SINFO:0,1,6,0,"TrueHD"
SINFO:0,1,14,0,"8"
SINFO:0,2,1,6202,"Audio"
SINFO:0,2,3,0,"{lang}"
SINFO:0,2,6,0,"DD"
SINFO:0,2,14,0,"2"
"#;

    /// Two MSG:4047 lines: an empty forced-only subtitle track MakeMKV removed (output track 2), then an audio gap,
    /// which is not a removal. Py: the rip of test_a_stream_makemkv_removed_as_empty_is_read_from_the_rip_log.
    const RIP_4047_PAIR: &str = r#"MSG:4047,16,3,"AV sync issue in stream 2 at 0:00:00 : {removed}","AV sync issue in stream %1 at %2 : %3","2","0:00:00","{removed}"
MSG:4047,16,3,"AV sync issue in stream 1 at 0:01:00 : audio gap","AV sync issue in stream %1 at %2 : %3","1","0:01:00","audio gap"
"#;

    /// Title 3 of a synthetic DVD-like scan: video, a 3D video stream (MVC), English audio, a derived English audio
    /// stream (flag 256), an audio stream without a language and with flag 4, Spanish audio, French and English
    /// subtitles. New in the port.
    const SCAN_B: &str = r#"TINFO:3,8,0,"12"
TINFO:3,9,0,"1:30:05"
SINFO:3,0,1,6201,"Video"
SINFO:3,0,6,0,"Mpeg2"
SINFO:3,0,41,0,"V_MPEG2"
SINFO:3,1,1,6201,"Video"
SINFO:3,1,6,0,"Mpeg4 MVC"
SINFO:3,2,1,6202,"Audio"
SINFO:3,2,3,0,"eng"
SINFO:3,2,6,0,"DD"
SINFO:3,2,14,0,"6"
SINFO:3,2,41,0,"A_AC3"
SINFO:3,3,1,6202,"Audio"
SINFO:3,3,3,0,"eng"
SINFO:3,3,6,0,"DD"
SINFO:3,3,14,0,"2"
SINFO:3,3,22,0,"256"
SINFO:3,4,1,6202,"Audio"
SINFO:3,4,6,0,"DD"
SINFO:3,4,14,0,"2"
SINFO:3,4,22,0,"4"
SINFO:3,5,1,6202,"Audio"
SINFO:3,5,3,0,"spa"
SINFO:3,5,6,0,"DD"
SINFO:3,6,1,6203,"Subtitles"
SINFO:3,6,3,0,"fre"
SINFO:3,6,6,0,"VobSub"
SINFO:3,7,1,6203,"Subtitles"
SINFO:3,7,3,0,"eng"
SINFO:3,7,6,0,"VobSub"
SINFO:3,7,41,0,"S_VOBSUB"
"#;

    fn track_scan(lang: &str) -> Scan {
        parse(&TRACK_SCAN.replace("{lang}", lang))
    }

    /// A stand-in for `mkvmerge -J`: tracks are (type, language, audio channels or None); no chapter entry when
    /// `chapters` is 0. Py: ident(tracks, chapters=2, seconds=600) (callers pass the Python's defaults explicitly).
    fn ident(tracks: &[(&str, &str, Option<i64>)], chapters: i64, seconds: i64) -> MkvmergeIdent {
        let tracks: Vec<serde_json::Value> = tracks
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(i, &(kind, lang, ch))| {
                let mut properties = serde_json::Map::new();
                properties.insert("language".to_string(), json!(lang));
                if let Some(ch) = ch.filter(|&ch| ch != 0) {
                    properties.insert("audio_channels".to_string(), json!(ch));
                }
                json!({"id": i, "type": kind, "codec": "x", "properties": properties})
            })
            .collect();
        let chapters = if chapters != 0 { json!([{"num_entries": chapters}]) } else { json!([]) };
        let duration = seconds * 1_000_000_000;
        serde_json::from_value(json!({
            "tracks": tracks,
            "chapters": chapters,
            "container": {"properties": {"duration": duration}}
        }))
        .unwrap()
    }

    /// The verdicts of TRACK_SCAN in `lang` against a file of `tracks`. Py: CompareTracks.verdicts.
    fn verdicts(lang: &str, tracks: &[(&str, &str, Option<i64>)], chapters: i64, seconds: i64) -> Verdicts {
        let scan = track_scan(lang);
        let file = ident(tracks, chapters, seconds);
        let want = expected_rows(&scan, 0, Selection::All).unwrap();
        checks(&want, &file_rows(&file).unwrap(), &scan.titles[&0], &file).unwrap().0
    }

    fn streams(rows: &[ExpectedRow]) -> Vec<u32> {
        rows.iter().map(|row| row.stream).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_matching_file_passes_every_check() {
        let v = verdicts("eng", &[("video", "und", None), ("audio", "eng", Some(8)), ("audio", "eng", Some(2))], 2, 600);
        assert_eq!(v, Verdicts { count: true, order: true, video: true, chapters: true, duration: true });
    }

    #[test]
    fn same_language_audio_tracks_in_the_wrong_order_fail() {
        let v = verdicts("eng", &[("video", "und", None), ("audio", "eng", Some(2)), ("audio", "eng", Some(8))], 2, 600);
        assert!(v.count);
        assert!(!v.order);
    }

    #[test]
    fn both_iso_639_2_forms_name_the_same_language() {
        let v = verdicts("fra", &[("video", "und", None), ("audio", "fre", Some(8)), ("audio", "fre", Some(2))], 2, 600);
        assert!(v.order);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_language_of_a_video_track_is_not_compared() {
        let v = verdicts("eng", &[("video", "eng", None), ("audio", "eng", Some(8)), ("audio", "eng", Some(2))], 2, 600);
        assert!(v.order);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_stream_makemkv_removed_as_empty_is_read_from_the_rip_log() {
        let removed = "Forced subtitles track #2 turned out to be empty and was removed from output file";
        let rip = RIP_4047_PAIR.replace("{removed}", removed);
        assert_eq!(removed_streams(&rip), BTreeSet::from([2_i64]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_removed_stream_is_not_expected_in_the_file() {
        let scan = track_scan("eng");
        let file = ident(&[("video", "und", None), ("audio", "eng", Some(8))], 2, 600);
        let (want, dropped) = without_removed(&expected_rows(&scan, 0, Selection::All).unwrap(), &BTreeSet::from([2_i64]));
        assert_eq!(streams(&dropped), [2_u32]);
        // MSG:4047 counts the selected streams, not the scan's: with the first stream deselected, output track 1 is
        // scan stream 2.
        let rows = expected_rows(&scan, 0, Selection::All).unwrap()[1..].to_vec();
        let (want2, dropped2) = without_removed(&rows, &BTreeSet::from([1_i64]));
        assert_eq!(streams(&dropped2), [2_u32]);
        let others: Vec<u32> = rows.iter().filter(|row| row.stream != 2).map(|row| row.stream).collect();
        assert_eq!(streams(&want2), others);
        let (v, _) = checks(&want, &file_rows(&file).unwrap(), &scan.titles[&0], &file).unwrap();
        assert!(v.count);
        assert!(v.order);
    }

    #[test]
    fn chapter_count_and_duration_are_checked() {
        let v = verdicts("eng", &[("video", "und", None), ("audio", "eng", Some(8)), ("audio", "eng", Some(2))], 1, 500);
        assert!(v.order);
        assert!(!v.chapters);
        assert!(!v.duration);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_stream_without_a_language_code_is_und_not_the_metadata_language() {
        // Attribute 28 is the disc's metadata language ("eng" even on Chinese subtitles); only attribute 3 names a
        // stream's language, and a stream without one has no language (spec 8.6).
        let scan = parse(
            r#"TINFO:0,8,0,"2"
TINFO:0,9,0,"0:10:00"
SINFO:0,0,1,6201,"Video"
SINFO:0,0,6,0,"MpegH"
SINFO:0,0,28,0,"eng"
SINFO:0,1,1,6202,"Audio"
SINFO:0,1,6,0,"DD"
SINFO:0,1,14,0,"2"
SINFO:0,1,28,0,"eng"
SINFO:0,2,1,6203,"Subtitles"
SINFO:0,2,3,0,"zho"
SINFO:0,2,6,0,"PGS"
SINFO:0,2,28,0,"eng"
SINFO:0,3,1,6203,"Subtitles"
SINFO:0,3,6,0,"PGS"
SINFO:0,3,28,0,"eng"
"#,
        );
        let want = expected_rows(&scan, 0, Selection::All).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(want.iter().map(|row| row.lang.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), ["eng", "und", "zho", "und"]);
        let eng = expected_rows(&scan, 0, Selection::Eng).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(streams(&eng), [0_u32, 1]);
        let file = ident(&[("video", "und", None), ("audio", "und", Some(2))], 2, 600);
        let (v, _) = checks(&eng, &file_rows(&file).unwrap(), &scan.titles[&0], &file).unwrap();
        assert!(v.order);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_empty_file_against_an_empty_title_fails() {
        let scan = parse("TINFO:0,9,0,\"0:10:00\"\n");
        let file = ident(&[], 0, 0);
        let (v, _) = checks(&[], &file_rows(&file).unwrap(), &scan.titles[&0], &file).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v, Verdicts { count: false, order: false, video: false, chapters: true, duration: false });
    }

    // New in the port.

    #[test]
    fn the_eng_selection_keeps_what_the_python_keeps() {
        // expected_rows(scan, 3, "eng") and (scan, 3, "all") as the Python gave them on SCAN_B: 3D video is never
        // expected; eng drops audio outside eng/und or with flag 256 or 1|2|4, and subtitles outside eng.
        let scan = parse(SCAN_B);
        assert_eq!(streams(&expected_rows(&scan, 3, Selection::Eng).unwrap()), [0_u32, 2, 7]);
        let all = expected_rows(&scan, 3, Selection::All).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(streams(&all), [0_u32, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]);
        assert_eq!(
            all.iter().map(|row| row.lang.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            ["und", "eng", "eng", "und", "spa", "fra", "eng"]
        );
        assert_eq!(all.iter().map(|row| row.flags).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [0_i64, 0, 256, 4, 0, 0, 0]);
        assert!(expected_rows(&scan, 0, Selection::All).unwrap().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn flags_that_are_not_a_number_are_an_error() {
        // int(a.get(22, "0") or 0) raised ValueError in the Python; exit 2 in the Rust.
        let scan = parse(&format!("{}SINFO:0,2,22,0,\"x\"\n", TRACK_SCAN.replace("{lang}", "eng")));
        assert_eq!(
            expected_rows(&scan, 0, Selection::All).unwrap_err(),
            "scan stream 0,2: attribute 22: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'x'"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unreadable_chapter_count_or_duration_is_an_error() {
        // int() and duration_seconds raised ValueError in the Python's checks; exit 2 in the Rust.
        let file = ident(&[("video", "und", None)], 2, 600);
        let scan = parse("TINFO:0,8,0,\"x\"\nTINFO:0,9,0,\"1:00\"\n");
        assert_eq!(
            checks(&[], &[], &scan.titles[&0], &file).unwrap_err(),
            "the title's chapter count (attribute 8): invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'x'"
        );
        let scan = parse("TINFO:0,8,0,\"2\"\nTINFO:0,9,0,\"1:00\"\n");
        assert_eq!(
            checks(&[], &[], &scan.titles[&0], &file).unwrap_err(),
            "the title's duration (attribute 9) is not H:MM:SS: '1:00'"
```
