```rust
/// Scan stream type -> file track type ("Video" -> "video", "Audio" -> "audio", "Subtitles" -> "subtitles"); any
/// other value is kept as it is. Py: TYPE.
pub const TYPE: [(&str, &str); 3] = [("Video", "video"), ("Audio", "audio"), ("Subtitles", "subtitles")];
/// The duration check's symmetric tolerance in seconds, for every format. Py: DURATION_TOLERANCE_S.
pub const DURATION_TOLERANCE_S: i64 = 2;
/// MakeMKV's log of the call that wrote the file, looked for beside mkvmerge.json in this order. Py: RIP_LOG_NAMES.
pub const RIP_LOG_NAMES: [&str; 2] = ["rip.txt", "extract.txt"];

/// A stream the scan predicts in the file. Field names and value types are the Python row's (reconcile.json).
/// Py: expected_rows' dict.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ExpectedRow {
    pub stream: u32,
    /// TYPE of attribute 1, the raw value when not in TYPE, None when the stream has no attribute 1.
    pub r#type: Option<String>,
    /// norm_lang(lang_raw).
    pub lang: String,
    /// Attribute 3, else (video only) attribute 28, else "und"; an empty value counts as absent.
    pub lang_raw: String,
    /// Attribute 6 ("" when absent).
    pub codec: String,
    /// Attribute 41 ("" when absent).
    pub out: String,
    /// Attribute 14 ("" when absent).
    pub ch: String,
    /// int_attr(22).
    pub flags: i64,
}

/// A track of the file. Py: file_rows' dict.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct FileRow {
    pub id: i64,
    pub r#type: String,
    /// norm_lang(properties.language).
    pub lang: String,
    /// properties.language, "und" when absent.
    pub lang_raw: String,
    pub codec: String,
    /// properties.audio_channels as mkvmerge wrote it (an int), or "" when absent; compared through py_str.
    pub ch: serde_json::Value,
    /// The property names starting "tag_", sorted.
    pub tags: Vec<String>,
}

/// The yes/no answers, in the Python's order. Py: checks' verdicts dict.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Verdicts {
    pub count: bool,
    pub order: bool,
    pub video: bool,
    pub chapters: bool,
    pub duration: bool,
}

impl Verdicts {
    /// Every verdict is yes. Py: all(verdicts.values()).
    pub fn all(&self) -> bool {
        self.count && self.order && self.video && self.chapters && self.duration
    }
}

/// The numbers behind them. Py: checks' numbers dict.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Numbers {
    pub scan_chapters: i64,
    pub file_chapters: i64,
    pub scan_seconds: u32,
    pub file_seconds: f64,
}

/// TYPE.get(raw, raw).
fn scan_type(raw: &str) -> String {
    TYPE.iter().find(|(scan, _)| *scan == raw).map_or(raw, |&(_, file)| file).to_string()
}

/// A present, non-empty attribute (Python's `a.get(n) or ...`).
fn truthy(value: Option<&String>) -> Option<&str> {
    value.map(String::as_str).filter(|text| !text.is_empty())
}

/// The scan's streams of `title`, in (title, stream) order, without 3D video (attribute 6 containing "MVC"), filtered
/// by `selection` as the Python does (eng: audio in eng/und without flags 256 and 1|2|4, subtitles in eng).
/// Err where int_attr raised (the Python crashed). Py: expected_rows.
pub fn expected_rows(scan: &Scan, title: u32, selection: Selection) -> Result<Vec<ExpectedRow>, String> {
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    // sorted(scan.streams.items()): the BTreeMap iterates in (title, stream) order already.
    for (&(t, stream), a) in &scan.streams {
        if t != title {
            continue;
        }
        let kind = a.get(&1).map(|raw| scan_type(raw));
        let flags = int_attr(a, 22).map_err(|e| format!("scan stream {t},{stream}: attribute 22: {e}"))?;
        // A stream's language is attribute 3 (spec 8.6). Attribute 28 is the disc's metadata language ("eng" even on
        // the Chinese subtitles of the pinned John Wick scan), so it stands in only for video, which has no
        // attribute 3 and whose language is never compared.
        let video = kind.as_deref() == Some("video");
        let lang_raw = truthy(a.get(&3))
            .or(if video { truthy(a.get(&28)) } else { None })
            .unwrap_or("und")
            .to_string();
        let lang = norm_lang(Some(lang_raw.as_str()));
        let codec = a.get(&6).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        if codec.contains("MVC") {
            continue;
        }
        if selection == Selection::Eng {
            let k = kind.as_deref();
            if k == Some("audio") && (!(lang == "eng" || lang == "und") || (flags & 256) != 0 || (flags & 7) != 0) {
                continue;
            }
            if k == Some("subtitles") && lang != "eng" {
                continue;
            }
        }
        rows.push(ExpectedRow {
            stream,
            r#type: kind,
            lang,
            lang_raw,
            codec,
            out: a.get(&41).cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
            ch: a.get(&14).cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
            flags,
        });
    }
    Ok(rows)
}

/// Output track indices MakeMKV left out of the file, from the rip log's MSG:4047 lines.
///
/// MakeMKV drops a forced-only subtitle track that turns out to be empty and says so: "AV sync issue in stream N at
/// T : Forced subtitles track #N turned out to be empty and was removed from output file". N counts the SELECTED
/// streams of the title in scan order (the output file's tracks before the removal), not the scan's stream numbers.
/// Other MSG:4047 lines are not removals. A first parameter too long for an i64 is left out (MakeMKV numbers output
/// tracks below 100). Py: removed_streams.
pub fn removed_streams(rip_text: &str) -> BTreeSet<i64> {
    parse(rip_text)
        .messages
        .iter()
        .filter(|m| m.code == 4047 && m.text.contains("removed from output file"))
        .filter_map(|m| m.params.first())
        .filter(|first| py_isdigit(first))
        .filter_map(|first| py_int(first))
        .collect()
}

/// Splits the predicted rows (the selected streams in scan order) into those still expected in the file and those
/// MakeMKV removed; `removed` holds positions in `rows` (see removed_streams). Py: without_removed.
pub fn without_removed(rows: &[ExpectedRow], removed: &BTreeSet<i64>) -> (Vec<ExpectedRow>, Vec<ExpectedRow>) {
    let kept = rows.iter().enumerate().filter(|(i, _)| !removed.contains(&(*i as i64))).map(|(_, row)| row.clone());
    let gone = rows.iter().enumerate().filter(|(i, _)| removed.contains(&(*i as i64))).map(|(_, row)| row.clone());
    (kept.collect(), gone.collect())
}

/// The file's tracks. Err when a track's language property is not a string (the Python crashed on it).
/// Py: file_rows.
pub fn file_rows(ident: &MkvmergeIdent) -> Result<Vec<FileRow>, String> {
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    for t in &ident.tracks {
        let language = match t.properties.get("language") {
            None => None,
            Some(serde_json::Value::String(text)) => Some(text.as_str()),
            Some(other) => {
                return Err(format!("track {}: its language property is not a string: {}", t.id, py_repr(other)));
            }
        };
        let mut tags: Vec<String> = t.properties.keys().filter(|key| key.starts_with("tag_")).cloned().collect();
        tags.sort();
        rows.push(FileRow {
            id: t.id,
            r#type: t.r#type.clone(),
            lang: norm_lang(language),
            lang_raw: language.unwrap_or("und").to_string(),
            codec: t.codec.clone(),
            ch: t
                .properties
                .get("audio_channels")
                .cloned()
                .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::Value::String(String::new())),
            tags,
        });
    }
    Ok(rows)
}

/// Type must agree; language too, except on video; audio channel counts (py_str of each side) when both sides state
/// one. Py: same_track.
pub fn same_track(w: &ExpectedRow, g: &FileRow) -> bool {
    if w.r#type.as_deref() != Some(g.r#type.as_str()) {
        return false;
    }
    if w.r#type.as_deref() != Some("video") && w.lang != g.lang {
        return false;
    }
    if w.r#type.as_deref() == Some("audio") {
        let (want, got) = (w.ch.as_str(), py_str(&g.ch));
        if !want.is_empty() && !got.is_empty() {
            return want == got;
        }
    }
    true
}

/// The yes/no answers and the numbers behind them, computed in the Python's order. Nothing passes on empty input.
/// Err (exit 2) when attribute 8 is not an int or attribute 9 is not "H:MM:SS" (the Python crashed). Py: checks.
pub fn checks(want: &[ExpectedRow], got: &[FileRow], title: &Attrs, ident: &MkvmergeIdent) -> Result<(Verdicts, Numbers), String> {
    let scan_chapters = int_attr(title, 8).map_err(|e| format!("the title's chapter count (attribute 8): {e}"))?;
    let file_chapters: i64 = ident.chapters.iter().map(|c| c.num_entries).sum();
    let duration = title.get(&9).map_or("0:00:00", String::as_str);
    let scan_seconds = duration_seconds(duration)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("the title's duration (attribute 9) is not H:MM:SS: {}", py_repr_str(duration)))?;
    let file_seconds = ident.container.properties.duration as f64 / 1e9;
    let numbers = Numbers { scan_chapters, file_chapters, scan_seconds, file_seconds };
    let same_count = want.len() == got.len() && !got.is_empty();
    let verdicts = Verdicts {
        count: same_count,
        order: same_count && want.iter().zip(got).all(|(w, g)| same_track(w, g)),
        video: got.iter().any(|g| g.r#type == "video"),
        chapters: numbers.scan_chapters == numbers.file_chapters,
        duration: numbers.scan_seconds > 0
            && (f64::from(numbers.scan_seconds) - numbers.file_seconds).abs() <= DURATION_TOLERANCE_S as f64,
    };
    Ok((verdicts, numbers))
}

/// "yes" or "no". Py: yes_no.
pub fn yes_no(ok: bool) -> &'static str {
    if ok {
        "yes"
    } else {
        "no"
    }
}
```

Python spellings in this step, through the shared helpers: `int(a.get(n, "0") or 0)` of an attribute is `int_attr` (Task 2); `params[0].isdigit()` and `int(params[0])` are `py_isdigit` and `py_int`; `str()` of a channel count is `py_str`; `repr()` in an error line is `py_repr` or `py_repr_str`; `sorted(scan.streams.items())` is the `BTreeMap`'s own order; `sorted()` of the `tag_` names is `Vec::sort` (UTF-8 byte order is code-point order, Python's `str` order); `(code or "und").lower()` and the `B_TO_T` mapping are `norm_lang` (Task 1).

```rust
/// MakeMKV's log of the rip: how it is printed on the RIP LOG line, and its text as Python's `read_text` gave it
/// ("\r\n" and a lone "\r" already turned into "\n"; `lazymkv-dev reconcile` does this before building it).
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct RipLog<'a> {
    pub shown: String,
    pub text: &'a str,
}

/// The full report of one rip (port spec 3.3), which is also reconcile.json and decide's "reconcile". Field order is
/// the JSON order.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Report {
    pub title: u32,
    pub selection: Selection,
    /// The rip log as printed (corpus/owner/<slug>/<label>/rip.txt), None when none was found.
    pub rip_log: Option<String>,
    /// The predicted streams still expected (after the removal).
    pub want: Vec<ExpectedRow>,
    /// The predicted streams MakeMKV removed (the REMOVED lines).
    pub dropped: Vec<ExpectedRow>,
    /// MSG:4047 indices beyond the prediction, sorted.
    pub unknown_removed: Vec<i64>,
    pub got: Vec<FileRow>,
    pub verdicts: Verdicts,
    pub numbers: Numbers,
    pub video_tracks: usize,
    /// Any file track with a tag_ property.
    pub statistics_tags: bool,
    /// 0 when every verdict is yes, else 1.
    pub exit_code: i32,
}

/// Everything compare_tracks.main computes for `title` of `scan` against `ident`, with the rip log when one was
/// found. Err (exit 2) where the Python crashed, checked in the Python's order: expected_rows, file_rows, a kept
/// stream without a type (the table's `:<9` raised on None), a title the scan does not list (KeyError), checks.
/// Py: compare_tracks.main.
pub fn reconcile(
    scan: &Scan,
    title: u32,
    ident: &MkvmergeIdent,
    selection: Selection,
    rip: Option<RipLog<'_>>,
) -> Result<Report, String> {
    let rows = expected_rows(scan, title, selection)?;
    let got = file_rows(ident)?;
    let (rip_log, removed) = match rip {
        Some(log) => (Some(log.shown), removed_streams(log.text)),
        None => (None, BTreeSet::new()),
    };
    let (want, dropped) = without_removed(&rows, &removed);
    if let Some(row) = want.iter().find(|row| row.r#type.is_none()) {
        return Err(format!("scan stream {title},{} has no type (attribute 1)", row.stream));
    }
    let attrs = scan.titles.get(&title).ok_or_else(|| format!("the scan lists no title {title}"))?;
    let (verdicts, numbers) = checks(&want, &got, attrs, ident)?;
    // sorted(i for i in removed if i >= len(want) + len(dropped)): the BTreeSet is sorted already.
    let unknown_removed = removed.iter().copied().filter(|&index| index >= rows.len() as i64).collect();
    let video_tracks = got.iter().filter(|g| g.r#type == "video").count();
    let statistics_tags = got.iter().any(|g| !g.tags.is_empty());
    let exit_code = if verdicts.all() { 0 } else { 1 };
    Ok(Report {
        title,
        selection,
        rip_log,
        want,
        dropped,
        unknown_removed,
        got,
        verdicts,
        numbers,
        video_tracks,
        statistics_tags,
        exit_code,
    })
}

/// str() of a row's type, as the REMOVED line prints it: "None" for a stream without attribute 1. (reconcile never
/// lets such a row into `want`, whose table line the Python could not print.)
fn type_shown(kind: &Option<String>) -> &str {
    kind.as_deref().unwrap_or("None")
}

/// The lines compare_tracks.main prints, byte for byte: the table (scan streams left, padded to 54 characters; file
/// tracks right), an empty line, RIP LOG, the REMOVED lines, TRACK COUNT to VERDICT, and the codecs line.
pub fn report_lines(report: &Report) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut lines = vec![format!("{:<54} | file", "scan")];
    for i in 0..report.want.len().max(report.got.len()) {
        let left = report.want.get(i).map_or_else(String::new, |w| {
            format!(
                "{:>2} {:<9} {:<4} {:<12} out={:<8} ch={:<2} f={}",
                w.stream,
                type_shown(&w.r#type),
                w.lang_raw,
                w.codec,
                w.out,
                w.ch,
                w.flags
            )
        });
        let right = report.got.get(i).map_or_else(String::new, |g| {
            format!("{:>2} {:<9} {:<4} {} ch={}", g.id, g.r#type, g.lang_raw, g.codec, py_str(&g.ch))
        });
        lines.push(format!("{left:<54} | {right}"));
    }
    lines.push(String::new());
    lines.push(format!("{RIP_LOG}{}", report.rip_log.as_deref().unwrap_or(NO_RIP_LOG)));
    for r in &report.dropped {
        lines.push(format!(
            "{REMOVED}scan stream {} ({} {} {} f={}): {REMOVED_NOT_EXPECTED}",
            r.stream,
            type_shown(&r.r#type),
            r.lang_raw,
            r.codec,
            r.flags
        ));
    }
    for index in &report.unknown_removed {
        lines.push(format!("{REMOVED}MSG:4047 names output track {index}{REMOVED_UNKNOWN}"));
    }
    lines.push(format!("{TRACK_COUNT}scan={} file={}", report.want.len(), report.got.len()));
    lines.push(format!("{ORDER_MATCH}{}{ORDER_MEANS}", yes_no(report.verdicts.order)));
    lines.push(format!("{CHAPTERS}scan={} file={}", report.numbers.scan_chapters, report.numbers.file_chapters));
    lines.push(format!(
        "{DURATION}scan={}s file={}s",
        report.numbers.scan_seconds,
        py_fixed(report.numbers.file_seconds, 1)
    ));
    lines.push(format!("{VIDEO_TRACKS}{}", report.video_tracks));
    lines.push(format!("{STATISTICS_TAGS}{}", if report.statistics_tags { "present" } else { "absent" }));
    let named: Vec<String> =
        report.verdicts.named().iter().map(|&(name, ok)| format!("{name}={}", yes_no(ok))).collect();
    lines.push(format!("{VERDICT}{}", named.join(" ")));
    lines.push(CODECS_NOT_COMPARED.to_string());
    lines
}
```

The DURATION line's `file_seconds` uses `py_fixed(x, 1)` (Python's `'%.1f'`, round half to even on the exact binary value: 600.25 prints `600.2`), as the interfaces' convention requires for `:.1f`.

```rust
    /// A folder under the system's temporary folder, removed when dropped. Py: TempDir (tempfile, "lazymkv-test-").
    struct TempDir(PathBuf);

    impl TempDir {
        fn new(name: &str) -> TempDir {
            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lazymkv-test-reconcile-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
            TempDir(dir)
        }

        fn write(&self, name: &str, text: &str) -> PathBuf {
            let path = self.0.join(name);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
            path
        }
    }

    impl Drop for TempDir {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
        }
    }

    /// The command run with `cwd` as the current directory: (exit code, stdout, stderr).
    fn run_in(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> (i32, String, String) {
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(cwd);
        let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect();
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = run(&ctx, &args, &mut out, &mut err);
        (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
    }

    /// The RIP LOG line of a run over fixture A, which exits 1 wherever its rip log is found.
    fn rip_line(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> String {
        let (code, out, err) = run_in(cwd, args);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (1, ""), "{args:?}");
        out.lines().find(|line| line.starts_with("RIP LOG")).unwrap_or_default().to_string()
    }

    /// The lines as print() writes them.
    fn printed(lines: &[&str]) -> String {
        lines.iter().map(|line| format!("{line}\n")).collect()
    }

    fn sha1_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
        use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};
        Sha1::digest(bytes).iter().map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}")).collect()
    }

            ),
        );
        let (code, out, _) = run_in(&dir.0, &[scan.to_str().unwrap(), "0", json.to_str().unwrap()]);
        assert!(out.contains("MSG:4047 names output track 9, which the prediction does not have"), "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("CHAPTERS"), "{out}");

        assert_eq!(

            "RIP LOG          logs/rip.txt"
        );
        // An empty --rip-log is falsy in the Python, so the log is looked for beside mkvmerge.json.
        assert_eq!(
            rip_line(&dir.0, &["scan.txt", "0", "sub/mkvmerge.json", "--rip-log", ""]),
            "RIP LOG          sub/extract.txt"
        );

    #[test]
    fn unreadable_inputs_exit_2() {
        // The Python crashed with a traceback (exit 1) on each of these; exit 2 is the deliberate change (spec 3.4).
        let dir = TempDir::new("unreadable");
        dir.write("scan.txt", SCAN_A);
        dir.write("mkvmerge.json", IDENT_A);
        dir.write("broken.json", "{\"tracks\": [");
        let cases: [(&[&str], &str); 5] = [
            (&["nothere.txt", "0", "mkvmerge.json"], "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'nothere.txt'"),
            (&["scan.txt", "0", "broken.json"], "broken.json: "),
            (
                &["scan.txt", "0", "mkvmerge.json", "--rip-log", "nothere.txt"],
                "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'nothere.txt'",
            ),
            (&["scan.txt", "5", "mkvmerge.json"], "the scan lists no title 5"),
            (&["scan.txt", "-1", "mkvmerge.json"], "the scan lists no title -1"),
        ];
        for (args, message) in cases {
            let (code, out, err) = run_in(&dir.0, args);
            assert_eq!(code, 2, "{args:?}");
            assert_eq!(out, "", "{args:?}");
            assert!(err.contains(message), "{args:?}: {err}");
        }
    }

    #[test]

            (&["scan.txt", "x", "y"], "argument title: invalid int value: 'x'"),
            (
                &["scan.txt", "0", "y", "--selection", "fr"],
                "argument --selection: invalid choice: 'fr' (choose from 'all', 'eng')",
            ),
            (&["scan.txt", "0", "y", "z", "w"], "unrecognized arguments: z w"),
        ];
        for (args, message) in cases {
            let (code, out, err) = run_in(&dir.0, args);
            assert_eq!(code, 2, "{args:?}");
            assert_eq!(out, "", "{args:?}");
            assert!(err.contains(message), "{args:?}: {err}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn paths_are_shown_as_pathlib_shows_them() {
        // str(PurePosixPath(p)) and str(PurePosixPath(p).parent / "rip.txt") as Python 3.9 printed them.
        let cases = [
            ("mkvmerge.json", "mkvmerge.json", "rip.txt"),
            ("a//b/./mkvmerge.json", "a/b/mkvmerge.json", "a/b/rip.txt"),
            ("/x/mkvmerge.json", "/x/mkvmerge.json", "/x/rip.txt"),
            ("//x/m.json", "//x/m.json", "//x/rip.txt"),
            ("///x/m.json", "/x/m.json", "/x/rip.txt"),
            ("../m.json", "../m.json", "../rip.txt"),
            ("a/", "a", "rip.txt"),
            ("./logs//extract.txt", "logs/extract.txt", "logs/rip.txt"),
            ("", ".", "rip.txt"),
            ("/", "/", "/rip.txt"),
            (".", ".", "rip.txt"),
            ("a/..", "a/..", "a/rip.txt"),
        ];
        for (given, path, beside) in cases {
            assert_eq!(shown(given), path, "{given:?}");
            assert_eq!(shown_beside(given, "rip.txt"), beside, "{given:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_evidence_rip_label_gives_the_pythons_output() {
        let Some(root) = repo_root(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))) else {
            skip("no repository root (a Cargo.toml with [workspace]) above crates/dev");
            return;
        };
        if !root.join("corpus").join("owner").is_dir() {
            skip("no evidence clone at corpus/owner");
            return;
        }
        for r in &EVIDENCE {
            let scan = format!("corpus/owner/{}/scan.txt", r.slug);
            let json = format!("corpus/owner/{}/{}/mkvmerge.json", r.slug, r.label);
            let rip = format!("corpus/owner/{}/{}/rip.txt", r.slug, r.label);
            let mut inputs = Vec::new();
            let mut absent = None;
            for path in [&scan, &json, &rip] {
                match std::fs::read(root.join(path)) {
                    Ok(bytes) => inputs.extend(bytes),
                    Err(_) => {
                        absent = Some(path.clone());
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            if let Some(path) = absent {
                skip(&format!("{path} is not in the evidence clone"));
                continue;
            }
            if sha1_hex(&inputs) != r.inputs {
                skip(&format!("{}/{}: its inputs changed since the Python's output was recorded", r.slug, r.label));
                continue;
            }
            let (code, out, err) =
                run_in(&root, &[scan.as_str(), r.title, json.as_str(), "--selection", r.selection]);
            let context = format!(
                "{}/{}: compare with `python3 scripts/phase0/compare_tracks.py {scan} {} {json} --selection {}` \
                 (until Task 15 deletes it)\n{out}{err}",
                r.slug, r.label, r.title, r.selection
            );
            assert_eq!(out.lines().find(|line| line.starts_with("VERDICT")), Some(r.verdict), "{context}");
            assert_eq!(sha1_hex(out.as_bytes()), r.stdout, "{context}");
            assert_eq!(code, r.exit, "{context}");
        }
    }
}
```

In `crates/dev/src/cmd/reconcile.rs`, insert this code after the last `use` line and before `#[cfg(test)]`:

```rust
/// The command's name as typed.
const NAME: &str = "reconcile";
/// argparse's usage line of compare_tracks.py, under the command's name.
const USAGE: &str = "reconcile [-h] [--selection {all,eng}] [--rip-log RIP_LOG] scan title mkvmerge_json";
/// What -h prints after the usage line: argparse's help of compare_tracks.py.
const HELP: &str = "
positional arguments:
  scan
  title
  mkvmerge_json

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --selection {all,eng}
  --rip-log RIP_LOG     MakeMKV's log of the rip; default: rip.txt or extract.txt beside the mkvmerge json
";
/// The positional arguments in order, as argparse names them.
const POSITIONALS: [&str; 3] = ["scan", "title", "mkvmerge_json"];
// argparse's error sentences, verbatim.
const REQUIRED: &str = "the following arguments are required: ";
const INVALID_INT: &str = "argument title: invalid int value: ";
const INVALID_CHOICE: &str = "argument --selection: invalid choice: ";
const CHOICES: &str = " (choose from 'all', 'eng')";
const UNRECOGNIZED: &str = "unrecognized arguments: ";
/// Python's FileNotFoundError text.
const NO_SUCH_FILE: &str = "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: ";
/// A title no scan lists (a negative one): core::reconcile's sentence for the Python's KeyError.
const NO_SUCH_TITLE: &str = "the scan lists no title ";

/// `lazymkv-dev reconcile`. Py: compare_tracks.main.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    if args.iter().any(|arg| arg == "-h" || arg == "--help") {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "usage: lazymkv-dev {USAGE}");
        let _ = write!(out, "{HELP}");
        return 0;
    }
    let mut parsed = Args::new(args, &["--selection", "--rip-log"]);
    let selection = match parsed.flag("--selection") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let rip_log = match parsed.flag("--rip-log") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let words = match parsed.positionals() {
        Ok(words) => words,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let selection = match selection.as_deref().map(|text| (text, Selection::parse(text))) {
        None => Selection::All,
        Some((_, Some(selection))) => selection,
        Some((text, None)) => {
            let message = format!("{INVALID_CHOICE}{}{CHOICES}", py_repr_str(text));
            return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message);
        }
    };
    // argparse converts the title as it takes it, so a bad title is reported before a missing argument.
    let title = match words.get(1).map(|word| (word, py_int(word))) {
        Some((word, None)) => {
            let message = format!("{INVALID_INT}{}", py_repr_str(word));
            return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message);
        }
        Some((_, Some(title))) => title,
        // Fewer than two words: reported as missing just below.
        None => 0,
    };
    if words.len() < POSITIONALS.len() {
        let message = format!("{REQUIRED}{}", POSITIONALS[words.len()..].join(", "));
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message);
    }
    if words.len() > POSITIONALS.len() {
        let message = format!("{UNRECOGNIZED}{}", words[POSITIONALS.len()..].join(" "));
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message);
    }
    match compare(ctx, &words[0], title, &words[2], rip_log.as_deref(), selection) {
        Ok((lines, code)) => {
            for line in lines {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "{line}");
            }
            code
        }
        Err(message) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {NAME}: error: {message}");
            2
        }
    }
}

/// Reads the scan, mkvmerge.json and the rip log as compare_tracks.main does, and returns the report's lines and its
/// exit code; Err where the Python crashed.
fn compare(
    ctx: &Ctx,
    scan_arg: &str,
    title: i64,
    json_arg: &str,
    rip_log: Option<&str>,
    selection: Selection,
) -> Result<(Vec<String>, i32), String> {
    let scan_shown = shown(scan_arg);
    let scan_text = read_file_text(&ctx.abs(&scan_shown), &scan_shown, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace)?;
    let scan = parse(&text_mode(&scan_text));
    let json_shown = shown(json_arg);
    let json_path = ctx.abs(&json_shown);
    let json_text = read_file_text(&json_path, &json_shown, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)?;
    let ident: MkvmergeIdent = serde_json::from_str(&json_text).map_err(|e| format!("{json_shown}: {e}"))?;
    // `Path(args.rip_log) if args.rip_log else next(...)`: an empty --rip-log is falsy, so the log is looked for
    // beside mkvmerge.json, rip.txt first; Path.exists is true for a file or a folder.
    let rip_found = match rip_log.filter(|given| !given.is_empty()) {
        Some(given) => {
            let given_shown = shown(given);
            Some((ctx.abs(&given_shown), given_shown))
        }
        None => {
            let folder = json_path.parent().map_or_else(|| ctx.abs("."), Path::to_path_buf);
            RIP_LOG_NAMES
                .iter()
                .map(|name| (folder.join(name), shown_beside(json_arg, name)))
                .find(|(path, _)| path.exists())
        }
    };
    let rip_text = match &rip_found {
        Some((path, path_shown)) => {
            Some(text_mode(&read_file_text(path, path_shown, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace)?))
        }
        None => None,
    };
    // A negative title (int() accepts one) is in no scan: the Python's KeyError.
    let title = u32::try_from(title).map_err(|_| format!("{NO_SUCH_TITLE}{title}"))?;
    let rip = rip_found.zip(rip_text.as_deref()).map(|((_, path_shown), text)| RipLog { shown: path_shown, text });
    let report = reconcile(&scan, title, &ident, selection, rip)?;
    Ok((report_lines(&report), report.exit_code))
}

/// `Path(given).read_text(encoding, errors)`: Err is the FileNotFoundError text for a missing file, else the path
/// and the error.
fn read_file_text(path: &Path, shown: &str, encoding: Encoding, errors: Errors) -> Result<String, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| match e.kind() {
        std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => format!("{NO_SUCH_FILE}{}", py_repr_str(shown)),
        _ => format!("{shown}: {e}"),
    })?;
    decode_text(&bytes, encoding, errors).map_err(|e| format!("{shown}: {e}"))
}

/// Python's text-mode read (universal newlines): "\r\n" and a lone "\r" become "\n", as `Path.read_text` gave the
/// scan and the rip log to robot.parse (which then splits on "\n" only).
fn text_mode(text: &str) -> String {
    text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace('\r', "\n")
}

/// The root and the components of a path as Python 3.9's PurePosixPath parses it: exactly two leading slashes are a
/// root of their own, one or more than two are "/"; empty and "." components are dropped.
fn pathlib_parts(text: &str) -> (&'static str, Vec<&str>) {
    let root = if text.starts_with("//") && !text.starts_with("///") {
        "//"
    } else if text.starts_with('/') {
        "/"
    } else {
        ""
    };
    (root, text.split('/').filter(|part| !part.is_empty() && *part != ".").collect())
}

/// str() of a parsed path: the root and the components joined by "/", "." for nothing.
fn pathlib_str(root: &str, parts: &[&str]) -> String {
    if root.is_empty() && parts.is_empty() {
        return ".".to_string();
    }
    format!("{root}{}", parts.join("/"))
}

/// str(Path(text)): how compare_tracks printed (and opened) a path it was given.
fn shown(text: &str) -> String {
    let (root, parts) = pathlib_parts(text);
    pathlib_str(root, &parts)
}

/// str(Path(text).parent / name): `name` beside the file `text` names (the parent is lexical, as pathlib's).
fn shown_beside(text: &str, name: &str) -> String {
    let (root, mut parts) = pathlib_parts(text);
    parts.pop();
    parts.push(name);
    pathlib_str(root, &parts)
}
```

Python spellings in this step: argparse's `type=int` is `py_int`; `repr()` in argparse's and FileNotFoundError's messages is `py_repr_str`; `read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")` of the scan and the rip log is `decode_text(.., Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace)` (a byte-order mark stays and `robot::parse` strips it) followed by `text_mode` (the text-mode newline translation `read_text` does and `decode_text` does not; Task 2's `scan` command does the same); `read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")` of `mkvmerge.json` is `decode_text(.., Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)`; `str(Path(...))` is `shown` and `str(Path(...).parent / name)` is `shown_beside` (Python 3.9's `PurePosixPath`, on every platform; the file system path is the same path taken against `ctx.cwd`).

Python ported: `scripts/phase0/audio_similarity.py` lines 64 to 110 (constants, `CONSTANTS`, `REVERSE_KEYS`, `_TW`), 112 to 333 (`read_levels`, `read_manifest`, `frame_ms_of`, `refusal`, `percentile`, `clamp`, `pearson`, `corr_at`, `smi`, `ok`, `analyse`), 365 to 399 (`reverse_measures`, `swapped`); `scripts/phase0/proxy_levels.py` `PROXY_FORMAT` and the parts of `audio-proxy.json` it reads; `scripts/phase0/audio_dataset.py` `parse_sets`' constant branch (`Constants::set`) and `Measurer`'s `json.dumps({k: getattr(sim, k) for k in sim.CONSTANTS}, sort_keys=True)` (`Constants::canonical_json`); `scripts/phase0/test_audio_similarity.py` lines 13 to 71 (`FPS`, `speech`, `programme`, `power_sum`, `commentary`, `level_file`, `raw_file`) and the classes `Reading` and `Measures`. `fmt` is Task 6's (`core::audio::report::fmt`); the verdict functions are Task 5's.

Exactness rules this task applies (Global Constraints): every loop runs in the Python's order in `f64`; Python's `sum` of floats is a left-to-right fold from `0.0` (`py_sum`), of complex numbers a fold from `(0.0, 0.0)`; `sorted` is a stable sort (`py_sorted`); `max` of `(r, lag)` tuples keeps the first maximum and breaks ties on the larger lag, as Python's tuple comparison does (`py_max_pair`); `int(x)` truncates (`py_trunc`); a negative list index counts from the end (`py_index`); `statistics.median` is Python 3.9's (`py_median`); `round()` in `frame_ms_of` is `f64::round_ties_even`; `str.splitlines` is `py_splitlines`, file iteration is `universal_lines`, `str.split()` is `py_split`, `str.strip()` is `py_strip`, `float()` is `py_float`, `format(x, "g")` is `py_g`, `'%.Nf'` is `py_fixed` (all Task 1). Where the Python raises inside `analyse` (only for nonsensical `--set` values: a negative lag constant, a negative `GAP_TRIM`, a `GAIN_PCT` outside 0 to 1, `TENTH_GAP_S` at or below 0), the Rust panics with the Python's exception text.

```rust
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Added by Task 4: the synthetic level series of test_audio_similarity.py and test_audio_dataset.py (both files define
// them identically). Each draws from PyRandom in the Python's order, so the ported tests measure the Python's numbers.
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// 20 ms frames per second. Py: FPS.
pub const FPS: usize = 50;

/// C pow() as CPython's `10 ** x` calls it. black_box keeps LLVM from rewriting pow(10, x) as exp10(x), which is not
/// always bit-identical to the C library's pow.
fn generator_pow(base: f64, exponent: f64) -> f64 {
    std::hint::black_box(base).powf(std::hint::black_box(exponent))
}

/// Syllables: `loud + uniform(-1, 1)` for randint(4, 7) frames, then `quiet + uniform(-1, 1)` for randint(4, 8)
/// frames, until `frames` levels are made; cut to `frames`. Py: speech(rnd, frames, loud, quiet).
pub fn speech(rnd: &mut PyRandom, frames: usize, loud: f64, quiet: f64) -> Vec<f64> {
    let mut out: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    while out.len() < frames {
        // `[loud + rnd.uniform(-1, 1)] * rnd.randint(4, 7)`: Python evaluates the list before the count.
        let level = loud + rnd.uniform(-1.0, 1.0);
        let count = rnd.randint(4, 7) as usize;
        out.extend(std::iter::repeat(level).take(count));
        let level = quiet + rnd.uniform(-1.0, 1.0);
        let count = rnd.randint(4, 8) as usize;
        out.extend(std::iter::repeat(level).take(count));
    }
    out.truncate(frames);
    out
}

/// A dialogue-driven programme: lines of randint(100, 200) frames of speech(-20, -30), the centre 1 dB below the mix,
/// then randint(75, 150) frames of room tone (the mix at -60 + uniform(-1, 1) for every frame, then the centre at
/// -75 + uniform(-1, 1) for every frame). Returns (mix, centre), each cut to seconds * FPS.
/// Py: programme(seconds=420, seed=1).
pub fn programme(seconds: usize, seed: u64) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
    let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(seed);
    let total = seconds * FPS;
    let mut mix: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    let mut centre: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    while mix.len() < total {
        let n = rnd.randint(2 * FPS as i64, 4 * FPS as i64) as usize;
        let line = speech(&mut rnd, n, -20.0, -30.0);
        centre.extend(line.iter().map(|v| v - 1.0));
        mix.extend(line);
        // int(1.5 * FPS) is 75
        let n = rnd.randint((1.5 * FPS as f64) as i64, 3 * FPS as i64) as usize;
        for _ in 0..n {
            mix.push(-60.0 + rnd.uniform(-1.0, 1.0));
        }
        for _ in 0..n {
            centre.push(-75.0 + rnd.uniform(-1.0, 1.0));
        }
    }
    mix.truncate(total);
    centre.truncate(total);
    (mix, centre)
}

/// 10 * log10(10 ** (a / 10) + 10 ** (b / 10)). Py: power_sum.
pub fn power_sum(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 {
    10.0 * (generator_pow(10.0, a / 10.0) + generator_pow(10.0, b / 10.0)).log10()
}

/// Two people talking all the way through: speech(-18, -27) for randint(150, 300) frames (the count drawn before the
/// speech), then randint(15, 30) frames at -100 dB, over `mix` ducked by 30 dB: power_sum(voice, mix - 30) per frame,
/// as long as `mix`. Py: commentary(mix, seed=7).
pub fn commentary(mix: &[f64], seed: u64) -> Vec<f64> {
    let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(seed);
    let mut voice: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    while voice.len() < mix.len() {
        let frames = rnd.randint(3 * FPS as i64, 6 * FPS as i64) as usize;
        let talk = speech(&mut rnd, frames, -18.0, -27.0);
        voice.extend(talk);
        let pause = rnd.randint(15, 30) as usize;
        voice.extend(std::iter::repeat(-100.0).take(pause));
    }
    voice.iter().zip(mix).map(|(&v, &m)| power_sum(v, m - 30.0)).collect()
}

/// A compact level file as audio-levels.ps1 writes it: the header line, then `'%.1f' % v` per line, "\n" ends.
/// Py: level_file (its write_text body).
pub fn level_file_text(values: &[f64]) -> String {
    let lines: Vec<String> = values.iter().map(|&v| crate::recording::py_fixed(v, 1)).collect();
    format!(
        "# lazymkv audio levels v2: frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400 unit=dB floor=-100 series=x file=x.mkv\n{}\n",
        lines.join("\n")
    )
}

/// ffmpeg's ametadata output, one frame every `step_s` seconds: "frame:k    pts:k    pts_time:<k * step_s :g>" and
/// "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=<v :.6f>" per value. Py: test_audio_similarity.raw_file (its write_text body).
pub fn raw_file_text(values: &[f64], step_s: f64) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for (k, &v) in values.iter().enumerate() {
        out.push_str(&format!(
            "frame:{k}    pts:{k}    pts_time:{}\nlavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level={}\n",
            crate::recording::py_g(k as f64 * step_s),
            crate::recording::py_fixed(v, 6)
        ));
    }
    out
}

```

```rust
        assert_eq!(frame_ms_of("pts_time:1\npts_time:1.03\npts_time:1.06\npts_time:1.09\n"), Some(30.0));
        // at most 201 lines are read ...
        assert_eq!(frame_ms_of(&format!("{}pts_time:0\npts_time:0.02\n", "x\n".repeat(201))), None);
        assert_eq!(frame_ms_of(&format!("{}pts_time:0\npts_time:0.02\n", "x\n".repeat(199))), Some(20.0));
        // ... and at most 50 times are kept
        let first: String = (0..50).map(|k| format!("pts_time:{}\n", py_g(k as f64 * 0.04))).collect();
        let later: String = (0..60).map(|k| format!("pts_time:{}\n", py_g(2.0 + k as f64 * 0.02))).collect();
        assert_eq!(frame_ms_of(&(first + &later)), Some(40.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn level_lines_are_read_as_the_python_reads_them() {
        let text = "x=1\nlavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level= -12.25 \nframe:3\n  \n-nan\nInfinity\n1_0.5\n\x0c-7.5\n";
        assert_eq!(parse_levels(text).unwrap(), vec![-12.25, FLOOR, f64::INFINITY, 10.5, -7.5]);
        assert_eq!(parse_levels("# h\n-20.0\nabc\n"), Err("could not convert string to float: 'abc'".to_string()));
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("rec", "rec");
        tree.insert_file("bom.txt", "\u{feff}# h\r\n-20.5\r\n-100.0\r\n");
        assert_eq!(read_levels(&tree, &PathKey::new("bom.txt")).unwrap(), vec![-20.5, FLOOR]);
        assert_eq!(
            read_levels(&tree, &PathKey::new("none.txt")),
            Err("[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'rec/none.txt'".to_string())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn manifest_lines_are_python_dicts() {
        let man = parse_manifest(
            "# lazymkv audio-levels v2\nfile=a.mkv seconds=3\nmain=1 codec=dts main=2 md5=aa x\ncand=3 codec=ac3\n\
             seconds=9 file=b.mkv extra=1\n# cand=9\nnovalue\ncand=4 a=b=c\n",
        );
        // a repeated key keeps its first place and takes the last value; words without '=' are left out
        assert_eq!(man.main, Some(kv(&[("main", "2"), ("codec", "dts"), ("md5", "aa")])));
        assert_eq!(man.cands, vec![kv(&[("cand", "3"), ("codec", "ac3")]), kv(&[("cand", "4"), ("a", "b=c")])]);
        // every other line updates one dict: file keeps its place and takes b.mkv
        assert_eq!(man.info, kv(&[("file", "b.mkv"), ("seconds", "9"), ("extra", "1")]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_folder_without_manifest_txt_reads_as_an_empty_manifest() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("rec", "rec");
        tree.insert_dir("x");
        assert_eq!(read_manifest(&tree, &PathKey::new("x")).unwrap(), Manifest::default());
    }

    #[test]
    fn streams_json_and_audio_proxy_json_parse() {
        let s = parse_streams(
            r#"{"streams": [{"index": 0, "codec_type": "video"}, {"index": 1, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": "ac3", "channels": 6, "tags": {"language": "eng", "title": "x"}}]}"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(s.streams.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(s.streams[1].channels, Some(6));
        assert_eq!(s.streams[1].tags.as_ref().unwrap().get("language").map(String::as_str), Some("eng"));
        assert!(parse_streams("{}").unwrap().streams.is_empty());
        assert!(parse_streams("[").is_err());
        let p = parse_proxy(
            r#"{"format": "lazymkv audio proxy v1", "source": {"file": "x.mkv", "bytes": 1, "audio_streams": 2}, "encoding": {"gain_db": -6.0, "read": "lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy"}, "tracks": [{"track": 0, "source_stream": 1, "series": "mix", "source": {"codec": "dts", "channels": 6, "language": "eng"}}, {"track": 1, "series": "fc"}]}"#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(p.format, Some(serde_json::Value::from(PROXY_FORMAT)));
        assert_eq!(p.source.get("audio_streams"), Some(&serde_json::Value::from(2)));
        assert_eq!(p.encoding.get("gain_db"), Some(&serde_json::Value::from(-6.0)));
        assert_eq!(p.tracks.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(p.tracks[0].source_stream, serde_json::Value::from(1));
        assert_eq!(p.tracks[1].source_stream, serde_json::Value::Null);
        assert_eq!(p.tracks[1].series.as_deref(), Some("fc"));
        assert!(p.tracks[1].source.is_none());
    }
}
```

```rust
//! A level folder written by audio-levels.ps1 (experiment 13), read as audio_similarity.py reads it: manifest.txt, the
//! level files (one speech-band RMS level in dB per 20 ms frame), streams.json and audio-proxy.json, and the refusal
//! of a folder the analysis must not measure. Text in, values out: the caller's Tree supplies the bytes.

use crate::recording::files::FfprobeStreams;
use crate::recording::{
    py_float, py_g, py_repr_str, py_split, py_splitlines, py_strip, read_text, universal_lines, Encoding, Errors,
    Ordered, PathKey, Tree,
};

/// dB; digital silence. Py: FLOOR.
pub const FLOOR: f64 = -100.0;
/// One level per 20 ms. Py: FRAME_MS.
pub const FRAME_MS: i64 = 20;
/// The same, in seconds. Py: FRAME_S.
pub const FRAME_S: f64 = 0.02;
/// The first line of manifest.txt starts with this. Py: MANIFEST_LINE.
pub const MANIFEST_LINE: &str = "# lazymkv audio-levels v2";
/// audio-proxy.json's format. Py: proxy_levels.PROXY_FORMAT.
pub const PROXY_FORMAT: &str = "lazymkv audio proxy v1";

/// The key of a level line in ffmpeg's raw ametadata output. Py: read_levels.
const RMS_KEY: &str = "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=";
/// The end of every refusal, verbatim. Py: refusal's `again`.
const AGAIN: &str = "this folder cannot be analysed: measure the title again with the new audio-levels.ps1, which writes audio-levels-20ms-<main>-<candidates>";

/// One manifest line's key=value pairs, in line order (dict semantics). Py: read_manifest's `fields`.
pub type Fields = Ordered<String>;

/// manifest.txt: the main stream's line, the candidates' lines in file order, and every other line's pairs merged
/// (info.update). Py: read_manifest's dict {"main", "cands", ...}.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Manifest {
    pub main: Option<Fields>,
    pub cands: Vec<Fields>,
    pub info: Fields,
}

/// A level series: one dB level per 20 ms frame, floored at FLOOR.
pub type Levels = Vec<f64>;
/// streams.json (a level folder's ffprobe stream list).
pub type Streams = FfprobeStreams;

/// audio-proxy.json, the parts proxy_levels reads; the objects are kept as JSON because the Python tests their keys'
/// presence. `encoding.read` may name proxy_levels.py or lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy: it is never checked.
/// Py: load_proxy_json, build, proxy_streams.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct AudioProxy {
    pub format: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    /// file, bytes, audio_streams, ...
    #[serde(default)]
    pub source: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
    /// gain_db, ...
    #[serde(default)]
    pub encoding: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tracks: Vec<ProxyTrack>,
}

/// One entry of audio-proxy.json's "tracks".
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct ProxyTrack {
    pub track: Option<i64>,
    /// An int in a good file (proxy_streams checks isinstance(..., int)); Null when the key is absent.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub source_stream: serde_json::Value,
    pub series: Option<String>,
    /// codec, profile, channels, layout, layout_guessed, language, title, sample_fmt, md5, ...
    pub source: Option<serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>>,
}

/// Parses manifest.txt's text: lines by py_splitlines, '#' lines and lines without '=' skipped, pairs from the
/// py_split words holding '=' (split at the first '='); a line with a "main" key is the main stream, one with a
/// "cand" key a candidate, any other line updates `info`. Py: read_manifest.
pub fn parse_manifest(text: &str) -> Manifest {
    let mut man = Manifest::default();
    for line in py_splitlines(text) {
        if line.starts_with('#') || !line.contains('=') {
            continue;
        }
        let mut fields: Fields = Ordered::new();
        for word in py_split(line) {
            if let Some((key, value)) = word.split_once('=') {
                fields.insert(key.to_string(), value.to_string());
            }
        }
        if fields.contains_key("main") {
            man.main = Some(fields);
        } else if fields.contains_key("cand") {
            man.cands.push(fields);
        } else {
            for (key, value) in fields.0 {
                man.info.insert(key, value);
            }
        }
    }
    man
}

/// `<folder>/manifest.txt` read as utf-8-sig with replacement and parsed; Manifest::default() when it does not exist
/// (the Python returns its empty dict). Py: read_manifest.
pub fn read_manifest(tree: &dyn Tree, folder: &PathKey) -> Result<Manifest, String> {
    let path = folder.join("manifest.txt");
    if !tree.exists(&path) {
        return Ok(Manifest::default());
    }
    Ok(parse_manifest(&read_text(tree, &path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)?))
}

/// Levels in dB, one per frame: compact files (blank, '#' and "frame:" lines skipped) and raw ametadata output (only
/// "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=" lines among the lines holding '='); a value holding "inf" or "nan" is FLOOR,
/// any other is max(FLOOR, float(value)). Lines by py_splitlines, each py_strip'ed. Err is Python's float() text.
/// Py: read_levels.
pub fn parse_levels(text: &str) -> Result<Levels, String> {
    let mut out: Levels = Vec::new();
    for raw in py_splitlines(text) {
        let mut line = py_strip(raw);
        if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') || line.starts_with("frame:") {
            continue;
        }
        if line.contains('=') {
            if !line.starts_with(RMS_KEY) {
                continue;
            }
            line = line.split_once('=').map_or("", |(_, value)| value);
        }
        if line.contains("inf") || line.contains("nan") {
            out.push(FLOOR);
            continue;
        }
        let value = py_float(line)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("could not convert string to float: {}", py_repr_str(line)))?;
        // Python's max(FLOOR, value): FLOOR unless value is greater
        out.push(if value > FLOOR { value } else { FLOOR });
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// A level file read as utf-8-sig with replacement and parsed. Py: read_levels(path).
pub fn read_levels(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey) -> Result<Levels, String> {
    parse_levels(&read_text(tree, path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)?)
}

/// Python's sorted() of floats: a stable ascending sort (equal values keep their order, -0.0 equals 0.0); a NaN,
/// which no level file yields, sorts last.
fn sort_floats(values: &mut [f64]) {
    values.sort_by(|a, b| match (a.is_nan(), b.is_nan()) {
        (false, false) => a.partial_cmp(b).expect("two numbers compare"),
        (false, true) => std::cmp::Ordering::Less,
        (true, false) => std::cmp::Ordering::Greater,
        (true, true) => std::cmp::Ordering::Equal,
    });
}

/// The frame length a level file states, in ms: float() of "frame_ms=" in a first line starting with '#' (None when
/// that word does not parse), else the median spacing of the first 50 "pts_time:" values (lines from universal_lines,
/// as Python iterates a text file; at most 201 lines read) times 1000, rounded half to even; None when neither is
/// there. Py: frame_ms_of.
pub fn frame_ms_of(text: &str) -> Option<f64> {
    let mut times: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    for (k, line) in universal_lines(text).into_iter().enumerate() {
        if k == 0 && line.starts_with('#') {
            for word in py_split(line) {
                if let Some(rest) = word.strip_prefix("frame_ms=") {
                    return py_float(rest);
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some((_, after)) = line.split_once("pts_time:") {
            if let Some(first) = py_split(after).first() {
                if let Some(t) = py_float(first) {
                    times.push(t);
                }
            }
        }
        if times.len() >= 50 || k >= 200 {
            break;
        }
    }
    let mut steps: Vec<f64> = times.windows(2).map(|pair| pair[1] - pair[0]).collect();
    if steps.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    sort_floats(&mut steps);
    Some((steps[steps.len() / 2] * 1000.0).round_ties_even())
}

/// "" when `folder` was written by the experiment-13 audio-levels.ps1 (manifest.txt beginning with MANIFEST_LINE,
/// frame_ms=20, a main stream, 20 ms frames in main-mix.txt, in main-fc.txt when it exists and in every cand-<n>.txt),
/// else the Python's one-line reason, beginning with tree.display(folder). Err only when a present file cannot be
/// read. Py: refusal.
pub fn refusal(tree: &dyn Tree, folder: &PathKey) -> Result<String, String> {
    let d = tree.display(folder);
    let manifest = folder.join("manifest.txt");
    if !tree.is_file(&manifest) {
        return Ok(format!("{d}: no manifest.txt, so it was not written by the new audio-levels.ps1 (the first measurement's folders, audio-levels-<main>-<cand>, hold 100 ms full-band levels); {AGAIN}"));
    }
    let text = read_text(tree, &manifest, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)?;
    let lines = py_splitlines(&text);
    if lines.first().map_or(true, |first| !first.starts_with(MANIFEST_LINE)) {
        return Ok(format!("{d}: manifest.txt does not begin with '{MANIFEST_LINE}'; {AGAIN}"));
    }
    let man = parse_manifest(&text);
    let frame_ms = man.info.get("frame_ms").map(String::as_str);
    if frame_ms != Some("20") {
        // str(FRAME_MS) is "20"
        let shown = frame_ms.unwrap_or("(none)");
        return Ok(format!("{d}: manifest.txt gives frame_ms={shown}, not {FRAME_MS}; {AGAIN}"));
    }
    if man.main.as_ref().map_or(true, |main| main.is_empty()) {
        return Ok(format!("{d}: manifest.txt names no main stream; {AGAIN}"));
    }
    let mut names: Vec<String> = vec!["main-mix.txt".to_string()];
    if tree.exists(&folder.join("main-fc.txt")) {
        names.push("main-fc.txt".to_string());
    }
    for cand in &man.cands {
        names.push(format!("cand-{}.txt", cand.get("cand").map_or("None", String::as_str)));
    }
    for name in &names {
        let path = folder.join(name);
        if !tree.is_file(&path) {
            return Ok(format!("{d}: {name} is missing; {AGAIN}"));
        }
        let ms = frame_ms_of(&read_text(tree, &path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)?);
        if ms != Some(FRAME_MS as f64) {
            let held = match ms {
                None => "frames of unknown length".to_string(),
                Some(v) => format!("{} ms frames", py_g(v)),
            };
            return Ok(format!("{d}: {name} holds {held}, not {FRAME_MS} ms; {AGAIN}"));
        }
    }
    Ok(String::new())
}

/// streams.json's text. Py: read_streams' json.loads(...).get("streams", []).
pub fn parse_streams(text: &str) -> Result<Streams, String> {
    serde_json::from_str(text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// audio-proxy.json's text (the caller reads it with read_text, utf-8-sig). Py: load_proxy_json's json.loads.
pub fn parse_proxy(text: &str) -> Result<AudioProxy, String> {
    serde_json::from_str(text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}
```

Insert this block at the top of `crates/core/src/audio/measures.rs`, above the line `#[cfg(test)]` that opens `mod constants_tests` (the two `use` lines are for Step 16's code; until then the build warns that `FLOOR` and `FRAME_S` are unused):

```rust
//! The measures of experiment 13 (spec 8.6's content rule): `analyse` compares a candidate's level series with the
//! main track's, frame by frame, as audio_similarity.py does, in the Python's loop order and in f64, so every measure
//! agrees with the Python's within 1e-9 (SMI within 1e-6, spec section 4). `Constants` are the module constants a
//! tuning run may change (`lazymkv-dev retune --set NAME=VALUE`).

use super::levels::{FLOOR, FRAME_S};
use crate::recording::py_float_repr;

/// 2 s windows; fixed by the level files, never set. Py: WIN.
pub const WIN: usize = 100;
/// 60 s blocks for the lag; never set. Py: BLOCK.
pub const BLOCK: usize = 3000;
/// 1.28 s modulation windows of 64 frames, fixed by the precomputed transform. Py: N_SMI.
pub const N_SMI: usize = 64;

/// The reverse run's measures kept as "rev_<name>", in this order. Py: REVERSE_KEYS.
pub const REVERSE_KEYS: [&str; 15] = [
    "overlap", "main_silent", "gap_s", "dc", "ag", "ag_s", "adl", "tenths", "tenths_comm", "tenths_ad", "smi",
    "smi_windows", "ls_db", "added_s", "gain_db",
];

/// A Python number that is an int or a float (a constant, a rule threshold, a --set value). Display is Python's
/// str() (py_float_repr for a float); serde keeps the kind (10 stays 10, 10.0 stays 10.0).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum Num {
    Int(i64),
    Float(f64),
}

impl Num {
    pub fn as_f64(self) -> f64 {
        match self {
            Num::Int(i) => i as f64,
            Num::Float(x) => x,
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Num {
    /// Python's str(): an int's digits, a float's repr ("0.7", "20.0", "1e-05").
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Num::Int(i) => write!(f, "{i}"),
            Num::Float(x) => f.write_str(&py_float_repr(*x)),
        }
    }
}

/// Whether a key holds an int or a float.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NumKind {
    Int,
    Float,
}

/// Why `set` refused: the name is not one of NAMES, or an Int key was given a value that is not a whole number.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SetError {
    Unknown,
    NotWhole,
}

/// The measure constants a tuning run may change, with the Python's defaults; fields in CONSTANTS order, so the serde
/// form is the snapshot's "constants". Py: the module constants named by CONSTANTS.
#[allow(non_snake_case)]
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Constants {
    /// A window whose levels correlate at least this much follows the main.
    pub MATCH_R: f64,
    /// Added sound must sit in a window that correlates less than this.
    pub MISMATCH_R: f64,
    /// Candidate active: within this many dB of its own 95th percentile.
    pub X_ACTIVE_BELOW: f64,
    /// Dialogue frame: the dialogue reference within this many dB of its own 95th percentile.
    pub DLG_BELOW: f64,
    /// A dialogue gap lasts at least this many frames ...
    pub GAP_MIN: i64,
    /// ... and loses this many frames at each end.
    pub GAP_TRIM: i64,
    /// Added: at least this many dB above the level the main predicts.
    pub ADDED_DB: f64,
    /// The main is digitally silent at or below this level.
    pub SILENT_DB: f64,
    /// Coarse lag search, +- this many 100 ms steps.
    pub COARSE_LAG: i64,
    /// Per-block lag search, +- this many frames around the global lag.
    pub BLOCK_LAG: i64,
    /// Per-window lag search, +- this many frames.
    pub WIN_LAG: i64,
    /// A lag (global or per block) is used only when the envelopes correlate at least this much.
    pub LAG_MIN_R: f64,
    /// The gain is this percentile of the candidate's level over the main's in matched windows.
    pub GAIN_PCT: f64,
    /// A tenth of the running time counts when it holds this many seconds of dialogue gaps.
    pub TENTH_GAP_S: f64,
    /// A counting tenth has commentary-like added sound at this AG or more (tenths_comm).
    pub TENTH_COMM_AG: f64,
    /// ... and audio-description-like added sound at this AG or more (tenths_ad).
    pub TENTH_AD_AG: f64,
}

impl Default for Constants {
    fn default() -> Constants {
        Constants {
            MATCH_R: 0.70,
            MISMATCH_R: 0.40,
            X_ACTIVE_BELOW: 20.0,
            DLG_BELOW: 25.0,
            GAP_MIN: 25,
            GAP_TRIM: 5,
            ADDED_DB: 10.0,
            SILENT_DB: -90.0,
            COARSE_LAG: 100,
            BLOCK_LAG: 100,
            WIN_LAG: 5,
            LAG_MIN_R: 0.5,
            GAIN_PCT: 0.75,
            TENTH_GAP_S: 10.0,
            TENTH_COMM_AG: 0.40,
            TENTH_AD_AG: 0.05,
        }
    }
}

/// 2**63, the first f64 above every i64.
const I64_END: f64 = 9_223_372_036_854_775_808.0;

impl Constants {
    /// The 16 names in CONSTANTS order, each with its kind. Py: CONSTANTS.
    pub const NAMES: [(&'static str, NumKind); 16] = [
        ("MATCH_R", NumKind::Float),
        ("MISMATCH_R", NumKind::Float),
        ("X_ACTIVE_BELOW", NumKind::Float),
        ("DLG_BELOW", NumKind::Float),
        ("GAP_MIN", NumKind::Int),
        ("GAP_TRIM", NumKind::Int),
        ("ADDED_DB", NumKind::Float),
        ("SILENT_DB", NumKind::Float),
        ("COARSE_LAG", NumKind::Int),
        ("BLOCK_LAG", NumKind::Int),
        ("WIN_LAG", NumKind::Int),
        ("LAG_MIN_R", NumKind::Float),
        ("GAIN_PCT", NumKind::Float),
        ("TENTH_GAP_S", NumKind::Float),
        ("TENTH_COMM_AG", NumKind::Float),
        ("TENTH_AD_AG", NumKind::Float),
    ];

    /// The value of a name exactly as NAMES spells it. Py: getattr(sim, name).
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Num> {
        Some(match name {
            "MATCH_R" => Num::Float(self.MATCH_R),
            "MISMATCH_R" => Num::Float(self.MISMATCH_R),
            "X_ACTIVE_BELOW" => Num::Float(self.X_ACTIVE_BELOW),
            "DLG_BELOW" => Num::Float(self.DLG_BELOW),
            "GAP_MIN" => Num::Int(self.GAP_MIN),
            "GAP_TRIM" => Num::Int(self.GAP_TRIM),
            "ADDED_DB" => Num::Float(self.ADDED_DB),
            "SILENT_DB" => Num::Float(self.SILENT_DB),
            "COARSE_LAG" => Num::Int(self.COARSE_LAG),
            "BLOCK_LAG" => Num::Int(self.BLOCK_LAG),
            "WIN_LAG" => Num::Int(self.WIN_LAG),
            "LAG_MIN_R" => Num::Float(self.LAG_MIN_R),
            "GAIN_PCT" => Num::Float(self.GAIN_PCT),
            "TENTH_GAP_S" => Num::Float(self.TENTH_GAP_S),
            "TENTH_COMM_AG" => Num::Float(self.TENTH_COMM_AG),
            "TENTH_AD_AG" => Num::Float(self.TENTH_AD_AG),
            _ => return None,
        })
    }

    /// Sets a name exactly as NAMES spells it (the caller upper-cases and has refused a non-finite value, as
    /// parse_sets does). A Float key keeps the value as a float, whole or not ("SILENT_DB=-80" stores -80.0); an Int
    /// key takes int(value) of a whole value and refuses a fraction with NotWhole (a non-finite value, or one outside
    /// i64, is NotWhole too). Returns the value stored. Py: parse_sets' constant branch.
    pub fn set(&mut self, name: &str, value: f64) -> Result<Num, SetError> {
        let kind = Self::NAMES
            .iter()
            .find(|entry| entry.0 == name)
            .map(|entry| entry.1)
            .ok_or(SetError::Unknown)?;
        let num = match kind {
            NumKind::Float => Num::Float(value),
            NumKind::Int => {
                if !value.is_finite() || value != value.trunc() || !(-I64_END..I64_END).contains(&value) {
                    return Err(SetError::NotWhole);
                }
                Num::Int(value as i64)
            }
        };
        match (name, num) {
            ("MATCH_R", Num::Float(v)) => self.MATCH_R = v,
            ("MISMATCH_R", Num::Float(v)) => self.MISMATCH_R = v,
            ("X_ACTIVE_BELOW", Num::Float(v)) => self.X_ACTIVE_BELOW = v,
            ("DLG_BELOW", Num::Float(v)) => self.DLG_BELOW = v,
            ("GAP_MIN", Num::Int(v)) => self.GAP_MIN = v,
            ("GAP_TRIM", Num::Int(v)) => self.GAP_TRIM = v,
            ("ADDED_DB", Num::Float(v)) => self.ADDED_DB = v,
            ("SILENT_DB", Num::Float(v)) => self.SILENT_DB = v,
            ("COARSE_LAG", Num::Int(v)) => self.COARSE_LAG = v,
            ("BLOCK_LAG", Num::Int(v)) => self.BLOCK_LAG = v,
            ("WIN_LAG", Num::Int(v)) => self.WIN_LAG = v,
            ("LAG_MIN_R", Num::Float(v)) => self.LAG_MIN_R = v,
            ("GAIN_PCT", Num::Float(v)) => self.GAIN_PCT = v,
            ("TENTH_GAP_S", Num::Float(v)) => self.TENTH_GAP_S = v,
            ("TENTH_COMM_AG", Num::Float(v)) => self.TENTH_COMM_AG = v,
            ("TENTH_AD_AG", Num::Float(v)) => self.TENTH_AD_AG = v,
            _ => unreachable!("Constants::NAMES gives every name the kind of its field"),
        }
        Ok(num)
    }

    /// json.dumps({name: value for name in CONSTANTS}, sort_keys=True): the cache key's constants part, with
    /// Python's default separators ", " and ": " and Python's number spelling.
    pub fn canonical_json(&self) -> String {
        let mut names: Vec<&str> = Self::NAMES.iter().map(|entry| entry.0).collect();
        names.sort_unstable();
        let parts: Vec<String> = names
            .iter()
            .map(|name| format!("\"{name}\": {}", json_number(self.get(name).expect("a name of NAMES"))))
            .collect();
        format!("{{{}}}", parts.join(", "))
    }
}

/// A number as json.dumps spells it: an int's digits, a float's repr, and NaN and the infinities as json.dumps'
/// NaN, Infinity and -Infinity.
fn json_number(num: Num) -> String {
    match num {
        Num::Int(i) => i.to_string(),
        Num::Float(x) if x.is_nan() => "NaN".to_string(),
        Num::Float(x) if x.is_infinite() => (if x > 0.0 { "Infinity" } else { "-Infinity" }).to_string(),
        Num::Float(x) => py_float_repr(x),
    }
}
```

```rust
        for t in (0..mix.len()).step_by(10 * FPS) {
            for u in t..mix.len().min(t + 3 * FPS) {
                mix[u] = -100.0;

    /// equal as ints, floats within 1e-9 (SMI within 1e-6, spec section 4), null where the Python had NaN.
    fn assert_like_python(expected: &str, m: &Measures) {
        let want: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(expected).expect("the Python's JSON parses");
        let got = serde_json::to_value(m).expect("measures serialise");
        let (want, got) = (want.as_object().unwrap(), got.as_object().unwrap());
        let keys = |o: &serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>| o.keys().cloned().collect::<Vec<String>>();
        assert_eq!(keys(got), keys(want));
        for (key, w) in want {
            let g = got.get(key).expect("the same keys");
            let tol = if key == "smi" || key == "rev_smi" { 1e-6 } else { 1e-9 };
            match (w, g) {
                (serde_json::Value::Number(a), serde_json::Value::Number(b)) if a.is_f64() => {
                    assert!(b.is_f64(), "{key}: {g} is not a float");
                    let (a, b) = (a.as_f64().unwrap(), b.as_f64().unwrap());
                    assert!((a - b).abs() <= tol, "{key}: python {a}, rust {b}");
                }
                _ => assert_eq!(g, w, "{key}"),
            }
        }
    }

        assert_like_python(COPY_PY, &analyse(mix, &copy, Some(centre.as_slice()), true, &consts));
        assert_like_python(COMMENTARY_PY, &analyse(mix, &commentary(mix, 7), Some(centre.as_slice()), true, &consts));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_empty_dialogue_is_the_main_track_and_too_short_is_either_track() {
        let (mix, _) = mix_centre();
        let consts = Constants::default();
        let empty: &[f64] = &[];
        let with_empty = analyse(&mix[..3000], &mix[..3000], Some(empty), true, &consts);
        let with_none = analyse(&mix[..3000], &mix[..3000], None, true, &consts);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&with_empty).unwrap(), serde_json::to_value(&with_none).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(
            analyse(&mix[..999], mix, None, true, &consts),
            Measures::Error { frames: Some(999), error: "too short".to_string() }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            analyse(mix, &mix[..999], None, true, &consts),
            Measures::Error { frames: Some(21000), error: "too short".to_string() }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reverse_measures_and_swapped_exchange_the_runs() {
        let m = Measures::Run(pans());
        let back = Run {
            overlap: 1.0,
            main_silent: 0.001,
            gap_s: 470.0,
            dc: 0.06,
            ag: 0.31,
            ag_s: 144.0,
            adl: 0.04,
            tenths: 10,
            tenths_comm: 1,
            tenths_ad: 10,
            smi: 0.39,
            smi_windows: 526,
            ls_db: 17.1,
            added_s: 796.0,
            gain_db: -6.7,
            ..Run::blank()
        };
        assert_eq!(reverse_measures(&m), Some(Measures::Run(back.clone())));
        let sw = swapped(&m).expect("a reverse block");
        let want = Run {
            rev: Reverse::Block(RevBlock {
                rev_error: String::new(),
                rev_overlap: 1.0,
                rev_main_silent: 0.0,
                rev_gap_s: 929.0,
                rev_dc: 0.08,
                rev_ag: 0.54,
                rev_ag_s: 505.0,
                rev_adl: 0.18,
                rev_tenths: Some(10),
                rev_tenths_comm: Some(9),
                rev_tenths_ad: Some(10),
                rev_smi: 0.51,
                rev_smi_windows: Some(0),
                rev_ls_db: 10.8,
                rev_added_s: 2016.0,
                rev_gain_db: 10.5,
            }),
            ..back
        };
        assert_eq!(sw, Measures::Run(want));
        assert_eq!(swapped(&sw), Some(m.clone()));
        // a reverse run with an error
        let mut failed = pans();
        if let Reverse::Block(block) = &mut failed.rev {
            block.rev_error = "too short".to_string();
        }
        let failed = Measures::Run(failed);
        let error = Some(Measures::Error { frames: None, error: "too short".to_string() });
        assert_eq!(reverse_measures(&failed), error);
        assert_eq!(swapped(&failed), error);
        // no reverse block: an error, the earlier form, analyse(reverse=False)
        let short = Measures::Error { frames: Some(500), error: "too short".to_string() };
        assert_eq!((reverse_measures(&short), swapped(&short)), (None, None));
        let earlier = Measures::Run(Run { rev: Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s: 29.0, rev_ag: 0.10 }, ..pans() });
        assert_eq!((reverse_measures(&earlier), swapped(&earlier)), (None, None));
        let absent = Measures::Run(Run { rev: Reverse::Absent, ..pans() });
        assert_eq!((reverse_measures(&absent), swapped(&absent)), (None, None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn measures_json_has_the_python_keys_kinds_and_null() {
        let short = Measures::Error { frames: Some(500), error: "too short".to_string() };
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&short).unwrap(), r#"{"frames":500,"error":"too short"}"#);
        let bare = Measures::Error { frames: None, error: "too short".to_string() };
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&bare).unwrap(), r#"{"error":"too short"}"#);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Measures>(r#"{"error":"too short"}"#).unwrap(), bare);
        // a block: the forward keys, rev_error, then the REVERSE_KEYS in order; ints as ints
        let m = Measures::Run(pans());
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&m).unwrap(), PANS_JSON);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Measures>(PANS_JSON).unwrap(), m);
        let value = serde_json::to_value(&m).unwrap();
        let keys: Vec<String> = value.as_object().unwrap().keys().cloned().collect();
        let rev_keys: Vec<String> = REVERSE_KEYS.iter().map(|k| format!("rev_{k}")).collect();
        assert_eq!((keys.len(), keys[15].as_str()), (31, "rev_error"));
        assert_eq!(keys[16..].to_vec(), rev_keys);
        // NaN is written as null and read back as NaN
        let blank = serde_json::to_value(Measures::Run(Run::blank())).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(blank["dc"], serde_json::Value::Null);
        assert_eq!(blank["tenths"], serde_json::json!(0));
        assert!(blank.get("frames").is_none());
        let read: Measures = serde_json::from_value(blank).unwrap();
        assert!(read.run().unwrap().dc.is_nan());
        // a reverse run with an error: rev_gap_s 0.0, the other values null
        let read: Measures = serde_json::from_str(FAILED_JSON).unwrap();
        match &read.run().unwrap().rev {
            Reverse::Block(block) => {
                assert_eq!((block.rev_error.as_str(), block.rev_gap_s, block.rev_tenths), ("too short", 0.0, None));
                assert!(block.rev_dc.is_nan());
            }
            other => panic!("not a block: {other:?}"),
        }
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&read).unwrap(), FAILED_JSON);
        // rev_ag without rev_tenths is the earlier form; a missing rev_gap_s reads as 0.0
        let earlier = Run { rev: Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s: 29.0, rev_ag: 0.1 }, ..pans() };
        let mut value = serde_json::to_value(Measures::Run(earlier.clone())).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_value::<Measures>(value.clone()).unwrap(), Measures::Run(earlier));
        value.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("rev_gap_s");
        let read: Measures = serde_json::from_value(value).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(read.run().unwrap().rev, Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s: 0.0, rev_ag: 0.1 });
        // a forward key that is missing is an error, not a silent default
        assert!(serde_json::from_str::<Measures>(r#"{"overlap": 1.0}"#).is_err());
    }
}
```
