```rust
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The measures of one pair
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The measures of one pair, every key of the Python dict as a typed field. The serde form writes the keys in the
/// Python's insertion order (frames, lag_ms, r_global, overlap, main_silent, dc, gain_db, gap_s, ag, ag_s, adl,
/// tenths, tenths_comm, tenths_ad, smi, smi_windows, ls_db, added_s, then rev_error and the 15 rev_ keys), NaN as
/// null, ints as ints; it reads null as NaN, "error" as the Error form, a "rev_tenths" key as a Block, "rev_ag"
/// without "rev_tenths" as Earlier. Py: analyse's dict.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Measures {
    /// `{"frames": n, "error": "too short"}` from analyse; `{"error": e}` (frames None) from reverse_measures and
    /// swapped when the reverse run had one.
    Error { frames: Option<i64>, error: String },
    /// A measured pair.
    Run(Run),
}

impl Measures {
    /// The "error" key. Py: `"error" in m`, `m["error"]`.
    pub fn error(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            Measures::Error { error, .. } => Some(error.as_str()),
            Measures::Run(_) => None,
        }
    }

    /// The measured pair, None for an Error.
    pub fn run(&self) -> Option<&Run> {
        match self {
            Measures::Run(run) => Some(run),
            Measures::Error { .. } => None,
        }
    }
}

/// The forward measures; a NaN f64 is the Python's float("nan").
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Run {
    /// Absent (None) in the dicts reverse_measures and swapped build.
    pub frames: Option<i64>,
    pub lag_ms: Option<i64>,
    pub r_global: Option<f64>,
    pub overlap: f64,
    pub main_silent: f64,
    /// NaN when the main track has no dialogue windows.
    pub dc: f64,
    pub gain_db: f64,
    pub gap_s: f64,
    pub ag: f64,
    pub ag_s: f64,
    pub adl: f64,
    pub tenths: i64,
    pub tenths_comm: i64,
    pub tenths_ad: i64,
    pub smi: f64,
    pub smi_windows: i64,
    pub ls_db: f64,
    pub added_s: f64,
    pub rev: Reverse,
}

impl Run {
    /// Every float NaN, every int 0, frames/lag_ms/r_global None, rev Absent: the base the ported Rule, ReverseRun and
    /// Report tests fill with struct update syntax, as the Python tests build partial dicts.
    pub fn blank() -> Run {
        let nan = f64::NAN;
        Run {
            frames: None,
            lag_ms: None,
            r_global: None,
            overlap: nan,
            main_silent: nan,
            dc: nan,
            gain_db: nan,
            gap_s: nan,
            ag: nan,
            ag_s: nan,
            adl: nan,
            tenths: 0,
            tenths_comm: 0,
            tenths_ad: 0,
            smi: nan,
            smi_windows: 0,
            ls_db: nan,
            added_s: nan,
            rev: Reverse::Absent,
        }
    }
}

/// The rev_ keys a measures dict carries.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Reverse {
    /// analyse(reverse=False), and the dicts reverse_measures builds: no rev_ key.
    Absent,
    /// Measures written before 2026-10-06: rev_gap_s and rev_ag alone (the earlier reverse test of verdict).
    Earlier { rev_gap_s: f64, rev_ag: f64 },
    /// rev_error and the 15 REVERSE_KEYS.
    Block(RevBlock),
}

/// The reverse run as stored. When it had an error, rev_gap_s is 0.0 and every other value is NaN (the ints None), as
/// `back.get(k, 0.0 if k == "gap_s" else nan)` gives; with an empty rev_error every int is Some.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct RevBlock {
    pub rev_error: String,
    pub rev_overlap: f64,
    pub rev_main_silent: f64,
    pub rev_gap_s: f64,
    pub rev_dc: f64,
    pub rev_ag: f64,
    pub rev_ag_s: f64,
    pub rev_adl: f64,
    pub rev_tenths: Option<i64>,
    pub rev_tenths_comm: Option<i64>,
    pub rev_tenths_ad: Option<i64>,
    pub rev_smi: f64,
    pub rev_smi_windows: Option<i64>,
    pub rev_ls_db: f64,
    pub rev_added_s: f64,
    pub rev_gain_db: f64,
}

/// NaN as None, so that serde writes null (nan_to_none).
fn nan_null(x: f64) -> Option<f64> {
    if x.is_nan() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(x)
    }
}

impl serde::Serialize for Measures {
    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        use serde::ser::SerializeMap;
        let mut map = serializer.serialize_map(None)?;
        match self {
            Measures::Error { frames, error } => {
                if let Some(n) = frames {
                    map.serialize_entry("frames", n)?;
                }
                map.serialize_entry("error", error)?;
            }
            Measures::Run(r) => {
                if let Some(v) = r.frames {
                    map.serialize_entry("frames", &v)?;
                }
                if let Some(v) = r.lag_ms {
                    map.serialize_entry("lag_ms", &v)?;
                }
                if let Some(v) = r.r_global {
                    map.serialize_entry("r_global", &nan_null(v))?;
                }
                map.serialize_entry("overlap", &nan_null(r.overlap))?;
                map.serialize_entry("main_silent", &nan_null(r.main_silent))?;
                map.serialize_entry("dc", &nan_null(r.dc))?;
                map.serialize_entry("gain_db", &nan_null(r.gain_db))?;
                map.serialize_entry("gap_s", &nan_null(r.gap_s))?;
                map.serialize_entry("ag", &nan_null(r.ag))?;
                map.serialize_entry("ag_s", &nan_null(r.ag_s))?;
                map.serialize_entry("adl", &nan_null(r.adl))?;
                map.serialize_entry("tenths", &r.tenths)?;
                map.serialize_entry("tenths_comm", &r.tenths_comm)?;
                map.serialize_entry("tenths_ad", &r.tenths_ad)?;
                map.serialize_entry("smi", &nan_null(r.smi))?;
                map.serialize_entry("smi_windows", &r.smi_windows)?;
                map.serialize_entry("ls_db", &nan_null(r.ls_db))?;
                map.serialize_entry("added_s", &nan_null(r.added_s))?;
                match &r.rev {
                    Reverse::Absent => {}
                    Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s, rev_ag } => {
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_gap_s", &nan_null(*rev_gap_s))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_ag", &nan_null(*rev_ag))?;
                    }
                    Reverse::Block(b) => {
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_error", &b.rev_error)?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_overlap", &nan_null(b.rev_overlap))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_main_silent", &nan_null(b.rev_main_silent))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_gap_s", &nan_null(b.rev_gap_s))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_dc", &nan_null(b.rev_dc))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_ag", &nan_null(b.rev_ag))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_ag_s", &nan_null(b.rev_ag_s))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_adl", &nan_null(b.rev_adl))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_tenths", &b.rev_tenths)?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_tenths_comm", &b.rev_tenths_comm)?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_tenths_ad", &b.rev_tenths_ad)?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_smi", &nan_null(b.rev_smi))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_smi_windows", &b.rev_smi_windows)?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_ls_db", &nan_null(b.rev_ls_db))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_added_s", &nan_null(b.rev_added_s))?;
                        map.serialize_entry("rev_gain_db", &nan_null(b.rev_gain_db))?;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        map.end()
    }
}

impl<'de> serde::Deserialize<'de> for Measures {
    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Measures, D::Error> {
        let map = <serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> as serde::Deserialize>::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        measures_from_map(&map).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)
    }
}

type JsonMap = serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>;

/// A float key's value: null is NaN.
fn float_value(key: &str, value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<f64, String> {
    if value.is_null() {
        return Ok(f64::NAN);
    }
    value.as_f64().ok_or_else(|| format!("field `{key}`: expected a number or null, got {value}"))
}

/// A float key that must be there (Python's m[key]).
fn float_at(map: &JsonMap, key: &str) -> Result<f64, String> {
    match map.get(key) {
        None => Err(format!("missing field `{key}`")),
        Some(value) => float_value(key, value),
    }
}

/// A float key read with a default (Python's m.get(key, default)).
fn float_or(map: &JsonMap, key: &str, default: f64) -> Result<f64, String> {
    match map.get(key) {
        None => Ok(default),
        Some(value) => float_value(key, value),
    }
}

/// An int key that must be there and be an int.
fn int_at(map: &JsonMap, key: &str) -> Result<i64, String> {
    match map.get(key) {
        None => Err(format!("missing field `{key}`")),
        Some(value) => value.as_i64().ok_or_else(|| format!("field `{key}`: expected an integer, got {value}")),
    }
}

/// An int key that must be there and may be null (a reverse run's int after an error).
fn nullable_int_at(map: &JsonMap, key: &str) -> Result<Option<i64>, String> {
    match map.get(key) {
        None => Err(format!("missing field `{key}`")),
        Some(serde_json::Value::Null) => Ok(None),
        Some(value) => {
            value.as_i64().map(Some).ok_or_else(|| format!("field `{key}`: expected an integer or null, got {value}"))
        }
    }
}

/// An int key that may be absent or null (frames and lag_ms of the reverse_measures and swapped dicts).
fn optional_int_at(map: &JsonMap, key: &str) -> Result<Option<i64>, String> {
    match map.get(key) {
        None | Some(serde_json::Value::Null) => Ok(None),
        Some(value) => value.as_i64().map(Some).ok_or_else(|| format!("field `{key}`: expected an integer, got {value}")),
    }
}

fn measures_from_map(map: &JsonMap) -> Result<Measures, String> {
    if let Some(error) = map.get("error") {
        let error = error.as_str().ok_or("field `error`: expected a string")?.to_string();
        return Ok(Measures::Error { frames: optional_int_at(map, "frames")?, error });
    }
    let rev = if map.contains_key("rev_tenths") {
        // m.get("rev_error") is falsy when it is absent or null
        let rev_error = match map.get("rev_error") {
            None | Some(serde_json::Value::Null) => String::new(),
            Some(value) => value.as_str().ok_or("field `rev_error`: expected a string")?.to_string(),
        };
        Reverse::Block(RevBlock {
            rev_error,
            rev_overlap: float_at(map, "rev_overlap")?,
            rev_main_silent: float_at(map, "rev_main_silent")?,
            rev_gap_s: float_at(map, "rev_gap_s")?,
            rev_dc: float_at(map, "rev_dc")?,
            rev_ag: float_at(map, "rev_ag")?,
            rev_ag_s: float_at(map, "rev_ag_s")?,
            rev_adl: float_at(map, "rev_adl")?,
            rev_tenths: nullable_int_at(map, "rev_tenths")?,
            rev_tenths_comm: nullable_int_at(map, "rev_tenths_comm")?,
            rev_tenths_ad: nullable_int_at(map, "rev_tenths_ad")?,
            rev_smi: float_at(map, "rev_smi")?,
            rev_smi_windows: nullable_int_at(map, "rev_smi_windows")?,
            rev_ls_db: float_at(map, "rev_ls_db")?,
            rev_added_s: float_at(map, "rev_added_s")?,
            rev_gain_db: float_at(map, "rev_gain_db")?,
        })
    } else if map.contains_key("rev_ag") {
        // verdict reads m.get("rev_gap_s", 0.0) and m["rev_ag"]
        Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s: float_or(map, "rev_gap_s", 0.0)?, rev_ag: float_at(map, "rev_ag")? }
    } else {
        Reverse::Absent
    };
    let r_global = match map.get("r_global") {
        None => None,
        Some(value) => Some(float_value("r_global", value)?),
    };
    Ok(Measures::Run(Run {
        frames: optional_int_at(map, "frames")?,
        lag_ms: optional_int_at(map, "lag_ms")?,
        r_global,
        overlap: float_at(map, "overlap")?,
        main_silent: float_at(map, "main_silent")?,
        dc: float_at(map, "dc")?,
        gain_db: float_at(map, "gain_db")?,
        gap_s: float_at(map, "gap_s")?,
        ag: float_at(map, "ag")?,
        ag_s: float_at(map, "ag_s")?,
        adl: float_at(map, "adl")?,
        tenths: int_at(map, "tenths")?,
        tenths_comm: int_at(map, "tenths_comm")?,
        tenths_ad: int_at(map, "tenths_ad")?,
        smi: float_at(map, "smi")?,
        smi_windows: int_at(map, "smi_windows")?,
        ls_db: float_at(map, "ls_db")?,
        added_s: float_at(map, "added_s")?,
        rev,
    }))
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Python's arithmetic, spelt out
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Python 3.9's sum() of floats: left to right from 0.0.
fn py_sum(values: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    values.iter().fold(0.0, |acc, &v| acc + v)
}

/// Python's sorted() of floats: a stable ascending sort (equal values keep their order, -0.0 equals 0.0); a NaN,
/// which the level series never hold, sorts last.
fn py_sorted(values: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {
    let mut sorted = values.to_vec();
    sorted.sort_by(|a, b| match (a.is_nan(), b.is_nan()) {
        (false, false) => a.partial_cmp(b).expect("two numbers compare"),
        (false, true) => std::cmp::Ordering::Less,
        (true, false) => std::cmp::Ordering::Greater,
        (true, true) => std::cmp::Ordering::Equal,
    });
    sorted
}

/// int() of a float: truncation toward zero (saturating beyond i64, which min() and py_index treat as Python treats
/// the big int); Python's ValueError and OverflowError texts for NaN and the infinities.
fn py_trunc(x: f64) -> i64 {
    if x.is_nan() {
        panic!("cannot convert float NaN to integer");
    }
    if x.is_infinite() {
        panic!("cannot convert float infinity to integer");
    }
    x.trunc() as i64
}

/// A Python list index: a negative one counts from the end; None where Python raises IndexError.
fn py_index(i: i64, len: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    let j = if i < 0 { i.checked_add(len as i64)? } else { i };
    if j >= 0 && (j as usize) < len {
        Some(j as usize)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

/// Python's tuple `a > b` for (r, lag): r decides, an equal r is decided by the lag.
fn pair_gt(a: (f64, i64), b: (f64, i64)) -> bool {
    if a.0 == b.0 {
        a.1 > b.1
    } else {
        a.0 > b.0
    }
}

/// Python's max() of (r, lag) tuples: the first item, replaced by every later item that is greater.
fn py_max_pair(items: impl IntoIterator<Item = (f64, i64)>) -> (f64, i64) {
    let mut items = items.into_iter();
    let mut best = items.next().expect("max() arg is an empty sequence");
    for item in items {
        if pair_gt(item, best) {
            best = item;
        }
    }
    best
}

/// Python's max() of floats: the first item, replaced by every later item that is greater.
fn py_max(items: impl IntoIterator<Item = f64>) -> f64 {
    let mut items = items.into_iter();
    let mut best = items.next().expect("max() arg is an empty sequence");
    for item in items {
        if item > best {
            best = item;
        }
    }
    best
}

/// statistics.median of Python 3.9: the middle of the sorted values, or the mean of the two middle ones.
fn py_median(data: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let sorted = py_sorted(data);
    let n = sorted.len();
    assert!(n > 0, "no median for empty data");
    if n % 2 == 1 {
        sorted[n / 2]
    } else {
        let i = n / 2;
        (sorted[i - 1] + sorted[i]) / 2.0
    }
}

/// C pow() as CPython's float `**` calls it. black_box keeps LLVM from rewriting pow(10, x) as exp10(x) and
/// pow(x, 2.0) as x * x; on the Mac the C library's pow(x, 2.0) differs from x * x in about 1 case in 750.
fn py_pow(base: f64, exponent: f64) -> f64 {
    std::hint::black_box(base).powf(std::hint::black_box(exponent))
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The measure helpers
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Not NaN. Py: ok.
pub fn ok(v: f64) -> bool {
    !v.is_nan()
}

/// `ordered[min(len - 1, int(share * len))]` of the sorted values (a negative index counts from the end, as in
/// Python), NaN for none. Py: percentile.
pub fn percentile(values: &[f64], share: f64) -> f64 {
    if values.is_empty() {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    let ordered = py_sorted(values);
    let len = ordered.len();
    let i = py_trunc(share * len as f64).min(len as i64 - 1);
    ordered[py_index(i, len).expect("list index out of range")]
}

/// Every level raised to at least the 95th percentile minus 45 dB. Py: clamp(values, below=45.0).
fn clamp(values: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {
    let floor = percentile(values, 0.95) - 45.0;
    // Python's max(v, floor): v unless floor is greater
    values.iter().map(|&v| if floor > v { floor } else { v }).collect()
}

/// Pearson's r of two equally long series; 0.0 for fewer than two values or a constant series. Py: pearson.
fn pearson(a: &[f64], b: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let n = a.len();
    if n < 2 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let ma = py_sum(a) / n as f64;
    let mb = py_sum(b) / n as f64;
    let (mut cov, mut va, mut vb) = (0.0f64, 0.0f64, 0.0f64);
    for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b) {
        let dx = x - ma;
        let dy = y - mb;
        cov += dx * dy;
        va += dx * dx;
        vb += dy * dy;
    }
    if va > 0.0 && vb > 0.0 {
        cov / (va * vb).sqrt()
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

/// Correlation of a[i] and b[i + lag] for i in [i0, i1) in steps of `step`; -2.0 when fewer than 10 pairs exist.
/// Py: corr_at.
fn corr_at(a: &[f64], b: &[f64], i0: i64, i1: i64, lag: i64, step: usize) -> f64 {
    let lo = i0.max(-lag);
    let hi = i1.min(b.len() as i64 - lag);
    if hi - lo < 10 {
        return -2.0;
    }
    let mut xs: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    let mut ys: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    for i in (lo..hi).step_by(step) {
        xs.push(a[i as usize]);
        ys.push(b[(i + lag) as usize]);
    }
    pearson(&xs, &ys)
}

/// _TW[k][n] = cmath.exp(-2j * math.pi * k * n / N_SMI) for k in 0..33, n in 0..64, as (re, im). CPython 3.9 forms
/// the exponent as (0.0, theta) with theta = (0.0 + (0.0 + (-2 * pi) * k) * n) / 64 (complex times int and complex
/// over int go through full complex arithmetic, which is where the `0.0 +` come from), and exp((0.0, theta)) is
/// (cos theta, sin theta). Py: _TW.
fn twiddles() -> &'static [[(f64, f64); N_SMI]; 33] {
    static TW: std::sync::OnceLock<[[(f64, f64); N_SMI]; 33]> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    TW.get_or_init(|| {
        let mut tw = [[(0.0f64, 0.0f64); N_SMI]; 33];
        for (k, row) in tw.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            for (n, entry) in row.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                let theta = (0.0 + (0.0 + (-2.0 * std::f64::consts::PI) * k as f64) * n as f64) / N_SMI as f64;
                *entry = (theta.cos(), theta.sin());
            }
        }
        tw
    })
}

/// Share of the linear envelope's modulation energy at 2.3 to 7.8 Hz: DFT bins 3 to 10 of 1 to 32 over 64 frames of
/// 20 ms, each bin summed n = 0..63 in order with the precomputed twiddles, |X_k| ** 2 by C pow; 0.0 when the total
/// is not positive. The mean is the sum of every given level over 64 and the first 64 are transformed, as the Python
/// does. Py: smi.
pub fn smi(levels_db: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let lin: Vec<f64> = levels_db.iter().map(|&v| py_pow(10.0, v / 20.0)).collect();
    let mean = py_sum(&lin) / N_SMI as f64;
    let x: Vec<f64> = lin.iter().map(|&v| v - mean).collect();
    assert!(x.len() >= N_SMI, "list index out of range");
    let tw = twiddles();
    let mut e = [0.0f64; 33];
    for (k, energy) in e.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        // sum() of complex numbers from (0.0, 0.0); each term is CPython 3.9's float * complex, (x + 0j) * (c + sj)
        let (mut re, mut im) = (0.0f64, 0.0f64);
        for n in 0..N_SMI {
            let (c, s) = tw[k][n];
            re += x[n] * c - 0.0 * s;
            im += x[n] * s + 0.0 * c;
        }
        *energy = py_pow(re.hypot(im), 2.0);
    }
    let total = py_sum(&e[1..33]);
    if total > 0.0 {
        py_sum(&e[3..11]) / total
    } else {
        0.0
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// analyse
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The measures of `cand` against `main` (levels in dB per 20 ms frame), in the Python's loop order: clamp, coarse
/// and fine lag, block lags, gaps, windows, DC, gain, added, tenths, SMI, LS, ADL; with `reverse`, the reverse run
/// analyse(cand, main, None, false) as the rev_ block. `dialogue` is the centre channel; None or Some(empty) means
/// `main` (`dialogue or main`). Error "too short" when either series has fewer than 10 windows. Panics with the
/// Python's exception text where the Python raised (only for --set values outside their sense: a negative lag
/// constant, a negative GAP_TRIM, a GAIN_PCT outside 0 to 1, a TENTH_GAP_S at or below 0). Py: analyse.
pub fn analyse(main: &[f64], cand: &[f64], dialogue: Option<&[f64]>, reverse: bool, consts: &Constants) -> Measures {
    let c = consts;
    let dialogue: &[f64] = match dialogue {
        Some(d) if !d.is_empty() => d,
        _ => main,
    };
    let n = main.len();
    if n < 10 * WIN || cand.len() < 10 * WIN {
        return Measures::Error { frames: Some(n as i64), error: "too short".to_string() };
    }
    let mc = clamp(main);
    let xc = clamp(cand);
    // Lag: tracks of one title share a timeline. Coarse +-10 s on 100 ms means, fine +-100 ms; kept only when the two
    // envelopes follow each other (r >= LAG_MIN_R), otherwise 0. Then per 60 s block +-2 s, kept when r >= LAG_MIN_R.
    let mk: Vec<f64> = (0..n - 4).step_by(5).map(|i| py_sum(&mc[i..i + 5]) / 5.0).collect();
    let xk: Vec<f64> = (0..xc.len() - 4).step_by(5).map(|i| py_sum(&xc[i..i + 5]) / 5.0).collect();
    let (_, lag_k) = py_max_pair(
        (-c.COARSE_LAG..c.COARSE_LAG + 1).map(|l| (corr_at(&mk, &xk, 0, mk.len() as i64, l, 2), l)),
    );
    let (r_glob, fine) =
        py_max_pair((5 * lag_k - 5..5 * lag_k + 6).map(|l| (corr_at(&mc, &xc, 0, n as i64, l, 5), l)));
    let lag = if r_glob < c.LAG_MIN_R { 0 } else { fine };
    let n_blocks = n.div_ceil(BLOCK);
    let mut block_lag: Vec<i64> = Vec::with_capacity(n_blocks);
    for b in 0..n_blocks {
        let (b0, b1) = (b * BLOCK, n.min((b + 1) * BLOCK));
        let (r, lb) = py_max_pair(
            (lag - c.BLOCK_LAG..lag + c.BLOCK_LAG + 1)
                .step_by(2)
                .map(|l| (corr_at(&mc, &xc, b0 as i64, b1 as i64, l, 4), l)),
        );
        block_lag.push(if r >= c.LAG_MIN_R { lb } else { lag });
    }
    let lag_of = |t: usize| block_lag[t / BLOCK];

    let n_cand = cand.len() as i64;
    let inside: Vec<bool> = (0..n).map(|t| (0..n_cand).contains(&(t as i64 + lag_of(t)))).collect();
    let frames: Vec<usize> = (0..n).filter(|&t| inside[t]).collect();
    let xa: Vec<f64> =
        (0..n).map(|t| if inside[t] { cand[(t as i64 + lag_of(t)) as usize] } else { FLOOR }).collect();
    let xa_inside: Vec<f64> = frames.iter().map(|&t| xa[t]).collect();
    let x95 = percentile(&xa_inside, 0.95);
    let m95 = percentile(&frames.iter().map(|&t| main[t]).collect::<Vec<f64>>(), 0.95);
    let d95 = percentile(
        &frames.iter().filter(|&&t| t < dialogue.len()).map(|&t| dialogue[t]).collect::<Vec<f64>>(),
        0.95,
    );
    let silent: Vec<bool> = main.iter().map(|&v| v <= c.SILENT_DB).collect();
    let active: Vec<bool> = (0..n).map(|t| inside[t] && xa[t] >= x95 - c.X_ACTIVE_BELOW).collect();
    let dlg: Vec<bool> =
        (0..n).map(|t| inside[t] && t < dialogue.len() && dialogue[t] >= d95 - c.DLG_BELOW).collect();

    let mut gap = vec![false; n];
    let mut t = 0usize;
    while t < n {
        if inside[t] && !dlg[t] {
            let mut u = t;
            while u < n && inside[u] && !dlg[u] {
                u += 1;
            }
            if (u - t) as i64 >= c.GAP_MIN {
                for k in (t as i64 + c.GAP_TRIM)..(u as i64 - c.GAP_TRIM) {
                    // gap[k] = not silent[k], with Python's negative indices
                    let i = py_index(k, n).expect("list index out of range");
                    gap[i] = !silent[i];
                }
            }
            t = u;
        } else {
            t += 1;
        }
    }

    let wins: Vec<usize> = (0..n - WIN + 1).step_by(WIN).filter(|&w| inside[w..w + WIN].iter().all(|&b| b)).collect();
    // rw: the best window correlation over +-WIN_LAG frames, by window number (w / WIN); None for a window not in wins
    let mut rw: Vec<Option<f64>> = vec![None; n / WIN + 1];
    for &w in &wins {
        rw[w / WIN] = Some(py_max(
            (-c.WIN_LAG..c.WIN_LAG + 1).map(|d| corr_at(&mc, &xc, w as i64, (w + WIN) as i64, lag_of(w) + d, 1)),
        ));
    }
    let rw_at = |w: usize| rw[w / WIN].expect("a window of wins has its correlation");
    let dwins: Vec<usize> =
        wins.iter().copied().filter(|&w| dlg[w..w + WIN].iter().filter(|&&b| b).count() >= WIN / 2).collect();
    let dc = if dwins.is_empty() {
        f64::NAN
    } else {
        dwins.iter().filter(|&&w| rw_at(w) >= c.MATCH_R).count() as f64 / dwins.len() as f64
    };
    let matched: Vec<usize> = wins.iter().copied().filter(|&w| rw_at(w) >= c.MATCH_R).collect();
    let mframes: Vec<usize> = matched
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|&w| w..w + WIN)
        .filter(|&u| main[u] >= m95 - 30.0 && xa[u] > FLOOR)
        .collect();
    let gain = if matched.len() >= std::cmp::max(10, wins.len() / 20) && !mframes.is_empty() {
        percentile(&mframes.iter().map(|&u| xa[u] - main[u]).collect::<Vec<f64>>(), c.GAIN_PCT)
    } else {
        x95 - m95
    };
    let added: Vec<bool> = (0..n)
        .map(|u| active[u] && xa[u] - gain - main[u] >= c.ADDED_DB && rw[u / WIN].unwrap_or(1.0) < c.MISMATCH_R)
        .collect();

    let n_gap = gap.iter().filter(|&&g| g).count();
    let n_ag = (0..n).filter(|&u| gap[u] && added[u]).count();
    let n_dlg = dlg.iter().filter(|&&b| b).count();
    let lo = *frames.first().expect("list index out of range");
    let hi = frames[frames.len() - 1] + 1;
    let mut tenths: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    for k in 0..10usize {
        let a = lo + k * (hi - lo) / 10;
        let b = lo + (k + 1) * (hi - lo) / 10;
        let g = gap[a..b].iter().filter(|&&x| x).count();
        if g as f64 * FRAME_S >= c.TENTH_GAP_S {
            if g == 0 {
                panic!("division by zero");
            }
            tenths.push((a..b).filter(|&u| gap[u] && added[u]).count() as f64 / g as f64);
        }
    }
    let s: Vec<f64> = (0..n - N_SMI)
        .step_by(N_SMI / 2)
        .filter(|&t0| added[t0..t0 + N_SMI].iter().filter(|&&b| b).count() >= N_SMI / 2)
        .map(|t0| smi(&xa[t0..t0 + N_SMI]))
        .collect();

    let rev = if reverse {
        Reverse::Block(rev_block(&analyse(cand, main, None, false, consts)))
    } else {
        Reverse::Absent
    };
    Measures::Run(Run {
        frames: Some(n as i64),
        lag_ms: Some(lag * 20),
        r_global: Some(r_glob),
        overlap: frames.len() as f64 / n as f64,
        main_silent: frames.iter().filter(|&&u| silent[u]).count() as f64 / frames.len() as f64,
        dc,
        gain_db: gain,
        gap_s: n_gap as f64 * FRAME_S,
        ag: if n_gap > 0 { n_ag as f64 / n_gap as f64 } else { f64::NAN },
        ag_s: n_ag as f64 * FRAME_S,
        adl: if n_dlg > 0 {
            (0..n).filter(|&u| dlg[u] && added[u]).count() as f64 / n_dlg as f64
        } else {
            f64::NAN
        },
        tenths: tenths.len() as i64,
        tenths_comm: tenths.iter().filter(|&&v| v >= c.TENTH_COMM_AG).count() as i64,
        tenths_ad: tenths.iter().filter(|&&v| v >= c.TENTH_AD_AG).count() as i64,
        smi: if s.is_empty() { f64::NAN } else { py_median(&s) },
        smi_windows: s.len() as i64,
        ls_db: x95 - percentile(&xa_inside, 0.50),
        added_s: added.iter().filter(|&&b| b).count() as f64 * FRAME_S,
        rev,
    })
}

/// A forward run's values as a reverse block (rev_error "").
fn block_of(r: &Run) -> RevBlock {
    RevBlock {
        rev_error: String::new(),
        rev_overlap: r.overlap,
        rev_main_silent: r.main_silent,
        rev_gap_s: r.gap_s,
        rev_dc: r.dc,
        rev_ag: r.ag,
        rev_ag_s: r.ag_s,
        rev_adl: r.adl,
        rev_tenths: Some(r.tenths),
        rev_tenths_comm: Some(r.tenths_comm),
        rev_tenths_ad: Some(r.tenths_ad),
        rev_smi: r.smi,
        rev_smi_windows: Some(r.smi_windows),
        rev_ls_db: r.ls_db,
        rev_added_s: r.added_s,
        rev_gain_db: r.gain_db,
    }
}

/// analyse's rev_ keys from the reverse run: `m["rev_error"] = back.get("error", "")` and
/// `m["rev_" + k] = back.get(k, 0.0 if k == "gap_s" else nan)`.
fn rev_block(back: &Measures) -> RevBlock {
    match back {
        Measures::Run(b) => block_of(b),
        Measures::Error { error, .. } => {
            let nan = f64::NAN;
            RevBlock {
                rev_error: error.clone(),
                rev_overlap: nan,
                rev_main_silent: nan,
                rev_gap_s: 0.0,
                rev_dc: nan,
                rev_ag: nan,
                rev_ag_s: nan,
                rev_adl: nan,
                rev_tenths: None,
                rev_tenths_comm: None,
                rev_tenths_ad: None,
                rev_smi: nan,
                rev_smi_windows: None,
                rev_ls_db: nan,
                rev_added_s: nan,
                rev_gain_db: nan,
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A reverse block as its own forward measures (the 15 keys, no frames, lag_ms or r_global). An int the block lacks
/// with an empty rev_error, which analyse never writes, reads as 0.
fn run_of_block(b: &RevBlock) -> Run {
    Run {
        frames: None,
        lag_ms: None,
        r_global: None,
        overlap: b.rev_overlap,
        main_silent: b.rev_main_silent,
        dc: b.rev_dc,
        gain_db: b.rev_gain_db,
        gap_s: b.rev_gap_s,
        ag: b.rev_ag,
        ag_s: b.rev_ag_s,
        adl: b.rev_adl,
        tenths: b.rev_tenths.unwrap_or(0),
        tenths_comm: b.rev_tenths_comm.unwrap_or(0),
        tenths_ad: b.rev_tenths_ad.unwrap_or(0),
        smi: b.rev_smi,
        smi_windows: b.rev_smi_windows.unwrap_or(0),
        ls_db: b.rev_ls_db,
        added_s: b.rev_added_s,
        rev: Reverse::Absent,
    }
}

/// The reverse run (the candidate as reference, the main stream as candidate) as its own measures: None when `m`
/// carries no reverse block ("rev_tenths" not in m: an Error, analyse(reverse=False), the earlier form); the Error
/// form `{"error": rev_error}` when the reverse run had one. Py: reverse_measures.
pub fn reverse_measures(m: &Measures) -> Option<Measures> {
    let block = match m {
        Measures::Run(Run { rev: Reverse::Block(block), .. }) => block,
        _ => return None,
    };
    if !block.rev_error.is_empty() {
        return Some(Measures::Error { frames: None, error: block.rev_error.clone() });
    }
    Some(Measures::Run(run_of_block(block)))
}

/// The measures of the same pair with the roles exchanged: the reverse run becomes the forward one and the forward
/// run the reverse block (frames, lag_ms and r_global left out). None for an Error or a measures without a reverse
/// block; the Error form when the reverse run had one. Py: swapped.
pub fn swapped(m: &Measures) -> Option<Measures> {
    let back = reverse_measures(m)?;
    let forward = m.run()?;
    match back {
        Measures::Error { error, .. } => Some(Measures::Error { frames: None, error }),
        Measures::Run(mut run) => {
            run.rev = Reverse::Block(block_of(forward));
            Some(Measures::Run(run))
        }
    }
}
```

The cache hook: `results` measures every pair through `&mut dyn AnalyseFn`. `Plain` is the Python's default `analyse`; Task 8's `Measurer` implements the same trait with the cache of spec 3.3 (`sha1("lazymkv-rule:" + RULE_VERSION + canonical constants JSON + per series its little-endian f64 bytes and "|", or "|" alone for none)`) and returns that key in `Measured.key`, which `results` keeps in `CandidateResult.key` and `Peer.key` (the Python's `Measurer.key_of[id(m)]`).

```rust
//! Tests of core::audio::rule. Ported one for one from scripts/phase0/test_audio_similarity.py, classes Rule (5),
//! ReverseRun (5), CrossLanguage (6) and PositionVeto (4), and from scripts/phase0/test_audio_dataset.py, class
//! Similarity (1): one module per class, each test under its Python name without `test_` (as Task 4 names the
//! Measures tests). The modules rule_set, spellings and results_contract are new. The synthetic level series are the
//! Python's (crate::testsupport over PyRandom).

use std::sync::OnceLock;

use crate::testsupport::{commentary, programme};

/// MIX, CENTRE = programme(): 420 s of a dialogue-driven programme (seed 1), computed once.
fn programme_pair() -> &'static (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
    static PAIR: OnceLock<(Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>)> = OnceLock::new();
    PAIR.get_or_init(|| programme(420, 1))
}

/// MIX.
fn mix() -> &'static [f64] {
    &programme_pair().0
}

/// commentary(MIX) (seed 7), computed once; the Python builds the same list at every call.
fn comment() -> &'static [f64] {
    static COMMENT: OnceLock<Vec<f64>> = OnceLock::new();
    COMMENT.get_or_init(|| commentary(mix(), 7))
}

/// Py: test_audio_similarity.py, class Rule (5 tests).
mod rule {
    use crate::audio::measures::{Measures, Reverse, Run};
    use crate::audio::rule::{verdict, Rule, Verdict};

    /// Rule.BASE: the measured commentary (the keys the Python dict has; Run::blank() gives the others).
    fn base() -> Run {
        Run {
            overlap: 1.0,
            main_silent: 0.03,
            gap_s: 355.0,
            dc: 0.03,
            ag: 0.66,
            ag_s: 234.0,
            adl: 0.18,
            tenths: 10,
            tenths_comm: 10,
            tenths_ad: 10,
            smi: 0.58,
            ls_db: 10.1,
            added_s: 518.0,
            rev: Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s: 29.0, rev_ag: 0.10 },
            ..Run::blank()
        }
    }

    /// Rule.v: sim.verdict(dict(BASE, **change)); the caller writes the change with struct update syntax.
    fn v(m: Run) -> Verdict {
        verdict(&Measures::Run(m), &Rule::default())
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_measured_commentary_has_the_pattern() {
        assert_eq!(v(base()), Verdict::Commentary);
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_condition_is_required() {
        assert_eq!(v(Run { dc: 0.31, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { ag: 0.49, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { tenths_comm: 8, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { tenths: 5, tenths_comm: 5, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { smi: 0.49, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { ls_db: 13.1, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { added_s: 59.0, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { main_silent: 0.11, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { gap_s: 89.0, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { overlap: 0.89, ..base() }), Verdict::NoteCommentary);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_main_track_that_adds_sound_to_the_candidate_makes_the_reference_unclear() {
        let earlier = |rev_gap_s, rev_ag| Run { rev: Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s, rev_ag }, ..base() };
        assert_eq!(v(earlier(150.0, 0.35)), Verdict::ReferenceUnclear);
        assert_eq!(v(earlier(60.0, 0.35)), Verdict::Commentary);
    }

    #[test]
    fn audio_description_is_only_ever_a_note() {
        let ad = Run {
            dc: 0.95,
            adl: 0.0,
            ag: 0.30,
            ag_s: 100.0,
            tenths_comm: 2,
            tenths_ad: 9,
            smi: 0.55,
            ls_db: 17.0,
            ..base()
        };
        assert_eq!(v(ad.clone()), Verdict::AdPattern);
        assert_eq!(v(Run { smi: 0.30, ..ad }), Verdict::NoteAd);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_copy_is_kept() {
        let copy = Run {
            dc: 1.0,
            ag: 0.0,
            ag_s: 0.0,
            adl: 0.0,
            tenths_comm: 0,
            tenths_ad: 0,
            smi: f64::NAN,
            ..base()
        };
        assert_eq!(v(copy), Verdict::Keep);
    }
}

/// Py: test_audio_similarity.py, class ReverseRun (5 tests). EXP-13 addendum 9.3: the reverse run is judged with the
/// commentary pattern itself (no number of its own).
mod reverse_run {
    use super::{comment, mix};
    use crate::audio::measures::{analyse, swapped, Constants, Measures, RevBlock, Reverse, Run};
    use crate::audio::rule::{not_judged, reverse_pattern, verdict, Rule, Verdict};
    use crate::testsupport::{power_sum, speech, PyRandom, FPS};

    /// ReverseRun.PANS: the English commentary of Pan's Labyrinth against the Spanish main track, as measured
    /// (all-tracks, 1-2-3), with its two earlier reverse keys (rev_gap_s 470.0, rev_ag 0.31).
    fn pans() -> Run {
        Run {
            overlap: 1.0,
            main_silent: 0.0,
            gap_s: 929.0,
            dc: 0.08,
            ag: 0.54,
            ag_s: 505.0,
            adl: 0.18,
            tenths: 10,
            tenths_comm: 9,
            tenths_ad: 10,
            smi: 0.51,
            ls_db: 10.8,
            added_s: 2016.0,
            rev: Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s: 470.0, rev_ag: 0.31 },
            ..Run::blank()
        }
    }

    /// PANS's rev_gap_s and rev_ag with ReverseRun.REV: the reverse block of dict(PANS, **REV).
    fn rev() -> RevBlock {
        RevBlock {
            rev_error: String::new(),
            rev_overlap: 1.0,
            rev_main_silent: 0.001,
            rev_gap_s: 470.0,
            rev_dc: 0.06,
            rev_ag: 0.31,
            rev_ag_s: 144.0,
            rev_adl: 0.04,
            rev_tenths: Some(10),
            rev_tenths_comm: Some(1),
            rev_tenths_ad: Some(10),
            rev_smi: 0.39,
            rev_smi_windows: Some(526),
            rev_ls_db: 17.1,
            rev_added_s: 796.0,
            rev_gain_db: -6.7,
        }
    }

    /// ReverseRun.m: dict(dict(PANS, **REV), **change); `change` sets forward keys on the Run, rev_ keys on the block.
    fn m(change: impl FnOnce(&mut Run, &mut RevBlock)) -> Measures {
        let (mut run, mut block) = (pans(), rev());
        change(&mut run, &mut block);
        run.rev = Reverse::Block(block);
        Measures::Run(run)
    }

    /// ReverseRun.v.
    fn v(change: impl FnOnce(&mut Run, &mut RevBlock)) -> Verdict {
        verdict(&m(change), &Rule::default())
    }

    /// The `pattern` dict of the Python test_a_reverse_run_with_the_commentary_pattern_makes_the_reference_unclear.
    fn pattern(b: &mut RevBlock) {
        b.rev_dc = 0.03;
        b.rev_ag = 0.66;
        b.rev_tenths_comm = Some(10);
        b.rev_smi = 0.58;
        b.rev_ls_db = 10.1;
        b.rev_added_s = 517.0;
    }

    /// film(seconds, seed): a film-like programme, lines of 2-3 s, then 2.5-4 s of quieter sound (music, effects),
    /// so that its level spread is a film's (about 23 dB). Returns (mix, centre). Py: test_audio_similarity.film, in
    /// its order of random draws.
    fn film(seconds: usize, seed: u64) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
        let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(seed);
        let (mut mix, mut centre) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        while mix.len() < seconds * FPS {
            let frames = rnd.randint(2 * FPS as i64, 3 * FPS as i64) as usize;
            let line = speech(&mut rnd, frames, -20.0, -30.0);
            mix.extend_from_slice(&line);
            centre.extend(line.iter().map(|v| v - 1.0));
            let n = rnd.randint((2.5 * FPS as f64) as i64, 4 * FPS as i64);
            for _ in 0..n {
                mix.push(-45.0 + rnd.uniform(-3.0, 3.0));
            }
            for _ in 0..n {
                centre.push(-75.0 + rnd.uniform(-1.0, 1.0));
            }
        }
        mix.truncate(seconds * FPS);
        centre.truncate(seconds * FPS);
        (mix, centre)
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_commentary_whose_film_plays_in_its_pauses_keeps_its_verdict() {
        assert_eq!(v(|_, _| {}), Verdict::Commentary);
        // measures written before the reverse block existed are judged by the earlier reverse test, which blocked it
        assert_eq!(verdict(&Measures::Run(pans()), &Rule::default()), Verdict::ReferenceUnclear);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_reverse_run_with_the_commentary_pattern_makes_the_reference_unclear() {
        assert_eq!(v(|_, b| pattern(b)), Verdict::ReferenceUnclear);
        // the reverse run cannot be judged
        assert_eq!(v(|_, b| { pattern(b); b.rev_gap_s = 29.0; }), Verdict::Commentary);
        // no pattern: a condition fails
        assert_eq!(v(|_, b| { pattern(b); b.rev_ls_db = 13.1; }), Verdict::Commentary);
        assert_eq!(v(|_, b| { pattern(b); b.rev_error = "too short".to_string(); }), Verdict::Commentary);
        let unjudged = |r: &mut Run, b: &mut RevBlock| {
            pattern(b);
            r.gap_s = 29.0;
            r.dc = 0.02;
            r.ag = 0.10;
            r.tenths = 0;
            r.tenths_comm = 0;
        };
        // whatever the forward run says
        assert_eq!(v(unjudged), Verdict::ReferenceUnclear);
        assert!(not_judged(&m(unjudged), &Rule::default()).contains("90 s"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn swapped_exchanges_the_two_runs() {
        let measures = m(|r, _| r.gain_db = 10.5);
        let back = swapped(&measures).expect("the measures carry a reverse block");
        let run = back.run().expect("the reverse run had no error");
        assert_eq!((run.dc, run.ag, run.gap_s, run.ls_db), (0.06, 0.31, 470.0, 17.1));
        let Reverse::Block(block) = &run.rev else { panic!("swapped gives a reverse block") };
        assert_eq!((block.rev_dc, block.rev_ag, block.rev_tenths_comm), (0.08, 0.54, Some(9)));
        // the programme against the commentary as reference
        assert_eq!(verdict(&back, &Rule::default()), Verdict::ReferenceUnclear);
        assert_eq!(swapped(&Measures::Run(pans())), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_programme_against_a_commentary_taken_as_the_reference_is_kept_and_flagged() {
        let m = analyse(comment(), mix(), None, true, &Constants::default());
        assert!(reverse_pattern(&m, &Rule::default()));
        assert_eq!(verdict(&m, &Rule::default()), Verdict::ReferenceUnclear);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_commentary_that_pauses_over_a_film_is_not_blocked_by_its_pauses() {
        let (film_mix, film_centre) = film(900, 3);
        let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(10);
        let mut voice: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
        // one speaker: 2.8 s of talk, 1.2 s of pause, the film 26 dB down underneath
        // (int(2.8 * FPS) is 140 and int(1.2 * FPS) is 60 in Python; the casts truncate the same products)
        while voice.len() < film_mix.len() {
            voice.extend(speech(&mut rnd, (2.8 * FPS as f64) as usize, -18.0, -27.0));
            voice.extend(std::iter::repeat(-100.0).take((1.2 * FPS as f64) as usize));
        }
        let cand: Vec<f64> = voice.iter().zip(&film_mix).map(|(&v, &x)| power_sum(v, x - 26.0)).collect();
        let m = analyse(&film_mix, &cand, Some(film_centre.as_slice()), true, &Constants::default());
        let Reverse::Block(block) = &m.run().expect("measured").rev else { panic!("analyse gives a reverse block") };
        // the earlier reverse test would block it
        assert!(block.rev_gap_s >= 90.0 && block.rev_ag >= 0.30);
        assert!(!reverse_pattern(&m, &Rule::default()));
        assert_eq!(verdict(&m, &Rule::default()), Verdict::Commentary);
    }
}

/// New: Rule::NAMES, get and set (spec 3.3: --set for a rule key).
mod rule_set {
    use crate::audio::measures::{Num, NumKind, SetError};
    use crate::audio::rule::Rule;

    #[test]
    fn names_defaults_and_serde_follow_the_python_rule() {
        let expected: [(&str, Num); 20] = [
            ("overlap_min", Num::Float(0.90)),
            ("main_silent_max", Num::Float(0.10)),
            ("gap_s_min", Num::Float(90.0)),
            ("dc_max", Num::Float(0.30)),
            ("ag_min", Num::Float(0.50)),
            ("tenths_min", Num::Int(6)),
            ("tenths_share", Num::Float(0.90)),
            ("smi_min", Num::Float(0.50)),
            ("ls_max", Num::Float(13.0)),
            ("added_s_min", Num::Float(60.0)),
            ("ad_dc_min", Num::Float(0.90)),
            ("ad_adl_max", Num::Float(0.02)),
            ("ad_ag_min", Num::Float(0.15)),
            ("ad_ag_s_min", Num::Float(45.0)),
            ("ad_tenths_share", Num::Float(0.60)),
            ("note_comm_dc_max", Num::Float(0.50)),
            ("note_comm_ag_min", Num::Float(0.30)),
            ("note_ad_dc_min", Num::Float(0.80)),
            ("note_ad_ag_min", Num::Float(0.10)),
            ("note_ad_ag_s_min", Num::Float(30.0)),
        ];
        assert_eq!(Rule::NAMES.map(|(name, _)| name), expected.map(|(name, _)| name));
        let ints: Vec<&str> = Rule::NAMES.iter().filter(|(_, kind)| *kind == NumKind::Int).map(|(name, _)| *name).collect();
        assert_eq!(ints, ["tenths_min"]);
        let rule = Rule::default();
        for (name, value) in expected {
            assert_eq!(rule.get(name), Some(value), "{name}");
        }
        assert_eq!(rule.get("DC_MAX"), None);
        let value = serde_json::to_value(&rule).expect("serialisable");
        let keys: Vec<&str> = value.as_object().expect("an object").keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
        assert_eq!(keys, expected.map(|(name, _)| name));
        assert!(value["tenths_min"].is_i64());
        assert!(value["gap_s_min"].is_f64());
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_matches_a_rule_key_whatever_its_case_and_keeps_a_float_a_float() {
        let mut rule = Rule::default();
        assert_eq!(rule.set("DC_MAX", 0.25), Ok(Num::Float(0.25)));
        assert_eq!(rule.dc_max, 0.25);
        assert_eq!(rule.set("Ls_Max", 12.0), Ok(Num::Float(12.0)));
        assert_eq!(rule.get("ls_max"), Some(Num::Float(12.0)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_takes_a_whole_number_for_tenths_min_and_refuses_what_is_not_a_rule_key() {
        let mut rule = Rule::default();
        assert_eq!(rule.set("TENTHS_MIN", 7.0), Ok(Num::Int(7)));
        assert_eq!(rule.tenths_min, 7);
        assert_eq!(rule.set("tenths_min", 6.5), Err(SetError::NotWhole));
        assert_eq!(rule.tenths_min, 7);
        // a measure constant, not a rule key: parse_sets (Task 8) tries the constants next
        assert_eq!(rule.set("SILENT_DB", -80.0), Err(SetError::Unknown));
        assert_eq!(rule.set("dc", 0.1), Err(SetError::Unknown));
        assert_eq!(rule, Rule { tenths_min: 7, ..Rule::default() });
    }
}

/// New: the Python's strings, verbatim.
mod spellings {
    use crate::audio::rule::{meaning, Verdict, VETO_MEANING};

    #[test]
    fn verdicts_are_spelt_as_the_python_writes_them() {
        let names: Vec<&str> = Verdict::ALL.iter().map(|v| v.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            names,
            [
                "duplicate",
                "commentary",
                "commentary-cross-language",
                "reference-unclear",
                "ad-pattern",
                "note-commentary",
                "note-ad",
                "keep",
                "not-judged",
            ]
        );
        for v in Verdict::ALL {
            assert_eq!(v.as_str().parse::<Verdict>(), Ok(v));
            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(v).expect("serialisable"), serde_json::Value::String(v.as_str().to_string()));
            let back: Verdict = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::Value::String(v.as_str().to_string())).expect("a verdict");
            assert_eq!(back, v);
        }
        assert!("Commentary".parse::<Verdict>().is_err());
        assert!("commentary_cross_language".parse::<Verdict>().is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn meanings_are_the_python_texts() {
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::Duplicate), "exact duplicate (same packets): keep the first copy, drop this one; no audio analysis needed");
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::Commentary), "commentary pattern: kept and flagged for review until experiment 13 answers yes, then dropped");
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage), "commentary pattern on a track in another language than the reference: keep and flag for review (commentary_detected); never dropped by content until real dubs in a wanted language have been measured (EXP-13 addendum 9.2)");
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::ReferenceUnclear), "the main track looks like a commentary over this one (reverse run): one of the two is not what its rank says (a commentary or a stem ranked first, or a stem among the candidates): keep, review");
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::AdPattern), "audio-description pattern: keep, note possible_audio_description (never dropped by content)");
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::NoteCommentary), "keep, note possible_commentary");
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::NoteAd), "keep, note possible_audio_description");
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::Keep), "keep: programme audio, nothing added");
        assert_eq!(meaning(Verdict::NotJudged), "keep: no content verdict");
        assert_eq!(VETO_MEANING, "the position veto holds (row 0, D21): the reference may not be the programme, so no commentary is confirmed on this title: keep, review (audio_reference_unclear)");
    }
}
```

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(clippy::module_inception)] // named after the Python class it ports
mod measures {
    //! Ported from test_audio_similarity.py::Measures (6 tests), every assertion: Task 4 wrote the assertions on the
    //! measures; Task 5 appended the verdict() and not_judged() assertions of core::audio::rule after them (Task 4's
    //! "Hand-over to Task 5" lines, with absolute paths).
    use super::*;
    use crate::testsupport::{commentary, FPS};

    #[test]
    fn a_quieter_delayed_copy_of_the_programme_is_kept() {
        let (mix, centre) = mix_centre();
        // 60 ms late, 6 dB down
        let mut copy = vec![-100.0; 3];
        copy.extend(mix[..mix.len() - 3].iter().map(|v| v - 6.0));
        let m = analyse(mix, &copy, Some(centre.as_slice()), true, &Constants::default());
        let r = m.run().expect("measured");
        assert_eq!(r.lag_ms, Some(60));
        assert!(r.dc >= 0.9, "dc {}", r.dc);
        assert_eq!(r.ag, 0.0);
        assert_eq!(crate::audio::rule::verdict(&m, &crate::audio::rule::Rule::default()), crate::audio::rule::Verdict::Keep);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_voice_talking_through_the_programme_has_the_commentary_pattern() {
        let (mix, centre) = mix_centre();
        let m = analyse(mix, &commentary(mix, 7), Some(centre.as_slice()), true, &Constants::default());
        let r = m.run().expect("measured");
        assert!(r.dc <= 0.30, "dc {}", r.dc);
        assert!(r.ag >= 0.50, "ag {}", r.ag);
        assert_eq!(r.tenths_comm, r.tenths);
        assert!(r.smi >= 0.50, "smi {}", r.smi);
        assert!(r.ls_db <= 13.0, "ls_db {}", r.ls_db);
        assert_eq!(crate::audio::rule::not_judged(&m, &crate::audio::rule::Rule::default()), "");
        assert_eq!(crate::audio::rule::verdict(&m, &crate::audio::rule::Rule::default()), crate::audio::rule::Verdict::Commentary);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_same_voice_is_not_confirmed_when_the_main_is_not_continuous_programme_sound() {
        let (mix0, centre0) = mix_centre();
        let (mut mix, mut centre) = (mix0.clone(), centre0.clone());
        // 3 s of digital silence in every 10 s: an isolated score, say
        for t in (0..mix.len()).step_by(10 * FPS) {
            for u in t..mix.len().min(t + 3 * FPS) {
                mix[u] = -100.0;
                centre[u] = -100.0;
            }
        }
        let m = analyse(&mix, &commentary(mix0, 7), Some(centre.as_slice()), true, &Constants::default());
        let r = m.run().expect("measured");
        // what not_judged() reads to give its "digitally silent" reason: the overlap passes, main_silent does not
        assert!(r.overlap >= 0.90, "overlap {}", r.overlap);
        assert!(r.main_silent > 0.10, "main_silent {}", r.main_silent);
        assert!(crate::audio::rule::not_judged(&m, &crate::audio::rule::Rule::default()).contains("silent"));
        assert_ne!(crate::audio::rule::verdict(&m, &crate::audio::rule::Rule::default()), crate::audio::rule::Verdict::Commentary);
    }

    #[test]
    fn steady_music_added_in_the_gaps_is_not_a_commentary() {
        let (mix, centre) = mix_centre();
        let cand: Vec<f64> =
            mix.iter().zip(centre.iter()).map(|(&m, &c)| if c > -50.0 { m } else { -35.0 }).collect();
        let m = analyse(mix, &cand, Some(centre.as_slice()), true, &Constants::default());
        let r = m.run().expect("measured");
        assert!(r.dc >= 0.8, "dc {}", r.dc);
        let v = crate::audio::rule::verdict(&m, &crate::audio::rule::Rule::default());
        assert!(![crate::audio::rule::Verdict::Commentary, crate::audio::rule::Verdict::ReferenceUnclear].contains(&v), "{v:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_candidate_covering_only_part_of_the_main_is_not_confirmed() {
        let (mix, centre) = mix_centre();
        let comm = commentary(mix, 7);
        let m = analyse(mix, &comm[..mix.len() * 7 / 10], Some(centre.as_slice()), true, &Constants::default());
        let r = m.run().expect("measured");
        assert!(r.overlap < 0.9, "overlap {}", r.overlap);
        assert_ne!(crate::audio::rule::verdict(&m, &crate::audio::rule::Rule::default()), crate::audio::rule::Verdict::Commentary);
    }

    #[test]
    fn too_little_audio_gives_no_verdict() {
        let (mix, _) = mix_centre();
        let m = analyse(&mix[..500], &mix[..500], None, true, &Constants::default());
        assert_eq!(m, Measures::Error { frames: Some(500), error: "too short".to_string() });
        assert_eq!(crate::audio::rule::verdict(&m, &crate::audio::rule::Rule::default()), crate::audio::rule::Verdict::NotJudged);
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the rule: thresholds, verdicts and patterns**

Replace the whole of `crates/core/src/audio/rule.rs` with:

```rust
//! The audio content rule of spec 8.6 (EXP-13-design.md sections 3 and 9; owner decision D21): the decision
//! thresholds, the verdict of one measured pair, the position veto (row 0) and the verdicts of a whole level folder.
//! Ported from scripts/phase0/audio_similarity.py: RULE, EARLIER_REVERSE, commentary_pattern, ad_pattern, not_judged,
//! reverse_pattern, verdict, MEANING and VETO_MEANING first; first_of_language, position_veto, cross_language and
//! results after them. Stereo width, codec and track position never decide what a track is (D15): position only
//! withholds a drop, through the veto.

use crate::audio::measures::{ok, reverse_measures, Measures, Num, NumKind, Reverse, Run, SetError};
use crate::recording::py_repr_str;

/// The rule's version, in the harness's cache key and the snapshot's "code"; bumped by hand with every change to a
/// measure, a constant's default or a threshold (spec 3.3, RP5). Replaces the Python's SHA-1 of audio_similarity.py.
pub const RULE_VERSION: u32 = 1;

/// The decision thresholds, with the Python's defaults (every one PROVISIONAL: EXP-13-design.md, section 3); fields
/// in RULE's order, so the serde form is the snapshot's "rule" (tenths_min an int, the others floats). Py: RULE.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub overlap_min: f64,
    pub main_silent_max: f64,
    pub gap_s_min: f64,
    pub dc_max: f64,
    pub ag_min: f64,
    pub tenths_min: i64,
    pub tenths_share: f64,
    pub smi_min: f64,
    pub ls_max: f64,
    pub added_s_min: f64,
    pub ad_dc_min: f64,
    pub ad_adl_max: f64,
    pub ad_ag_min: f64,
    pub ad_ag_s_min: f64,
    pub ad_tenths_share: f64,
    pub note_comm_dc_max: f64,
    pub note_comm_ag_min: f64,
    pub note_ad_dc_min: f64,
    pub note_ad_ag_min: f64,
    pub note_ad_ag_s_min: f64,
}

impl Default for Rule {
    /// RULE as audio_similarity.py writes it.
    fn default() -> Rule {
        Rule {
            overlap_min: 0.90,
            main_silent_max: 0.10,
            gap_s_min: 90.0,
            dc_max: 0.30,
            ag_min: 0.50,
            tenths_min: 6,
            tenths_share: 0.90,
            smi_min: 0.50,
            ls_max: 13.0,
            added_s_min: 60.0,
            ad_dc_min: 0.90,
            ad_adl_max: 0.02,
            ad_ag_min: 0.15,
            ad_ag_s_min: 45.0,
            ad_tenths_share: 0.60,
            note_comm_dc_max: 0.50,
            note_comm_ag_min: 0.30,
            note_ad_dc_min: 0.80,
            note_ad_ag_min: 0.10,
            note_ad_ag_s_min: 30.0,
        }
    }
}

impl Rule {
    /// The 20 keys in RULE's order, each with its kind (only tenths_min is Int).
    pub const NAMES: [(&'static str, NumKind); 20] = [
        ("overlap_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("main_silent_max", NumKind::Float),
        ("gap_s_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("dc_max", NumKind::Float),
        ("ag_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("tenths_min", NumKind::Int),
        ("tenths_share", NumKind::Float),
        ("smi_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("ls_max", NumKind::Float),
        ("added_s_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("ad_dc_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("ad_adl_max", NumKind::Float),
        ("ad_ag_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("ad_ag_s_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("ad_tenths_share", NumKind::Float),
        ("note_comm_dc_max", NumKind::Float),
        ("note_comm_ag_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("note_ad_dc_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("note_ad_ag_min", NumKind::Float),
        ("note_ad_ag_s_min", NumKind::Float),
    ];

    /// The value of a key exactly as NAMES spells it; None for any other name. Py: RULE[key].
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Num> {
        let value = match key {
            "tenths_min" => return Some(Num::Int(self.tenths_min)),
            "overlap_min" => self.overlap_min,
            "main_silent_max" => self.main_silent_max,
            "gap_s_min" => self.gap_s_min,
            "dc_max" => self.dc_max,
            "ag_min" => self.ag_min,
            "tenths_share" => self.tenths_share,
            "smi_min" => self.smi_min,
            "ls_max" => self.ls_max,
            "added_s_min" => self.added_s_min,
            "ad_dc_min" => self.ad_dc_min,
            "ad_adl_max" => self.ad_adl_max,
            "ad_ag_min" => self.ad_ag_min,
            "ad_ag_s_min" => self.ad_ag_s_min,
            "ad_tenths_share" => self.ad_tenths_share,
            "note_comm_dc_max" => self.note_comm_dc_max,
            "note_comm_ag_min" => self.note_comm_ag_min,
            "note_ad_dc_min" => self.note_ad_dc_min,
            "note_ad_ag_min" => self.note_ad_ag_min,
            "note_ad_ag_s_min" => self.note_ad_ag_s_min,
            _ => return None,
        };
        Some(Num::Float(value))
    }

    /// Sets a key as `--set NAME=VALUE` does for a rule threshold (Py: parse_sets' rule branch) and returns the value
    /// stored. The name is matched case-insensitively: it is lower-cased here as parse_sets lower-cases it (the caller
    /// may lower-case it first). tenths_min takes a whole number only and stores it as an int (NotWhole otherwise,
    /// the rule unchanged); every other key keeps the value as a float. Unknown for a name that is not a key of RULE
    /// (parse_sets then tries the measure constants). The value is finite: parse_sets refuses a non-finite one, with
    /// the Python's message, before it calls this; a non-finite value for tenths_min is NotWhole here. The messages
    /// that list the valid names belong to parse_sets (Task 8), which has the item as the user typed it.
    pub fn set(&mut self, key: &str, value: f64) -> Result<Num, SetError> {
        let key = key.to_lowercase();
        let Some(&(_, kind)) = Rule::NAMES.iter().find(|(name, _)| *name == key) else {
            return Err(SetError::Unknown);
        };
        match kind {
            NumKind::Int => {
                // Python: `if value != int(value)`; tenths_min is the only Int key of NAMES.
                if !value.is_finite() || value != value.trunc() {
                    return Err(SetError::NotWhole);
                }
                self.tenths_min = value as i64;
                Ok(Num::Int(self.tenths_min))
            }
            NumKind::Float => {
                let slot = self.float_slot(&key).ok_or(SetError::Unknown)?;
                *slot = value;
                Ok(Num::Float(value))
            }
        }
    }

    /// The f64 field a Float key of NAMES names.
    fn float_slot(&mut self, key: &str) -> Option<&mut f64> {
        Some(match key {
            "overlap_min" => &mut self.overlap_min,
            "main_silent_max" => &mut self.main_silent_max,
            "gap_s_min" => &mut self.gap_s_min,
            "dc_max" => &mut self.dc_max,
            "ag_min" => &mut self.ag_min,
            "tenths_share" => &mut self.tenths_share,
            "smi_min" => &mut self.smi_min,
            "ls_max" => &mut self.ls_max,
            "added_s_min" => &mut self.added_s_min,
            "ad_dc_min" => &mut self.ad_dc_min,
            "ad_adl_max" => &mut self.ad_adl_max,
            "ad_ag_min" => &mut self.ad_ag_min,
            "ad_ag_s_min" => &mut self.ad_ag_s_min,
            "ad_tenths_share" => &mut self.ad_tenths_share,
            "note_comm_dc_max" => &mut self.note_comm_dc_max,
            "note_comm_ag_min" => &mut self.note_comm_ag_min,
            "note_ad_dc_min" => &mut self.note_ad_dc_min,
            "note_ad_ag_min" => &mut self.note_ad_ag_min,
            "note_ad_ag_s_min" => &mut self.note_ad_ag_s_min,
            _ => return None,
        })
    }
}

/// The earlier reverse test (EXP-13-design.md section 2 item 13: 90 s of the candidate's gaps, reverse AG 0.30). It
/// is replaced by the reverse commentary pattern (addendum 9.3) and used only for measures that carry rev_gap_s and
/// rev_ag alone (Reverse::Earlier, as the code before 2026-10-06 wrote them): it can only keep. Py: EARLIER_REVERSE.
pub const EARLIER_REVERSE_GAP_S_MIN: f64 = 90.0;
pub const EARLIER_REVERSE_AG_MIN: f64 = 0.30;

/// A candidate's verdict; `as_str` and serde give the Python's strings; ALL is audio_dataset.VERDICTS' order.
/// Py: the verdict strings.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum Verdict {
    Duplicate,
    Commentary,
    CommentaryCrossLanguage,
    ReferenceUnclear,
    AdPattern,
    NoteCommentary,
    NoteAd,
    Keep,
    NotJudged,
}

impl Verdict {
    /// duplicate, commentary, commentary-cross-language, reference-unclear, ad-pattern, note-commentary, note-ad,
    /// keep, not-judged. Py: audio_dataset.VERDICTS.
    pub const ALL: [Verdict; 9] = [
        Verdict::Duplicate,
        Verdict::Commentary,
        Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage,
        Verdict::ReferenceUnclear,
        Verdict::AdPattern,
        Verdict::NoteCommentary,
        Verdict::NoteAd,
        Verdict::Keep,
        Verdict::NotJudged,
    ];

    /// The Python's string.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Verdict::Duplicate => "duplicate",
            Verdict::Commentary => "commentary",
            Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage => "commentary-cross-language",
            Verdict::ReferenceUnclear => "reference-unclear",
            Verdict::AdPattern => "ad-pattern",
            Verdict::NoteCommentary => "note-commentary",
            Verdict::NoteAd => "note-ad",
            Verdict::Keep => "keep",
            Verdict::NotJudged => "not-judged",
        }
    }
}

impl std::str::FromStr for Verdict {
    type Err = String;

    /// Only the Python's spelling of a verdict; Err "'<text>' is not a verdict" otherwise.
    fn from_str(text: &str) -> Result<Verdict, String> {
        Verdict::ALL
            .into_iter()
            .find(|v| v.as_str() == text)
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("{} is not a verdict", py_repr_str(text)))
    }
}

/// The report's meaning of a verdict, verbatim. Py: MEANING.
pub fn meaning(v: Verdict) -> &'static str {
    match v {
        Verdict::Duplicate => "exact duplicate (same packets): keep the first copy, drop this one; no audio analysis needed",
        Verdict::Commentary => "commentary pattern: kept and flagged for review until experiment 13 answers yes, then dropped",
        Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage => "commentary pattern on a track in another language than the reference: keep and flag for review (commentary_detected); never dropped by content until real dubs in a wanted language have been measured (EXP-13 addendum 9.2)",
        Verdict::ReferenceUnclear => "the main track looks like a commentary over this one (reverse run): one of the two is not what its rank says (a commentary or a stem ranked first, or a stem among the candidates): keep, review",
        Verdict::AdPattern => "audio-description pattern: keep, note possible_audio_description (never dropped by content)",
        Verdict::NoteCommentary => "keep, note possible_commentary",
        Verdict::NoteAd => "keep, note possible_audio_description",
        Verdict::Keep => "keep: programme audio, nothing added",
        Verdict::NotJudged => "keep: no content verdict",
    }
}

/// The veto's meaning, verbatim. Py: VETO_MEANING.
pub const VETO_MEANING: &str = "the position veto holds (row 0, D21): the reference may not be the programme, so no commentary is confirmed on this title: keep, review (audio_reference_unclear)";

/// The commentary pattern of the forward run or of a reverse run (rows 3 and 4). Py: commentary_pattern.
pub fn commentary_pattern(m: &Run, rule: &Rule) -> bool {
    ok(m.dc)
        && m.dc <= rule.dc_max
        && ok(m.ag)
        && m.ag >= rule.ag_min
        && m.tenths >= rule.tenths_min
        && (m.tenths_comm as f64) >= rule.tenths_share * (m.tenths as f64)
        && ok(m.smi)
        && m.smi >= rule.smi_min
        && m.ls_db <= rule.ls_max
        && m.added_s >= rule.added_s_min
}

/// The audio-description pattern (row 5). Py: ad_pattern.
pub fn ad_pattern(m: &Run, rule: &Rule) -> bool {
    ok(m.dc)
        && m.dc >= rule.ad_dc_min
        && ok(m.adl)
        && m.adl <= rule.ad_adl_max
        && ok(m.ag)
        && m.ag >= rule.ad_ag_min
        && m.ag_s >= rule.ad_ag_s_min
        && m.tenths >= rule.tenths_min
        && (m.tenths_ad as f64) >= rule.ad_tenths_share * (m.tenths as f64)
        && ok(m.smi)
        && m.smi >= rule.smi_min
}

/// Why the content rule may not confirm anything for this pair (the error, or one of the four sentences), "" when it
/// may. Py: not_judged.
pub fn not_judged(m: &Measures, rule: &Rule) -> String {
    let run = match m {
        Measures::Error { error, .. } => return error.clone(),
        Measures::Run(run) => run,
    };
    if run.overlap < rule.overlap_min {
        return "the tracks overlap for less than 90% of the main track".to_string();
    }
    if run.main_silent > rule.main_silent_max {
        return "the main track is digitally silent for more than 10% of the time (not continuous programme sound)".to_string();
    }
    if run.gap_s < rule.gap_s_min {
        return "the main track has less than 90 s of dialogue gaps".to_string();
    }
    if !ok(run.dc) {
        return "the main track has no dialogue windows".to_string();
    }
    String::new()
}

/// True when the reverse run may be judged and has the commentary pattern: the reference looks like a commentary
/// over the candidate (EXP-13 addendum 9.3). The same thresholds as the forward pattern. Py: reverse_pattern.
pub fn reverse_pattern(m: &Measures, rule: &Rule) -> bool {
    match reverse_measures(m) {
        Some(r) => match r.run() {
            Some(run) => not_judged(&r, rule).is_empty() && commentary_pattern(run, rule),
            None => false,
        },
        None => false,
    }
}

/// One verdict of rows 3 to 9: commentary, reference-unclear, ad-pattern, note-commentary, note-ad, keep, or
/// not-judged for an error (never duplicate or commentary-cross-language: results gives those). reference-unclear:
/// the reverse run has the commentary pattern, whatever the forward run says; for measures without a reverse block,
/// the earlier reverse test applies. Py: verdict.
pub fn verdict(m: &Measures, rule: &Rule) -> Verdict {
    let run = match m {
        Measures::Error { .. } => return Verdict::NotJudged,
        Measures::Run(run) => run,
    };
    let why = not_judged(m, rule);
    if reverse_measures(m).is_some() {
        if reverse_pattern(m, rule) {
            return Verdict::ReferenceUnclear;
        }
        if why.is_empty() && commentary_pattern(run, rule) {
            return Verdict::Commentary;
        }
    } else if why.is_empty() && commentary_pattern(run, rule) {
        // m.get("rev_ag", nan) and m.get("rev_gap_s", 0.0): absent keys never pass the earlier test.
        let earlier = match run.rev {
            Reverse::Earlier { rev_gap_s, rev_ag } => {
                ok(rev_ag) && rev_gap_s >= EARLIER_REVERSE_GAP_S_MIN && rev_ag >= EARLIER_REVERSE_AG_MIN
            }
            _ => false,
        };
        return if earlier { Verdict::ReferenceUnclear } else { Verdict::Commentary };
    }
    if why.is_empty() && ad_pattern(run, rule) {
        return Verdict::AdPattern;
    }
    if ok(run.dc) && ok(run.ag) && run.dc <= rule.note_comm_dc_max && run.ag >= rule.note_comm_ag_min {
        return Verdict::NoteCommentary;
    }
    if ok(run.dc)
        && ok(run.ag)
        && run.dc >= rule.note_ad_dc_min
        && run.ag >= rule.note_ad_ag_min
        && run.ag_s >= rule.note_ad_ag_s_min
    {
        return Verdict::NoteAd;
    }
    Verdict::Keep
}
```

```rust
//! Tests of core::audio::reference, all new: the ported Python tests reach these functions only through results
//! (rule/tests.rs) and levels_args (Task 8). Every expected value is what the Python function returns for the same
//! input (audio_similarity.py and audio_dataset.py at the port's commit).

use crate::audio::levels::Fields;
use crate::audio::reference::{
    ffprobe_audio, first_of_language, is_lossless, manifest_stream, original_language, placed_first,
    programme_reference, rank, read_streams, wanted, AudioStream,
};
use crate::recording::files::FfprobeStream;
use crate::recording::{MemTree, Ordered, PathKey};

/// A stream as placed_first takes it: (stream, channels, lossless, language, description).
fn s(stream: i64, channels: i64, lossless: bool, language: &str, description: &str) -> AudioStream {
    AudioStream { stream, channels, lossless, language: language.to_string(), description: description.to_string() }
}

/// A manifest line's fields, in order.
fn fields(pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Fields {
    Ordered(pairs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v.to_string())).collect())
}

/// One entry of an ffprobe stream list; no tags at all when `tags` is empty.
fn probe(
    index: i64,
    codec_type: &str,
    codec: Option<&str>,
    profile: Option<&str>,
    channels: Option<i64>,
    layout: Option<&str>,
    tags: &[(&str, &str)],
) -> FfprobeStream {
    FfprobeStream {
        index,
        codec_type: Some(codec_type.to_string()),
        codec_name: codec.map(str::to_string),
        profile: profile.map(str::to_string),
        channels,
        channel_layout: layout.map(str::to_string),
        tags: if tags.is_empty() {
            None
        } else {
            Some(Ordered(tags.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v.to_string())).collect()))
        },
    }
}

#[test]
fn is_lossless_names_the_lossless_codecs_and_dts_hd_ma() {
    let cases = [
        (Some("truehd"), None),
        (Some("mlp"), None),
        (Some("flac"), None),
        (Some("pcm_s24le"), None),
        (Some("dts"), Some("DTS-HD MA + DTS:X")),
        (Some("dts"), Some("DTS-HD_MA")), // a manifest's spelling
        (Some("eac3"), Some("DTS-HD MA")),
        (Some("dts"), Some("DTS")),
        (Some("ac3"), None),
        (None, None),
    ];
    assert_eq!(
        cases.map(|(codec, profile)| is_lossless(codec, profile)),
        [true, true, true, true, true, true, true, false, false, false]
    );
}

#[test]
fn rank_and_placed_first_follow_8_6_step_3() {
    assert_eq!(rank(&s(2, 6, false, "eng", "x")), (-6, true, 2));
    // most channels, then lossless, then the earlier stream
    let streams = [s(1, 2, false, "eng", "x"), s(2, 6, false, "eng", "x"), s(3, 6, true, "eng", "x")];
    assert_eq!(placed_first(&streams).stream, 3);
}

#[test]
fn placed_first_applies_the_guards_g1_and_g2() {
    // G1: a lossy stream of two channels or fewer never comes before a lossless one
    assert_eq!(placed_first(&[s(1, 2, false, "eng", "x"), s(2, 1, true, "eng", "x")]).stream, 2);
    // G2: a lossy stereo top that is not the first stream and has more channels than it gives way to it
    assert_eq!(placed_first(&[s(1, 1, false, "eng", "x"), s(2, 2, false, "eng", "x")]).stream, 1);
    assert_eq!(placed_first(&[s(1, 2, false, "eng", "x"), s(2, 2, false, "eng", "x")]).stream, 1);
}

#[test]
fn ffprobe_audio_lists_the_audio_streams_in_file_order_with_their_description() {
    let streams = [
        probe(0, "video", Some("hevc"), None, None, None, &[]),
        probe(1, "audio", Some("truehd"), None, Some(8), Some("7.1"), &[("language", "eng"), ("title", "Main")]),
        probe(2, "audio", Some("ac3"), None, None, None, &[]),
        probe(3, "audio", Some("dts"), Some("DTS-HD MA"), Some(6), None, &[("language", "")]),
        probe(4, "subtitle", Some("hdmv_pgs_subtitle"), None, None, None, &[]),
    ];
    assert_eq!(
        ffprobe_audio(&streams),
        [
            s(1, 8, true, "eng", "truehd 8 ch 7.1 Main"),
            s(2, 0, false, "und", "ac3 None ch"),
            s(3, 6, true, "und", "dts DTS-HD MA 6 ch"),
        ]
    );
}

#[test]
fn read_streams_is_none_without_a_streams_json_file() {
    let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
    tree.insert_dir("a");
    assert_eq!(read_streams(&tree, &PathKey::new("a")), Ok(None));
    // read as utf-8-sig: a byte-order mark is allowed
    tree.insert_file(
        "b/streams.json",
        "\u{feff}{\"streams\": [{\"index\": 0, \"codec_type\": \"video\"}, {\"index\": 1, \"codec_type\": \"audio\", \"codec_name\": \"ac3\", \"channels\": 2}]}",
    );
    let list = read_streams(&tree, &PathKey::new("b")).expect("it parses").expect("it is there");
    assert_eq!(list.iter().map(|stream| stream.index).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [0, 1]);
    tree.insert_file("c/streams.json", "not json");
    assert!(read_streams(&tree, &PathKey::new("c")).is_err());
    // a folder named streams.json is not the file
    tree.insert_dir("d/streams.json");
    assert_eq!(read_streams(&tree, &PathKey::new("d")), Ok(None));
}

#[test]
fn manifest_stream_reads_a_manifest_line() {
    assert_eq!(
        manifest_stream(&fields(&[("cand", "3"), ("codec", "dts"), ("profile", "DTS-HD_MA"), ("channels", "6"), ("language", "eng")])),
        Ok(s(3, 6, true, "eng", "dts 6 ch"))
    );
    // channels that are not an int count 0; no codec is "?"; no language is "und"
    assert_eq!(manifest_stream(&fields(&[("cand", "4"), ("channels", "x")])), Ok(s(4, 0, false, "und", "? 0 ch")));
    assert_eq!(
        manifest_stream(&fields(&[("main", "1"), ("codec", "ac3"), ("channels", "2"), ("language", "fra")])),
        Ok(s(1, 2, false, "fra", "ac3 2 ch"))
    );
    // info.get("cand") or info.get("main"): an empty cand= falls back to main=
    assert_eq!(manifest_stream(&fields(&[("cand", ""), ("main", "2")])), Ok(s(2, 0, false, "und", "? 0 ch")));
    assert_eq!(
        manifest_stream(&fields(&[("cand", "x")])),
        Err("invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'x'".to_string())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        manifest_stream(&fields(&[])),
        Err("int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a number, not 'NoneType'".to_string())
    );
}

#[test]
fn original_language_says_how_it_was_found() {
    let unreadable = "original language unknown (no readable tmdb.json)";
    let gives_none = "original language unknown (tmdb.json gives none)";
    let cases: [(&str, Option<&str>, &[&str], &str); 12] = [
        ("no-file", None, &[], unreadable),
        ("not-json", Some("not json"), &[], unreadable),
        ("a-list", Some("[]"), &[], unreadable),
        ("no-key", Some("{}"), &[], gives_none),
        ("empty", Some(r#"{"original_language": ""}"#), &[], gives_none),
        ("en", Some(r#"{"original_language": "en"}"#), &[], "original language English (TMDb en)"),
        (
            "xx",
            Some(r#"{"original_language": "xx"}"#),
            &[],
            "original language none (TMDb xx: a work without speech; English is the reference language)",
        ),
        (
            "qq",
            Some(r#"{"original_language": "qq"}"#),
            &[],
            "original language unknown (TMDb 'qq' is not in audio_similarity.ISO639)",
        ),
        ("es", Some(r#"{"original_language": "es"}"#), &["spa"], "original language spa (TMDb es)"),
        ("de", Some(r#"{"original_language": "de"}"#), &["deu", "ger"], "original language deu/ger (TMDb de)"),
        (
            "a-number",
            Some(r#"{"original_language": 5}"#),
            &[],
            "original language unknown (TMDb 5 is not in audio_similarity.ISO639)",
        ),
        ("bom", Some("\u{feff}{\"original_language\": \"ja\"}"), &["jpn"], "original language jpn (TMDb ja)"),
    ];
    let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
    for (slug, text, codes, what) in cases {
        tree.insert_dir(slug);
        if let Some(text) = text {
            tree.insert_file(&format!("{slug}/tmdb.json"), text);
        }
        let (got_codes, got_what) = original_language(&tree, &PathKey::new(slug));
        assert_eq!((got_codes, got_what.as_str()), (codes, what), "{slug}");
    }
}

#[test]
```

```rust
/// CENTRE.
fn centre() -> &'static [f64] {
    &programme_pair().1
}

/// sim.results(d): RULE, the module constants and analyse (Plain).
fn results_of(tree: &MemTree, folder: &PathKey) -> FolderResults {

}

/// sim.results(d, rule).
fn results_with(tree: &MemTree, folder: &PathKey, rule: &Rule) -> FolderResults {
```
