```rust
/// Py: test_audio_similarity.py, class PositionVeto (4 tests). Row 0 of the rule (owner decision D21): a reference
/// that is not the first stream of its language, when that first stream is lossless or has more than two channels,
/// confirms no commentary on the title.
mod position_veto {
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    use super::{centre, comment, mix};
    use crate::audio::measures::{analyse, Constants, Measures};
    use crate::audio::rule::{
        first_of_language, position_veto, results, AnalyseFn, FolderResults, Measured, Rule, Verdict, Veto,
    };
    use crate::recording::files::FfprobeStream;
    use crate::recording::{MemTree, Ordered, PathKey};
    use crate::testsupport::level_file_text;

    /// A stream of these tests: (index, codec_name, profile, channels, language).
    type Stream<'a> = (i64, &'a str, Option<&'a str>, i64, &'a str);

    /// The ffprobe stream list PositionVeto.veto and streams_json build: a video stream 0, then the audio streams.
    fn stream_list(streams: &[Stream]) -> Vec<FfprobeStream> {
        let mut list = vec![FfprobeStream {
            index: 0,
            codec_type: Some("video".to_string()),
            codec_name: None,
            profile: None,
            channels: None,
            channel_layout: None,
            tags: None,
        }];
        for &(index, codec, profile, channels, language) in streams {
            list.push(FfprobeStream {
                index,
                codec_type: Some("audio".to_string()),
                codec_name: Some(codec.to_string()),
                profile: profile.map(str::to_string),
                channels: Some(channels),
                channel_layout: None,
                tags: Some(Ordered(vec![("language".to_string(), language.to_string())])),
            });
        }
        list
    }

    /// PositionVeto.veto: sim.position_veto(<that list>, main).
    fn veto(streams: &[Stream], main: i64) -> Veto {
        position_veto(Some(stream_list(streams).as_slice()), main)
    }

    /// streams_json(d, streams): the folder's streams.json as audio-levels.ps1 writes it (ffprobe's stream list).
    fn streams_json(tree: &mut MemTree, dir: &str, streams: &[Stream]) {
        let mut list = vec![serde_json::json!({"index": 0, "codec_type": "video"})];
        for &(index, codec, profile, channels, language) in streams {
            list.push(serde_json::json!({
                "index": index, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": codec, "profile": profile, "channels": channels,
                "tags": {"language": language}
            }));
        }
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/streams.json"), serde_json::json!({"streams": list}).to_string());
    }

    /// The Python test's analyse_fn: analyse with a cache keyed by (len(main), round(sum(cand), 1), dialogue is
    /// None), so that the second results() reuses the first one's measures. The key holds the exact bits of
    /// sum(cand) in place of round(..., 1) (py_round is Task 10's): it only has to tell the three candidates apart,
    /// and the same series always gives the same sum.
    struct Cache {
        measured: HashMap<(usize, u64, bool), Measures>,
    }

    impl AnalyseFn for Cache {
        fn measure(&mut self, main: &[f64], cand: &[f64], dialogue: Option<&[f64]>) -> Measured {
            let key = (main.len(), cand.iter().sum::<f64>().to_bits(), dialogue.is_none());
            let measures = self
                .measured
                .entry(key)
                .or_insert_with(|| analyse(main, cand, dialogue, true, &Constants::default()))
                .clone();
            Measured { measures, key: None }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn it_holds_when_a_lossless_first_stream_is_not_the_reference() {
        // 8.6 ranks the 5.1 first
        let v = veto(&[(1, "truehd", None, 2, "eng"), (2, "ac3", None, 6, "eng")], 2);
        assert_eq!(v.holds, Some(true));
        assert_eq!(
            v.why,
            "the reference, stream 2 (ac3 6 ch), is not the first eng stream of the file: stream 1 (truehd 2 ch) comes first and is lossless or has more than two channels, so the reference choice may be inverted"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn it_holds_when_a_multichannel_lossy_first_stream_is_not_the_reference() {
        let v = veto(&[(1, "ac3", None, 6, "eng"), (2, "dts", Some("DTS-HD MA"), 6, "eng")], 2);
        assert_eq!(v.holds, Some(true));
        assert!(v.why.contains("stream 1 (ac3 6 ch) comes first"), "{}", v.why);
    }

    #[test]
    fn it_does_not_hold_otherwise() {
        assert_eq!(
            veto(&[(1, "ac3", None, 2, "eng"), (2, "dts", Some("DTS"), 6, "eng")], 2),
            Veto {
                holds: Some(false),
                why: "the reference, stream 2 (dts DTS 6 ch), is not the first eng stream of the file, but stream 1 (ac3 2 ch), which comes first, is lossy with two channels or fewer".to_string(),
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            veto(&[(1, "dts", Some("DTS-HD MA"), 6, "eng"), (2, "ac3", None, 2, "eng")], 1),
            Veto {
                holds: Some(false),
                why: "the reference, stream 1 (dts DTS-HD MA 6 ch), is the first eng stream of the file".to_string(),
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(veto(&[(1, "ac3", None, 2, "eng")], 1).holds, Some(false)); // a single stream
        assert_eq!(veto(&[(1, "truehd", None, 8, "fra"), (2, "ac3", None, 6, "spa")], 2).holds, Some(false)); // other language
        assert_eq!(
            position_veto(None, 1),
            Veto { holds: None, why: "not checked: the folder has no streams.json".to_string() }
        );
        assert_eq!(veto(&[(2, "ac3", None, 6, "eng")], 5).holds, None);
        assert_eq!(first_of_language(&[], 1), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn it_never_turns_a_keep_into_a_drop() {
        // a quieter, 60 ms late copy of the programme
        let copy: Vec<f64> = [-100.0; 3].iter().copied().chain(mix()[..mix().len() - 3].iter().map(|v| v - 6.0)).collect();
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        let dir = "audio-levels-20ms-2-1-3-4";
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-mix.txt"), level_file_text(mix()));
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-fc.txt"), level_file_text(centre()));
        for (n, values) in [(1, &copy[..]), (3, comment()), (4, mix())] {
            tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/cand-{n}.txt"), level_file_text(values));
        }
        tree.insert_file(
            &format!("{dir}/manifest.txt"),
            concat!(
                "# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)\nfile=x.mkv bytes=1 seconds=1 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400\n",
                "main=2 codec=dts profile=DTS-HD_MA channels=6 layout=5.1(side) language=eng fc=yes frames=1 md5=aa\n",
                "cand=1 codec=dts profile=DTS channels=6 layout=5.1(side) language=eng frames=1 md5=bb\n",
                "cand=3 codec=ac3 profile=- channels=2 layout=stereo language=eng frames=1 md5=cc\n",
                "cand=4 codec=dts profile=DTS-HD_MA channels=6 layout=5.1(side) language=eng frames=1 md5=aa\n"
            ),
        );
        let d = PathKey::new(dir);
        let mut cache = Cache { measured: HashMap::new() };
        // no streams.json: the veto is not checked
        let free = results(&tree, &d, &Rule::default(), &Constants::default(), &mut cache).expect("analysed");
        streams_json(
            &mut tree,
            dir,
            &[
                (1, "dts", Some("DTS"), 6, "eng"),
                (2, "dts", Some("DTS-HD MA"), 6, "eng"),
                (3, "ac3", None, 2, "eng"),
                (4, "dts", Some("DTS-HD MA"), 6, "eng"),
            ],
        );
        let vetoed = results(&tree, &d, &Rule::default(), &Constants::default(), &mut cache).expect("analysed");
        let verdicts = |res: &FolderResults| res.candidates.iter().map(|c| c.verdict).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert_eq!(free.veto.holds, None);
        assert_eq!(verdicts(&free), [Verdict::Keep, Verdict::Commentary, Verdict::Duplicate]);
        assert_eq!(vetoed.veto.holds, Some(true));
        assert_eq!(verdicts(&vetoed), [Verdict::ReferenceUnclear, Verdict::ReferenceUnclear, Verdict::Duplicate]);
        assert_eq!(
            vetoed.candidates.iter().map(|c| c.before_veto).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [Some(Verdict::Keep), Some(Verdict::Commentary), None]
        );
        // The report's "  veto: holds (row 0, D21): ..." line and the "verdict: reference-unclear (<VETO_MEANING>;
        // rows 3 to 9 alone: commentary)" line (Task 6) print the veto's why and the before_veto checked above.
        assert!(
            vetoed.veto.why.starts_with(
                "the reference, stream 2 (dts DTS-HD MA 6 ch), is not the first eng stream of the file: stream 1 (dts DTS 6 ch) comes first"
            ),
            "{}",
            vetoed.veto.why
        );
    }
}

/// Py: test_audio_similarity.py, class CrossLanguage (6 tests).
mod cross_language {
    use super::{centre, comment, mix, results_of};
    use crate::audio::levels::Fields;
    use crate::audio::measures::{analyse, Constants};
    use crate::audio::rule::{cross_language, verdict, Rule, Verdict};
    use crate::lang::{iso639, ISO639, TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE};
    use crate::recording::{py_fixed, MemTree, Ordered, PathKey};
    use crate::testsupport::{level_file_text, speech, PyRandom};

    /// MANIFEST.format(fc=..., main=..., cand=...): what audio-levels.ps1 writes for main stream 1 and candidate 3.
    fn manifest(fc: &str, main: &str, cand: &str) -> String {
        format!("# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)\nfile=x.mkv bytes=1 seconds=1 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400\nmain=1 codec=dts profile=DTS-HD_MA channels=6 layout=5.1(side) language=eng fc={fc} frames=1 md5={main}\ncand=3 codec=ac3 profile=- channels=2 layout=stereo language=eng frames=1 md5={cand}\n")
    }

    /// A candidate of CrossLanguage.folder: (stream, levels, channels, language, codec, profile). The Python's
    /// defaults (language eng, codec ac3, profile "-") are written out at every call.
    type Cand<'a> = (i64, &'a [f64], i64, &'a str, &'a str, &'a str);

    /// CrossLanguage.folder: a Spanish film's level folder (main stream 1, DTS-HD MA 5.1 with its centre channel)
    /// with the candidates given.
    fn folder(tree: &mut MemTree, cands: &[Cand]) -> PathKey {
        let numbers: Vec<String> = cands.iter().map(|c| c.0.to_string()).collect();
        let dir = format!("audio-levels-20ms-1-{}", numbers.join("-"));
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-mix.txt"), level_file_text(mix()));
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-fc.txt"), level_file_text(centre()));
        let mut lines = vec![
            "# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)".to_string(),
            "file=x.mkv bytes=1 seconds=1 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400".to_string(),
            "main=1 codec=dts profile=DTS-HD_MA channels=6 layout=5.1(side) language=spa fc=yes frames=1 md5=aa".to_string(),
        ];
        for &(n, values, ch, lang, codec, profile) in cands {
            tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/cand-{n}.txt"), level_file_text(values));
            lines.push(format!(
                "cand={n} codec={codec} profile={profile} channels={ch} layout=x language={lang} frames=1 md5=m{n}"
            ));
        }
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/manifest.txt"), lines.join("\n") + "\n");
        PathKey::new(&dir)
    }

    /// A manifest line's fields, in order.
    fn fields(pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Fields {
        Ordered(pairs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v.to_string())).collect())
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_commentary_in_another_language_is_judged_against_the_programme_reference() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        let dir = "audio-levels-20ms-1-3";
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-mix.txt"), level_file_text(mix()));
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-fc.txt"), level_file_text(centre()));
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/cand-3.txt"), level_file_text(comment()));
        tree.insert_file(
            &format!("{dir}/manifest.txt"),
            manifest("yes", "aa", "bb").replace("layout=5.1(side) language=eng", "layout=5.1(side) language=spa"),
        );
        let res = results_of(&tree, &PathKey::new(dir));
        let c = &res.candidates[0];
        // never a drop verdict (addendum 9.2)
        assert_eq!((c.cross_language.as_str(), c.verdict), ("eng against spa", Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage));
        // no other English stream: nothing to compare it with
        assert_eq!(c.peer, None);
        // The report's line "stream 3: ac3 2 ch stereo eng (cross-language: eng against spa)" (Task 6) prints these
        // manifest fields and the cross_language checked above.
        assert_eq!(
            ["codec", "channels", "layout", "language"].map(|k| c.info.get(k).map(String::as_str)),
            [Some("ac3"), Some("2"), Some("stereo"), Some("eng")]
        );
        assert_eq!(cross_language(&fields(&[("language", "spa")]), &fields(&[("language", "und")])), "");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_companion_of_a_dub_follows_the_dub_and_gets_only_a_note() {
        // The dub stand-in has the commentary pattern against the original, as a loosely timed dub can (addendum
        // 9.2); its 2.0 companion is the same mix 6 dB down and 60 ms late.
        let dub = comment();
        let companion: Vec<f64> = [-100.0; 3].iter().copied().chain(dub[..dub.len() - 3].iter().map(|v| v - 6.0)).collect();
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        let d = folder(&mut tree, &[(2, dub, 6, "eng", "ac3", "-"), (3, &companion[..], 2, "eng", "ac3", "-")]);
        let res = results_of(&tree, &d);
        let [first, second] = &res.candidates[..] else { panic!("two candidates") };
        // the first English stream
        assert_eq!((first.verdict, &first.peer), (Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage, &None));
        let peer = second.peer.as_ref().expect("a peer run");
        assert_eq!((peer.stream.as_str(), peer.verdict), ("2", Verdict::Keep));
        let dc = peer.measures.run().expect("measured").dc;
        assert!(dc > 0.9, "{dc}");
        assert_eq!(second.verdict, Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        // The report's line "    peer: against stream 2 (placed first in the candidate's language): DC 1.00 ...:
        // keep, so not confirmed" (Task 6) prints fmt(dc) and the peer verdict checked above.
        assert_eq!(py_fixed(dc, 2), "1.00");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_commentary_beside_a_dub_keeps_the_cross_language_verdict() {
        // a dub that is the programme
        let shifted: Vec<f64> = mix().iter().map(|v| v - 2.0).collect();
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        let d = folder(&mut tree, &[(2, &shifted[..], 6, "eng", "ac3", "-"), (3, comment(), 2, "eng", "ac3", "-")]);
        let res = results_of(&tree, &d);
        let [dub, comm] = &res.candidates[..] else { panic!("two candidates") };
        assert_eq!(dub.verdict, Verdict::Keep);
        let peer = comm.peer.as_ref().expect("a peer run");
        assert_eq!((peer.stream.as_str(), peer.verdict), ("2", Verdict::Commentary));
        assert_eq!(comm.verdict, Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_peer_is_the_first_stream_of_the_candidates_own_language_as_8_6_ranks_it() {
        let shifted: Vec<f64> = mix().iter().map(|v| v - 2.0).collect();
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        // a Spanish core (6 channels) beside the English commentary: not the commentary's peer
        let d = folder(&mut tree, &[(2, &shifted[..], 6, "spa", "ac3", "-"), (3, comment(), 2, "eng", "ac3", "-")]);
        let res = results_of(&tree, &d);
        let [core, comm] = &res.candidates[..] else { panic!("two candidates") };
        assert_eq!((core.verdict, comm.verdict, &comm.peer), (Verdict::Keep, Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage, &None));
        // two English 5.1 streams: the lossless one (the manifest writes DTS-HD_MA) is placed first
        let d = folder(&mut tree, &[(4, comment(), 6, "eng", "ac3", "-"), (5, mix(), 6, "eng", "dts", "DTS-HD_MA")]);
        let res = results_of(&tree, &d);
        let [comm, _dub] = &res.candidates[..] else { panic!("two candidates") };
        assert_eq!(comm.peer.as_ref().map(|peer| peer.stream.as_str()), Some("5"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_language_table_is_iso_639_and_tmdbs_own_codes() {
        assert_eq!(
            (iso639("ml"), iso639("bo"), iso639("es")),
            (Some(&["mal"][..]), Some(&["bod", "tib"][..]), Some(&["spa"][..]))
        );
        assert!(iso639("cn").expect("cn").contains(&"yue"));
        assert!(iso639("sh").expect("sh").contains(&"hrv"));
        assert!(iso639(TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE).is_none());
        assert!(ISO639.len() >= 185, "{}", ISO639.len());
        for (_, codes) in ISO639 {
            // Python: codes and all(len(c) == 3 and c.isalpha() and c.islower() for c in codes). len counts code
            // points; isalpha is every character a letter; islower is every cased character lower case and at least
            // one cased character (no helper for it exists in core; the codes are ASCII).
            let good = !codes.is_empty()
                && codes.iter().all(|c| {
                    c.chars().count() == 3
                        && c.chars().all(char::is_alphabetic)
                        && c.chars().any(char::is_lowercase)
                        && !c.chars().any(char::is_uppercase)
                });
            assert!(good, "{codes:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_dub_is_kept_by_where_its_speech_sits_not_by_dc() {
        let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(11);
        // other words, in the programme's dialogue windows only
        let other = speech(&mut rnd, mix().len(), -20.0, -30.0);
        let dub: Vec<f64> = other
            .iter()
            .zip(mix())
            .zip(centre())
            .map(|((&o, &x), &c)| if c > -50.0 { o } else { x })
            .collect();
        let m = analyse(mix(), &dub, Some(centre()), true, &Constants::default());
        let run = m.run().expect("measured");
        assert!(run.dc < 0.9, "{}", run.dc);
        assert!(run.ag < 0.10, "{}", run.ag);
        assert_eq!(verdict(&m, &Rule::default()), Verdict::Keep);
    }
}

/// Py: test_audio_dataset.py, class Similarity (1 test).
mod similarity {
    use super::{centre, comment, mix, results_of, results_with};
    use crate::audio::levels::refusal;
    use crate::audio::measures::Constants;
    use crate::audio::rule::{Dialogue, Rule, Verdict};
    use crate::recording::{MemTree, PathKey};
    use crate::testsupport::level_file_text;

    /// test_audio_dataset.folder(label_dir, main_md5, cands, fc) with its other arguments at their defaults
    /// (channels 6, main 1, streams None: the default streams.json, langs None: every stream English);
    /// cands are (stream, levels, md5).
    fn folder(tree: &mut MemTree, label_dir: &str, main_md5: &str, cands: &[(i64, &[f64], &str)], fc: bool) -> PathKey {
        let (main, channels) = (1_i64, 6_i64);
        let mut numbers = vec![main.to_string()];
        numbers.extend(cands.iter().map(|c| c.0.to_string()));
        let dir = format!("{label_dir}/audio-levels-20ms-{}", numbers.join("-"));
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-mix.txt"), level_file_text(mix()));
        if fc {
            tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-fc.txt"), level_file_text(centre()));
        }
        let mut lines = vec![
            "# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)".to_string(),
            "file=x.mkv bytes=1 seconds=1 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400".to_string(),
            format!(
                "main={main} codec=dts profile=- channels={channels} layout={} language=eng fc={} frames={} md5={main_md5}",
                if fc { "5.1(side)" } else { "stereo" },
                if fc { "yes" } else { "no" },
                mix().len()
            ),
        ];
        for &(n, values, md5) in cands {
            tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/cand-{n}.txt"), level_file_text(values));
            lines.push(format!(
                "cand={n} codec=ac3 profile=- channels=2 layout=stereo language=eng frames={} md5={md5}",
                values.len()
            ));
        }
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/manifest.txt"), lines.join("\n") + "\n");
        // every stream up to the highest measured one, English, the main with `channels` and the others 2
        let top = cands.iter().map(|c| c.0).fold(main, i64::max);
        let mut streams = vec![serde_json::json!({"index": 0, "codec_type": "video"})];
        for k in 1..=top {
            let (ch, codec) = if k == main { (channels, "dts") } else { (2, "ac3") };
            streams.push(serde_json::json!({
                "index": k, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": codec, "profile": null, "channels": ch,
                "tags": {"language": "eng", "title": format!("t{k}")}
            }));
        }
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/streams.json"), serde_json::json!({"streams": streams}).to_string());
        PathKey::new(&dir)
    }

    #[test]
    fn results_are_the_report_as_data_and_a_reference_only_folder_is_valid() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        let short = &comment()[..600];
        let d = folder(&mut tree, "t", "m", &[(3, comment(), "c"), (4, mix(), "m"), (5, short, "s")], true);
        let res = results_of(&tree, &d);
        let rows: Vec<(&str, Verdict, Option<&str>, &str)> = res
            .candidates
            .iter()
            .map(|r| (r.stream.as_str(), r.verdict, r.duplicate_of.as_deref(), r.not_judged.as_str()))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            rows,
            [
                ("3", Verdict::Commentary, None, ""),
                ("4", Verdict::Duplicate, Some("1"), ""),
                ("5", Verdict::NotJudged, None, "too short"),
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(res.dialogue, Dialogue::Fc);
        // The report's "verdict: commentary" line (Task 6) prints the first candidate's verdict checked above.
        let strict = Rule { dc_max: 0.0, ..Rule::default() };
        assert_eq!(results_with(&tree, &d, &strict).candidates[0].verdict, Verdict::NoteCommentary);
        let r = folder(&mut tree, "r", "m", &[], false);
        assert_eq!(refusal(&tree, &r), Ok(String::new()));
        // The report's "no candidate stream: nothing to judge" line (Task 6) follows from this empty list.
        assert!(results_of(&tree, &r).candidates.is_empty());
        for (name, _) in Constants::NAMES {
            assert!(Constants::default().get(name).is_some(), "{name}");
        }
    }
}

/// New: results' contract with its callers: the refusal is its error, every pair goes through the hook Task 8's
/// cache plugs into and keeps the hook's key, the centre channel's SILENT_DB test reads the constants given, and Veto
/// and Dialogue serialise as the Python writes them.
mod results_contract {
    use crate::audio::measures::{Constants, Measures, Run};
    use crate::audio::rule::{results, AnalyseFn, Dialogue, Measured, Plain, Rule, Verdict, Veto};
    use crate::recording::{MemTree, PathKey, Tree};
    use crate::testsupport::level_file_text;

    /// A hook that measures nothing: every pair gets the measured commentary of class Rule without a reverse block
    /// (so its verdict is commentary) and the key "key-<n>" for the n-th call; it records (frames of main, frames of
    /// cand, whether a dialogue curve was given).
    struct Stub {
        calls: Vec<(usize, usize, bool)>,
    }

    impl AnalyseFn for Stub {
        fn measure(&mut self, main: &[f64], cand: &[f64], dialogue: Option<&[f64]>) -> Measured {
            self.calls.push((main.len(), cand.len(), dialogue.is_some()));
            let commentary = Run {
                overlap: 1.0,
                main_silent: 0.0,
                gap_s: 355.0,
                dc: 0.03,
                ag: 0.66,
                ag_s: 234.0,
                adl: 0.18,
                tenths: 10,
                tenths_comm: 10,
                tenths_ad: 10,
                smi: 0.58,
                ls_db: 10.1,
                added_s: 518.0,
                ..Run::blank()
            };
            Measured { measures: Measures::Run(commentary), key: Some(format!("key-{}", self.calls.len())) }
        }
    }

    /// A level folder of constant levels: main stream 1 in `main_lang` (1200 frames at -30 dB), main-fc.txt at
    /// `fc_db` when given, and English candidates (stream, frames, channels) at -30 dB.
    fn constant_folder(tree: &mut MemTree, dir: &str, main_lang: &str, fc_db: Option<f64>, cands: &[(i64, usize, i64)]) -> PathKey {
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-mix.txt"), level_file_text(&vec![-30.0; 1200]));
        if let Some(db) = fc_db {
            tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/main-fc.txt"), level_file_text(&vec![db; 1200]));
        }
        let mut lines = vec![
            "# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)".to_string(),
            "file=x.mkv bytes=1 seconds=1 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400".to_string(),
            format!(
                "main=1 codec=dts profile=DTS-HD_MA channels=6 layout=5.1(side) language={main_lang} fc={} frames=1 md5=aa",
                if fc_db.is_some() { "yes" } else { "no" }
            ),
        ];
        for &(n, frames, ch) in cands {
            tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/cand-{n}.txt"), level_file_text(&vec![-30.0; frames]));
            lines.push(format!("cand={n} codec=ac3 profile=- channels={ch} layout=x language=eng frames=1 md5=m{n}"));
        }
        tree.insert_file(&format!("{dir}/manifest.txt"), lines.join("\n") + "\n");
        PathKey::new(dir)
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_hook_measures_every_pair_and_its_keys_are_kept() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        let d = constant_folder(&mut tree, "audio-levels-20ms-1-2-3", "spa", Some(-20.0), &[(2, 1100, 6), (3, 1000, 2)]);
        let mut stub = Stub { calls: Vec::new() };
        let res = results(&tree, &d, &Rule::default(), &Constants::default(), &mut stub).expect("analysed");
        // the forward runs against main-mix with main-fc as dialogue, then the peer run of stream 3 against stream 2
        // (stream 2 is placed first among the English candidates: 6 channels against 2)
        assert_eq!(stub.calls, [(1200, 1100, true), (1200, 1000, true), (1100, 1000, false)]);
        let [two, three] = &res.candidates[..] else { panic!("two candidates") };
        assert_eq!(
            (two.verdict, two.key.as_deref(), two.peer.is_none(), two.cross_language.as_str()),
            (Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage, Some("key-1"), true, "eng against spa")
        );
        assert_eq!((three.verdict, three.key.as_deref()), (Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage, Some("key-2")));
        let peer = three.peer.as_ref().expect("a peer run");
        assert_eq!((peer.stream.as_str(), peer.verdict, peer.key.as_deref()), ("2", Verdict::Commentary, Some("key-3")));
        assert_eq!((res.dialogue, res.frames), (Dialogue::Fc, 1200));
        assert_eq!(res.veto, Veto { holds: None, why: "not checked: the folder has no streams.json".to_string() });
        assert_eq!(res.folder, tree.display(&d));
        assert_eq!(res.main.get("main").map(String::as_str), Some("1"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_centre_channel_at_or_below_silent_db_is_not_the_dialogue_curve() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        let d = constant_folder(&mut tree, "audio-levels-20ms-1-2", "eng", Some(-100.0), &[(2, 1100, 2)]);
        let mut stub = Stub { calls: Vec::new() };
        let res = results(&tree, &d, &Rule::default(), &Constants::default(), &mut stub).expect("analysed");
        assert_eq!((res.dialogue, stub.calls), (Dialogue::Mix, vec![(1200, 1100, false)]));
        // the same centre channel is the dialogue curve when SILENT_DB is set lower (a --set trial)
        let consts = Constants { SILENT_DB: -110.0, ..Constants::default() };
        let mut stub = Stub { calls: Vec::new() };
        let res = results(&tree, &d, &Rule::default(), &consts, &mut stub).expect("analysed");
        assert_eq!((res.dialogue, stub.calls), (Dialogue::Fc, vec![(1200, 1100, true)]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_refused_folder_is_the_error_and_nothing_is_measured() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "lazymkv-test");
        tree.insert_dir("audio-levels-20ms-5-6");
        let d = PathKey::new("audio-levels-20ms-5-6");
        let mut stub = Stub { calls: Vec::new() };
        let err = results(&tree, &d, &Rule::default(), &Constants::default(), &mut stub).expect_err("refused");
        assert_eq!(
            err,
            format!(
                "{}: no manifest.txt, so it was not written by the new audio-levels.ps1 (the first measurement's folders, audio-levels-<main>-<cand>, hold 100 ms full-band levels); this folder cannot be analysed: measure the title again with the new audio-levels.ps1, which writes audio-levels-20ms-<main>-<candidates>",
                tree.display(&d)
            )
        );
        assert!(stub.calls.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn veto_dialogue_and_plain_are_what_the_python_writes() {
        let veto = Veto { holds: None, why: "not checked".to_string() };
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&veto).expect("serialisable"), r#"{"holds":null,"why":"not checked"}"#);
        let holds = Veto { holds: Some(true), why: String::new() };
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&holds).expect("serialisable"), r#"{"holds":true,"why":""}"#);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&Dialogue::Fc).expect("serialisable"), r#""fc""#);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&Dialogue::Mix).expect("serialisable"), r#""mix""#);
        // Plain is analyse with the reverse run and no cache key
        let consts = Constants::default();
        let short = vec![-30.0; 500];
        let measured = Plain { consts: &consts }.measure(&short, &short, None);
        assert_eq!(measured.key, None);
        assert_eq!(measured.measures.error(), Some("too short"));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The streams the audio rule reads and the stream it judges against: spec 8.6's ranking (step 3) with its guards G1
//! and G2 (step 4) as far as ffprobe's facts go, the programme reference of EXP-13 addendum 9.1, and the readers of a
//! level folder's stream facts (its manifest lines and its streams.json).
//! Ported from scripts/phase0/audio_similarity.py (is_lossless, rank, placed_first, ffprobe_audio, read_streams,
//! manifest_stream) and scripts/phase0/audio_dataset.py (original_language, programme_reference, wanted,
//! first_of_language).

use crate::audio::levels::{parse_streams, Fields};
use crate::audio::rule::first_of_language as rule_first_of_language;
use crate::lang::{iso639, NO_LANGUAGE, TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE};
use crate::recording::files::FfprobeStream;
use crate::recording::{
    py_int, py_repr, py_repr_str, py_truthy, read_json, read_text, Encoding, Errors, PathKey, Tree,
};

/// A stream as placed_first takes it: the Python's tuple (stream, channels, lossless, language, description).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AudioStream {
    pub stream: i64,
    pub channels: i64,
    pub lossless: bool,
    pub language: String,
    pub description: String,
}

/// Lossless audio as spec 8.6 ranks it: truehd, mlp, flac, pcm*, or a profile holding "DTS-HD MA" once '_' is read
/// as a space (ffprobe names DTS:X tracks "DTS-HD MA + DTS:X"; a level folder's manifest writes "DTS-HD_MA").
/// Py: is_lossless.
pub fn is_lossless(codec: Option<&str>, profile: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    let c = codec.unwrap_or("");
    matches!(c, "truehd" | "mlp" | "flac")
        || c.starts_with("pcm")
        || profile.unwrap_or("").replace('_', " ").contains("DTS-HD MA")
}

/// Spec 8.6 step 3's sort key: most channels, then lossless, then the earlier stream. Py: rank.
pub fn rank(a: &AudioStream) -> (i64, bool, i64) {
    (-a.channels, !a.lossless, a.stream)
}

/// The stream spec 8.6 places first among the given streams of one language: rank (step 3), then its guards (step
/// 4) as far as ffprobe's facts go. G1: a lossy stream of two channels or fewer (the spec says 256 kb/s or less;
/// streams.json carries no bit rate) never comes before a lossless one. G2: a lossy stream of two channels or fewer
/// that is not the language's first stream and has more channels than that first stream gives way to it.
/// `streams` is never empty: the Python indexes [0], and this panics on an empty slice where the Python raised
/// IndexError. Py: placed_first.
pub fn placed_first(streams: &[AudioStream]) -> AudioStream {
    let mut ranked: Vec<&AudioStream> = streams.iter().collect();
    ranked.sort_by_key(|a| rank(a)); // stable, as sorted()
    let top = *ranked.first().expect("placed_first takes at least one stream");
    if !top.lossless && top.channels <= 2 {
        if let Some(lossless) = ranked.iter().find(|a| a.lossless) {
            return AudioStream::clone(lossless);
        }
        // min() keeps the first of equal stream numbers, and so does min_by_key.
        if let Some(first) = streams.iter().min_by_key(|a| a.stream) {
            if first.stream != top.stream && first.channels < top.channels {
                return first.clone();
            }
        }
    }
    top.clone()
}

/// The audio streams of an ffprobe stream list (a level folder's streams.json, a rip's ffprobe-streams.json) in file
/// order, in the form placed_first takes: the index, the channels (0 when absent), is_lossless of codec and profile,
/// the language tag ("und" when absent or empty), and a description joining the codec, the profile, "<channels> ch"
/// ("None ch" when ffprobe gives no channels), the layout and the title tag, each left out when absent or empty.
/// A codec_name that is absent or null is "" (ffprobe always writes it for an audio stream). Py: ffprobe_audio.
pub fn ffprobe_audio(streams: &[FfprobeStream]) -> Vec<AudioStream> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for s in streams {
        if s.codec_type.as_deref() != Some("audio") {
            continue;
        }
        let tag = |key: &str| s.tags.as_ref().and_then(|tags| tags.get(key)).map(String::as_str);
        let codec = s.codec_name.as_deref().unwrap_or("");
        let channels = format!("{} ch", s.channels.map_or_else(|| "None".to_string(), |n| n.to_string()));
        let what = [Some(codec), s.profile.as_deref(), Some(channels.as_str()), s.channel_layout.as_deref(), tag("title")];
        let description = what.iter().flatten().filter(|w| !w.is_empty()).copied().collect::<Vec<&str>>().join(" ");
        out.push(AudioStream {
            stream: s.index,
            channels: s.channels.unwrap_or(0),
            lossless: is_lossless(Some(codec), s.profile.as_deref()),
            language: tag("language").filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).unwrap_or("und").to_string(),
            description,
        });
    }
    out
}

/// The stream list of a level folder's streams.json (ffprobe's list of the file's streams), read as utf-8-sig; None
/// when the folder has no such file; Err with the read or parse error. Py: read_streams.
pub fn read_streams(tree: &dyn Tree, folder: &PathKey) -> Result<Option<Vec<FfprobeStream>>, String> {
    let path = folder.join("streams.json");
    if !tree.is_file(&path) {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let text = read_text(tree, &path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)?;
    Ok(Some(parse_streams(&text)?.streams))
}

/// A manifest line's stream in the form placed_first takes: the cand= value, else the main= value (`cand or main`),
/// as an int; channels= as an int, 0 when it is not one; is_lossless of codec= and profile=; language=, "und" when
/// absent or empty; the description "<codec, ? when absent> <channels> ch". Err with the Python's int() text when the
/// stream number is not an int or absent. Py: manifest_stream.
pub fn manifest_stream(info: &Fields) -> Result<AudioStream, String> {
    let n = match info.get("cand") {
        Some(cand) if !cand.is_empty() => Some(cand.as_str()),
        _ => info.get("main").map(String::as_str),
    };
    // int(info.get("channels") or 0), 0 on ValueError
    let channels = info.get("channels").and_then(|text| py_int(text)).unwrap_or(0);
    let codec = info.get("codec").map(String::as_str);
    Ok(AudioStream {
        stream: int_text(n)?,
        channels,
        lossless: is_lossless(codec, info.get("profile").map(String::as_str)),
        language: info.get("language").filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| "und".to_string()),
        description: format!("{} {channels} ch", codec.unwrap_or("?")),
    })
}

/// (codes, what): the three-letter codes of the work's original language from <slug_dir>/tmdb.json (read as
/// utf-8-sig), and a phrase saying how it was found. codes is empty when the original language is English, none or
/// unknown. Py: audio_dataset.original_language; its phrases verbatim (the "audio_similarity.ISO639" in one of them
/// included: levels-args prints it).
pub fn original_language(tree: &dyn Tree, slug_dir: &PathKey) -> (&'static [&'static str], String) {
    const UNREADABLE: &str = "original language unknown (no readable tmdb.json)";
    // except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError): no file, not UTF-8, not JSON, not a JSON object
    let Ok(data) = read_json::<serde_json::Value>(tree, &slug_dir.join("tmdb.json")) else {
        return (&[], UNREADABLE.to_string());
    };
    let Some(object) = data.as_object() else {
        return (&[], UNREADABLE.to_string());
    };
    let code = match object.get("original_language") {
        Some(code) if py_truthy(code) => code,
        _ => return (&[], "original language unknown (tmdb.json gives none)".to_string()),
    };
    let Some(code) = code.as_str() else {
        // A number or true: the Python's `code not in ISO639` holds and {code!r} is its repr. (A list or an object
        // made the Python raise TypeError; it gets the same sentence here.)
        return (&[], format!("original language unknown (TMDb {} is not in audio_similarity.ISO639)", py_repr(code)));
    };
    if code == "en" {
        return (&[], "original language English (TMDb en)".to_string());
    }
    if code == TMDB_NO_LANGUAGE {
        return (
            &[],
            format!("original language none (TMDb {code}: a work without speech; English is the reference language)"),
        );
    }
    match iso639(code) {
        None => (
            &[],
            format!("original language unknown (TMDb {} is not in audio_similarity.ISO639)", py_repr_str(code)),
        ),
        Some(codes) => (codes, format!("original language {} (TMDb {code})", codes.join("/"))),
    }
}

/// (stream, why): the title's programme reference (EXP-13 addendum 9.1): the stream spec 8.6 places first in the
/// work's original language when the title has one in it ("the original language"), else in English ("English"),
/// else among all streams ("any language (no stream is in a wanted language)": measured for the dataset only).
/// `audio` is never empty (placed_first). Py: audio_dataset.programme_reference.
pub fn programme_reference(audio: &[AudioStream], original: &[&str]) -> (AudioStream, &'static str) {
    let english: &[&str] = &["eng"];
    for (codes, why) in [(original, "the original language"), (english, "English")] {
        let mine: Vec<AudioStream> =
            audio.iter().filter(|a| codes.iter().any(|code| *code == a.language)).cloned().collect();
        if !mine.is_empty() {
            return (placed_first(&mine), why);
        }
    }
    (placed_first(audio), "any language (no stream is in a wanted language)")
}

/// A stream measured as a candidate: in English or the original language (R4), or with no language code (the app
/// does not judge those; phase 0 measures them for the dataset). Py: audio_dataset.wanted.
pub fn wanted(a: &AudioStream, original: &[&str]) -> bool {
    a.language == "eng"
        || original.iter().any(|code| *code == a.language)
        || NO_LANGUAGE.iter().any(|code| *code == a.language)
}

/// rule::first_of_language over a streams.json, as (stream, description); None without streams.json (`streams or
/// []`). It is the condition of the position veto (row 0, D21). Py: audio_dataset.first_of_language.
pub fn first_of_language(streams: Option<&[FfprobeStream]>, main: i64) -> Option<(i64, String)> {
    let audio = ffprobe_audio(streams.unwrap_or(&[]));
    rule_first_of_language(&audio, main).map(|first| (first.stream, first.description))
}

/// int() of a manifest value as the Python calls it: its ValueError text for a value that is not an int, its
/// TypeError text for a key that is absent (None).
fn int_text(text: Option<&str>) -> Result<i64, String> {
    match text {
        None => Err("int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a number, not 'NoneType'".to_string()),
        Some(text) => {
            py_int(text).ok_or_else(|| format!("invalid literal for int() with base 10: {}", py_repr_str(text)))
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;
```

Then insert the following between the end of `pub fn verdict` and the final two lines `#[cfg(test)]` / `mod tests;`:

```rust
/// Row 0 of the rule (EXP-13 addendum 9.5; owner decision D21) for the title whose reference is a given stream:
/// holds is Some(true) when the reference is not the first stream of its language in the file and that first stream
/// is lossless or has more than two channels (the reference choice may be inverted: a score or a commentary ranked
/// above the programme, so the rule confirms no commentary on the title); Some(false) when the reference is that
/// first stream, or that first stream is lossy with two channels or fewer; None when it cannot be checked. why names
/// the streams. Position never decides what a track is (D15): the veto only withholds a drop. Serialised as
/// {"holds": true|false|null, "why": "..."}. Py: position_veto's tuple.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Veto {
    pub holds: Option<bool>,
    pub why: String,
}

/// The first stream of `audio` (file order) in stream `main`'s language when it is not `main` and is lossless or has
/// more than two channels; None otherwise and when `main` is not in `audio`. A lossy first stream of two channels or
/// fewer is what G1 and G2 pass over on purpose, so it raises nothing. Py: audio_similarity.first_of_language.
pub fn first_of_language(audio: &[AudioStream], main: i64) -> Option<AudioStream> {
    let mine = audio.iter().find(|a| a.stream == main)?;
    // min() keeps the first of equal stream numbers, and so does min_by_key.
    let first = audio.iter().filter(|a| a.language == mine.language).min_by_key(|a| a.stream)?;
    if first.stream == main || !(first.lossless || first.channels > 2) {
        None
    } else {
        Some(first.clone())
    }
}

/// Row 0 for the title whose reference is stream `main`; `streams` None means the folder has no streams.json.
/// Py: position_veto, its sentences verbatim.
pub fn position_veto(streams: Option<&[FfprobeStream]>, main: i64) -> Veto {
    let Some(streams) = streams else {
        return Veto { holds: None, why: "not checked: the folder has no streams.json".to_string() };
    };
    let audio = ffprobe_audio(streams);
    let Some(reference) = audio.iter().find(|a| a.stream == main) else {
        return Veto { holds: None, why: format!("not checked: stream {main} is not an audio stream of streams.json") };
    };
    let head = format!("the reference, stream {main} ({}),", reference.description);
    let language = &reference.language;
    // min() keeps the first of equal stream numbers; the reference itself is one of these streams.
    let first = audio.iter().filter(|a| a.language == *language).min_by_key(|a| a.stream).unwrap_or(reference);
    if first.stream == main {
        return Veto { holds: Some(false), why: format!("{head} is the first {language} stream of the file") };
    }
    if first_of_language(&audio, main).is_none() {
        return Veto {
            holds: Some(false),
            why: format!(
                "{head} is not the first {language} stream of the file, but stream {} ({}), which comes first, is lossy with two channels or fewer",
                first.stream, first.description
            ),
        };
    }
    Veto {
        holds: Some(true),
        why: format!(
            "{head} is not the first {language} stream of the file: stream {} ({}) comes first and is lossless or has more than two channels, so the reference choice may be inverted",
            first.stream, first.description
        ),
    }
}

/// "<candidate language> against <main language>" when both lines name a language (not NO_LANGUAGE) and they
/// differ, else "". Py: cross_language.
pub fn cross_language(main_info: &Fields, cand_info: &Fields) -> String {
    let a = cand_info.get("language").map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    let b = main_info.get("language").map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    if NO_LANGUAGE.iter().any(|code| *code == a) || NO_LANGUAGE.iter().any(|code| *code == b) || a == b {
        return String::new();
    }
    format!("{a} against {b}")
}

/// What `results` calls to measure a pair: the Python's analyse_fn(main, cand, dialogue). Plain is the Python's
/// default (analyse, no cache). Task 8's Measurer keeps the cache of spec 3.3 (keyed by sha1 of "lazymkv-rule:",
/// RULE_VERSION, the canonical constants JSON, then per series its little-endian f64 bytes and "|", or "|" alone for
/// none) and returns the key with the measures, in place of the Python's Measurer.key_of[id(m)] lookup.
pub trait AnalyseFn {
    fn measure(&mut self, main: &[f64], cand: &[f64], dialogue: Option<&[f64]>) -> Measured;
}

/// Measures and the cache key they are kept under (None when no cache is used).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Measured {
    pub measures: Measures,
    pub key: Option<String>,
}

/// analyse(main, cand, dialogue, true, consts), no cache: the Python's default analyse_fn.
pub struct Plain<'c> {
    pub consts: &'c Constants,
}

impl AnalyseFn for Plain<'_> {
    fn measure(&mut self, main: &[f64], cand: &[f64], dialogue: Option<&[f64]>) -> Measured {
        Measured { measures: analyse(main, cand, dialogue, true, self.consts), key: None }
    }
}

/// Which curve the forward runs used as dialogue: the main stream's centre channel (main-fc.txt) or its mixdown.
/// Serialised "fc" | "mix".
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Dialogue {
    Fc,
    Mix,
}

/// A level folder's measures and verdicts as data. Py: results' dict.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct FolderResults {
    /// tree.display(folder). Py: str(d).
    pub folder: String,
    pub manifest: Manifest,
    /// The manifest's main line (empty when none).
    pub main: Fields,
    /// Frames of main-mix.txt.
    pub frames: usize,
    /// Fc when main-fc.txt exists and is not all at or below SILENT_DB.
    pub dialogue: Dialogue,
    pub candidates: Vec<CandidateResult>,
    pub veto: Veto,
}

/// One candidate. Py: results' candidate dict.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct CandidateResult {
    /// The manifest's cand= value, a string as the Python keeps it.
    pub stream: String,
    pub info: Fields,
    /// The stream (main= or cand= value) with the same packet MD5, for an exact duplicate.
    pub duplicate_of: Option<String>,
    /// None for a duplicate.
    pub measures: Option<Measures>,
    /// The cache key of `measures` (Measured.key).
    pub key: Option<String>,
    pub verdict: Verdict,
    pub not_judged: String,
    pub cross_language: String,
    pub peer: Option<Peer>,
    /// What rows 3 to 9 said when the veto replaced it with ReferenceUnclear.
    pub before_veto: Option<Verdict>,
}

/// The peer run of a cross-language candidate. Py: results' "peer" dict.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Peer {
    pub stream: String,
    pub measures: Measures,
    pub key: Option<String>,
    pub verdict: Verdict,
}

/// The measures and verdict of every candidate of a level folder written by audio-levels.ps1, as data, in the order
/// of audio_similarity.results(folder, rule, analyse_fn):
/// 1. refusal: Err with its reason before anything is read or measured;
/// 2. manifest.txt, main-mix.txt, and main-fc.txt when it exists and is not all at or below consts.SILENT_DB (then it
///    is the dialogue curve of the forward runs; otherwise they get none, and analyse uses the mixdown);
/// 3. the veto from streams.json for the manifest's main stream (holds None, why "not checked", without a main=
///    value);
/// 4. per candidate in manifest order: a duplicate of the main stream or of an earlier candidate by packet MD5 (no
///    measure), else the forward run against main-mix through `analyse_fn`, its verdict and not_judged;
/// 5. a cross-language candidate whose verdict is commentary gets commentary-cross-language, and when 8.6 places
///    another non-duplicate candidate of its language first, the peer run (that stream's levels as main, this one's
///    as candidate, no dialogue curve): note-commentary unless the peer verdict is commentary;
/// 6. when the veto holds, every candidate that is not a duplicate becomes reference-unclear, its earlier verdict
///    kept in before_veto.
///
/// Err also when a file cannot be read, a level does not parse, streams.json does not parse, or a manifest stream
/// number is not an int (the Python's ValueError and OSError texts). `consts` is the set of measure constants in
/// force: SILENT_DB is read here, `analyse_fn` applies the others. Py: audio_similarity.results.
pub fn results(
    tree: &dyn Tree,
    folder: &PathKey,
    rule: &Rule,
    consts: &Constants,
    analyse_fn: &mut dyn AnalyseFn,
) -> Result<FolderResults, String> {
    let why = refusal(tree, folder)?;
    if !why.is_empty() {
        return Err(why);
    }
    let manifest: Manifest = read_manifest(tree, folder)?;
    let main = read_levels(tree, &folder.join("main-mix.txt"))?;
    let fc_path = folder.join("main-fc.txt");
    let mut fc = if tree.exists(&fc_path) { read_levels(tree, &fc_path)? } else { Vec::new() };
    if !fc.is_empty() && py_max(&fc) <= consts.SILENT_DB {
        fc = Vec::new();
    }
    let mainfo: Fields = manifest.main.clone().unwrap_or_default();
    // position_veto(read_streams(d), int(mainfo["main"])) if mainfo.get("main") else (None, "not checked"):
    // streams.json is read before the stream number is parsed, as the Python evaluates the arguments.
    let veto = match mainfo.get("main") {
        Some(stream) if !stream.is_empty() => {
            let streams = read_streams(tree, folder)?;
            position_veto(streams.as_deref(), int_text(Some(stream.as_str()))?)
        }
        _ => Veto { holds: None, why: "not checked".to_string() },
    };
    let dialogue: Option<&[f64]> = if fc.is_empty() { None } else { Some(fc.as_slice()) };
    let mut seen: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
    if let Some(md5) = mainfo.get("md5").filter(|md5| !md5.is_empty()) {
        seen.insert(md5.clone(), mainfo.get("main").cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| "?".to_string()));
    }
    let mut candidates: Vec<CandidateResult> = Vec::new();
    for c in &manifest.cands {
        // Every candidate line has cand= (parse_manifest files a line under cands by that key).
        let sid = c.get("cand").cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        let mut r = CandidateResult {
            stream: sid.clone(),
            info: c.clone(),
            duplicate_of: None,
            measures: None,
            key: None,
            verdict: Verdict::Duplicate,
            not_judged: String::new(),
            cross_language: cross_language(&mainfo, c),
            peer: None,
            before_veto: None,
        };
        let md5 = c.get("md5");
        match md5.and_then(|md5| seen.get(md5)).cloned() {
            Some(first) => r.duplicate_of = Some(first),
            None => {
                if let Some(md5) = md5.filter(|md5| !md5.is_empty()) {
                    seen.insert(md5.clone(), sid.clone());
                }
                let cand = read_levels(tree, &folder.join(&format!("cand-{sid}.txt")))?;
                let measured = analyse_fn.measure(&main, &cand, dialogue);
                r.verdict = verdict(&measured.measures, rule);
                r.not_judged = match measured.measures.error() {
                    Some(error) => error.to_string(),
                    None => not_judged(&measured.measures, rule),
                };
                r.measures = Some(measured.measures);
                r.key = measured.key;
            }
        }
        candidates.push(r);
    }
    for i in 0..candidates.len() {
        if candidates[i].verdict != Verdict::Commentary || candidates[i].cross_language.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let mut own = Vec::new();
        for x in &candidates {
            if x.duplicate_of.is_none() && x.info.get("language") == candidates[i].info.get("language") {
                own.push(manifest_stream(&x.info)?);
            }
        }
        let peer = placed_first(&own).stream;
        candidates[i].verdict = Verdict::CommentaryCrossLanguage;
        if peer != int_text(Some(candidates[i].stream.as_str()))? {
            let peer_levels = read_levels(tree, &folder.join(&format!("cand-{peer}.txt")))?;
            let own_levels = read_levels(tree, &folder.join(&format!("cand-{}.txt", candidates[i].stream)))?;
            let measured = analyse_fn.measure(&peer_levels, &own_levels, None);
            let peer_verdict = verdict(&measured.measures, rule);
            let r = &mut candidates[i];
            r.peer = Some(Peer {
                stream: peer.to_string(),
                measures: measured.measures,
                key: measured.key,
                verdict: peer_verdict,
            });
            if peer_verdict != Verdict::Commentary {
                r.verdict = Verdict::NoteCommentary;
            }
        }
    }
    if veto.holds == Some(true) {
        for r in candidates.iter_mut().filter(|r| r.duplicate_of.is_none()) {
            r.before_veto = Some(r.verdict);
            r.verdict = Verdict::ReferenceUnclear;
        }
    }
    Ok(FolderResults {
        folder: tree.display(folder),
        frames: main.len(),
        dialogue: if fc.is_empty() { Dialogue::Mix } else { Dialogue::Fc },
        main: mainfo,
        manifest,
        candidates,
        veto,
    })
}

/// int() of a manifest value as the Python calls it: its ValueError text for a value that is not an int, its
/// TypeError text for a key that is absent (None).
fn int_text(text: Option<&str>) -> Result<i64, String> {
    match text {
        None => Err("int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a number, not 'NoneType'".to_string()),
        Some(text) => {
            py_int(text).ok_or_else(|| format!("invalid literal for int() with base 10: {}", py_repr_str(text)))
        }
    }
}

/// max() of a non-empty list as Python's max: a later value replaces the one kept only when it is greater.
fn py_max(values: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    let mut top = values[0];
    for &v in &values[1..] {
        if v > top {
            top = v;
        }
    }
    top
}
```

```rust
    fn langs(pairs: &[(&str, &[u32])]) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<u32>> {
        pairs.iter().map(|(lang, streams)| (lang.to_string(), streams.to_vec())).collect()
    }

    fn firefly_scan() -> Vec<u8> {
        let path = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
            .join("../../corpus/thediscdb/series/Firefly (2002)/2003-dvd-the-complete-series/disc01.txt");
        std::fs::read(&path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("the pinned Firefly scan {}: {e}", path.display()))
    }

    #[test]
    fn titles_list_audio_by_language_without_derived_streams_longest_first() {
        let info = audio_by_title(&parse(SCAN)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(info[&0], TitleAudio { seconds: 1309, segments: vec![7], languages: langs(&[("eng", &[1, 3])]) });
        assert_eq!(info[&1].languages, langs(&[("eng", &[1]), ("fra", &[3])]));
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("tmp", "tmp");
        tree.insert_file("some-disc/scan.txt", SCAN);
        tree.insert_file("some-disc/e16/rip-summary.json", r#"{"ok": true, "title": 0}"#);
        let lines = titles_report(&tree, &PathKey::new("some-disc")).unwrap();
        let order: Vec<&str> = lines[2..].iter().map(|line| py_split(line)[1]).collect();
        assert_eq!(order, ["2", "1", "0", "3"]);
        assert!(lines[2].contains("shares segments with title 0, 1"), "{}", lines[2]);
        assert!(!lines[3].contains("<-"), "{}", lines[3]);
        assert!(lines[4].contains("<- eng x2; ripped as e16"), "{}", lines[4]);
        assert!(lines[5].contains("<- eng x2"), "{}", lines[5]); // no flags attribute at all: not derived
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_dvds_segments_are_not_compared_across_titles() {
        // A DVD title's segments are the cells of its own program chain, numbered from 1 in every title.
        assert!(!dvd_scan(&parse(SCAN)));
        let dvd = format!("CINFO:1,6206,\"DVD disc\"\n{SCAN}");
        assert!(dvd_scan(&parse(&dvd)));
        assert!(dvd_scan(&parse(&format!("{SCAN}SINFO:0,0,5,0,\"V_MPEG2\"\n"))));
        assert!(!dvd_scan(&parse(&format!("{dvd}TINFO:0,16,0,\"00800.mpls\"\n")))); // a source file: a Blu-ray
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("tmp", "tmp");
        tree.insert_file("firefly/scan.txt", firefly_scan());
        let lines = titles_report(&tree, &PathKey::new("firefly")).unwrap();
        assert!(lines[2].contains("so shared segments are not looked for"), "{}", lines[2]);
        assert!(lines.iter().all(|line| !line.contains("shares segments")), "{lines:#?}");
        let one: Vec<&String> = lines.iter().filter(|line| py_split(line).starts_with(&["title", "1"])).collect();
        assert_eq!(one.len(), 1, "{lines:#?}");
        // the episode with a commentary, not skipped
        assert!(one[0].contains("audio eng 1,4; fre 2; spa 3   <- eng x2"), "{}", one[0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_title_with_one_stream_in_each_wanted_language_is_marked() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("tmp", "tmp");
        tree.insert_file("some-film/scan.txt", SCAN.replace("SINFO:1,3,3,0,\"fra\"", "SINFO:1,3,3,0,\"spa\""));
        let film = PathKey::new("some-film");
        // original language unknown: English alone is wanted
        assert!(!titles_report(&tree, &film).unwrap()[3].contains("<-"));
        tree.insert_file("some-film/tmdb.json", r#"{"original_language": "es"}"#);
        let lines = titles_report(&tree, &film).unwrap();
        assert!(lines[0].contains("TMDb original language: es"), "{}", lines[0]);
        assert_eq!(py_split(&lines[3])[1], "1");
        assert!(lines[3].contains("audio eng 1; spa 3   <- wanted x2 (eng 1, spa 1)"), "{}", lines[3]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn segments_reads_numbers_and_ranges_and_skips_malformed_parts() {
        // Each case as the Python's segments() gave it.
        let cases: [(&str, &[i64]); 12] = [
            ("7", &[7]),
            ("10,11", &[10, 11]),
            ("1-3", &[1, 2, 3]),
            (" 4 , 5-6 ", &[4, 5, 6]),
            ("x,2", &[2]),
            ("3-x", &[]),
            ("", &[]),
            ("5-3", &[]),
            ("-5", &[]),
            ("3-", &[3]),
            ("1-2,3,4-6", &[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]),
            ("2-2", &[2]),
        ];
        for (text, want) in cases {
            assert_eq!(segments(text), want, "segments({text:?})");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn titles_reports_are_the_pythons_line_for_line() {
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("tmp", "tmp");
        tree.insert_file("some-disc/scan.txt", SCAN);
        tree.insert_file("some-disc/e16/rip-summary.json", r#"{"ok": true, "title": 0}"#);
        tree.insert_file("some-film/scan.txt", SCAN.replace("SINFO:1,3,3,0,\"fra\"", "SINFO:1,3,3,0,\"spa\""));
        tree.insert_file("some-film/tmdb.json", r#"{"original_language": "es"}"#);
        tree.insert_file("firefly/scan.txt", firefly_scan());
        assert_eq!(titles_report(&tree, &PathKey::new("some-disc")).unwrap(), SOME_DISC);
        assert_eq!(titles_report(&tree, &PathKey::new("some-film")).unwrap(), SOME_FILM_ES);
        assert_eq!(titles_report(&tree, &PathKey::new("firefly")).unwrap(), FIREFLY);
    }

    #[test]
    fn edge_cases_of_rip_summaries_languages_and_durations_are_the_pythons() {
        let info = audio_by_title(&parse(EXTRA)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(info[&1], TitleAudio { seconds: 60, segments: vec![], languages: BTreeMap::new() });
        assert_eq!(info[&5], TitleAudio { seconds: 0, segments: vec![], languages: BTreeMap::new() });
        assert_eq!(info[&6].languages, langs(&[("eng", &[1]), ("und", &[2])]));
        assert_eq!(info[&7], TitleAudio { seconds: 1800, segments: vec![3, 8], languages: langs(&[("deu", &[1, 2])]) });
        assert!(!info.contains_key(&9));
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("tmp", "tmp");
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/scan.txt", EXTRA);
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/tmdb.json", r#"{"original_language": "de", "fetched_at": "2026-10-01"}"#);
        // not JSON: skipped (the Python's `except ValueError`)
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/bad/rip-summary.json", "{");
        // a title that is not an int: skipped
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/str/rip-summary.json", r#"{"ok": true, "title": "6"}"#);
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/fail/rip-summary.json", r#"{"ok": false, "title": 6}"#);
        // isinstance(True, int) holds in Python: title 1; no "ok": failed
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/bool/rip-summary.json", r#"{"title": true}"#);
        // a byte-order mark is read past (utf-8-sig); ok 1 is truthy
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/bom/rip-summary.json", b"\xef\xbb\xbf{\"ok\": 1, \"title\": 7}".to_vec());
        // a float is not an int: skipped
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/float/rip-summary.json", r#"{"ok": true, "title": 7.0}"#);
        tree.insert_file("extra-disc/a-ok/rip-summary.json", r#"{"ok": true, "title": 6}"#);
        assert_eq!(titles_report(&tree, &PathKey::new("extra-disc")).unwrap(), EXTRA_DISC);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_golden_folder_is_never_listed_as_a_rip() {
        // Review Focus item 2: spec section 5 reserves the folder name golden/, and Tree::glob never returns it.
        let mut tree = MemTree::new("tmp", "tmp");
        tree.insert_file("some-disc/scan.txt", SCAN);
        tree.insert_file("some-disc/golden/rip-summary.json", r#"{"ok": true, "title": 0}"#);
        let lines = titles_report(&tree, &PathKey::new("some-disc")).unwrap();
        assert!(lines.iter().all(|line| !line.contains("ripped as")), "{lines:#?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unreadable_flags_attribute_on_an_audio_stream_is_an_error() {
        // int(a.get(22, "0") or 0) raised ValueError in the Python (a crash); the command exits 2 on it.
        let scan = parse("TINFO:0,9,0,\"0:01:00\"\nSINFO:0,1,1,0,\"Audio\"\nSINFO:0,1,22,0,\"x\"\n");
        let error = audio_by_title(&scan).unwrap_err();
        assert!(error.contains("invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'x'"), "{error}");
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write `core::audio::titles`**

Insert above the `#[cfg(test)]` line of `crates/core/src/audio/titles.rs`. Loop orders are the Python's: titles in `scan.titles` order and streams in sorted `(title, stream)` order (both `BTreeMap`s), rip summaries in sorted path order (`Tree::glob`), titles longest first then by number. `str.isdigit` and `int` are `py_isdigit` and `py_int`, `str.strip` is `py_strip`, `{original or 'unknown'}` is `py_truthy` and `py_str`, `ISO639.get` is `iso639`.

```rust
//! The `titles` listing of a recorded scan (EXP-13 addendum 9.1): every title longest first, its audio streams by
//! language without the streams MakeMKV derived from another, a mark when one language has two or more streams or
//! the wanted languages have two or more together, the labels it was ripped under, and the titles it shares
//! segments with (not on a DVD). Py: audio_similarity.segments, audio_by_title, dvd_scan, titles_report.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use serde_json::Value;

use crate::lang::{iso639, NO_LANGUAGE};
use crate::recording::{
    decode_text, py_int, py_isdigit, py_str, py_strip, py_truthy, read_json, read_text, Encoding, Errors, PathKey,
    Tree,
};
use crate::robot::{duration_seconds, int_attr, parse, Scan};

/// Scan flag (attribute 22) of a stream MakeMKV derived from another, such as the DTS core of a DTS-HD MA track.
/// Py: DERIVED.
const DERIVED: i64 = 2048;

/// The listing's second line, verbatim.
const AUDIO_LINE: &str =
    "  audio: scan stream numbers by language, leaving out streams MakeMKV derived from another (flag 2048)";

/// The listing's line for a DVD, verbatim.
const DVD_LINE: &str = "  segments: a DVD's are the cells of each title's own program chain, numbered from 1 in every title, so shared segments are not looked for (a play-all title is not marked)";

/// A scan's segment map (title attribute 26), such as "7", "10,11" or "1-3", as segment numbers; a part that is not
/// a number or a range of numbers is skipped. Py: segments.
pub fn segments(text: &str) -> Vec<i64> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for part in text.split(',') {
        let part = py_strip(part);
        // part.partition("-")
        let (lo, hi) = match part.find('-') {
            Some(at) => (&part[..at], &part[at + 1..]),
            None => (part, ""),
        };
        if py_isdigit(lo) && (hi.is_empty() || py_isdigit(hi)) {
            // A number too large for i64 is skipped (the Python would build a range it cannot hold).
            if let (Some(first), Some(last)) = (py_int(lo), py_int(if hi.is_empty() { lo } else { hi })) {
                out.extend(first..=last);
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

/// One title's duration, segments and audio streams by language (derived streams, flag 2048, left out; "" is
/// "und"). Py: the tuples of audio_by_title.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct TitleAudio {
    pub seconds: u32,
    pub segments: Vec<i64>,
    pub languages: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u32>>,
}

/// Every title of a scan; a title whose duration does not parse has 0 seconds. Err where int_attr(22) raised (the
/// Python's ValueError). Py: audio_by_title.
pub fn audio_by_title(scan: &Scan) -> Result<BTreeMap<u32, TitleAudio>, String> {
    let mut out = BTreeMap::new();
    for (&title, a) in &scan.titles {
        let seconds = duration_seconds(a.get(&9).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("0:00:00")).unwrap_or(0);
        let segs = segments(a.get(&26).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or(""));
        out.insert(title, TitleAudio { seconds, segments: segs, languages: BTreeMap::new() });
    }
    for (&(title, stream), a) in &scan.streams {
        // `title not in out or a.get(1) != "Audio" or int(a.get(22, "0") or 0) & DERIVED`, in that order: the
        // flags attribute is read only for an audio stream of a listed title.
        let Some(entry) = out.get_mut(&title) else { continue };
        if a.get(&1).map(String::as_str) != Some("Audio") {
            continue;
        }
        if int_attr(a, 22)? & DERIVED != 0 {
            continue;
        }
        let language = match a.get(&3) {
            Some(code) if !code.is_empty() => code.clone(),
            _ => "und".to_string(),
        };
        entry.languages.entry(language).or_default().push(stream);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// True for the scan of a DVD: no title names its source file (attribute 16, a Blu-ray's playlist), and the disc
/// says DVD (disc attribute 1) or a stream is DVD video or DVD subtitles (codec V_MPEG2 or S_VOBSUB). Py: dvd_scan.
pub fn dvd_scan(scan: &Scan) -> bool {
    if scan.titles.values().any(|a| a.contains_key(&16)) {
        return false;
    }
    scan.disc.get(&1).map_or(false, |disc| disc.contains("DVD"))
        || scan
            .streams
            .values()
            .any(|s| matches!(s.get(&5).map(String::as_str), Some("V_MPEG2") | Some("S_VOBSUB")))
}

/// The `titles` listing of `<recording>/scan.txt`, line for line. Err when scan.txt or tmdb.json cannot be read, or
/// a rip-summary.json cannot be read from disk or is JSON but not an object, or tmdb.json is not an object or its
/// original_language is a list or an object (where the Python crashed). Py: titles_report.
pub fn titles_report(tree: &dyn Tree, recording: &PathKey) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let scan = parse(&read_text(tree, &recording.join("scan.txt"), Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)?);

    // The labels each title was ripped under: <label>/rip-summary.json with an int "title", " (failed)" unless "ok".
    let mut ripped: BTreeMap<i64, Vec<String>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for path in tree.glob(recording, "*/rip-summary.json") {
        let bytes = tree.read(&path).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        // json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")) under `except ValueError: continue`: a decoding error
        // (UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError) and a JSON syntax error skip the file.
        let Ok(text) = decode_text(&bytes[..], Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict) else { continue };
        let Ok(rip) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text) else { continue };
        let Some(rip) = rip.as_object() else {
            return Err(format!("{}: not a JSON object", tree.display(&path)));
        };
        // isinstance(rip.get("title"), int): a JSON integer, or a bool (True is the int 1 in Python).
        let title = match rip.get("title") {
            Some(Value::Number(n)) => n.as_i64(),
            Some(Value::Bool(b)) => Some(i64::from(*b)),
            _ => None,
        };
        let Some(title) = title else { continue };
        let ok = rip.get("ok").map_or(false, py_truthy);
        let label = format!("{}{}", path.parent().name(), if ok { "" } else { " (failed)" });
        ripped.entry(title).or_default().push(label);
    }

    // TMDb's original language: the wanted languages are English and its codes.
    let tmdb = recording.join("tmdb.json");
    let original = if tree.exists(&tmdb) {
        match read_json::<Value>(tree, &tmdb)? {
            Value::Object(doc) => doc.get("original_language").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null),
            _ => return Err(format!("{}: not a JSON object", tree.display(&tmdb))),
        }
    } else {
        Value::Null
    };
    let codes: &[&str] = match &original {
        Value::String(code) => iso639(code).unwrap_or(&[]),
        Value::Array(_) | Value::Object(_) => {
            return Err(format!("{}: original_language is not a language code", tree.display(&tmdb)));
        }
        _ => &[],
    };
    let wanted = |lang: &str| lang == "eng" || codes.contains(&lang);

    let info = audio_by_title(&scan)?;
    let dvd = dvd_scan(&scan);
    let shown = if py_truthy(&original) { py_str(&original) } else { "unknown".to_string() };
    let mut lines = vec![
        format!("{}: {} titles, longest first; TMDb original language: {}", recording.name(), info.len(), shown),
        AUDIO_LINE.to_string(),
    ];
    if dvd {
        lines.push(DVD_LINE.to_string());
    }
    let mut order: Vec<u32> = info.keys().copied().collect();
    // sorted(info, key=lambda t: (-info[t][0], t))
    order.sort_by(|a, b| info[b].seconds.cmp(&info[a].seconds).then(a.cmp(b)));
    for title in order {
        let t = &info[&title];
        let audio: Vec<String> = t
            .languages
            .iter()
            .map(|(lang, streams)| {
                let numbers: Vec<String> = streams.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
                format!("{} {}", lang, numbers.join(","))
            })
            .collect();
        let audio = if audio.is_empty() { "none".to_string() } else { audio.join("; ") };
        let mut notes: Vec<String> = t
            .languages
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, streams)| streams.len() >= 2)
            .map(|(lang, streams)| format!("<- {} x{}", lang, streams.len()))
            .collect();
        let mine: Vec<(&String, &Vec<u32>)> = t
            .languages
            .iter()
            .filter(|(lang, _)| wanted(lang.as_str()) || NO_LANGUAGE.contains(&lang.as_str()))
            .collect();
        let together: usize = mine.iter().map(|(_, streams)| streams.len()).sum();
        if together >= 2 && mine.iter().all(|(_, streams)| streams.len() < 2) {
            let each: Vec<String> = mine.iter().map(|(lang, streams)| format!("{} {}", lang, streams.len())).collect();
            notes.push(format!("<- wanted x{} ({})", together, each.join(", ")));
        }
        if let Some(labels) = ripped.get(&i64::from(title)) {
            notes.push(format!("ripped as {}", labels.join(", ")));
        }
        let shared: Vec<String> = if dvd {
            Vec::new()
        } else {
            info.iter()
                .filter(|&(&other, o)| other != title && t.segments.iter().any(|s| o.segments.contains(s)))
                .map(|(other, _)| other.to_string())
                .collect()
        };
        if !shared.is_empty() {
            notes.push(format!("shares segments with title {}", shared.join(", ")));
        }
        let segs: Vec<String> = t.segments.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        let place = if segs.is_empty() { "?".to_string() } else { segs.join(",") };
        let duration = scan.titles[&title].get(&9).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("?");
        let line = format!("  title {:>3}  {:>8}  segments {:<8}  audio {}", title, duration, place, audio);
        lines.push(if notes.is_empty() { line } else { format!("{}   {}", line, notes.join("; ")) });
    }
    Ok(lines)
}
```
