```rust
//! The text rule for English subtitle tracks (design spec 8.7, experiment 14; EXP-14-design.md section 3): the port
//! of the phase 0 Python `subtitle_text` of commit 75fa76a's tree, translated in its loop order. Every threshold is
//! in `Rule` and is PROVISIONAL.
//!
//! `core` reads nothing: `load_title` and `subs_run` take the recording and the OCR text as trees (port spec 3.2).
//! Event lines and event words hold subtitle text in memory only; the lines this module prints hold numbers,
//! classes and decisions only, and `SubsJson` holds no line, word or word pair.
//!
//! Exactness (port spec section 4):
//! - every `round(x, 3)` and `round(x, 4)` of the Python is `py_round` (half to even on the exact binary value);
//! - every pattern runs on folded text, which is ASCII. Python's `\s` also matches `\x1c` to `\x1f` (`str.isspace`)
//!   where the Rust crates' `\s` does not, so the patterns spell it `[\s\x1C-\x1F]` and `\S` as `[^\s\x1C-\x1F]`;
//!   `str.isalpha` and `str.lower` on ASCII are `is_ascii_alphabetic` and `to_ascii_lowercase`;
//! - `bisect`, `sorted`, `min` and `max` keep their tie rules (stable sorts; the first of equals wins);
//! - spec87 iterates its dialogue group in CPython 3.9's set order (`PySet`), which decides SDH against regular when
//!   the group's two tracks have the same number of events.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::sync::LazyLock;

use unicode_normalization::char::canonical_combining_class;
use unicode_normalization::UnicodeNormalization;

use crate::recording::{py_fixed, py_strip, Ordered};

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the thresholds

/// The rule's thresholds with the Python's defaults (all PROVISIONAL); the field names are RULE's keys. Tests change
/// one with struct update syntax (`Rule { SDH_SO: 0, ..Rule::default() }`, the Python's mock.patch.dict).
/// Py: subtitle_text.RULE.
#[allow(non_snake_case)]
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Rule {
    /// sub_clear_max_bytes (spec 8.7): larger packets are displayed events.
    pub CLEAR_MAX_BYTES: i64,
    /// subs_tolerance_ms (spec 8.7), in seconds.
    pub TOL_S: f64,
    /// subs_same_min: timing says same group.
    pub SAME_MIN: f64,
    /// subs_diff_max: timing says different groups.
    pub DIFF_MAX: f64,
    /// A full track has at least this share of the largest English track's events.
    pub FULL_SHARE: f64,
    /// 8.7: a separately authored forced track has fewer events.
    pub FORCED_MAX_EVENTS: i64,
    /// Readability: share of events with 2 or more letters.
    pub READ_LETTER_EVENTS: f64,
    /// Share of word-like tokens (note stand-ins and '|' not counted).
    pub READ_WORDLIKE: f64,
    pub READ_MIN_WORDS: i64,
    /// A cue counts only in an event whose own tokens are at least this word-like.
    pub EVENT_WORDLIKE: f64,
    /// Language (stopword shares on ASCII-folded words).
    pub LANG_MIN_WORDS: i64,
    /// English when the English share is at least this.
    pub EN_MIN: f64,
    /// Another language when English is at most this ...
    pub EN_MAX_OTHER: f64,
    /// ... and that language's share is at least this ...
    pub OTHER_MIN: f64,
    /// ... and at least this many times the English share.
    pub OTHER_RATIO: f64,
    /// SDH evidence on one track: share of capital lines at which the whole track is in capitals.
    pub CAPS_STYLE: f64,
    /// Marker events (cue, label or '>>').
    pub SDH_M: i64,
    /// ... per event.
    pub SDH_RATE: f64,
    /// Sound-only events (every letter inside a cue or label).
    pub SDH_SO: i64,
    /// Events with a cue that names a sound.
    pub SDH_CS: i64,
    /// At most this many marker events: no SDH evidence.
    pub REG_M_MAX: i64,
    /// More events with damaged brackets than this: not placed.
    pub ODD_MAX: i64,
    /// More capital sound lines without brackets than this: not placed (UK style?).
    pub CAPS_CUE_MAX: i64,
    /// Pair: capital-only events with no counterpart (reported; review only).
    pub UC_MIN: i64,
    /// Content of two tracks (time-free bigram containment).
    pub CB_MIN_BIGRAMS: i64,
    /// Both directions at least this: same words.
    pub CB_SAME: f64,
    /// Both directions at most this: other words.
    pub CB_DIFF: f64,
    /// Subset: the smaller track's bigrams found in the larger at least this ...
    pub CB_SUBSET_IN: f64,
    /// ... and the larger's found in the smaller under this ...
    pub CB_SUBSET_BACK: f64,
    /// ... and the smaller has at most this share of the larger's events.
    pub SUBSET_EVENTS: f64,
    /// Forced candidate confirmed: its bigrams found in the dialogue track.
    pub FORCED_CB: f64,
    /// Forced candidate with this share of note-line events: lyrics, review.
    pub NOTE_LINES: f64,
}

impl Default for Rule {
    fn default() -> Rule {
        Rule {
            CLEAR_MAX_BYTES: 64,
            TOL_S: 0.300,
            SAME_MIN: 0.70,
            DIFF_MAX: 0.30,
            FULL_SHARE: 0.10,
            FORCED_MAX_EVENTS: 150,
            READ_LETTER_EVENTS: 0.90,
            READ_WORDLIKE: 0.85,
            READ_MIN_WORDS: 20,
            EVENT_WORDLIKE: 0.50,
            LANG_MIN_WORDS: 50,
            EN_MIN: 0.20,
            EN_MAX_OTHER: 0.08,
            OTHER_MIN: 0.12,
            OTHER_RATIO: 3.0,
            CAPS_STYLE: 0.50,
            SDH_M: 5,
            SDH_RATE: 0.010,
            SDH_SO: 3,
            SDH_CS: 2,
            REG_M_MAX: 0,
            ODD_MAX: 2,
            CAPS_CUE_MAX: 2,
            UC_MIN: 3,
            CB_MIN_BIGRAMS: 20,
            CB_SAME: 0.50,
            CB_DIFF: 0.20,
            CB_SUBSET_IN: 0.60,
            CB_SUBSET_BACK: 0.50,
            SUBSET_EVENTS: 0.70,
            FORCED_CB: 0.60,
            NOTE_LINES: 0.30,
        }
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ Python's spellings

/// round(x, ndigits) as Python 3.9 rounds a float (float___round__): a NaN or an infinity, or more digits than a
/// double has, is x itself; otherwise the exact decimal expansion of x rounded half to even to `ndigits` places
/// (`_Py_dg_dtoa` mode 3, the digits '%.Nf' prints, here `py_fixed`), read back as the nearest double. Every
/// round(x, 3) and round(x, 4) of the module goes through it, because those values meet thresholds. Negative
/// `ndigits` (rounding to tens) is not used by the module and panics. Py: round.
pub fn py_round(x: f64, ndigits: i32) -> f64 {
    // NDIGITS_MAX of floatobject.c: (DBL_MANT_DIG - DBL_MIN_EXP) * 0.30103, truncated.
    if !x.is_finite() || ndigits > 323 {
        return x;
    }
    assert!(ndigits >= 0, "py_round: negative ndigits are not used by subtitle_text");
    py_fixed(x, ndigits as usize).parse::<f64>().expect("'%.Nf' of a finite float reads back")
}

/// Python's titlecase letters (general category Lt, Unicode 13): `str.islower` and `str.isupper` refuse a string
/// holding one. Py: Py_UNICODE_ISTITLE.
fn is_titlecase(c: char) -> bool {
    matches!(
        c,
        '\u{01C5}'
            | '\u{01C8}'
            | '\u{01CB}'
            | '\u{01F2}'
            | '\u{1F88}'..='\u{1F8F}'
            | '\u{1F98}'..='\u{1F9F}'
            | '\u{1FA8}'..='\u{1FAF}'
            | '\u{1FBC}'
            | '\u{1FCC}'
            | '\u{1FFC}'
    )
}

/// str.islower: no uppercase or titlecase character and at least one lowercase one. Python's lowercase and uppercase
/// are the Unicode derived properties Lowercase and Uppercase, which `char::is_lowercase` and `char::is_uppercase`
/// test. Py: unicode_islower_impl.
fn py_islower(s: &str) -> bool {
    let mut cased = false;
    for c in s.chars() {
        if c.is_uppercase() || is_titlecase(c) {
            return false;
        }
        if !cased && c.is_lowercase() {
            cased = true;
        }
    }
    cased
}

/// str.isupper: no lowercase or titlecase character and at least one uppercase one. Py: unicode_isupper_impl.
fn py_isupper(s: &str) -> bool {
    let mut cased = false;
    for c in s.chars() {
        if c.is_lowercase() || is_titlecase(c) {
            return false;
        }
        if !cased && c.is_uppercase() {
            cased = true;
        }
    }
    cased
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ CPython's set order

/// CPython 3.9's set table constants (Objects/setobject.c).
const SET_MINSIZE: usize = 8;
const LINEAR_PROBES: usize = 9;
const PERTURB_SHIFT: u32 = 5;

/// A set of stream numbers laid out as CPython 3.9's set object lays out non-negative ints (hash(n) == n; nothing is
/// ever removed), so that iterating it gives the Python's order. Only spec87 needs it: it sorts its dialogue group's
/// members by event count with a stable sort, so two members with the same count keep the set's order.
/// Py: set_add_entry, set_insert_clean, set_table_resize, set_merge, set_copy and set_or of setobject.c (3.9).
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct PySet {
    table: Vec<Option<i64>>,
    fill: usize,
    used: usize,
}

impl PySet {
    /// set(): an empty table of SET_MINSIZE slots.
    fn empty() -> PySet {
        PySet { table: vec![None; SET_MINSIZE], fill: 0, used: 0 }
    }

    /// `{n}`: BUILD_SET adds its one item to an empty set.
    fn singleton(n: i64) -> PySet {
        let mut set = PySet::empty();
        set.add(n);
        set
    }

    fn mask(&self) -> usize {
        self.table.len() - 1
    }

    /// hash(n) of a non-negative int below 2**61 - 1 is n.
    fn hash(key: i64) -> usize {
        assert!(key >= 0, "stream numbers are not negative");
        key as usize
    }

    /// set_insert_clean: the first empty slot of the probe sequence (no key equal to `key` is in the table).
    fn insert_clean(table: &mut [Option<i64>], key: i64) {
        let mask = table.len() - 1;
        let hash = PySet::hash(key);
        let mut perturb = hash;
        let mut i = hash & mask;
        loop {
            if table[i].is_none() {
                table[i] = Some(key);
                return;
            }
            if i + LINEAR_PROBES <= mask {
                for j in 1..=LINEAR_PROBES {
                    if table[i + j].is_none() {
                        table[i + j] = Some(key);
                        return;
                    }
                }
            }
            perturb >>= PERTURB_SHIFT;
            i = (i * 5 + 1 + perturb) & mask;
        }
    }

    /// set_table_resize: the smallest power of two above `minused` (at least SET_MINSIZE), every key reinserted in
    /// the old table's slot order.
    fn resize(&mut self, minused: usize) {
        let mut size = SET_MINSIZE;
        while size <= minused {
            size <<= 1;
        }
        let old = std::mem::replace(&mut self.table, vec![None; size]);
        for key in old.into_iter().flatten() {
            PySet::insert_clean(&mut self.table, key);
        }
        self.fill = self.used;
    }

    /// set_add_entry: nothing when `key` is in the probe sequence, else the first empty slot of it, then a resize
    /// to used * 4 once fill * 5 >= mask * 3.
    fn add(&mut self, key: i64) {
        let mask = self.mask();
        let hash = PySet::hash(key);
        let mut perturb = hash;
        let mut i = hash & mask;
        let slot = 'probe: loop {
            match self.table[i] {
                None => break 'probe i,
                Some(k) if k == key => return,
                Some(_) => {}
            }
            if i + LINEAR_PROBES <= mask {
                for j in 1..=LINEAR_PROBES {
                    match self.table[i + j] {
                        None => break 'probe i + j,
                        Some(k) if k == key => return,
                        Some(_) => {}
                    }
                }
            }
            perturb >>= PERTURB_SHIFT;
            i = (i * 5 + 1 + perturb) & mask;
        };
        self.table[slot] = Some(key);
        self.fill += 1;
        self.used += 1;
        if self.fill * 5 >= mask * 3 {
            let minused = if self.used > 50_000 { self.used * 2 } else { self.used * 4 };
            self.resize(minused);
        }
    }

    /// set_merge (`update` with another set): one resize first when the keys may not fit, then the table copied
    /// as it is, or inserted clean in the other's slot order into an empty table, or added one by one.
    fn merge(&mut self, other: &PySet) {
        if other.used == 0 {
            return;
        }
        if (self.fill + other.used) * 5 >= self.mask() * 3 {
            self.resize((self.used + other.used) * 2);
        }
        if self.fill == 0 && self.mask() == other.mask() && other.fill == other.used {
            self.table = other.table.clone();
            self.fill = other.fill;
            self.used = other.used;
            return;
        }
        if self.fill == 0 {
            self.fill = other.used;
            self.used = other.used;
            for key in other.table.iter().flatten() {
                PySet::insert_clean(&mut self.table, *key);
            }
            return;
        }
        for key in other.table.iter().flatten() {
            self.add(*key);
        }
    }

    /// set_copy: a new set merged from this one. `a | a` is this copy (set_or returns it when both are one object).
    fn copy(&self) -> PySet {
        let mut set = PySet::empty();
        set.merge(self);
        set
    }

    /// `self | other` for two different set objects (set_or): a copy of self updated with other.
    fn union(&self, other: &PySet) -> PySet {
        let mut set = self.copy();
        set.merge(other);
        set
    }

    /// The keys in slot order. Py: iter(set).
    fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = i64> + '_ {
        self.table.iter().flatten().copied()
    }

    fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.used
    }

    fn contains(&self, key: i64) -> bool {
        self.iter().any(|k| k == key)
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ folding

/// FOLD_MAP: the music notes and the pilcrow become '#', the note stand-in, so that an engine that ever returns a
/// note is read the same way as one that returns '#'. The inverted ? and ! are dropped: an ASCII-only engine cannot
/// read them, and Tesseract's English model turns them into other characters anyway. Py: FOLD_MAP.
fn fold_map(c: char) -> Option<&'static str> {
    Some(match c {
        '\u{2018}' | '\u{2019}' | '\u{201A}' | '\u{2032}' | '\u{00B4}' | '\u{0060}' | '\u{02BC}' => "'",
        '\u{201C}' | '\u{201D}' | '\u{201E}' | '\u{00AB}' | '\u{00BB}' | '\u{2033}' => "\"",
        '\u{2010}' | '\u{2011}' | '\u{2012}' | '\u{2013}' | '\u{2014}' | '\u{2015}' | '\u{2212}' => "-",
        '\u{2026}' => "...",
        '\u{00A0}' => " ",
        '\u{2669}' | '\u{266A}' | '\u{266B}' | '\u{266C}' | '\u{266D}' | '\u{266F}' | '\u{00B6}' => "#",
        '\u{00BF}' | '\u{00A1}' => "",
        '\u{00DF}' => "ss",
        '\u{00E6}' => "ae",
        '\u{00C6}' => "AE",
        '\u{0153}' => "oe",
        '\u{0152}' => "OE",
        '\u{00F8}' => "o",
        '\u{00D8}' => "O",
        '\u{0142}' => "l",
        '\u{0141}' => "L",
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// ASCII text: FOLD_MAP, then NFKD without characters of non-zero canonical combining class
/// (`unicodedata.combining`), then every other non-ASCII character dropped. Py: fold.
pub fn fold(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut mapped = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for c in s.chars() {
        match fold_map(c) {
            Some(to) => mapped.push_str(to),
            None => mapped.push(c),
        }
    }
    mapped.nfkd().filter(|&c| canonical_combining_class(c) == 0 && (c as u32) < 128).collect()
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ lines and OCR corrections

/// Lines of the proof of concept's text, whose lines are joined with ' | ' while Tesseract reads a capital I as
/// '|'. With the frame's true line count, the extra bare '|' tokens are taken as I, preferring the text start, a
/// '|' after another '|' and a '|' before a lower-case word; without it (`nlines` None or 0), every ' | ' is a line
/// break. `nxt[:1] in '-(['` is true for an empty next token too (the empty string is in every string), which the
/// score keeps. Py: split_joined.
pub fn split_joined(text: &str, nlines: Option<i64>) -> Vec<String> {
    let toks: Vec<&str> = text.split(' ').collect();
    let bare: Vec<usize> = toks.iter().enumerate().filter(|(_, tok)| **tok == "|").map(|(i, _)| i).collect();
    let n_i: usize = match nlines {
        None | Some(0) => 0,
        Some(n) => (bare.len() as i64 - (n - 1)).max(0) as usize,
    };
    let score = |i: usize| -> i64 {
        let nxt = toks.get(i + 1).copied().unwrap_or("");
        let first: String = nxt.chars().take(1).collect();
        let mut s = if i == 0 { 3 } else { 0 };
        if i > 0 && toks[i - 1] == "|" {
            s += 1;
        }
        if py_islower(&first) || first == "'" {
            s += 2;
        }
        if py_isupper(&first) || first.is_empty() || matches!(first.as_str(), "-" | "(" | "[") {
            s -= 1;
        }
        s
    };
    let mut ranked = bare.clone();
    ranked.sort_by_key(|&i| (-score(i), i));
    let as_i: BTreeSet<usize> = ranked.into_iter().take(n_i).collect();
    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut cur: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    for (i, &tok) in toks.iter().enumerate() {
        if tok == "|" && !as_i.contains(&i) {
            lines.push(cur.join(" "));
            cur = Vec::new();
        } else {
            cur.push(tok);
        }
    }
    lines.push(cur.join(" "));
    lines.iter().map(|x| py_strip(x)).filter(|x| !x.is_empty()).map(str::to_string).collect()
}

/// The seven corrections for English text from Tesseract (I read as '|', 'l' or '1'), applied to English-tagged
/// streams in this order: (name, pattern, replacement). They use look-behind and look-ahead, so they run on
/// `fancy_regex`; `[\s\x1C-\x1F]` is Python's `\s` (see the module notes). Py: CORRECTIONS.
const CORRECTION_PATTERNS: [(&str, &str, &str); 7] = [
    // "|", "|!", "|'m"
    ("pipe_I", r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])\|(?=[\s\x1C-\x1F'.,?!]|$)", "I"),
    // "|t's"
    ("pipe_word_I", r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])\|(?=[a-z])", "I"),
    // "he|lo"
    ("pipe_l", r"(?<=[a-z])\|(?=[a-z])", "l"),
    // "BORlS", "WHlSTLlNG"
    ("caps_I", r"(?<=[A-Z])[l1|](?=[A-Z])", "I"),
    ("caps_O", r"(?<=[A-Z])0(?=[A-Z])", "O"),
    ("l1_pronoun", r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9'])[l1](?='(?:m|ll|d|ve)\b)", "I"),
    // "lam", "1am"
    ("i_am", r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])[|l1]am\b", "I am"),
];

/// The counter correct() adds after the seven: the '|' left, each turned into 'l'.
const PIPE_LEFT: &str = "pipe_left";

/// (name, pattern, replacement) of the seven corrections, compiled once. Py: CORRECTIONS.
pub fn corrections() -> &'static [(&'static str, fancy_regex::Regex, &'static str)] {
    static COMPILED: LazyLock<Vec<(&'static str, fancy_regex::Regex, &'static str)>> = LazyLock::new(|| {
        CORRECTION_PATTERNS
            .iter()
            .map(|&(name, pattern, rep)| (name, fancy_regex::Regex::new(pattern).expect("a correction compiles"), rep))
            .collect()
    });
    COMPILED.as_slice()
}

/// re.subn(pattern, rep, text): one pass over the original text, every non-overlapping match replaced, and the
/// number of replacements (fancy_regex's replace_all with a counting replacer). Py: rx.subn.
fn subn(rx: &fancy_regex::Regex, rep: &str, text: &str) -> (String, usize) {
    let mut k = 0usize;
    let out = rx
        .replace_all(text, |_: &fancy_regex::Captures<'_>| {
            k += 1;
            rep
        })
        .into_owned();
    (out, k)
}

/// The seven corrections in order, each counted under its name as re.subn counts, then the '|' left counted as
/// pipe_left and turned into 'l'. `counts` gets every name on every call, in that order. Py: correct.
pub fn correct(line: &str, counts: &mut Ordered<usize>) -> String {
    let mut line = line.to_string();
    for (name, rx, rep) in corrections() {
        let (fixed, k) = subn(rx, rep, &line);
        line = fixed;
        let total = counts.get(name).copied().unwrap_or(0) + k;
        counts.insert(name.to_string(), total);
    }
    let k = line.matches('|').count();
    let total = counts.get(PIPE_LEFT).copied().unwrap_or(0) + k;
    counts.insert(PIPE_LEFT.to_string(), total);
    line.replace('|', "l")
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ markers (on folded, corrected text)

/// Compiles one marker pattern with the `regex` crate, which has no look-around: compiling is the proof that the
/// pattern needs none (port spec 3.3).
fn marker(pattern: &str) -> regex::Regex {
    regex::Regex::new(pattern).expect("a marker pattern compiles without look-around")
}

/// A cue: a bracketed or parenthesised span of 2 to 80 characters, with at least 2 letters and only letters, digits,
/// spaces and light punctuation inside (OCR junk does not make one). Either bracket may close the other. Py: RE_CUE.
static RE_CUE: LazyLock<regex::Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    marker(r"[\[(][\s\x1C-\x1F]*([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 ',.!?&:;/\-]{0,78}[A-Za-z0-9.!?'])[\s\x1C-\x1F]*[\])]")
});
/// A capital speaker label at the start of a line, after an optional dash, followed by text on the same line.
/// Py: RE_LABEL (used with .match: the pattern starts with ^).
static RE_LABEL: LazyLock<regex::Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    marker(
        r"^[\s\x1C-\x1F]*(?:-[\s\x1C-\x1F]*)?([A-Z][A-Z0-9'.\-]*(?:[\s\x1C-\x1F]+[A-Z0-9'.\-]+){0,2})[\s\x1C-\x1F]*:[\s\x1C-\x1F]+[^\s\x1C-\x1F]",
    )
});
/// Py: RE_CHEV (used with .match).
static RE_CHEV: LazyLock<regex::Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| marker(r"^[\s\x1C-\x1F]*>>"));
/// Lyrics (note stand-in, strict): '#' or '*' at either end of a line, after folding (real notes are '#').
/// Py: RE_NOTE (used with .search).
static RE_NOTE: LazyLock<regex::Regex> =
    LazyLock::new(|| marker(r"^[\s\x1C-\x1F]*[#*]|[#*][\s\x1C-\x1F]*$"));
/// Lyrics (loose, ENGINE-DEPENDENT, reported only): a lone token reported as a Tesseract misread of a note.
/// Py: RE_NOTE_LOOSE (used with .search).
static RE_NOTE_LOOSE: LazyLock<regex::Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    marker(
        r"^[\s\x1C-\x1F]*(?:J|JJ|Jf|Ji|Jl|P|D|d|f|\$|%)[\s\x1C-\x1F]+[^\s\x1C-\x1F]|[^\s\x1C-\x1F][\s\x1C-\x1F]+(?:J|JJ|Jf|Ji|Jl|P|D|d|f|\$|%)[\s\x1C-\x1F]*$",
    )
});
/// Damaged brackets, on the folded text before corrections: a line wrapped in '|' or '{' '}' (a misread bracket
/// pair), counted per event together with unbalanced () and []. Py: RE_WRAP (used with .match).
static RE_WRAP: LazyLock<regex::Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    marker(
        r"^[\s\x1C-\x1F]*-?[\s\x1C-\x1F]*[|{][\s\x1C-\x1F]*[A-Za-z][^|{}()\[\]]*[A-Za-z.!?][\s\x1C-\x1F]*[|}][\s\x1C-\x1F]*$",
    )
});
/// Py: RE_WORD (used with .findall; its one group does not capture).
static RE_WORD: LazyLock<regex::Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| marker(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?"));
/// Py: RE_WORDLIKE, used with .fullmatch, so anchored here at both ends.
static RE_WORDLIKE: LazyLock<regex::Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    marker(r#"^(?:["'(\[-]*(?:[A-Za-z]+(?:[-'][A-Za-z]+)*|\d+(?:[.,:]\d+)*)["'.,!?:;)\]-]*)$"#)
});

/// STOP's word lists before its two adjustments, in its order. Py: STOP's literals.
const STOP_LISTS: [(&str, &str); 4] = [
    (
        "en",
        "the and is are was were be been to of in on at for with that this it you i he she we they my your me \
him her not do don't what have has will just so if there here can all get go know it's i'm you're that's would \
could did didn't can't from about out up yes oh well right okay",
    ),
    (
        "es",
        "el la los las de del que y en un una es se lo le por con para su al te mi tu yo pero como mas esta \
este eso esto si ya hay muy bien nos os usted senor ella ellos aqui nada todo cuando donde porque tengo tiene \
puede vamos",
    ),
    (
        "fr",
        "le les des du et est je tu il elle nous vous ils que qui ne pas pour dans sur avec ce cette mais ou mon \
ma oui non c'est j'ai tout bien ca moi toi lui suis sont fait rien ici",
    ),
    (
        "de",
        "der die das und ist ich du er sie wir ihr nicht ein eine zu mit auf fur den dem des es ja nein was wie \
aber auch noch mir mich dich hier sein haben bin bist wird kann",
    ),
];

/// English words that are common Spanish words, taken out of English. Py: the set subtracted from STOP['en'].
const NOT_ENGLISH: [&str; 10] = ["me", "he", "has", "a", "no", "son", "come", "sin", "con", "pan"];

/// The stopword sets in STOP's order (en, es, fr, de): a word in two lists counts for neither, and English loses
/// NOT_ENGLISH. Py: STOP after its two adjustments.
static STOP: LazyLock<Vec<(&'static str, BTreeSet<&'static str>)>> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    let mut langs_of: BTreeMap<&'static str, BTreeSet<&'static str>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for (lang, words) in STOP_LISTS {
        for word in words.split_whitespace() {
            langs_of.entry(word).or_default().insert(lang);
        }
    }
    STOP_LISTS
        .iter()
        .map(|&(lang, words)| {
            let mut set: BTreeSet<&'static str> =
                words.split_whitespace().filter(|word| langs_of[*word].len() == 1).collect();
            if lang == "en" {
                for word in NOT_ENGLISH {
                    set.remove(word);
                }
            }
            (lang, set)
        })
        .collect()
});

/// One language's stopwords. Py: STOP[lang].
fn stop(lang: &str) -> &'static BTreeSet<&'static str> {
    &STOP.iter().find(|(l, _)| *l == lang).expect("a language of STOP").1
}

/// Py: wordlike (RE_WORDLIKE.fullmatch).
fn wordlike(tok: &str) -> bool {
    RE_WORDLIKE.is_match(tok)
}
```

```rust
        let records = read_jsonl(jsonl).unwrap();
        let counts: BTreeMap<i64, Option<i64>> = BTreeMap::from([(1, Some(2)), (3, None)]);
        let recs = ocr_records(&records, &counts).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            recs,
            [
                rec(1.0, false, &["| went", "| home"]),
                rec(7.5, true, &["a", "3"]),
                rec(0.0, false, &["b", "c"]),
                rec(4.0, false, &["x", "y"]),
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn pair_text_pairs_by_time_with_the_pythons_ties() {
        // Equal counts: by order.
        let mut events = at(&[1.0, 2.0]);
        let recs = [rec(9.0, false, &["p"]), rec(0.0, false, &["q"])];
        assert_eq!(pair_text(&mut events, &recs), (PairMethod::Order, 0));
        assert_eq!(events[0].lines, ["p"]);
        // By time from the first frame ('t' plus the first event's start): ('time', 1) and
        // [['a', 'b'], ['c'], [], ['e']] (b is as near to 10.0 as to 10.4 in decimal, nearer 10.0 in binary).
        let mut events = at(&[10.0, 10.4, 11.0, 20.0]);
        let recs = [
            rec(0.0, false, &["a"]),
            rec(0.2, false, &["b"]),
            rec(0.65, false, &["c"]),
            rec(5.0, false, &["d"]),
            rec(9.8, false, &["e"]),
        ];
        assert_eq!(pair_text(&mut events, &recs), (PairMethod::Time, 1));
        let lines: Vec<Vec<String>> = events.iter().map(|e| e.lines.clone()).collect();
        assert_eq!(lines, [vec!["a", "b"], vec!["c"], vec![], vec!["e"]]);
        // Packet times ('pts'): no offset; ('time', 2) and [['tie'], []].
        let mut events = at(&[10.0, 10.4]);
        let recs = [rec(10.2, true, &["tie"]), rec(10.71, true, &["late"]), rec(9.6999, true, &["early"])];
        assert_eq!(pair_text(&mut events, &recs), (PairMethod::Time, 2));
        let lines: Vec<Vec<String>> = events.iter().map(|e| e.lines.clone()).collect();
        assert_eq!(lines, [vec!["tie"], vec![]]);
        // No events: every frame is left; no frames for one event: ('time', 0).
        assert_eq!(pair_text(&mut [], &recs), (PairMethod::Time, 3));
        assert_eq!(pair_text(&mut at(&[1.0]), &[]), (PairMethod::Time, 0));
    }
}
```

```rust
// ------------------------------------------------------------------ loading

use crate::recording::files::{OcrLine, Packet};
use crate::recording::{py_float_value, py_int_value, py_str};

/// Python's `a < b` for two floats as a total order for sorting: -0.0 equals 0.0 (Python's == says so and its
/// stable sort keeps their order); a NaN, which no input holds, sorts after every number instead of breaking the
/// sort. Py: the float comparisons of sorted() and list.sort().
fn py_cmp(a: f64, b: f64) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
    let zero_is_zero = |x: f64| if x == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { x };
    zero_is_zero(a).total_cmp(&zero_is_zero(b))
}

/// bisect.bisect_left on a list of floats, CPython's loop (the list need not be sorted). Py: bisect.bisect_left.
fn bisect_left(a: &[f64], x: f64) -> usize {
    let (mut lo, mut hi) = (0, a.len());
    while lo < hi {
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
        if a[mid] < x {
            lo = mid + 1;
        } else {
            hi = mid;
        }
    }
    lo
}

/// A displayed event: start and duration in seconds, and its OCR lines (empty when it has none). Holds subtitle
/// text in `lines`: in memory only. Py: the event dicts.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Event {
    pub start: f64,
    pub dur: f64,
    pub lines: Vec<String>,
}

/// One OCR frame with text: its time, whether that time is a packet time ('pts' in the record), its lines.
/// Py: ocr_records' dicts.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct OcrRecord {
    pub t: f64,
    pub pts: bool,
    pub lines: Vec<String>,
}

/// How pair_text paired: "order" (equal counts) or "time".
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PairMethod {
    Order,
    Time,
}

impl PairMethod {
    /// The Python's word.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            PairMethod::Order => "order",
            PairMethod::Time => "time",
        }
    }
}

/// Displayed events: packets with a pts_time larger than `clear_max_bytes` (every packet with a size when it is 0;
/// a packet without a size is size 0), duration 0.0 for None, "" or "N/A", sorted by start (stable). Err is the
/// Python's int() or float() text. Py: packet_events.
pub fn packet_events(packets: &[Packet], clear_max_bytes: i64) -> Result<Vec<Event>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for p in packets {
        let Some(pts) = &p.pts_time else {
            continue;
        };
        let size = match &p.size {
            Some(size) => py_int_value(size)?,
            None => 0,
        };
        if size <= clear_max_bytes {
            continue;
        }
        let start = py_float_value(pts)?;
        let dur = match &p.duration_time {
            None | Some(serde_json::Value::Null) => 0.0,
            Some(serde_json::Value::String(text)) if text.is_empty() || text == "N/A" => 0.0,
            Some(other) => py_float_value(other)?,
        };
        out.push(Event { start, dur, lines: Vec::new() });
    }
    out.sort_by(|a, b| py_cmp(a.start, b.start));
    Ok(out)
}

/// (t, lines) for every OCR frame with text. A record with a 'lines' array (the final ocr-subs.ps1) is taken as it
/// is (each item as str(), stripped, blanks dropped); the proof of concept's ' | '-joined text is split with the
/// frame's line count from `counts` (frame -> lines of sub-<n>.frames.json). The time is 'pts', else 't', else 0.0.
/// Never Err today (the records are typed); the Result keeps the reader's signature. Py: ocr_records (after its two
/// reads, which load_title does).
pub fn ocr_records(records: &[OcrLine], counts: &BTreeMap<i64, Option<i64>>) -> Result<Vec<OcrRecord>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for r in records {
        let lines: Vec<String> = match &r.lines {
            Some(serde_json::Value::Array(items)) => items
                .iter()
                .map(|item| py_strip(&py_str(item)).to_string())
                .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
                .collect(),
            _ => {
                let text = py_strip(r.text.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
                if text.is_empty() {
                    Vec::new()
                } else {
                    split_joined(text, r.frame.and_then(|frame| counts.get(&frame).copied().flatten()))
                }
            }
        };
        if !lines.is_empty() {
            out.push(OcrRecord { t: r.pts.or(r.t).unwrap_or(0.0), pts: r.pts.is_some(), lines });
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Gives each displayed event its OCR lines. Equal counts: by order (the k-th frame with text is the k-th event;
/// true on every real track so far). Otherwise by time: the proof of concept's 't' is the packet time minus the
/// file's first packet time, on a 0.25 s grid; each frame goes to the nearer of the two events around it (the
/// earlier on a tie) when it is within 0.30 s. Returns the method and the number of frames left unmatched.
/// Py: pair_text.
pub fn pair_text(events: &mut [Event], recs: &[OcrRecord]) -> (PairMethod, usize) {
    if recs.len() == events.len() {
        for (e, r) in events.iter_mut().zip(recs) {
            e.lines = r.lines.clone();
        }
        return (PairMethod::Order, 0);
    }
    for e in events.iter_mut() {
        e.lines = Vec::new();
    }
    if events.is_empty() {
        return (PairMethod::Time, recs.len());
    }
    let starts: Vec<f64> = events.iter().map(|e| e.start).collect();
    let off = if recs.first().is_some_and(|r| r.pts) {
        0.0
    } else {
        events[0].start - recs.first().map_or(0.0, |r| r.t)
    };
    let mut left = 0;
    for r in recs {
        let t = r.t + off;
        let i = bisect_left(&starts, t);
        // min((j for j in (i - 1, i) if 0 <= j < len(starts)), key=...): the first of equal distances wins.
        let mut best: Option<usize> = None;
        let candidates = [i.checked_sub(1), Some(i).filter(|&j| j < starts.len())];
        for j in candidates.into_iter().flatten() {
            match best {
                Some(b) if (starts[j] - t).abs() >= (starts[b] - t).abs() => {}
                _ => best = Some(j),
            }
        }
        let best = best.expect("an event lies on one side of every time");
        if (starts[best] - t).abs() <= 0.30 {
            events[best].lines.extend(r.lines.iter().cloned());
        } else {
            left += 1;
        }
    }
    (PairMethod::Time, left)
}
```

```rust
// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the generators of test_subtitle_text

use crate::testsupport::PyRandom;

/// Made-up words (letters only), so that no real subtitle text is needed. Py: made_up.
fn made_up(consonants: &str, vowels: &str, count: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut words = Vec::new();
    for a in consonants.chars() {
        for v in vowels.chars() {
            for b in consonants.chars() {
                for w in vowels.chars() {
                    words.push(format!("{a}{v}{b}{w}n"));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    words.truncate(count);
    words
}

static NOUNS: LazyLock<Vec<String>> = LazyLock::new(|| made_up("bdgkl", "aeiou", 400));
static VERBS: LazyLock<Vec<String>> = LazyLock::new(|| made_up("mprst", "aeiou", 200));
static OTHER: LazyLock<Vec<String>> = LazyLock::new(|| made_up("fhvwz", "aeiou", 400));
static OTHER_VERBS: LazyLock<Vec<String>> = LazyLock::new(|| made_up("cjnqx", "aeiou", 200));
/// Py: SPANISH (a made-up sentence of common Spanish words).
const SPANISH: &str = "el perro de la casa y los ninos que no tienen nada para comer pero ella dice que esta bien con \
                       su madre aqui en el pueblo cuando llueve";

fn spanish() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    SPANISH.split_whitespace().collect()
}

/// Which word lists a sentence draws from: NOUNS with VERBS, or OTHER with OTHER_VERBS. Py: `nouns is NOUNS`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Words {
    Nouns,
    Other,
}

/// Py: sentence(rnd, nouns), its four choices in the Python's order.
fn sentence(rnd: &mut PyRandom, nouns: Words) -> String {
    let (nouns, verbs): (&[String], &[String]) = match nouns {
        Words::Nouns => (NOUNS.as_slice(), VERBS.as_slice()),
        Words::Other => (OTHER.as_slice(), OTHER_VERBS.as_slice()),
    };
    let verb = rnd.choice(verbs).clone();
    let a = rnd.choice(nouns).clone();
    let b = rnd.choice(nouns).clone();
    let c = rnd.choice(nouns).clone();
    format!("we {verb} the {a} and the {b} with the {c}")
}

/// str.capitalize on ASCII: the first character upper case, the rest lower case.
fn capitalize(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut chars = s.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(first) => first.to_ascii_uppercase().to_string() + &chars.as_str().to_ascii_lowercase(),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}

/// Py: track(n, events, tag='eng', forced=False).
fn track(n: i64, events: Vec<Event>, tag: &str, forced: bool) -> Track {
    Track::new(n, tag, None, forced, events)
}

/// Py: track(n, events) (an English stream, not flagged forced).
fn eng(n: i64, events: Vec<Event>) -> Track {
    track(n, events, "eng", false)
}

/// Py: dialogue(count, seed, nouns, start, step).
fn dialogue(count: usize, seed: u64, nouns: Words, start: f64, step: f64) -> Vec<Event> {
    let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(seed);
    (0..count)
        .map(|i| Event {
            start: start + i as f64 * step,
            dur: 2.5,
            lines: vec![capitalize(&sentence(&mut rnd, nouns)) + "."],
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Py: dialogue() with its defaults (120 events, seed 1, NOUNS, from 10.0 s every 4.0 s).
fn base() -> Vec<Event> {
    dialogue(120, 1, Words::Nouns, 10.0, 4.0)
}

/// list.sort(key=lambda e: e['start']): stable.
fn sort_by_start(events: &mut [Event]) {
    events.sort_by(|a, b| py_cmp(a.start, b.start));
}

/// Adds stand-alone sound cues between events and capital speaker labels to some events. Py: sdh_version(events)
/// with its defaults (8 cues, 6 labels).
fn sdh_version(events: &[Event]) -> Vec<Event> {
    let (cues, labels) = (8usize, 6usize);
    let mut out: Vec<Event> = events.to_vec();
    let step = events.len() / (cues.max(labels) + 1);
    for k in 0..labels {
        let e = &mut out[2 + step * k];
        e.lines[0] = format!("ANNA: {}", e.lines[0]);
    }
    let sounds = [
        "(DOOR SLAMS)",
        "(PHONE RINGING)",
        "(GLASS SHATTERS)",
        "[sighs]",
        "(SIREN WAILING)",
        "(KNOCKING)",
        "(DOG BARKING)",
        "(WIND HOWLING)",
        "(COUGHS)",
        "(THUNDER RUMBLING)",
    ];
    for k in 0..cues {
        let e = &events[3 + step * k];
        out.push(Event { start: e.start + 2.8, dur: 0.9, lines: vec![sounds[k % sounds.len()].to_string()] });
    }
    sort_by_start(&mut out);
    out
}

/// Py: measured(*tracks).
fn measured(tracks: Vec<Track>) -> Vec<Track> {
    measured_with(&Rule::default(), tracks)
}

/// measured under a changed rule (the Python's mock.patch.dict(st.RULE, ...)).
fn measured_with(rule: &Rule, mut tracks: Vec<Track>) -> Vec<Track> {
    for t in tracks.iter_mut() {
        measure(t, rule);
    }
    tracks
}

/// The characters of OCR junk. Py: 'xq#%}{3|'.
const JUNK: [char; 8] = ['x', 'q', '#', '%', '}', '{', '3', '|'];

/// Events of OCR junk: an unreadable track. Py: junk(count, seed, start, step).
fn junk(count: usize, seed: u64, start: f64, step: f64) -> Vec<Event> {
    let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(seed);
    (0..count)
        .map(|i| {
            let line: String = (0..12).map(|_| *rnd.choice(&JUNK)).collect();
            Event { start: start + i as f64 * step, dur: 0.8, lines: vec![line] }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Readable made-up text with one English stopword in nine words: its language is 'unknown' (T1b).
/// Py: unclear(count, seed, start, step).
fn unclear(count: usize, seed: u64, start: f64, step: f64) -> Vec<Event> {
    let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(seed);
    (0..count)
        .map(|i| {
            let words: Vec<String> = (0..8).map(|_| rnd.choice(OTHER.as_slice()).clone()).collect();
            Event { start: start + i as f64 * step, dur: 2.5, lines: vec![capitalize(&format!("the {}", words.join(" "))) + "."] }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The OCR junk garbled() appends to every line.
const GARBLE: &str = " x#%}{ q|}{# 3%}{x }{#q";

/// The same events with OCR junk after every line: the words stay, but the track is unreadable. Py: garbled.
fn garbled(events: &[Event]) -> Vec<Event> {
    events
        .iter()
        .map(|e| Event { lines: e.lines.iter().map(|line| line.clone() + GARBLE).collect(), ..e.clone() })
        .collect()
}

/// Another language's stream without OCR text: its packets only (T4's timing). Py: unread(n, events, tag).
fn unread(n: i64, events: &[Event], tag: &str) -> Track {
    let events = events.iter().map(|e| Event { start: e.start, dur: e.dur, lines: Vec::new() }).collect();
    let mut t = Track::new(n, tag, None, false, events);
    t.text = Some(false);
    t
}

/// One event per three words of the list, no word used twice: two tracks share exactly the bigrams of the events
/// they share, so a track's share of another's words is its share of events. Py: distinct(words, start, step).
fn distinct(words: &[String], start: f64, step: f64) -> Vec<Event> {
    (0..words.len() / 3)
        .map(|i| {
            let line = format!("we {} the {} and the {}", words[3 * i], words[3 * i + 1], words[3 * i + 2]);
            Event { start: start + i as f64 * step, dur: 2.5, lines: vec![capitalize(&line) + "."] }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Spanish lines as the tests build them: `count` events from `start` every `step` s, eight words each, capitalised,
/// drawn from Random(2). Py: the comprehension of test_language and its copies.
fn spanish_events(count: usize, start: f64, step: f64) -> Vec<Event> {
    let mut rnd = PyRandom::new(2);
    let words = spanish();
    (0..count)
        .map(|i| {
            let line: Vec<&str> = (0..8).map(|_| *rnd.choice(&words)).collect();
            Event { start: start + step * i as f64, dur: 2.0, lines: vec![capitalize(&line.join(" "))] }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A decision as the Python's dicts write it.
fn dec(role: Role, review: Option<&str>, note: Option<&str>) -> Decision {
    Decision { role, review: review.map(str::to_string), note: note.map(str::to_string) }
}

/// st.decide under `rule`, checking the owner's 'ambiguous = keep': no track is dropped with a review.
/// Py: Rule.decide.
fn checked_decide_with(rule: &Rule, tracks: &[Track], orig_lang: &str) -> BTreeMap<i64, Decision> {
    let v = decide(tracks, Some(orig_lang), rule);
    for (n, r) in &v {
        assert!(!(r.role == Role::Drop && r.review.is_some()), "s{n} is dropped with a review");
    }
    v
}

/// Py: Rule.decide with the default RULE.
fn checked_decide(tracks: &[Track], orig_lang: &str) -> BTreeMap<i64, Decision> {
    checked_decide_with(&Rule::default(), tracks, orig_lang)
}

/// The same events `delta` seconds later. Py: [dict(e, start=e['start'] + delta) for e in events].
fn later(events: &[Event], delta: f64) -> Vec<Event> {
    events.iter().map(|e| Event { start: e.start + delta, ..e.clone() }).collect()
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ Classes

mod classes {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn sdh_track() {
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, sdh_version(&base()))]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Sdh);
        assert_eq!(m.SO, 8);
        assert_eq!(m.LABEL, 6);
        assert_eq!(m.lang, "en");
    }

    #[test]
    fn regular_track() {
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, base())]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Regular);
        assert_eq!(m.M, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn inline_asides_are_not_sdh() {
        let mut ev = base();
        for k in 0..9 {
            ev[4 + 10 * k].lines[0].push_str(" (FBI)");
        }
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, ev)]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert_eq!(m.M, 9);
        assert_eq!(m.SO, 0);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Unclear);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bracketed_notes_without_sounds_are_not_sdh() {
        let mut ev = base();
        for k in 0..8 {
            let start = ev[3 + 12 * k].start + 2.8;
            ev.push(Event { start, dur: 0.9, lines: vec!["[SIGN]".to_string()] });
        }
        sort_by_start(&mut ev);
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, ev)]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert_eq!(m.SO, 8);
        assert_eq!(m.CS, 0);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Unclear);
    }

    #[test]
    fn capital_sound_lines_without_brackets_are_unclear() {
        let mut ev = base();
        for k in 0..5 {
            let start = ev[3 + 12 * k].start + 2.8;
            ev.push(Event { start, dur: 0.9, lines: vec!["DOOR SLAMS".to_string()] });
        }
        sort_by_start(&mut ev);
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, ev)]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert_eq!(m.CAPS_CUE, 5);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Unclear);
    }

    #[test]
    fn all_capital_track_keeps_bracketed_cues_only() {
        let mut ev = sdh_version(&base());
        for e in ev.iter_mut() {
            e.lines = e.lines.iter().map(|line| line.to_uppercase()).collect();
        }
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, ev)]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert!(m.caps_style);
        assert_eq!(m.LABEL, 0);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Sdh);
        let upper: Vec<Event> = base()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|e| Event { lines: e.lines.iter().map(|line| line.to_uppercase()).collect(), ..e })
            .collect();
        let r = measured(vec![eng(0, upper)]);
        assert_eq!(measures_of(&r[0]).class, Class::Regular);
    }

    #[test]
    fn damaged_brackets_are_unclear() {
        let mut ev = base();
        for k in 0..4 {
            let start = ev[3 + 12 * k].start + 2.8;
            ev.push(Event { start, dur: 0.9, lines: vec!["|door closes|".to_string()] });
        }
        sort_by_start(&mut ev);
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, ev)]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert_eq!(m.ODD, 4);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Unclear);
    }

    #[test]
    fn note_stand_ins_do_not_make_a_track_unreadable() {
        let mut ev = sdh_version(&base());
        for e in ev.iter_mut().step_by(2) {
            e.lines = e.lines.iter().map(|line| format!("# {line} #")).collect();
        }
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, ev)]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert!(m.readable);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Sdh);
        assert!(m.NOTE > 50, "{}", m.NOTE);
    }

    #[test]
    fn note_only_events_do_not_make_a_track_unreadable() {
        let mut ev = sdh_version(&base());
        // gaps = [e['start'] + 3.3 for e in ev[5:115:5]]
        let gaps: Vec<f64> = ev[5..115].iter().step_by(5).map(|e| e.start + 3.3).collect();
        for (k, start) in gaps.iter().enumerate() {
            let line = if k % 2 == 1 { "#" } else { "J" };
            ev.push(Event { start: *start, dur: 0.5, lines: vec![line.to_string()] });
        }
        sort_by_start(&mut ev);
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, ev)]);
        let m = measures_of(&tracks[0]);
        assert_eq!(m.note_only, 22);
        assert_eq!(m.events, 150);
        assert!(m.readable);
        assert_eq!(m.class, Class::Sdh);
    }

    #[test]
    fn garbage_is_unreadable() {
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, junk(60, 3, 10.0, 1.0))]);
        assert_eq!(measures_of(&tracks[0]).class, Class::Unreadable);
        // T0: an unreadable track is always reviewed, also a flagged forced track with no dialogue track beside it.
        let mut forced = tracks[0].clone();
        forced.forced = true;
        let v = decide(&[forced], Some("en"), &Rule::default());
        assert_eq!(v[&0].review.as_deref(), Some(AMBIGUOUS));
    }

    #[test]
    fn language() {
        let tracks = measured(vec![track(0, spanish_events(80, 10.0, 3.0), "spa", false)]);
        assert_eq!(measures_of(&tracks[0]).lang, "es");
        let e = measured(vec![eng(0, base())]);
        assert_eq!(measures_of(&e[0]).lang, "en");
    }
}

    use super::*;

    #[test]

            split.push(Event { start: e.start + 1.3, dur: 1.2, ..e.clone() });

        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, sdh_version(&b)), eng(1, split)]);
        let v = checked_decide(&tracks, "en");

        }

    /// T6's drop guards, one test each: the track meets every other T6 condition (outside the dialogue group, other
    /// words and other timing than every member, readable English, original language English) and fails just one.
    /// Py: assert_t6_fixture.
    fn assert_t6_fixture(rule: &Rule, tracks: &[Track], n: usize, dialogue_ns: &[usize]) {
        let t = &tracks[n];
        assert!(measures_of(t).readable);
        assert_eq!(measures_of(t).lang, "en");
        for &k in dialogue_ns {
            let p = pair(t, &tracks[k], rule);
            assert_eq!((p.content, p.timing), (Content::Different, Timing::Diff), "s{n} against s{k}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn t6_keeps_a_track_with_sound_only_cues() {
        let mut comm = dialogue(100, 5, Words::Other, 11.7, 4.0);
        let cues: Vec<Event> = (0..2)
            .map(|k| Event { start: comm[10 + 30 * k].start + 2.8, dur: 0.9, lines: vec!["(DOOR SLAMS)".to_string()] })
            .collect();
        comm.extend(cues);
        sort_by_start(&mut comm);
        let b = base();
        let rule = Rule::default();
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, sdh_version(&b)), eng(1, b.clone()), eng(2, comm)]);
        assert_t6_fixture(&rule, &tracks, 2, &[0, 1]);
        assert_eq!(measures_of(&tracks[2]).SO, 2);
        assert_ne!(measures_of(&tracks[2]).class, Class::Sdh);
        let v = checked_decide(&tracks, "en");
        assert_eq!((v[&0].role, v[&1].role), (Role::Sdh, Role::Regular));
        assert_eq!((v[&2].role, v[&2].review.as_deref()), (Role::Keep, Some(AMBIGUOUS)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn t6_keeps_an_sdh_track() {
        // With today's thresholds an SDH track always has sound-only events (SDH_SO); retuned to 0, the class guard
        // alone must keep a track classed SDH whose cues all sit beside dialogue.
        let b = base();
        let comm: Vec<Event> = dialogue(100, 5, Words::Other, 11.7, 4.0)
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(i, e)| if i % 12 == 3 { Event { lines: vec![format!("{} (DOOR SLAMS)", e.lines[0])], ..e } } else { e })
            .collect();
        let rule = Rule { SDH_SO: 0, ..Rule::default() };
        let tracks = measured_with(&rule, vec![eng(0, sdh_version(&b)), eng(1, b.clone()), eng(2, comm)]);
        assert_t6_fixture(&rule, &tracks, 2, &[0, 1]);
        assert_eq!(measures_of(&tracks[2]).SO, 0);
        assert_eq!(measures_of(&tracks[2]).class, Class::Sdh);
        let v = checked_decide_with(&rule, &tracks, "en");
        assert_eq!((v[&0].role, v[&1].role), (Role::Sdh, Role::Regular));
        assert_eq!((v[&2].role, v[&2].review.as_deref()), (Role::Keep, Some(AMBIGUOUS)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn t6_keeps_a_track_of_a_two_track_group() {
        let b = base();
        let comm = dialogue(100, 5, Words::Other, 11.7, 4.0);
        let rule = Rule::default();
        let tracks = measured(vec![
            eng(0, sdh_version(&b)),
            eng(1, b.clone()),
            eng(2, later(&b, 0.05)),
            eng(3, comm.clone()),
            eng(4, later(&comm, 0.1)),
        ]);
        for n in [3, 4] {
            assert_t6_fixture(&rule, &tracks, n, &[0, 1, 2]);
            assert_eq!(measures_of(&tracks[n]).SO, 0);
            assert_ne!(measures_of(&tracks[n]).class, Class::Sdh);
        }
        assert_eq!(pair(&tracks[3], &tracks[4], &rule).content, Content::Same);
        let v = checked_decide(&tracks, "en");
        assert_eq!(v[&0].note.as_deref(), Some("more than two tracks in the dialogue group"));
        for n in [3, 4] {
            assert_eq!((v[&n].role, v[&n].review.as_deref()), (Role::Keep, Some(AMBIGUOUS)));
        }
    }

    /// The track of `order` that stands for letter `k`.
    fn by<'a>(tracks: &'a [Track], order: &str, k: char) -> &'a Track {
        &tracks[order.find(k).expect("a letter of the order")]
    }

    #[test]
    fn one_way_chain_of_full_tracks_gives_the_same_verdicts_in_any_numbering() {
        // T2 on three full tracks: A's words in B, B's words in C, A's words not in C. A and B are both forced
        // candidates, whatever their stream numbers (T2 compares with the full tracks as they were before it).
        let words: Vec<String> =
            NOUNS.iter().chain(VERBS.iter()).chain(OTHER.iter()).chain(OTHER_VERBS.iter()).cloned().collect();
        let c = distinct(&words[..600], 10.0, 4.0);
        let q = distinct(&words[600..720], 11.7, 4.0);
        let mut b: Vec<Event> = c[..90].iter().chain(q.iter()).cloned().collect();
        sort_by_start(&mut b);
        let mut a: Vec<Event> = c[85..90].iter().chain(q.iter()).cloned().collect();
        sort_by_start(&mut a);
        let events = |k: char| -> Vec<Event> {
            match k {
                'A' => a.clone(),
                'B' => b.clone(),
                _ => c.clone(),
            }
        };
        let rule = Rule::default();
        let mut verdicts: BTreeMap<&str, BTreeMap<char, Decision>> = BTreeMap::new();
        for order in ["ABC", "BAC"] {
            let tracks = measured(order.chars().enumerate().map(|(n, k)| eng(n as i64, events(k))).collect());
            let (ta, tb, tc) = (by(&tracks, order, 'A'), by(&tracks, order, 'B'), by(&tracks, order, 'C'));
            assert!(subset_of(ta, tb, pair(ta, tb, &rule).cb, &rule));
            assert!(subset_of(tb, tc, pair(tb, tc, &rule).cb, &rule));
            assert!(!subset_of(ta, tc, pair(ta, tc, &rule).cb, &rule));
            let v = checked_decide(&tracks, "en");
            verdicts.insert(order, order.chars().enumerate().map(|(n, k)| (k, v[&(n as i64)].clone())).collect());
        }
        assert_eq!(verdicts["ABC"], verdicts["BAC"]);
        let expected: BTreeMap<char, Decision> = BTreeMap::from([
            ('C', dec(Role::Regular, None, None)),
            ('B', dec(Role::Forced, None, Some("words found in the dialogue track"))),
            ('A', dec(Role::Keep, Some(AMBIGUOUS), Some("forced candidate shares no words with the dialogue track"))),
        ]);
        assert_eq!(verdicts["ABC"], expected);
    }

    #[test]
    fn readable_partial_track_is_dropped() {
        let other = dialogue(160, 8, Words::Other, 11.7, 9.0);
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, dialogue(1700, 1, Words::Nouns, 10.0, 4.0)), eng(1, other)]);
        assert_eq!(checked_decide(&tracks, "en")[&1], dec(Role::Drop, None, Some("partial_subtitle_dropped")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn unreadable_tracks_are_not_judged_by_their_words() {
        let b = base();
        // An unreadable full track whose words are a subset: 8.7 decides it (two aligned tracks), not T2.
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, b.clone()), eng(1, garbled(&b[40..70]))]);
        assert!(!measures_of(&tracks[1]).readable);
        let v = checked_decide(&tracks, "en");
        assert_eq!((v[&1].role, v[&1].review.as_deref()), (Role::Regular, Some(AMBIGUOUS)));
        assert_eq!(spec87(&tracks, &Rule::default())[&1], "regular");
        // A readable candidate beside an unreadable dialogue track: forced as 8.7 says, but reviewed.
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(0, garbled(&b)), eng(1, b[40..50].to_vec())]);
        let v = checked_decide(&tracks, "en");
        assert_eq!(v[&1], dec(Role::Forced, Some(AMBIGUOUS), Some("dialogue track unreadable")));
    }

    #[test]
    fn before_yes() {
        // The test's own name hides the function inside this module; the full path reaches it.
        use crate::subtitle::text::before_yes as before_yes_of;
        assert_eq!(
            before_yes_of(&dec(Role::Sdh, None, None), "regular"),
            "regular (review: subtitle_text_disagrees)"
        );
        assert_eq!(before_yes_of(&dec(Role::Regular, None, None), "regular"), "regular");
        assert_eq!(
            before_yes_of(&dec(Role::Regular, Some(AMBIGUOUS), None), "regular"),
            "regular (review: subtitle_text_disagrees)"
        );
        assert_eq!(before_yes_of(&dec(Role::Keep, Some(AMBIGUOUS), None), "keep (review)"), "keep (review)");
        assert_eq!(before_yes_of(&dec(Role::Sdh, None, None), "sdh (review)"), "sdh (review)");
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ new: spec87's set order

mod added_rule {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn spec87_breaks_an_event_count_tie_in_cpythons_set_order() {
        // Two English full tracks with the same number of events in one dialogue group: spec87 sorts the group's
        // members by event count with a stable sort over the set, so the set's order picks the SDH track.
        // ((first stream, second stream), the one spec87 called sdh) as Python 3.9.6 printed them.
        let cases: [((i64, i64), i64); 8] = [
            ((3, 11), 11),
            ((11, 3), 3),
            ((2, 10), 2),
            ((10, 2), 10),
            ((0, 8), 0),
            ((8, 0), 8),
            ((0, 1), 0),
            ((1, 0), 0),
        ];
        let b = base();
        let rule = Rule::default();
        for ((first, second), sdh) in cases {
            let tracks = measured(vec![eng(first, b.clone()), eng(second, later(&b, 0.1))]);
            let today = spec87(&tracks, &rule);
            let regular = if sdh == first { second } else { first };
            assert_eq!(
                (today[&sdh].as_str(), today[&regular].as_str()),
                ("sdh", "regular"),
                "s{first} then s{second}"
            );
        }
        // Three tracks joined through each other (the second union is of one set with itself): kept for review.
        let tracks = measured(vec![eng(16, b.clone()), eng(0, later(&b, 0.1)), eng(8, later(&b, 0.2))]);
        let today = spec87(&tracks, &rule);
        for n in [16, 0, 8] {
            assert_eq!(today[&n], "keep (review)");
        }
    }
}
```
