```rust
// ------------------------------------------------------------------ printing and the title

use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};

use crate::recording::files::{read_jsonl, FrameEntry, PacketsFile, SubsIndexEntry, Tmdb};
use crate::recording::{read_json, read_text, Encoding, Errors, PathKey, Tree};
use crate::subtitle::align::TEXT_CODECS;

/// The table analyse prints, header and rule. Py: analyse's two literal lines.
const TABLE_HEADER: &str = "| Stream | Tag | Events | Class | Rule | Review | Note | 8.7 today | Before yes |";
const TABLE_RULE: &str = "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|";

/// The per-stream measures line (numbers only). Py: track_line.
pub fn track_line(t: &Track) -> String {
    let m = measures_of(t);
    let shares: Vec<String> = m.shares.iter().map(|(lang, share)| format!("{lang}={}", py_fixed(*share, 3))).collect();
    format!(
        "stream s{} {}: events={} lines={} words={} letters={} wordlike={} readable={} lang={} ({}) CUE={} LABEL={} \
         CHEV={} M={} rate={} SO={} CS={} caps_share={} CAPS_CUE={} NOTE={} NOTE_LOOSE={} ODD={} class={}",
        t.n,
        t.tag,
        m.events,
        m.lines,
        m.words,
        py_fixed(m.letter_events, 3),
        py_fixed(m.wordlike, 3),
        if m.readable { "yes" } else { "no" },
        m.lang,
        shares.join(" "),
        m.CUE,
        m.LABEL,
        m.CHEV,
        m.M,
        py_fixed(m.rate, 4),
        m.SO,
        m.CS,
        py_fixed(m.caps_share, 3),
        m.CAPS_CUE,
        m.NOTE,
        m.NOTE_LOOSE,
        m.ODD,
        m.class.as_str()
    )
}

/// 'n/a' or '%.3f'. Py: fmt.
fn fmt3(x: Option<f64>) -> String {
    match x {
        None => "n/a".to_string(),
        Some(x) => py_fixed(x, 3),
    }
}

/// `t.get('codec') or '?'`.
fn codec_or_question(t: &Track) -> &str {
    match t.codec.as_deref() {
        Some(codec) if !codec.is_empty() => codec,
        _ => "?",
    }
}

/// A text codec name (the DVD closed captions, which MakeMKV converts to SubRip): one of the words of mkvmerge's
/// text subtitle codec names. Py: is_text_codec.
pub fn is_text_codec(codec: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    let codec = codec.unwrap_or("");
    TEXT_CODECS.iter().any(|word| codec.contains(word))
}

/// One printed pair: its numbers and the subset phrase ("s0 in s1" or "no").
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct PairRow {
    pub a: i64,
    pub b: i64,
    pub pair: Pair,
    pub subset: String,
}

/// What analyse printed and decided.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Analysis {
    pub lines: Vec<String>,
    pub decide: BTreeMap<i64, Decision>,
    pub spec87: BTreeMap<i64, String>,
    pub pairs: Vec<PairRow>,
}

/// The table cells of one stream: (rule role, review, note, 8.7 today, before yes), with the Python's '?' and '-'
/// for what is missing (a stream decide or spec87 left out; none does today).
fn table_cells<'a>(
    verdict: Option<&'a Decision>,
    today: Option<&'a String>,
) -> (&'a str, &'a str, &'a str, &'a str, String) {
    let (role, review, note) = match verdict {
        Some(v) => (v.role.as_str(), v.review.as_deref(), v.note.as_deref()),
        None => ("?", None, None),
    };
    let today = today.map_or("?", String::as_str);
    let dash = |text: Option<&'a str>| -> &'a str {
        match text {
            Some(text) if !text.is_empty() => text,
            _ => "-",
        }
    };
    (role, dash(review), dash(note), today, before_yes_text(role, truthy(review), today))
}

/// Measures every read track and prints the stream, pair, table and row: lines, then decides; `label` is the rip
/// label (the row lines' "<label>/evidence.mks"). Py: analyse.
pub fn analyse(tracks: &mut [Track], orig_lang: Option<&str>, label: &str, rule: &Rule) -> Analysis {
    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for t in tracks.iter_mut() {
        if t.set_aside {
            lines.push(format!(
                "stream s{} {}: set aside (closed captions: {} is a text stream; 8.7 sets it aside), {} events",
                t.n,
                t.tag,
                codec_or_question(t),
                t.events.len()
            ));
            continue;
        }
        if !t.has_text() {
            lines.push(format!(
                "stream s{} {}: not read (no OCR text), {} events, used for timing only",
                t.n,
                t.tag,
                t.events.len()
            ));
            continue;
        }
        measure(t, rule);
        lines.push(format!("{}  [{}]", track_line(t), t.pairing.as_deref().unwrap_or("")));
        let m = measures_of(t);
        // {k: v for k, v in sorted(corrections.items()) if v}
        let mut corrections: Vec<(&str, usize)> =
            m.corrections.iter().filter(|(_, count)| **count != 0).map(|(name, count)| (name, *count)).collect();
        corrections.sort();
        if !corrections.is_empty() {
            let shown: Vec<String> = corrections.iter().map(|(name, count)| format!("{name}={count}")).collect();
            lines.push(format!("  corrections: {}", shown.join(" ")));
        }
        if m.note_only > 0 {
            lines.push(format!("  note-only events: {} (left out of letters)", m.note_only));
        }
    }
    let tracks: &[Track] = tracks;
    let read: Vec<usize> = (0..tracks.len()).filter(|&i| tracks[i].has_text()).collect();
    let mut pairs: Vec<PairRow> = Vec::new();
    for (x, &a) in read.iter().enumerate() {
        for &b in &read[x + 1..] {
            let (ta, tb) = (&tracks[a], &tracks[b]);
            let p = pair(ta, tb, rule);
            let subset = if subset_of(ta, tb, p.cb, rule) {
                format!("s{} in s{}", ta.n, tb.n)
            } else if subset_of(tb, ta, (p.cb.1, p.cb.0), rule) {
                format!("s{} in s{}", tb.n, ta.n)
            } else {
                "no".to_string()
            };
            lines.push(format!(
                "pair s{} s{}: aligned={}/{} timing={} CB={}/{} content={} UC={}/{} subset={}",
                ta.n,
                tb.n,
                py_fixed(p.aligned.0, 3),
                py_fixed(p.aligned.1, 3),
                p.timing.as_str(),
                fmt3(p.cb.0),
                fmt3(p.cb.1),
                p.content.as_str(),
                p.uc.0,
                p.uc.1,
                subset
            ));
            pairs.push(PairRow { a: ta.n, b: tb.n, pair: p, subset });
        }
    }
    let verdict = decide(tracks, orig_lang, rule);
    let today = spec87(tracks, rule);
    lines.push(format!("original language: {}", or_unknown(orig_lang)));
    lines.push(TABLE_HEADER.to_string());
    lines.push(TABLE_RULE.to_string());
    for t in tracks {
        let class = if t.has_text() {
            measures_of(t).class.as_str()
        } else if t.set_aside {
            "set aside"
        } else {
            "not read"
        };
        let (role, review, note, today_role, before) = table_cells(verdict.get(&t.n), today.get(&t.n));
        lines.push(format!(
            "| s{} | {} | {} | {} | {} | {} | {} | {} | {} |",
            t.n,
            t.tag,
            t.events.len(),
            class,
            role,
            review,
            note,
            today_role,
            before
        ));
    }
    for t in tracks {
        let v = verdict.get(&t.n);
        let what = if t.has_text() {
            let m = measures_of(t);
            format!("M {}, SO {}, CS {}, lang {}, {}", m.M, m.SO, m.CS, m.lang, m.class.as_str())
        } else if t.set_aside {
            "set aside (closed captions)".to_string()
        } else {
            "not read (timing only)".to_string()
        };
        // v.get('role') is None (printed "None") for a stream without a decision; the review part shows the note.
        let role = v.map_or("None", |v| v.role.as_str());
        let review = match v {
            Some(v) if truthy(v.review.as_deref()) => format!(" (review: {})", v.note.as_deref().unwrap_or("None")),
            _ => String::new(),
        };
        lines.push(format!(
            "row: | {}/evidence.mks | s{}: {} {}, {} events | {}: {}{} | |",
            label,
            t.n,
            codec_or_question(t),
            t.tag,
            t.events.len(),
            what,
            role,
            review
        ));
    }
    Analysis { lines, decide: verdict, spec87: today, pairs }
}

/// frame -> line count of sub-<n>.frames.json when the file exists (a later entry for a frame wins). Py: the counts
/// of ocr_records.
fn frame_counts(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey) -> Result<BTreeMap<i64, Option<i64>>, String> {
    let mut counts = BTreeMap::new();
    if tree.exists(path) {
        let frames: Vec<FrameEntry> = read_json(tree, path)?;
        for f in frames {
            counts.insert(f.frame, f.lines);
        }
    }
    Ok(counts)
}

/// Every stream of `<rec>/subs/index.json` with its displayed events (a text stream: every packet, spec 8.7). A
/// stream with OCR text (`<text>/sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl` in `text_tree`, paired with `<rec>/subs-ocr/sub-<n>.frames.json`)
/// gets its lines and its pairing line; a text stream without OCR text is set aside (closed captions, 8.7); any other
/// stream without OCR text is marked unread (`text: Some(false)`). Err is the text the Python's "cannot read the
/// input" line printed (the FileNotFoundError, int(), float() or decoding text; serde_json's text for a JSON
/// error). Py: load_title.
pub fn load_title(
    rec_tree: &dyn Tree,
    rec: &PathKey,
    text_tree: &dyn Tree,
    text: &PathKey,
    clear_max_bytes: i64,
) -> Result<Vec<Track>, String> {
    let index: Vec<SubsIndexEntry> = read_json(rec_tree, &rec.join("subs/index.json"))?;
    let mut tracks = Vec::new();
    for entry in &index {
        let n = entry.n;
        let codec = entry.codec.as_deref();
        let txt = is_text_codec(codec);
        let packets: PacketsFile = read_json(rec_tree, &rec.join(&format!("subs/sub-{n}.packets.json")))?;
        let mut events = packet_events(packets.packets(), if txt { 0 } else { clear_max_bytes })?;
        let tag = match entry.language.as_deref() {
            Some(language) if !language.is_empty() => language,
            _ => "und",
        };
        let mut t = Track::new(n, tag, codec, entry.forced.unwrap_or(false), Vec::new());
        let jsonl = text.join(&format!("sub-{n}.ocr.jsonl"));
        if text_tree.exists(&jsonl) {
            let records = read_jsonl(&read_text(text_tree, &jsonl, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)?)?;
            let counts = frame_counts(rec_tree, &rec.join(&format!("subs-ocr/sub-{n}.frames.json")))?;
            let recs = ocr_records(&records, &counts)?;
            let (method, left) = pair_text(&mut events, &recs);
            t.pairing = Some(format!("text by {}, {} frames with text, {} unmatched", method.as_str(), recs.len(), left));
        } else if txt {
            t.set_aside = true;
        } else {
            t.text = Some(false);
        }
        t.events = events;
        tracks.push(t);
    }
    Ok(tracks)
}

/// One `subs` run: stdout and stderr lines, the exit code (0; 2 for unreadable input, no OCR text at all, or an
/// English or no-language bitmap stream without it), the tracks, the original language used, the analysis (None
/// on exit 2). Py: subtitle_text.main.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct SubsRun {
    pub stdout: Vec<String>,
    pub stderr: Vec<String>,
    pub exit_code: i32,
    pub tracks: Vec<Track>,
    pub orig_lang: Option<String>,
    pub analysis: Option<Analysis>,
}

/// main's flow after argument parsing: load_title, the two input checks, `orig_lang` or else
/// `<rec>/../tmdb.json`'s original_language, the header line, analyse. The folders are printed as the trees display
/// them (`str(Path)`). A tmdb.json that cannot be read crashed the Python; here it is "cannot read the input: ..."
/// and exit 2 (port spec 3.4). Py: subtitle_text.main.
pub fn subs_run(
    rec_tree: &dyn Tree,
    rec: &PathKey,
    text_tree: &dyn Tree,
    text: &PathKey,
    orig_lang: Option<&str>,
    clear_max_bytes: i64,
    rule: &Rule,
) -> SubsRun {
    let mut run =
        SubsRun { stdout: Vec::new(), stderr: Vec::new(), exit_code: 2, tracks: Vec::new(), orig_lang: None, analysis: None };
    match load_title(rec_tree, rec, text_tree, text, clear_max_bytes) {
        Ok(tracks) => run.tracks = tracks,
        Err(error) => {
            run.stderr.push(format!("cannot read the input: {error}"));
            return run;
        }
    }
    let rec_shown = rec_tree.display(rec);
    let text_shown = text_tree.display(text);
    if !run.tracks.iter().any(Track::has_text) {
        run.stderr.push(format!("no sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl in {text_shown} for the streams of {rec_shown}/subs/index.json"));
        return run;
    }
    // An English or no-language bitmap stream without text would leave the rule judging fewer tracks than the title
    // has: an input error, never a silent skip.
    let missing: Vec<(i64, String)> = run
        .tracks
        .iter()
        .filter(|t| t.text == Some(false) && matches!(t.tag.as_str(), "eng" | "en" | "und"))
        .map(|t| (t.n, t.tag.clone()))
        .collect();
    for (n, tag) in &missing {
        run.stderr.push(format!(
            "stream s{n} {tag}: no OCR text (no sub-{n}.ocr.jsonl in {text_shown}); read it with ocr-subs.ps1"
        ));
    }
    if !missing.is_empty() {
        return run;
    }
    let mut orig = orig_lang.map(str::to_string);
    let tmdb = rec.parent().join("tmdb.json");
    if orig.is_none() && rec_tree.exists(&tmdb) {
        match read_json::<Tmdb>(rec_tree, &tmdb) {
            Ok(info) => orig = info.original_language,
            Err(error) => {
                run.stderr.push(format!("cannot read the input: {error}"));
                return run;
            }
        }
    }
    let unread = run.tracks.iter().filter(|t| t.text == Some(false)).count();
    let aside = run.tracks.iter().filter(|t| t.set_aside).count();
    let mut extra = String::new();
    if unread > 0 {
        extra.push_str(&format!(", {unread} not read (another language)"));
    }
    if aside > 0 {
        extra.push_str(&format!(", {aside} set aside (closed captions)"));
    }
    let with_text = run.tracks.iter().filter(|t| t.has_text()).count();
    run.stdout.push(format!("{rec_shown}: {with_text} subtitle streams with OCR text{extra}; rule thresholds are provisional"));
    let analysis = analyse(&mut run.tracks, orig.as_deref(), rec.name(), rule);
    run.stdout.extend(analysis.lines.iter().cloned());
    run.orig_lang = orig;
    run.analysis = Some(analysis);
    run.exit_code = 0;
    run
}

/// <label>/subs.json (port spec section 5) and decide's "subtitles": numbers, classes and decisions only; no event
/// features, words or bigrams.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubsJson {
    /// The reading folder the OCR text came from (<DIR>/<slug>/<label>/<reading>/).
    pub reading: String,
    pub exit_code: i32,
    pub orig_lang: Option<String>,
    pub streams: Vec<SubsStreamJson>,
    pub pairs: Vec<PairJson>,
    /// "sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl" -> SHA-1 (lowercase hex) of the file's bytes, in stream order.
    pub text_sha1: Ordered<String>,
}

/// One stream of SubsJson.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct SubsStreamJson {
    pub n: i64,
    pub tag: String,
    pub codec: Option<String>,
    pub forced: bool,
    pub events: usize,
    /// "read" | "set aside" | "not read".
    pub status: String,
    /// Track.pairing (the pairing line).
    pub pairing: Option<String>,
    /// The measures (markers, class, language and corrections included); None when not read.
    pub m: Option<Measures>,
    pub decide: Option<Decision>,
    pub spec87: Option<String>,
    pub before_yes: Option<String>,
}

/// One pair of SubsJson: the two stream numbers, the pair measures flattened in, the subset phrase.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct PairJson {
    pub a: i64,
    pub b: i64,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub pair: Pair,
    pub subset: String,
}

/// Lowercase hex SHA-1 of some bytes.
fn sha1_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    Sha1::digest(bytes).iter().map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}")).collect()
}

/// SubsJson of a run: per stream its facts, status, pairing, measures and the three outcomes (decide, spec87 and
/// before_yes as the table printed them; None when the run stopped before analyse), the printed pairs, and the
/// SHA-1 of every OCR text file the run read through `text_tree` (the streams with a pairing).
pub fn subs_json(run: &SubsRun, reading: &str, text_tree: &dyn Tree, text: &PathKey) -> SubsJson {
    let mut streams = Vec::new();
    let mut text_sha1: Ordered<String> = Ordered::new();
    for t in &run.tracks {
        let status = if t.has_text() {
            "read"
        } else if t.set_aside {
            "set aside"
        } else {
            "not read"
        };
        let (decision, today, before) = match &run.analysis {
            Some(analysis) => {
                let decision = analysis.decide.get(&t.n).cloned();
                let today = analysis.spec87.get(&t.n).cloned();
                let (_, _, _, _, before) = table_cells(analysis.decide.get(&t.n), analysis.spec87.get(&t.n));
                (decision, today, Some(before))
            }
            None => (None, None, None),
        };
        streams.push(SubsStreamJson {
            n: t.n,
            tag: t.tag.clone(),
            codec: t.codec.clone(),
            forced: t.forced,
            events: t.events.len(),
            status: status.to_string(),
            pairing: t.pairing.clone(),
            m: t.measured.as_ref().map(|measured| measured.m.clone()),
            decide: decision,
            spec87: today,
            before_yes: before,
        });
        if t.has_text() {
            let name = format!("sub-{}.ocr.jsonl", t.n);
            if let Ok(bytes) = text_tree.read(&text.join(&name)) {
                text_sha1.insert(name, sha1_hex(&bytes));
            }
        }
    }
    let pairs = match &run.analysis {
        Some(analysis) => analysis
            .pairs
            .iter()
            .map(|row| PairJson { a: row.a, b: row.b, pair: row.pair.clone(), subset: row.subset.clone() })
            .collect(),
        None => Vec::new(),
    };
    SubsJson {
        reading: reading.to_string(),
        exit_code: run.exit_code,
        orig_lang: run.orig_lang.clone(),
        streams,
        pairs,
        text_sha1,
    }
}

        let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect();
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = run(ctx, &args, &mut out, &mut err);
        (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
    }

    /// `run` with `dir` as the current directory.
    fn run_in(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> (i32, String, String) {
        run_with(&Ctx::for_test(dir), args)
    }

    #[test]
    fn run_prints_the_pythons_lines_from_disk() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("rec-form");
        write_label(&tmp, "rec", "text");
        let (code, out, err) = run_in(&tmp.0, &["--rec", "rec", "--text", "text", "--orig-lang", "en"]);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
        assert_eq!(out, REC_EN);
        // A trailing slash and the "=" spelling change nothing (pathlib drops the slash).
        let (code, out, _) = run_in(&tmp.0, &["--rec=rec/", "--text=text", "--orig-lang=en"]);
        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (0, REC_EN));
    }

    #[test]
    fn run_reads_a_slug_a_recording_path_and_a_label_folder_alike() {

        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (0, SLUG_ES));

    fn run_reports_input_errors_as_the_python() {

        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (2, ""));

    }

        let tmp = TempDir::new("usage");
        let cases: [(&[&str], &str); 7] = [
            (&[], "one of the arguments --rec or <slug|dir> <label> is required"),
            (&["--rec", "rec"], "the following arguments are required: --text"),
            (&["--rec", "rec", "slug", "label", "--text", "t"], "argument --rec: not allowed with <slug|dir> <label>"),
            (&["slug", "--text", "t"], "the following arguments are required: label"),
            (&["a", "b", "c", "--text", "t"], "unrecognized arguments: c"),
            (&["--rec", "rec", "--text", "t", "--clear-max-bytes", "x"], "argument --clear-max-bytes: invalid int value: 'x'"),

        ];
        for (args, message) in cases {

                "{args:?}"
            );
        }

        assert_eq!((code, out), (0, format!("usage: lazymkv-dev {}\n", super::USAGE)));

    fn sha1_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
        use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};
        Sha1::digest(bytes).iter().map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}")).collect()
    }

    /// index.json then every sub-*.packets.json of a subs folder, by name. Py: the inputs of Task 9's record.
    fn evidence_inputs(folder: &Path) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut bytes = std::fs::read(folder.join("index.json")).unwrap();
        let mut names: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(folder)
            .unwrap()
            .filter_map(|entry| entry.ok()?.file_name().into_string().ok())
            .filter(|name| name.starts_with("sub-") && name.ends_with(".packets.json"))
            .collect();
        names.sort();
        for name in names {
            bytes.extend(std::fs::read(folder.join(name)).unwrap());
        }
        bytes
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_evidence_subs_index_loads_as_the_python_loaded_it() {
        let Some(root) = repo_root(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))) else {
            skip("no repository root (a Cargo.toml with [workspace]) above crates/dev");
            return;
        };
        let evidence = root.join("corpus").join("owner");
        if !evidence.is_dir() {
            skip("no evidence clone at corpus/owner");
            return;
        }
        let empty = TempDir::new("evidence-no-text");
        let empty_shown = empty.0.to_str().unwrap().to_string();
        let empty_shown = if cfg!(windows) { empty_shown.replace('\\', "/") } else { empty_shown };
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&root);
        for r in &EVIDENCE {
            let subs = evidence.join(r.slug).join(r.label).join("subs");
            let shown = format!("corpus/owner/{}/{}/subs", r.slug, r.label);
            if !subs.join("index.json").is_file() {
                skip(&format!("{shown}/index.json is not in the evidence clone"));
                continue;
            }
            if sha1_hex(&evidence_inputs(&subs)) != r.inputs {
                skip(&format!("{shown}: its inputs changed since the Python's output was recorded"));
                continue;
            }
            let recording = resolve_recording(&ctx, Some(evidence.to_str().unwrap()), r.slug)
                .unwrap_or_else(|refused| panic!("{}", refused.line));
            let rec = recording.dir.join(r.label);
            let tracks = load_title(&recording.tree, &rec, &MemTree::new("no-text", ""), &PathKey::root(), 64)
                .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{shown}: {error}"));
            let got: Vec<(i64, String, String, &str, usize, String)> = tracks
                .iter()
                .map(|t| {
                    let times: Vec<String> =
                        t.events.iter().map(|e| format!("{} {}", py_float_repr(e.start), py_float_repr(e.dur))).collect();
                    let status = if t.set_aside { "set aside" } else { "not read" };
                    let codec = t.codec.clone().unwrap_or_default();
                    (t.n, t.tag.clone(), codec, status, t.events.len(), sha1_hex(times.join("\n").as_bytes()))
                })
                .collect();
            let want: Vec<(i64, String, String, &str, usize, String)> = r
                .streams
                .iter()
                .map(|&(n, tag, codec, status, events, hash)| {
                    (n, tag.to_string(), codec.to_string(), status, events, hash.to_string())
                })
                .collect();
            assert_eq!(got, want, "{shown}: recorded from the Python at evidence commit 41c5c51");
            // The command over the same label without OCR text: the Python's line and exit 2.
            let args = ["--evidence", evidence.to_str().unwrap(), r.slug, r.label, "--text", empty.0.to_str().unwrap()];
            let (code, out, err) = run_in(&root, &args);
            assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (2, ""), "{shown}: {err}");
            assert_eq!(err, format!("no sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl in {empty_shown} for the streams of {shown}/index.json\n"));
        }
    }
}

import contextlib, io, json, os, pathlib, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath('scripts/phase0'))

WORDS = ['babin', 'dagon', 'gikol', 'kubal', 'lodin', 'bekan', 'dulog', 'gamin', 'kodel', 'labun', 'bodig']


def lines_of(k):

        return ['(DOOR SLAMS)']
    return ['We %s the %s and the %s.' % (WORDS[k % 11], WORDS[(3 * k + 1) % 11], WORDS[(7 * k + 2) % 11])]


def write_label(rec, text):
    (rec / 'subs').mkdir(parents=True)
    text.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    packets = []
    for k in range(30):
        start = 10.0 + 4.0 * k
        packets.append({'pts_time': '%.3f' % start, 'duration_time': '2.500', 'size': '4000'})
        packets.append({'pts_time': '%.3f' % (start + 2.5), 'duration_time': '0.021', 'size': '30'})
    cc = [{'pts_time': '%.3f' % (20.0 + 3 * i), 'duration_time': '2.000', 'size': '40'} for i in range(3)]
    index = [{'n': 0, 'language': 'eng', 'codec': 'HDMV PGS', 'forced': False},
             {'n': 1, 'language': 'eng', 'codec': 'SubRip/SRT', 'forced': False},
             {'n': 2, 'language': 'fre', 'codec': 'HDMV PGS', 'forced': False}]
    (rec / 'subs' / 'index.json').write_bytes(b'\xef\xbb\xbf' + json.dumps(index, indent=4).replace('\n', '\r\n').encode())
    for n, p in ((0, packets), (1, cc), (2, packets)):
        (rec / 'subs' / ('sub-%d.packets.json' % n)).write_text(json.dumps({'packets': p}))
    recs = [json.dumps({'frame': k, 't': 4.0 * k, 'lines': lines_of(k)}) for k in range(30)]
    (text / 'sub-0.ocr.jsonl').write_bytes(('\r\n'.join(recs) + '\r\n').encode())


root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
write_label(root / 'rec', root / 'text')
write_label(root / 'corpus/owner/test-disc-2000-bluray/all-tracks', root / 'text')
(root / 'corpus/owner/test-disc-2000-bluray/tmdb.json').write_text('{"original_language": "es", "fetched_at": "2026-10-13"}')
os.chdir(root)
for name, argv in (('REC_EN', ['--rec', 'rec', '--text', 'text', '--orig-lang', 'en']),
                   ('SLUG_ES', ['--rec', 'corpus/owner/test-disc-2000-bluray/all-tracks', '--text', 'text']),
                   ('missing', ['--rec', 'missing', '--text', 'text']),
                   ('no-text', ['--rec', 'rec', '--text', 'no-text'])):
    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
        code = st.main(argv)
    print(name, code, repr(err.getvalue()))
    print(out.getvalue(), end='')

Argument checks run in argparse's order: a flag without its value and an unknown flag first (`Args`), then `--clear-max-bytes`'s `int()`, then the positionals, then `--text`.

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev subs (--rec DIR | <slug|dir> <label>) [--text DIR] [--orig-lang CODE] [--clear-max-bytes N]
//! [--evidence DIR]` (port spec 3.4): the English subtitle text rule over one rip label, line for line as the Python
//! `subtitle_text` printed it (numbers only, no subtitle text). The OCR text folder (`--text`, else
//! LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT) holds sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl as the Python read it. Exit 0; 2 for an argument error, unreadable
//! input, no OCR text, or an English or no-language bitmap stream without OCR text; 3 when a slug is given and the
//! evidence clone is absent.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;

use lazymkv_core::recording::{py_int, py_repr_str, Loader, MemTree, PathKey, Tree};
use lazymkv_core::subtitle::text::{subs_run, Rule};

use crate::evidence::{ocr_text_dir, resolve_recording, Ctx};
use crate::{usage_error, Args};

/// The command's name as typed.
const NAME: &str = "subs";
/// The usage line, after "usage: lazymkv-dev " (argparse's form: the command's name first).
pub const USAGE: &str =
    "subs [--evidence DIR] (--rec DIR | <slug|dir> <label>) [--text DIR] [--orig-lang CODE] [--clear-max-bytes N]";
/// The command table's synopsis: spec 3.4's arguments after the name.
pub const SYNOPSIS: &str =
    "(--rec DIR | <slug|dir> <label>) [--text DIR] [--orig-lang CODE] [--clear-max-bytes N] [--evidence DIR]";

/// The command, registered in COMMANDS as "subs".
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    if args.iter().any(|arg| arg == "-h" || arg == "--help") {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "usage: lazymkv-dev {USAGE}");
        return 0;
    }
    let mut parsed = Args::new(args, &["--rec", "--text", "--orig-lang", "--clear-max-bytes", "--evidence"]);
    let rec_flag = match parsed.flag("--rec") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let text_flag = match parsed.flag("--text") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let orig_lang = match parsed.flag("--orig-lang") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let clear_flag = match parsed.flag("--clear-max-bytes") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let evidence = match parsed.flag("--evidence") {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    let words = match parsed.positionals() {
        Ok(words) => words,
        Err(message) => return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message),
    };
    // argparse's type=int, with RULE['CLEAR_MAX_BYTES'] as the default.
    let clear_max_bytes = match clear_flag {
        None => Rule::default().CLEAR_MAX_BYTES,
        Some(text) => match py_int(&text) {
            Some(number) => number,
            None => {
                let message = format!("argument --clear-max-bytes: invalid int value: {}", py_repr_str(&text));
                return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message);
            }
        },
    };
    if words.len() > 2 {
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &format!("unrecognized arguments: {}", words[2..].join(" ")));
    }
    if rec_flag.is_some() && !words.is_empty() {
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, "argument --rec: not allowed with <slug|dir> <label>");
    }
    if rec_flag.is_none() && words.is_empty() {
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, "one of the arguments --rec or <slug|dir> <label> is required");
    }
    if rec_flag.is_none() && words.len() == 1 {
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, "the following arguments are required: label");
    }
    let Some(text_dir) = ocr_text_dir(ctx, text_flag.as_deref()) else {
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, "the following arguments are required: --text");
    };
    // The folder as the user wrote it (flag or environment), printed as pathlib prints it.
    let text_given = text_flag.or_else(|| ctx.env.get("LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT").cloned()).unwrap_or_default();
    let (rec_tree, rec): (Box<dyn Tree>, PathKey) = match rec_flag {
        Some(dir) => rec_folder_tree(ctx, &dir),
        None => match resolve_recording(ctx, evidence.as_deref(), &words[0]) {
            Ok(recording) => {
                let rec = recording.dir.join(&words[1]);
                (Box::new(recording.tree) as Box<dyn Tree>, rec)
            }
            Err(refused) => {
                let _ = writeln!(err, "{}", refused.line);
                return refused.code;
            }
        },
    };
    let mut text_tree = MemTree::new(&py_path(&given_path(&text_given)).text, "");
    add_folder_files(&mut text_tree, &PathKey::root(), &text_dir);
    let run = subs_run(
        rec_tree.as_ref(),
        &rec,
        &text_tree,
        &PathKey::root(),
        orig_lang.as_deref(),
        clear_max_bytes,
        &Rule::default(),
    );
    for line in &run.stdout {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "{line}");
    }
    for line in &run.stderr {
        let _ = writeln!(err, "{line}");
    }
    run.exit_code
}

/// What pathlib makes of a path argument (POSIX): str(Path(arg)), str(Path(arg).parent) and Path(arg).name; empty
/// and "." parts dropped, a leading "/" kept, "." for nothing.
struct PyPath {
    text: String,
    parent: String,
    name: String,
}

fn py_path(arg: &str) -> PyPath {
    let absolute = arg.starts_with('/');
    let parts: Vec<&str> = arg.split('/').filter(|part| !part.is_empty() && *part != ".").collect();
    let join = |parts: &[&str]| -> String {
        let body = parts.join("/");
        if absolute {
            format!("/{body}")
        } else if body.is_empty() {
            ".".to_string()
        } else {
            body
        }
    };
    let text = join(&parts);
    match parts.split_last() {
        Some((name, rest)) => PyPath { text, parent: join(rest), name: name.to_string() },
        None => PyPath { parent: text.clone(), text, name: String::new() },
    }
}

/// A path argument with Windows separators written as '/' (on the mini PC), as the evidence module does.
fn given_path(arg: &str) -> String {
    if cfg!(windows) {
        arg.replace('\\', "/")
    } else {
        arg.to_string()
    }
}

/// The --rec folder as the rule reads it: a tree printed as pathlib prints the argument's parent, holding the
/// parent's tmdb.json and the files of the folder's subs/ and subs-ocr/ (the only files the rule reads), so that the
/// rest of the parent is not walked; and the folder's key in it. For ".", "/" and the like (no name), the folder is
/// its own parent, as Path('.').parent is Path('.').
fn rec_folder_tree(ctx: &Ctx, arg: &str) -> (Box<dyn Tree>, PathKey) {
    let shown = py_path(&given_path(arg));
    let rec_dir = ctx.abs(arg);
    let (display, rec, parent_dir): (String, PathKey, PathBuf) = if shown.name.is_empty() {
        (shown.text.clone(), PathKey::root(), rec_dir.clone())
    } else {
        let parent_dir = rec_dir.parent().map(Path::to_path_buf).unwrap_or_else(|| rec_dir.clone());
        (shown.parent.clone(), PathKey::new(&shown.name), parent_dir)
    };
    let mut tree = MemTree::new(&display, &shown.name);
    add_file(&mut tree, &rec.parent().join("tmdb.json"), &parent_dir.join("tmdb.json"));
    for folder in ["subs", "subs-ocr"] {
        add_folder_files(&mut tree, &rec.join(folder), &rec_dir.join(folder));
    }
    (Box::new(tree), rec)
}

/// Adds the file at `path` under `key`, read on first use, when `path` is a file.
fn add_file(tree: &mut MemTree, key: &PathKey, path: &Path) {
    if !path.is_file() {
        return;
    }
    let shown = tree.display(key);
    let path = path.to_path_buf();
    let load: Loader = Arc::new(move || std::fs::read(&path).map_err(|error| os_error_text(&error, &shown)));
    tree.insert_lazy(&key.to_string(), load);
}

/// Adds every file directly in `dir` under `key`; nothing when `dir` cannot be listed (its files are then missing,
/// as they were for the Python).
fn add_folder_files(tree: &mut MemTree, key: &PathKey, dir: &Path) {
    let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) else {
        return;
    };
    tree.insert_dir(&key.to_string());
    let mut names: Vec<String> =
        entries.filter_map(|entry| entry.ok()).filter_map(|entry| entry.file_name().into_string().ok()).collect();
    names.sort();
    for name in names {
        add_file(tree, &key.join(&name), &dir.join(&name));
    }
}

/// Python's OSError text: "[Errno <n>] <strerror>: '<path>'" (Rust's message without its " (os error n)").
fn os_error_text(error: &std::io::Error, shown: &str) -> String {
    match error.raw_os_error() {
        Some(code) => {
            let text = error.to_string();
            let description = match text.rfind(" (os error ") {
                Some(at) => text[..at].to_string(),
                None => text,
            };
            format!("[Errno {}] {}: {}", code, description, py_repr_str(shown))
        }
        None => error.to_string(),
    }
}
```

    struct TempDir(PathBuf);

    impl TempDir {
        fn new(name: &str) -> TempDir {
            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lazymkv-test-proxy-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
            TempDir(dir)
        }
    }

    impl Drop for TempDir {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
        }
    }

    /// A file's text.
    fn read(path: &Path) -> String {
        std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
    }

    /// Owned words of a command line.
    fn words(list: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
        list.iter().map(|word| word.to_string()).collect()
    }

    /// Frames per series, in order.
    fn ordered(pairs: &[(&str, usize)]) -> Ordered<usize> {
        Ordered(pairs.iter().map(|(name, n)| (name.to_string(), *n)).collect())
    }

    /// A refusal as build returns it.
    fn refused(text: &str) -> Result<Ordered<usize>, String> {
        Err(text.to_string())
    }

    /// Every call the fake programs received, in order.
    type Log = Rc<RefCell<Vec<Call>>>;

    /// A program's answer: exit 0, nothing printed.
    fn ok() -> Output {
        Output { status: 0, stdout: String::new(), stderr: String::new() }
    }

    /// What `ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=index,codec_type:stream_tags -of json` prints for audio tracks
    /// given as (track number, source stream, series).
    fn probe_output(tracks: &[(i64, i64, &str)]) -> Output {
        let streams: Vec<Value> = tracks
            .iter()
            .map(|&(index, n, series)| {
                json!({"index": index, "codec_type": "audio",
                       "tags": {"LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM": n.to_string(), "LAZYMKV_SERIES": series}})
            })
            .collect();
        Output { status: 0, stdout: json!({ "streams": streams }).to_string(), stderr: String::new() }
    }

    /// The names a filter graph's ametadata writes to, raw-<name>.txt.
    /// Py: re.findall(r"file=raw-([a-z0-9-]+)\.txt", graph).
    fn raw_names(graph: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        graph
            .split("file=raw-")
            .skip(1)
            .filter_map(|rest| {
                let name: String =
                    rest.chars().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || *c == '-').collect();
                (!name.is_empty() && rest[name.len()..].starts_with(".txt")).then_some(name)
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// A FakeRunner for the two programs: ffprobe answers `probe`; ffmpeg writes `raw` into every raw-<name>.txt of
    /// its filter graph, in its working folder, and answers `ffmpeg`. Every call is logged in `log`.
    /// Py: ProxyStreams' fake ffmpeg and its patched proxy_tracks.
    fn fake(probe: Output, raw: String, ffmpeg: Output, log: &Log) -> FakeRunner {
        let log = Rc::clone(log);
        FakeRunner::new(Box::new(
            move |program: &str, args: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>| -> std::io::Result<Output> {
                log.borrow_mut().push(Call {
                    program: program.to_string(),
                    args: args.to_vec(),
                    cwd: cwd.map(Path::to_path_buf),
                });
                if program == "ffprobe" {
                    return Ok(probe.clone());
                }
                let at = args.iter().position(|arg| arg == "-filter_complex").expect("ffmpeg is given a filter graph");
                let dir = cwd.expect("ffmpeg runs in the new folder");
                for name in raw_names(&args[at + 1]) {
                    std::fs::write(dir.join(format!("raw-{name}.txt")), &raw)?;
                }
                Ok(ffmpeg.clone())
            },
        ))
    }

    /// A test context in `dir` whose ffprobe and ffmpeg are `runner`.
    fn ctx_with(dir: &Path, runner: FakeRunner) -> Ctx {
        let mut ctx = Ctx::for_test(dir);
        ctx.runner = Box::new(runner);
        ctx
    }

    /// build from `ctx`'s folder with the relative proxy path "audio-proxy.mka" and `info` (None: read the file).
    fn build_with(ctx: &Ctx, out: &str, main: i64, cands: &[i64], info: Option<Value>) -> Result<Ordered<usize>, String> {
        let info: Option<AudioProxy> = info.map(|value| serde_json::from_value(value).unwrap());
        build(ctx, Path::new("audio-proxy.mka"), "audio-proxy.mka", Path::new(out), main, cands, info)
    }

    /// The command's exit code, stdout and stderr for `list`.
    fn call(ctx: &Ctx, list: &[&str]) -> (i32, String, String) {
        let (mut out, mut err): (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = run(ctx, &words(list), &mut out, &mut err);
        (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
    }

    /// The same, as expected.
    fn printed(code: i32, out: &str, err: &str) -> (i32, String, String) {
        (code, out.to_string(), err.to_string())
    }

    /// A stream of the rip as ProxyStreams.info takes it: (index, codec, profile, channels, layout, language).
    type Facts = (i64, &'static str, &'static str, i64, &'static str, &'static str);

    /// Two DTS streams in English (the reference, stream 2, is the second) and an AC-3 stream without a language.
    /// Py: ProxyStreams.VETO.
    const VETO: [Facts; 3] = [
        (1, "dts", "DTS", 6, "5.1(side)", "eng"),
        (2, "dts", "DTS-HD MA", 6, "5.1(side)", "eng"),
        (3, "ac3", "", 2, "stereo", ""),
    ];

    /// audio-proxy.json for `streams`: a mix track each, and an fc track for more than two channels; `count`
    /// replaces source.audio_streams. Py: ProxyStreams.info.
    fn info_value(streams: &[Facts], count: Option<usize>) -> Value {
        let mut tracks: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
        for &(n, codec, profile, ch, layout, lang) in streams {
            let source = json!({"codec": codec, "profile": profile, "channels": ch, "layout": layout,
                                "layout_guessed": "", "language": lang, "title": format!("t{n}"),
                                "sample_fmt": "fltp", "md5": format!("m{n}")});
            let series: &[&str] = if ch > 2 { &["mix", "fc"] } else { &["mix"] };
            for s in series {
                let track = tracks.len();
                tracks.push(json!({"track": track, "source_stream": n, "series": s, "source": source.clone()}));
            }
        }
        json!({"format": PROXY_FORMAT,
               "source": {"file": "x.mkv", "bytes": 1, "audio_streams": count.unwrap_or(streams.len())},
               "encoding": {"gain_db": -18}, "tracks": tracks})
    }

    /// The same, parsed. Py: ProxyStreams.info.
    fn info(streams: &[Facts], count: Option<usize>) -> AudioProxy {
        serde_json::from_value(info_value(streams, count)).unwrap()
    }

    fn mixed_run(dir: &Path) -> (Result<Ordered<usize>, String>, Vec<Call>) {
        let log = Log::default();
        let ffmpeg = Output { status: 0, stdout: "o\n".to_string(), stderr: String::new() };
        let ctx = ctx_with(dir, fake(mixed_probe(), RAW.to_string(), ffmpeg, &log));
        let info: AudioProxy = serde_json::from_str(MIXED_INFO).unwrap();
        let result = build(&ctx, Path::new("audio-proxy.mka"), "audio-proxy.mka", Path::new("out1"), 1, &[2, 5], Some(info));
        let calls = log.borrow().clone();
        (result, calls)
    }

    /// Py: test_audio_dataset ProxyStreams. proxy_levels writes streams.json from audio-proxy.json, so a rebuilt
    /// folder keeps its position veto.
    mod proxy_streams {
        use super::*;

        #[test]
        fn the_streams_are_those_ffprobe_lists() {
            let streams = proxy_streams(&info(&VETO, None)).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(
                streams[2],
                json!({"index": 3, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": "ac3", "channels": 2,
                       "channel_layout": "stereo", "tags": {"title": "t3"}})
            );
            // json.dumps writes the keys in this order (the Python's dict comparison did not look at it).
            assert_eq!(
                dumps(&streams[2], Style::PY_DEFAULT),
                r#"{"index": 3, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": "ac3", "channels": 2, "channel_layout": "stereo", "tags": {"title": "t3"}}"#
            );
            let parsed: Vec<FfprobeStream> = serde_json::from_value(Value::Array(streams)).unwrap();
            let stream = |n: i64, channels: i64, lossless: bool, language: &str, description: &str| AudioStream {
                stream: n,
                channels,
                lossless,
                language: language.to_string(),
                description: description.to_string(),
            };
            assert_eq!(
                ffprobe_audio(&parsed),
                vec![
                    stream(1, 6, false, "eng", "dts DTS 6 ch 5.1(side) t1"),
                    stream(2, 6, true, "eng", "dts DTS-HD MA 6 ch 5.1(side) t2"),
                    stream(3, 2, false, "und", "ac3 2 ch stereo t3"),
                ]
            );
            assert_eq!(position_veto(Some(parsed.as_slice()), 2).holds, Some(true));
            assert_eq!(proxy_streams(&info(&VETO, Some(4))), None); // a stream of the rip is missing
            let mut partial = info_value(&VETO, None);
            partial["tracks"][0]["source"].as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("language");
            assert_eq!(proxy_streams(&serde_json::from_value(partial).unwrap()), None);
        }

        #[test]
        fn build_writes_streams_json_beside_the_levels() {
            let tmp = TempDir::new("veto");
            let root = tmp.0.clone();
            let (mix, _) = programme(420, 1);
            let raw: String = mix[..200].iter().map(|v| format!("{KEY}{}\n", py_fixed(*v, 6))).collect();
            let probe = probe_output(&[(0, 1, "mix"), (1, 1, "fc"), (2, 2, "mix"), (3, 2, "fc"), (4, 3, "mix")]);
            let ctx = ctx_with(&root, fake(probe, raw, ok(), &Log::default()));
            let mka = root.join("audio-proxy.mka");
            let shown = mka.display().to_string();
            let frames = build(&ctx, &mka, &shown, &root.join("veto"), 2, &[3], Some(info(&VETO, None))).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(frames, ordered(&[("main-mix", 200), ("main-fc", 200), ("cand-3", 200)]));
            let tree = DiskTree::open(&root, &root.display().to_string()).unwrap();
            let written = read_streams(&tree, &PathKey::new("veto")).unwrap();
            let expected: Vec<FfprobeStream> =
                serde_json::from_value(Value::Array(proxy_streams(&info(&VETO, None)).unwrap())).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(written.as_deref(), Some(expected.as_slice()));
            assert_eq!(position_veto(written.as_deref(), 2).holds, Some(true));
            // What the Python wrote for exactly these inputs, byte for byte.
            assert_eq!(read(&root.join("veto/streams.json")), VETO_STREAMS_JSON);
            assert_eq!(read(&root.join("veto/manifest.txt")), VETO_MANIFEST);
            for (series, bytes) in [("main-mix", 1513), ("main-fc", 1512), ("cand-3", 1511)] {
                let text = read(&root.join(format!("veto/{series}.txt")));
                assert_eq!(text.len(), bytes, "{series}");
                assert_eq!(text.matches("\r\n").count(), 201, "{series}");
                let head = format!(
                    "# lazymkv audio levels v2: frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400 unit=dB floor=-100 series={series} file=audio-proxy.mka\r\n-19.9\r\n-19.9\r\n-19.9\r\n-19.9\r\n-30.5\r\n"
                );
                assert!(text.starts_with(&head), "{series}: {text:.200}");
                assert!(!root.join(format!("veto/raw-{series}.txt")).exists());
            }
            // Deliberate (spec section 4): the path as given; the Python wrote the resolved one.
            assert_eq!(read(&root.join("veto/proxy.txt")), format!("levels rebuilt from {shown}\n"));
            build(&ctx, &mka, &shown, &root.join("short"), 2, &[3], Some(info(&VETO, Some(4)))).unwrap();
            assert!(!root.join("short/streams.json").exists());
            assert!(root.join("short/manifest.txt").is_file());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_proxys_tracks_come_from_its_own_tags() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("tracks");
        let mka = tmp.0.join("audio-proxy.mka");
        let log = Log::default();
        let tracks = proxy_tracks(&ctx_with(&tmp.0, fake(mixed_probe(), String::new(), ok(), &log)), &mka).unwrap();
        let expected: BTreeMap<(i64, String), String> =
            [(1, "mix", "1"), (1, "fc", "2"), (2, "mix", "3"), (3, "side", "4"), (5, "mix", "7")]
                .iter()
                .map(|&(n, series, track)| ((n, series.to_string()), track.to_string()))
                .collect();
        assert_eq!(tracks, expected);
        let shown = mka.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        assert_eq!(
            log.borrow()[0].args,
            words(&["-v", "error", "-show_entries", "stream=index,codec_type:stream_tags", "-of", "json", &shown])
        );
        let absent = ctx_with(&tmp.0, FakeRunner::absent());
        assert_eq!(proxy_tracks(&absent, &mka), Err("[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'ffprobe'".to_string()));
        let named = Output {
            status: 0,
            stdout: r#"{"streams": [{"index": 1, "codec_type": "audio", "tags": {"LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM": "one"}}]}"#
                .to_string(),
            stderr: String::new(),
        };
        let bad = ctx_with(&tmp.0, fake(named, String::new(), ok(), &Log::default()));
        assert_eq!(proxy_tracks(&bad, &mka), Err("invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'one'".to_string()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn build_runs_ffprobe_then_one_ffmpeg_pass_as_the_python_did() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("args");
        let (result, calls) = mixed_run(&tmp.0);
        assert_eq!(result, Ok(ordered(&[("main-mix", 10), ("main-fc", 10), ("cand-2", 10), ("cand-5", 10)])));
        let mka = resolve_like_python(&tmp.0.join("audio-proxy.mka")).to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        assert_eq!(calls.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(
            calls[0],
            Call {
                program: "ffprobe".to_string(),
                args: words(&["-v", "error", "-show_entries", "stream=index,codec_type:stream_tags", "-of", "json", &mka]),
                cwd: None,
            }
        );
        let mut ffmpeg = words(&["-v", "error", "-nostdin", "-i", &mka, "-filter_complex", PYTHON_GRAPH]);
        for i in 0..4 {
            ffmpeg.extend(words(&["-map", &format!("[o{i}]"), "-f", "null", &format!("o{i}")]));
        }
        assert_eq!(calls[1], Call { program: "ffmpeg".to_string(), args: ffmpeg, cwd: Some(tmp.0.join("out1")) });
    }

    #[test]
    fn build_writes_the_files_as_the_python_did() {

            .unwrap()
            .map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())

        assert_eq!(read(&out.join("manifest.txt")), MIXED_MANIFEST);
        assert_eq!(read(&out.join("ffmpeg.txt")), "o\n");

    #[test]
    fn build_refuses_as_the_python_does() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("refusals");
        let root = tmp.0.as_path();
        let three = format!("{KEY}-20.000000\n").repeat(3);
        let ctx = ctx_with(root, fake(mixed_probe(), three.clone(), ok(), &Log::default()));
        std::fs::create_dir(root.join("good")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(build_with(&ctx, "good", 1, &[2], Some(small_info())), refused("good already exists"));
        assert_eq!(build_with(&ctx, "./good/", 1, &[2], Some(small_info())), refused("good already exists"));
        assert_eq!(
            build_with(&ctx, "e1", 9, &[2], Some(small_info())),
            refused("the proxy has no track of stream 9 (it holds [1, 2, 3, 5])")
        );
        for cands in [[2, 1], [2, 2]] {
            assert_eq!(
                build_with(&ctx, "e2", 1, &cands, Some(small_info())),
                refused("the main stream is also a candidate, or a candidate is listed twice")
            );
        }
        assert!(!root.join("e1").exists() && !root.join("e2").exists());
        let mut upper = small_info();
        upper["tracks"][2]["source"]["sample_fmt"] = json!("S32P");
        assert_eq!(
            build_with(&ctx, "e4", 1, &[2], Some(upper)),
            refused("audio-proxy.json gives stream 2 the sample format 'S32P'")
        );
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(root.join("e4")).unwrap().count(), 0, "made, then left empty, as the Python leaves it");
        // A stream's facts are its last track's: track 1's "s32p" stands and track 0's "s32 p" is never read.
        let mut last = small_info();
        last["tracks"][0]["source"]["sample_fmt"] = json!("s32 p");
        assert!(build_with(&ctx, "e4b", 1, &[2], Some(last)).is_ok());

        let failing = Output { status: 3, stdout: "partial\n".to_string(), stderr: format!("\n  {}zzzz\n", "y".repeat(299)) };
        let log = Log::default();
        let loud = ctx_with(root, fake(mixed_probe(), three.clone(), failing, &log));
        let mut gain = small_info();
        gain["encoding"] = json!({"gain_db": 6.5});
        assert_eq!(build_with(&loud, "e5", 1, &[], Some(gain)), Err(format!("ffmpeg failed (exit 3): {}z", "y".repeat(299))));
        assert_eq!(read(&root.join("e5/ffmpeg.txt")), format!("partial\n\n  {}zzzz\n", "y".repeat(299)));
        assert!(log.borrow()[1].args[6].contains(",volume=-6.5dB,"));

        let mka_shown = resolve_like_python(&root.join("audio-proxy.mka")).display().to_string();
        let unreadable =
            Output { status: 1, stdout: String::new(), stderr: " Invalid data found when processing input\n".to_string() };
        let probe_fails = ctx_with(root, fake(unreadable, three.clone(), ok(), &Log::default()));
        assert_eq!(
            build_with(&probe_fails, "e6", 1, &[2], Some(small_info())),
            Err(format!("ffprobe cannot read {mka_shown}: Invalid data found when processing input"))
        );
        assert!(!root.join("e6").exists());
        let absent = ctx_with(root, FakeRunner::absent());
        assert_eq!(
            build_with(&absent, "e6", 1, &[2], Some(small_info())),
            refused("[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'ffprobe'")
        );

        // audio-proxy.json read from beside the proxy (info None).
        let json_shown = resolve_like_python(&root.join("audio-proxy.json")).display().to_string();
        assert_eq!(
            build_with(&ctx, "e10", 1, &[2], None),
            Err(format!("{json_shown} is missing: without it the proxy is incomplete (audio-levels.ps1 writes it last)"))
        );
        let mut v0 = small_info();
        v0["format"] = json!("lazymkv audio proxy v0");
        std::fs::write(root.join("audio-proxy.json"), v0.to_string()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            build_with(&ctx, "e7", 1, &[2], None),
            Err(format!("{json_shown}: format is 'lazymkv audio proxy v0', not 'lazymkv audio proxy v1'"))
        );
        let mut unnamed = small_info();
        unnamed.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("format");
        std::fs::write(root.join("audio-proxy.json"), unnamed.to_string()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            build_with(&ctx, "e8", 1, &[2], None),
            Err(format!("{json_shown}: format is None, not 'lazymkv audio proxy v1'"))
        );
        let mut marked = b"\xef\xbb\xbf".to_vec();
        marked.extend_from_slice(SMALL_INFO.as_bytes());
        std::fs::write(root.join("audio-proxy.json"), marked).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(build_with(&ctx, "e9", 1, &[2], None), Ok(ordered(&[("main-mix", 3), ("main-fc", 3), ("cand-2", 3)])));
        assert_eq!(read(&root.join("e9/manifest.txt")), SMALL_MANIFEST);
    }

    #[test]
    fn run_reads_its_arguments_and_prints_as_the_python_did() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("run");
        let root = tmp.0.as_path();
        std::fs::write(root.join("audio-proxy.json"), SMALL_INFO).unwrap();
        let ctx = ctx_with(root, fake(mixed_probe(), format!("{KEY}-20.000000\n").repeat(3), ok(), &Log::default()));
        let usage = "usage: lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy <audio-proxy.mka> <new folder> --main <stream> [--cand <stream>[,<stream>...]]\n";
        let done = |folder: &str, series: &str| format!("levels from audio-proxy.mka: {series} -> {folder}\n");
        let both = "main-mix 3 frames, main-fc 3 frames, cand-2 3 frames";
        let alone = "main-mix 3 frames, main-fc 3 frames";
        let not_int = "invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'x'\n";
        assert_eq!(call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good", "--main", "1", "--cand", "2"]), printed(0, &done("good", both), ""));
        assert_eq!(call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good", "--main", "1", "--cand", "2"]), printed(1, "", "good already exists\n"));
        assert_eq!(call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good"]), printed(1, "", usage));
        assert_eq!(call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good2", "--cand", "1"]), printed(1, "", usage));
        assert_eq!(call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good3", "--main", "1", "--cand"]), printed(0, &done("good3", alone), ""));
        assert_eq!(call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good4", "--main", "x"]), printed(1, "", not_int));
        assert_eq!(call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good5", "--main", "1", "--cands", "2"]), printed(0, &done("good5", alone), ""));
        assert_eq!(
            call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good6", "--main", " +1 ", "--cand", ",2,", "extra"]),
            printed(0, &done("good6", both), "")
        );
        assert_eq!(call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "good8", "--main", "1", "--cand", "2,x"]), printed(1, "", not_int));
        let missing = resolve_like_python(&root.join("missing")).join("audio-proxy.json");
        assert_eq!(
            call(&ctx, &["missing/audio-proxy.mka", "good7", "--main", "1"]),
            printed(
                1,
                "",
                &format!("{} is missing: without it the proxy is incomplete (audio-levels.ps1 writes it last)\n", missing.display())
            )
        );
        // audio-proxy.json without every audio stream of the rip: no streams.json, and the note (its command renamed).
        std::fs::write(root.join("audio-proxy.json"), SMALL_INFO.replace("\"audio_streams\": 2", "\"audio_streams\": 3"))
            .unwrap();
        let note = "note: audio-proxy.json does not record every audio stream of the rip, so no streams.json was written: lazymkv-dev retune counts none of this folder's candidates (copy the rip's ffprobe-streams.json there as streams.json)\n";
        assert_eq!(
            call(&ctx, &["audio-proxy.mka", "noted", "--main", "1", "--cand", "2"]),
            printed(0, &format!("{}{note}", done("noted", both)), "")
        );
    }

    #[test]

    #[test]
    fn manifest_words_and_the_volume_are_spelt_as_python_spells_them() {
        assert_eq!(word(None), "-");
        assert_eq!(word(Some(&Value::Null)), "-");
        assert_eq!(word(Some(&json!(""))), "-");
        assert_eq!(word(Some(&json!("a b\t c"))), "a_b_c");
        assert_eq!(word(Some(&json!("x\u{1c}y"))), "x_y");
        assert_eq!(word(Some(&json!("\u{a0}lead"))), "_lead");
        assert_eq!(word(Some(&json!(0))), "0");
        assert_eq!(word(Some(&json!(false))), "False");
        assert_eq!(word(Some(&json!(1.5))), "1.5");
        for (gain, undo) in [
            (-18.0, ",volume=18dB"),
            (6.5, ",volume=-6.5dB"),
            (0.1, ",volume=-0.1dB"),
            (-1e-7, ",volume=1e-07dB"),
            (123456789.0, ",volume=-1.23457e+08dB"),
            (0.0, ""),
            (-0.0, ""),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(volume_undo(gain), undo, "gain {gain}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn paths_are_resolved_and_shown_as_pathlib_does() {
        for (given, shown) in [
            ("good", "good"),
            ("good/", "good"),
            ("./a//b/./", "a/b"),
            ("", "."),
            ("./", "."),
            ("/", "/"),
            ("//", "//"),
            ("//x", "//x"),
            ("///x/", "/x"),
            ("a/../b", "a/../b"),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(py_path_str(given), shown, "{given:?}");
        }
        let tmp = TempDir::new("resolve");
        let real = resolve_like_python(&tmp.0);
        assert!(real.is_absolute() && real.is_dir());
        assert!(!real.to_string_lossy().starts_with(r"\\?\"));
        assert_eq!(resolve_like_python(&tmp.0.join("nowhere/../audio-proxy.mka")), real.join("audio-proxy.mka"));
        assert_eq!(resolve_like_python(&tmp.0.join("nowhere/x.mka")), real.join("nowhere").join("x.mka"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn real_ffmpeg_rebuilds_the_levels_of_a_made_proxy() {
        for tool in ["ffmpeg", "ffprobe"] {
            match RealRunner.run(tool, &words(&["-version"]), None) {
                Ok(answer) if answer.status == 0 => {}
                Ok(answer) => return skip(&format!("{tool} -version exited {}", answer.status)),
                Err(_) => return skip(&format!("{tool} is not on PATH")),
            }
        }
        let tmp = TempDir::new("real");
        // Three mono FLAC tracks of 2 s at 8 kHz, tagged as audio-levels.ps1 tags them: stream 1's mix (1 kHz) and
        // centre (1 kHz, 6 dB lower), stream 2's mix (500 Hz), each stored 18 dB below what the chain measures.
        let make = words(&[
            "-v", "error", "-nostdin", "-y",
            "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "aevalsrc=0.0630957*sin(2*PI*1000*t):s=8000:d=2",
            "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "aevalsrc=0.0315479*sin(2*PI*1000*t):s=8000:d=2",
            "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "aevalsrc=0.0630957*sin(2*PI*500*t):s=8000:d=2",
            "-map", "0:a", "-map", "1:a", "-map", "2:a", "-c:a", "flac",
            "-metadata:s:a:0", "LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM=1", "-metadata:s:a:0", "LAZYMKV_SERIES=mix",
            "-metadata:s:a:1", "LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM=1", "-metadata:s:a:1", "LAZYMKV_SERIES=fc",
            "-metadata:s:a:2", "LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM=2", "-metadata:s:a:2", "LAZYMKV_SERIES=mix",
            "audio-proxy.mka",
        ]);
        let made = RealRunner.run("ffmpeg", &make, Some(tmp.0.as_path())).unwrap();
        if made.status != 0 {
            return skip(&format!("this ffmpeg cannot make the test proxy (lavfi, flac, matroska): {}", made.stderr.trim()));
        }
        std::fs::write(tmp.0.join("audio-proxy.json"), REAL_PROXY_JSON).unwrap();
        let mut ctx = Ctx::for_test(&tmp.0);
        ctx.runner = Box::new(RealRunner);
        let frames = build(&ctx, Path::new("audio-proxy.mka"), "audio-proxy.mka", Path::new("out"), 1, &[2], None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(frames, ordered(&[("main-mix", 100), ("main-fc", 100), ("cand-2", 100)]));
        let out = tmp.0.join("out");
        assert_eq!(read(&out.join("manifest.txt")), REAL_MANIFEST);
        assert_eq!(read(&out.join("streams.json")), REAL_STREAMS_JSON);
        assert_eq!(read(&out.join("proxy.txt")), "levels rebuilt from audio-proxy.mka\n");
        assert!(out.join("ffmpeg.txt").is_file());
        // The Python on ffmpeg 8.1.2 gave -9.0 (one frame -9.1), -15.1, and -9.5 (one frame -9.7) for these tracks.
        for (series, level) in [("main-mix", -9.0), ("main-fc", -15.1), ("cand-2", -9.5)] {
            assert!(!out.join(format!("raw-{series}.txt")).exists());
            let text = read(&out.join(format!("{series}.txt")));
            let mut lines = text.split("\r\n");
            let header = format!(
                "# lazymkv audio levels v2: frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400 unit=dB floor=-100 series={series} file=audio-proxy.mka"
            );
            assert_eq!(lines.next(), Some(header.as_str()));
            let values: Vec<f64> = lines.filter(|line| !line.is_empty()).map(|line| line.parse().unwrap()).collect();
            assert_eq!(values.len(), 100, "{series}");
            assert!(values.iter().all(|v| (v - level).abs() <= 0.3), "{series}: {values:?}");
        }
    }
}
