- [ ] **Step 4: Write the command**

Insert this block at the top of `crates/dev/src/cmd/levels_from_proxy.rs`, above the line `#[cfg(test)]`. It follows `proxy_levels.py` statement by statement: `build` checks and acts in the Python's order (audio-proxy.json, the gain, ffprobe, `out` exists, the tracks, the candidates, the new folder, the readers, ffmpeg, `ffmpeg.txt`, the exit code, the level files, `manifest.txt`, `streams.json`, `proxy.txt`); the level conversion is Task 1's `pyjson::write_level_file` (`convert_levels`: universal newlines, `Decimal` rounding half away from zero, `CRLF`); `-gain:g` is `py_g`; `{x!r}` is `py_repr_str` / `py_repr`; `str(value)` is `py_str`; truthiness is `py_truthy`; re's `\s` is `py_is_space`.

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy`: rebuilds an audio-levels folder from a title's compact audio copy, the proxy
//! that audio-levels.ps1 writes to the tuning dataset (`<slug>\<label>\audio-proxy.mka`, with audio-proxy.json
//! beside it), without the disc or the rip. The proxy holds every audio stream of the ripped title as one mono FLAC
//! track (its mixdown, series "mix"), a second track with the centre channel ("fc") for a layout with one, and a
//! side track ("side", not read here), stored gain_db below the signal the level chain measures; every track carries
//! the tags LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM (ffprobe's stream number in the rip) and LAZYMKV_SERIES. Each track is read back in
//! float, the stored gain is undone, the samples are converted to the sample format the source stream decodes to
//! (sample_fmt in audio-proxy.json), and the chain of audio-levels.ps1 runs over every track in one ffmpeg pass. The
//! files written are those audio-levels.ps1 writes (manifest.txt, main-mix.txt, main-fc.txt, cand-<n>.txt), plus
//! streams.json when audio-proxy.json records every audio stream of the rip, ffmpeg.txt and proxy.txt.
//! Py: proxy_levels.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Component, Path, PathBuf};

use lazymkv_core::audio::levels::{parse_proxy, AudioProxy, MANIFEST_LINE, PROXY_FORMAT};
use lazymkv_core::recording::{
    decode_text, py_float_value, py_g, py_int, py_int_value, py_is_space, py_repr, py_repr_str, py_str, py_strip,
    py_truthy, Encoding, Errors, Ordered,
};
use serde_json::{Map, Value};

use crate::evidence::Ctx;
use crate::pyjson::{write_level_file, write_manifest, write_streams_json};
use crate::runner::Output;

/// The level chain of audio-levels.ps1 after a track's reader: 8 kHz, the 300-3400 Hz band, 160-sample (20 ms)
/// frames, each frame's RMS level, printed by ametadata into the file named next. Py: TAIL.
const TAIL: &str = concat!(
    "aresample=8000,highpass=f=300,lowpass=f=3400,asetnsamples=n=160:p=0,",
    "astats=metadata=1:reset=1:measure_perchannel=none:measure_overall=RMS_level,",
    "ametadata=print:key=lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level:file=",
);
/// The file beside the proxy that describes it. Py: load_proxy_json.
const PROXY_JSON: &str = "audio-proxy.json";
/// After the path of a missing audio-proxy.json. Py: load_proxy_json.
const MISSING: &str = "is missing: without it the proxy is incomplete (audio-levels.ps1 writes it last)";
/// Py: build.
const TWICE: &str = "the main stream is also a candidate, or a candidate is listed twice";
/// A level file's header up to its series name. Py: build's header.
const LEVEL_HEADER: &str = "# lazymkv audio levels v2: frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400 unit=dB floor=-100 series=";
/// streams.json's first value. Py: build.
const FROM_PROXY: &str = "audio-proxy.json (audio streams only)";
/// The usage line (exit 1, as the Python's sys.exit). Py: main, with the command's new name.
const USAGE: &str =
    "usage: lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy <audio-proxy.mka> <new folder> --main <stream> [--cand <stream>[,<stream>...]]";
/// Printed after the frames when no streams.json was written. Py: main, with lazymkv-dev retune for the harness's
/// old name.
const NO_STREAMS_NOTE: &str = concat!(
    "note: audio-proxy.json does not record every audio stream of the rip, so no streams.json was written: ",
    "lazymkv-dev retune counts none of this folder's candidates (copy the rip's ffprobe-streams.json there as ",
    "streams.json)",
);

/// Writes a level folder for `main` and `cands` from the proxy `mka`: ffprobe for the proxy's tracks, one ffmpeg
/// pass (cwd `out`) through ctx.runner, level files by pyjson::level_file_text, manifest.txt, streams.json when
/// proxy_streams gives one, proxy.txt as "levels rebuilt from <mka_shown>" (the path as given, not resolved:
/// spec section 4). `info` None reads audio-proxy.json beside `mka`. Returns frames per series in write order
/// (main-mix, main-fc, cand-<n> ...). Err with the Python's SystemExit texts. Relative `mka` and `out` are taken
/// against ctx.cwd. Py: proxy_levels.build.
pub fn build(
    ctx: &Ctx,
    mka: &Path,
    mka_shown: &str,
    out: &Path,
    main: i64,
    cands: &[i64],
    info: Option<AudioProxy>,
) -> Result<Ordered<usize>, String> {
    let mka = resolve_like_python(&ctx.cwd.join(mka));
    let out_shown = py_path_str(&out.to_string_lossy());
    let out = ctx.cwd.join(out);
    let info = match info {
        Some(info) => info,
        None => load_proxy_json(&mka)?,
    };
    let gain = match info.encoding.get("gain_db") {
        Some(value) => py_float_value(value)?,
        None => 0.0,
    };
    let tracks = proxy_tracks(ctx, &mka)?;
    if out.exists() {
        return Err(format!("{out_shown} already exists"));
    }
    let measured: Vec<i64> = std::iter::once(main).chain(cands.iter().copied()).collect();
    let mix = |n: i64| (n, "mix".to_string());
    for &n in &measured {
        if !tracks.contains_key(&mix(n)) {
            let held: BTreeSet<i64> = tracks.keys().map(|(stream, _)| *stream).collect();
            let held: Vec<String> = held.iter().map(|stream| stream.to_string()).collect();
            return Err(format!("the proxy has no track of stream {n} (it holds [{}])", held.join(", ")));
        }
    }
    let distinct: BTreeSet<i64> = cands.iter().copied().collect();
    if cands.contains(&main) || distinct.len() != cands.len() {
        return Err(TWICE.to_string());
    }
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&out).map_err(|e| format!("{out_shown}: {e}"))?;
    let fc = (main, "fc".to_string());
    let has_fc = tracks.contains_key(&fc);
    // (series, source stream, proxy track) in the Python's order: main-mix, main-fc, cand-<n> ...
    let mut series: Vec<(String, i64, &str)> = vec![("main-mix".to_string(), main, tracks[&mix(main)].as_str())];
    if has_fc {
        series.push(("main-fc".to_string(), main, tracks[&fc].as_str()));
    }
    for &n in cands {
        series.push((format!("cand-{n}"), n, tracks[&mix(n)].as_str()));
    }
    let mut chains = Vec::new();
    for (i, (name, stream, track)) in series.iter().enumerate() {
        chains.push(format!("[0:{track}]{}{TAIL}raw-{name}.txt[o{i}]", reader(&info, *stream, gain)?));
    }
    let mut args: Vec<String> = ["-v", "error", "-nostdin", "-i"].iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect();
    args.push(mka.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
    args.push("-filter_complex".to_string());
    args.push(chains.join(";"));
    for i in 0..series.len() {
        args.extend(["-map".to_string(), format!("[o{i}]"), "-f".to_string(), "null".to_string(), format!("o{i}")]);
    }
    let run = run_tool(ctx, "ffmpeg", &args, Some(out.as_path()))?;
    write_file(&out.join("ffmpeg.txt"), &format!("{}{}", run.stdout, run.stderr))?;
    if run.status != 0 {
        return Err(format!("ffmpeg failed (exit {}): {}", run.status, first_chars(py_strip(&run.stderr), 300)));
    }
    let proxy_name = word_str(&mka.file_name().map(|name| name.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default());
    let mut frames: Ordered<usize> = Ordered::new();
    for (name, _, _) in &series {
        let raw_path = out.join(format!("raw-{name}.txt"));
        let bytes = std::fs::read(&raw_path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", raw_path.display()))?;
        let raw = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Strict)?;
        let header = format!("{LEVEL_HEADER}{name} file={proxy_name}");
        let count = write_level_file(&out.join(format!("{name}.txt")), &raw, &header)?;
        frames.insert(name.clone(), count);
        std::fs::remove_file(&raw_path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", raw_path.display()))?;
    }
    let src = &info.source;
    let mut lines = vec![
        format!("{MANIFEST_LINE} (experiment 13)"),
        format!(
            "file={} bytes={} seconds=0 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400 from_proxy={proxy_name}",
            word(src.get("file")),
            src.get("bytes").map_or_else(|| "0".to_string(), py_str)
        ),
    ];
    for &n in &measured {
        let s = facts_of(&info, n);
        let (role, fc_word, key) = if n == main {
            (format!("main={n}"), format!(" fc={}", if has_fc { "yes" } else { "no" }), "main-mix".to_string())
        } else {
            (format!("cand={n}"), String::new(), format!("cand-{n}"))
        };
        let count = frames.get(&key).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        let guess = match s.get("layout_guessed") {
            Some(value) if py_truthy(value) => format!(" layout_guessed={}", py_str(value)),
            _ => String::new(),
        };
        let md5 = match s.get("md5") {
            Some(value) if py_truthy(value) => py_str(value),
            _ => format!("unknown-{n}"),
        };
        lines.push(format!(
            "{role} codec={} profile={} channels={} layout={}{guess} language={}{fc_word} frames={count} md5={md5}",
            word(s.get("codec")),
            word(s.get("profile")),
            s.get("channels").map_or_else(|| "0".to_string(), py_str),
            word(s.get("layout")),
            word(s.get("language")),
        ));
    }
    write_manifest(&out.join("manifest.txt"), &lines).map_err(|e| format!("manifest.txt: {e}"))?;
    if let Some(streams) = proxy_streams(&info) {
        let mut doc = Map::new();
        doc.insert("from_proxy".to_string(), Value::from(FROM_PROXY));
        doc.insert("streams".to_string(), Value::Array(streams));
        write_streams_json(&out.join("streams.json"), &Value::Object(doc)).map_err(|e| format!("streams.json: {e}"))?;
    }
    write_file(&out.join("proxy.txt"), &format!("levels rebuilt from {mka_shown}\n"))?;
    Ok(frames)
}

/// streams.json's "streams" from audio-proxy.json, None unless it records every audio stream with codec, channels
/// and language: the fields ffprobe_audio and position_veto read (index, codec_type, codec_name, channels, profile,
/// channel_layout, the language and title tags), in stream order; an empty profile, layout or tag is left out, as
/// ffprobe leaves it out. A stream's facts are those of its first track (setdefault). Py: proxy_streams.
pub fn proxy_streams(info: &AudioProxy) -> Option<Vec<Value>> {
    let empty = Map::new();
    let mut facts: Vec<(i64, &Map<String, Value>)> = Vec::new();
    for track in &info.tracks {
        let source = track.source.as_ref().unwrap_or(&empty);
        let n = track.source_stream.as_i64()?;
        if !["codec", "channels", "language"].iter().all(|key| source.contains_key(*key)) {
            return None;
        }
        if !facts.iter().any(|(m, _)| *m == n) {
            facts.push((n, source));
        }
    }
    let count = info.source.get("audio_streams");
    if facts.is_empty() || !count.is_some_and(|value| py_eq_int(value, facts.len() as i64)) {
        return None;
    }
    facts.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| *n);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for (n, s) in facts {
        let mut stream = Map::new();
        stream.insert("index".to_string(), Value::from(n));
        stream.insert("codec_type".to_string(), Value::from("audio"));
        stream.insert("codec_name".to_string(), s["codec"].clone());
        let channels = if py_truthy(&s["channels"]) { py_int_value(&s["channels"]).ok()? } else { 0 };
        stream.insert("channels".to_string(), Value::from(channels));
        if let Some(profile) = s.get("profile").filter(|value| py_truthy(value)) {
            stream.insert("profile".to_string(), profile.clone());
        }
        if let Some(layout) = s.get("layout").filter(|value| py_truthy(value)) {
            stream.insert("channel_layout".to_string(), layout.clone());
        }
        let mut tags = Map::new();
        for key in ["language", "title"] {
            if let Some(value) = s.get(key).filter(|value| py_truthy(value)) {
                tags.insert(key.to_string(), value.clone());
            }
        }
        if !tags.is_empty() {
            stream.insert("tags".to_string(), Value::Object(tags));
        }
        out.push(Value::Object(stream));
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// The command, registered in COMMANDS as "levels-from-proxy". The words are read exactly as the Python's main
/// reads them: `<mka> <out> --main N`, then `--cand LIST` only as the fifth and sixth words; any other word after
/// them is ignored. Every failure prints one line to `err` and exits 1. Py: proxy_levels.main.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    if args.len() < 4 || args[2] != "--main" {
        let _ = writeln!(err, "{USAGE}");
        return 1;
    }
    let Some(main) = py_int(&args[3]) else {
        let _ = writeln!(err, "{}", not_an_int(&args[3]));
        return 1;
    };
    let mut cands = Vec::new();
    if args.len() >= 6 && args[4] == "--cand" {
        for piece in args[5].split(',').filter(|piece| !piece.is_empty()) {
            let Some(n) = py_int(piece) else {
                let _ = writeln!(err, "{}", not_an_int(piece));
                return 1;
            };
            cands.push(n);
        }
    }
    match build(ctx, Path::new(&args[0]), &args[0], Path::new(&args[1]), main, &cands, None) {
        Ok(frames) => {
            let done: Vec<String> = frames.iter().map(|(name, count)| format!("{name} {count} frames")).collect();
            let _ = writeln!(out, "levels from {}: {} -> {}", args[0], done.join(", "), args[1]);
            if !ctx.cwd.join(&args[1]).join("streams.json").is_file() {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "{NO_STREAMS_NOTE}");
            }
            0
        }
        Err(message) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "{message}");
            1
        }
    }
}

/// int()'s ValueError text, printed where the Python crashed on a stream number.
fn not_an_int(text: &str) -> String {
    format!("invalid literal for int() with base 10: {}", py_repr_str(text))
}

/// audio-proxy.json beside the proxy, read as utf-8-sig and checked for its format. Py: load_proxy_json.
fn load_proxy_json(mka: &Path) -> Result<AudioProxy, String> {
    let path = mka.with_file_name(PROXY_JSON);
    let shown = path.display().to_string();
    if !path.is_file() {
        return Err(format!("{shown} {MISSING}"));
    }
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).map_err(|e| format!("{shown}: {e}"))?;
    let text = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)?;
    let data = parse_proxy(&text)?;
    let format = data.format.clone().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
    if format.as_str() != Some(PROXY_FORMAT) {
        return Err(format!("{shown}: format is {}, not {}", py_repr(&format), py_repr_str(PROXY_FORMAT)));
    }
    Ok(data)
}

/// {(source stream, series): the proxy's track number as a filter graph names it} from the proxy's own tags (tag
/// names upper-cased, the series "mix" when not tagged), read by ffprobe. Py: proxy_tracks.
fn proxy_tracks(ctx: &Ctx, mka: &Path) -> Result<BTreeMap<(i64, String), String>, String> {
    let shown = mka.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    let mut args: Vec<String> = ["-v", "error", "-show_entries", "stream=index,codec_type:stream_tags", "-of", "json"]
        .iter()
        .map(|arg| arg.to_string())
        .collect();
    args.push(shown.clone());
    let probe = run_tool(ctx, "ffprobe", &args, None)?;
    if probe.status != 0 {
        return Err(format!("ffprobe cannot read {shown}: {}", first_chars(py_strip(&probe.stderr), 300)));
    }
    let doc: Value = serde_json::from_str(&probe.stdout).map_err(|e| format!("ffprobe's output: {e}"))?;
    let Value::Object(doc) = doc else {
        return Err("ffprobe's output is not a JSON object".to_string());
    };
    let mut out = BTreeMap::new();
    for stream in doc.get("streams").and_then(Value::as_array).into_iter().flatten() {
        let Some(stream) = stream.as_object() else { continue };
        let mut tags: BTreeMap<String, &Value> = BTreeMap::new();
        if let Some(Value::Object(given)) = stream.get("tags") {
            for (key, value) in given {
                tags.insert(key.to_uppercase(), value);
            }
        }
        if stream.get("codec_type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("audio") {
            continue;
        }
        let Some(source) = tags.get("LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM") else { continue };
        let source = py_int_value(source)?;
        let series = tags.get("LAZYMKV_SERIES").map_or_else(|| "mix".to_string(), |value| py_str(value));
        let index = stream.get("index").ok_or_else(|| "KeyError: 'index'".to_string())?;
        out.insert((source, series), py_str(index));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// The start of a track's chain: float mono, the stored gain undone, then the sample format the source stream
/// decodes to (sample_fmt in audio-proxy.json, "fltp" when it gives none), because ffmpeg's filters compute in that
/// format and 16-bit arithmetic reads quiet frames lower. Py: build's reader.
fn reader(info: &AudioProxy, stream: i64, gain: f64) -> Result<String, String> {
    let facts = facts_of(info, stream);
    let fmt = match facts.get("sample_fmt") {
        Some(value) if py_truthy(value) => match value.as_str() {
            Some(text) => text.to_string(),
            None => return Err("TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object".to_string()),
        },
        _ => "fltp".to_string(),
    };
    if fmt.is_empty() || !fmt.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_lowercase() || b.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return Err(format!("audio-proxy.json gives stream {stream} the sample format {}", py_repr_str(&fmt)));
    }
    Ok(format!("aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:channel_layouts=mono{},aformat=sample_fmts={fmt},", volume_undo(gain)))
}

/// ",volume=<-gain>dB" with -gain spelt by format(x, "g"), or nothing for a gain of 0. Py: `undo` in build's reader.
fn volume_undo(gain: f64) -> String {
    if gain != 0.0 {
        format!(",volume={}dB", py_g(-gain))
    } else {
        String::new()
    }
}

/// What audio-proxy.json says about stream `n`: the `source` of the last track of that stream (build's dict
/// comprehension keeps the last), {} when there is none. Py: build's `source.get(n, {})`.
fn facts_of(info: &AudioProxy, n: i64) -> Map<String, Value> {
    info.tracks
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|track| py_eq_int(&track.source_stream, n))
        .and_then(|track| track.source.clone())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Python's `==` between a JSON value and an int: numbers by value, true and false as 1 and 0, nothing else.
fn py_eq_int(value: &Value, n: i64) -> bool {
    match value {
        Value::Number(number) => {
            if let Some(i) = number.as_i64() {
                i == n
            } else if let Some(u) = number.as_u64() {
                i64::try_from(u).map_or(false, |u| u == n)
            } else {
                number.as_f64().map_or(false, |f| f == n as f64)
            }
        }
        Value::Bool(flag) => i64::from(*flag) == n,
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// A manifest value: "-" for None, null or "", otherwise str(value) with every run of whitespace as one "_".
/// Py: word.
fn word(value: Option<&Value>) -> String {
    match value {
        None | Some(Value::Null) => word_str(""),
        Some(value) => word_str(&py_str(value)),
    }
}

/// word() of a str: re.sub(r"\s+", "_", text), "-" for "" (re's \s on str is str.isspace).
fn word_str(text: &str) -> String {
    if text.is_empty() {
        return "-".to_string();
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut in_space = false;
    for c in text.chars() {
        if py_is_space(c) {
            if !in_space {
                out.push('_');
            }
            in_space = true;
        } else {
            out.push(c);
            in_space = false;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// The first `n` characters of `text`. Py: text[:n].
fn first_chars(text: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    text.chars().take(n).collect()
}

/// ctx.runner.run, with Python's FileNotFoundError text when the program is not on PATH (the Python crashed there).
fn run_tool(ctx: &Ctx, program: &str, args: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>) -> Result<Output, String> {
    ctx.runner.run(program, args, cwd).map_err(|e| {
        if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound {
            format!("[Errno 2] No such file or directory: {}", py_repr_str(program))
        } else {
            format!("{program}: {e}")
        }
    })
}

/// Writes a text file as Path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8") does on the Mac: UTF-8, no newline translation.
fn write_file(path: &Path, text: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    std::fs::write(path, text).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
}

/// Python's Path.resolve() (strict=False) of an absolute path: the longest part that exists, resolved through its
/// symbolic links, then the rest with "." dropped and ".." taking a name off. Windows' verbatim prefix (\\?\C:\) is
/// dropped so ffmpeg gets the path Python would have given it.
fn resolve_like_python(path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let parts: Vec<Component> = path.components().collect();
    for cut in (1..=parts.len()).rev() {
        let head: PathBuf = parts[..cut].iter().collect();
        if let Ok(mut resolved) = std::fs::canonicalize(&head) {
            for part in &parts[cut..] {
                match part {
                    Component::CurDir => {}
                    Component::ParentDir => {
                        resolved.pop();
                    }
                    other => resolved.push(other.as_os_str()),
                }
            }
            return strip_verbatim(resolved);
        }
    }
    path.to_path_buf()
}

/// `\\?\C:\x` as `C:\x`; any other path unchanged.
fn strip_verbatim(path: PathBuf) -> PathBuf {
    let plain = path
        .to_str()
        .and_then(|text| text.strip_prefix(r"\\?\"))
        .filter(|rest| rest.as_bytes().get(1) == Some(&b':'))
        .map(PathBuf::from);
    plain.unwrap_or(path)
}

/// How POSIX pathlib spells a path given as text: repeated '/' as one (a leading "//" kept, as POSIX allows), "."
/// parts left out, no trailing '/', "." for nothing. Py: str(pathlib.Path(text)).
fn py_path_str(text: &str) -> String {
    let (root, rest) = if text.starts_with("//") && !text.starts_with("///") {
        ("//", &text[2..])
    } else if text.starts_with('/') {
        ("/", text.trim_start_matches('/'))
    } else {
        ("", text)
    };
    let parts: Vec<&str> = rest.split('/').filter(|part| !part.is_empty() && *part != ".").collect();
    if root.is_empty() && parts.is_empty() {
        return ".".to_string();
    }
    format!("{root}{}", parts.join("/"))
}

What this task settles that the spec and the interfaces leave open (each is in the code below; none changes a reader's verdict line, count or order):

1. Exit codes are the Python's (spec 3.4: `exp02` 0/1, `encoding` 0, `hit-rate` 0/1, `exp11` 0/1/2, `compare-scans` 0/1, `ocr-compare` 0/2), plus the Global Constraints' "exit 2 where the Python crashed": a missing argument of the four readers that read `sys.argv[1]` directly (the Python raised `IndexError`), an unreadable file or folder, a `meta.json`, `mkvmerge.json` or `rip-summary.json` that does not parse, a title word that is not a number in `exp11 coverage <where>@<title>`. Those print `lazymkv-dev <cmd>: error: <message>` (or the argparse-style usage lines for a missing argument) on stderr. Further words after the four readers' arguments are ignored, as the Python ignored them.
2. `-h` or `--help` as the first word of `exp02`, `encoding`, `hit-rate` or `compare-scans` prints `usage: lazymkv-dev <cmd> <args>` and exits 0 (the Python took the word as a path and crashed). `exp11` and `ocr-compare` print argparse's help with the program name replaced by `lazymkv-dev <cmd>` (80 columns, as the Python printed it on the Mac).
3. `compare-scans` prints each title key as `(a, b, c)` with every part written by `pyjson::dumps` with `Style::PY_DEFAULT` (`"00800.mpls"`, `null` for an absent attribute), the deliberate change spec 3.4 names; the lists keep the Python's order, which sorted `str(key)`, the tuple's Python repr (`compare_scans::python_repr`), so `("it's.mpls", null, null)` still comes before `("a.mpls", null, null)`.
4. Robot logs read with `Path.read_text` (the scan and runs of `exp02`, both scans of `compare-scans`, `exp11`'s scan) get Python's text-mode newline translation (`"\r\n"` and a lone `"\r"` become `"\n"`) before `robot::parse`, as Task 3's `reconcile` does; `decode_text` alone does not translate.
5. `exp02` sorts its runs by title number with a stable sort over `Tree::glob`'s `PathKey` order; the Python's ties (`title-1.txt` beside `title-01.txt`) kept the directory's order, which no recording has.
6. Files the Python read as untyped dicts are read through the typed views Task 1 gives (`Meta`, `Summary`, `FrameEntry`, `OcrLine`, `OcrSummary`): a field of an unexpected type makes the file unreadable (exit 2) where the Python might have read on (02-interfaces.md, open point 10). An OCR record `{"summary": null}` counts as a frame (the Python skipped it), and a crop box that is not a list ends the run with exit 2.
7. `ocr-compare`'s `statistics.mean` is `exact_mean`: the exact sum of the floats over big integers (64-bit limbs), divided by the count and rounded once, ties to even, as `float(Fraction(total, n))`; a NaN or an infinity among the values gives the plain sum of the non-finite values over the count, as `statistics._sum` keeps only those. `statistics.median` is `median`. Its error lines carry Python's `OSError` and `UnicodeDecodeError` texts; JSON syntax errors carry `serde_json`'s (open point 6).
8. The stream-number and crop patterns and `exp02`'s run numbers take ASCII digits only (open point 9).
9. The `COMMANDS` synopsis is the argument part only, as Task 1 defines the table and every earlier task writes its row (this task follows Task 1).
10. No Rust file of this task names a `.py` file or `python3` (Task 15's `git grep 'python3\|\.py\b'`): the Python modules are named without their suffix (`Py: exp02_check.check_run`). Printed lines keep the Python's words verbatim, `subtitle_text.measure` and `compare_tracks` among them.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::run;
    use crate::evidence::Ctx;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

    /// Py: SAVING.
    const SAVING: &str = "MSG:5014,0,2,\"Saving 1 titles into directory x\",\"Saving %1 titles into directory %2\",\"1\",\"x\"\n";
    /// Py: SCAN.
    const SCAN: &str = "TINFO:0,16,0,\"00001.mpls\"\nTINFO:1,16,0,\"00002.mpls\"\n";

    /// Py: ADDED.format(f=file, n=number).
    fn added(file: &str, number: u32) -> String {
        format!("MSG:3307,0,2,\"File {file} was added as title #{number}\",\"File %1 was added as title #%2\",\"{file}\",\"{number}\"\n")
    }

    /// Py: BOTH_ADDED.
    fn both_added() -> String {
        format!("{}{}{SAVING}", added("00001.mpls", 0), added("00002.mpls", 1))
    }

    /// A folder under the system's temporary folder, removed when dropped. Py: TempDir.
    struct TempDir(PathBuf);

    impl TempDir {
        fn new(name: &str) -> TempDir {
            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lazymkv-test-exp02-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
            TempDir(dir)
        }

        /// Py: TempDir.write (UTF-8, parent folders made).
        fn write(&self, name: &str, text: &str) -> PathBuf {
            let path = self.0.join(name);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
            path
        }
    }

    impl Drop for TempDir {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
        }
    }

    /// The command over `dir`: (exit code, stdout, stderr). Py: quiet(exp02_check.main, dir).
    fn quiet(dir: &Path) -> (i32, String, String) {
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(dir);
        let args = vec![dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned()];
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = run(&ctx, &args, &mut out, &mut err);
        (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
    }

    /// The lines as print() writes them.
    fn printed(lines: &[&str]) -> String {
        lines.iter().map(|line| format!("{line}\n")).collect()
    }

    #[test]

        tmp.write("exp02/title-1.txt", &both_added());

        let tmp = TempDir::new("profile");

    #[test]

                "title   1: scan source=00002.mpls rip #1=00002.mpls match=yes 5014=yes added-before-5014=yes 3308-lines=0 3309-lines=0",

    #[test]

        // title-x.txt does not match title-[0-9]*.txt; 2 sorts before 10 as a number.

Insert at the top of `crates/dev/src/cmd/exp02.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]`. Python spellings in it: `str.isdigit` is `py_isdigit` and `int()` is `py_int` (Task 1); the glob and its `sorted(..., key=int)` are `Tree::glob` (`PathKey` order) followed by a stable sort on the number; `read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")` and `"utf-8-sig"` are `read_text` with `Encoding::Utf8` / `Encoding::Utf8Sig` and `Errors::Replace`, then `text_mode` for the text-mode newline translation; `sorted()` of the added file names is the `BTreeSet`'s order (code points).

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev exp02 <dir>`: experiment 2, do the 3307/3308 title numbers of a rip call equal the index ripped?
//! Py: exp02_check, its lines verbatim. Exit 0 when every run says yes; 1 when a run says no or there is no run;
//! 2 where the Python crashed (no argument; the folder, its scan.txt or a run unreadable).

use crate::evidence::{Ctx, DiskTree};
use crate::usage_error;
use lazymkv_core::recording::{py_int, py_isdigit, read_text, Encoding, Errors, PathKey, Tree};
use lazymkv_core::robot::{parse, Scan};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::io::Write;

/// The command's name as typed.
const NAME: &str = "exp02";
/// Its usage after "usage: lazymkv-dev ". The Python read sys.argv[1] and ignored any further word; so does this.
const USAGE: &str = "exp02 <dir>";
/// A missing folder argument (the Python crashed with an IndexError).
const REQUIRED: &str = "the following arguments are required: dir";
/// The runs below <dir>/exp02, as the Python's glob names them.
const RUN_PATTERN: &str = "title-[0-9]*.txt";

/// The facts for one rip call of a title that was stopped after the saving message. Py: check_run's dict.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RunFacts {
    /// The scan's attribute 16 (source file) of the title; None when the scan does not list it.
    pub expected: Option<String>,
    /// Every file this run added under the title's number, sorted and joined with "/"; None when none.
    pub added: Option<String>,
    /// The run added the scan's source file, and no other file, under the title's number.
    pub matched: bool,
    /// The run printed the saving message: MSG:5014, or MSG:5015 when a profile is in use (MakeMKV 2.0.0).
    pub saw_5014: bool,
    /// The run has a saving message and a 3307/3308 line, and every 3307/3308 line comes before the first saving
    /// message.
    pub before: bool,
    /// How many MSG:3308 lines the run has.
    pub n3308: usize,
    /// How many MSG:3309 lines the run has.
    pub n3309: usize,
}

/// The facts for the run `log` of `title` against `scan`. The printed labels keep the name 5014 and are true for
/// either saving code. Nothing passes by default: a title the scan does not list, a run with no 3307/3308 line, and
/// a title number added for two different files are all a "NO". Py: exp02_check.check_run.
pub fn check_run(scan: &Scan, title: i64, log: &Scan) -> RunFacts {
    let codes: Vec<u32> = log.messages.iter().map(|message| message.code).collect();
    // title number -> every file added under that number in this run
    let mut added: BTreeMap<i64, BTreeSet<String>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for message in &log.messages {
        let params = &message.params;
        if (message.code == 3307 || message.code == 3308) && params.len() >= 2 {
            let last = params[params.len() - 1].as_str();
            if py_isdigit(last) {
                if let Some(number) = py_int(last) {
                    added.entry(number).or_default().insert(params[0].clone());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let added_at = positions(&codes, &[3307, 3308]);
    let saving_at = positions(&codes, &[5014, 5015]);
    let expected = u32::try_from(title)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|number| scan.titles.get(&number))
        .and_then(|attrs| attrs.get(&16))
        .cloned();
    let saw_5014 = !saving_at.is_empty();
    let before = saw_5014 && !added_at.is_empty() && added_at.iter().all(|at| *at < saving_at[0]);
    let files = added.get(&title);
    let matched = match (&expected, files) {
        (Some(source), Some(files)) => files.len() == 1 && files.contains(source),
        _ => false,
    };
    // "/".join(sorted(...)) or None: an empty join is None too.
    let joined = files
        .map(|files| files.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("/"))
        .filter(|text| !text.is_empty());
    RunFacts {
        expected,
        added: joined,
        matched,
        saw_5014,
        before,
        n3308: positions(&codes, &[3308]).len(),
        n3309: positions(&codes, &[3309]).len(),
    }
}

/// The places in `codes` that hold one of `wanted`, in order.
fn positions(codes: &[u32], wanted: &[u32]) -> Vec<usize> {
    codes.iter().enumerate().filter(|(_, code)| wanted.contains(*code)).map(|(at, _)| at).collect()
}

/// "yes" or "NO", as the run lines spell them.
fn yes_or_no(ok: bool) -> &'static str {
    if ok {
        "yes"
    } else {
        "NO"
    }
}

/// str() of an optional string: the string, or "None".
fn or_none(text: &Option<String>) -> &str {
    text.as_deref().unwrap_or("None")
}

/// The title number of a run file: the first run of digits in its stem (the name without its last suffix, as
/// pathlib's stem). Err when there is none or it overflows i64 (the glob guarantees one; Python's int has no limit).
fn run_number(name: &str) -> Result<i64, String> {
    let stem = match name.rfind('.') {
        Some(at) if at > 0 && at < name.len() - 1 => &name[..at],
        _ => name,
    };
    let Some(start) = stem.find(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit()) else {
        return Err(format!("{name}: no title number in the name"));
    };
    let digits: String = stem[start..].chars().take_while(char::is_ascii_digit).collect();
    py_int(&digits).ok_or_else(|| format!("{name}: the title number {digits} is too large"))
}

/// The text as Python's text-mode read hands it to robot.parse: "\r\n" and a lone "\r" become "\n" (Path.read_text
/// translates newlines; decode_text does not).
fn text_mode(text: &str) -> String {
    text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace('\r', "\n")
}

/// Writes exp02_check.main's lines for the recording `rec` of `tree` as it goes, and returns whether experiment 2
/// says yes; Err where the Python crashed, after the lines written so far. Py: exp02_check.main.
pub fn report(tree: &dyn Tree, rec: &PathKey, out: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<bool, String> {
    let scan = parse(&text_mode(&read_text(tree, &rec.join("scan.txt"), Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace)?));
    let mut runs: Vec<(i64, PathKey)> = Vec::new();
    for path in tree.glob(&rec.join("exp02"), RUN_PATTERN) {
        runs.push((run_number(path.name())?, path));
    }
    // sorted(..., key=title number) is stable: two names with one number keep the glob's order.
    runs.sort_by_key(|(number, _)| *number);
    let mut all_ok = !runs.is_empty();
    for (title, path) in &runs {
        let log = parse(&text_mode(&read_text(tree, path, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Replace)?));
        let r = check_run(&scan, *title, &log);
        all_ok = all_ok && r.saw_5014 && r.before && r.matched;
        let _ = writeln!(
            out,
            "title {:>3}: scan source={} rip #{}={} match={} 5014={} added-before-5014={} 3308-lines={} 3309-lines={}",
            title,
            or_none(&r.expected),
            title,
            or_none(&r.added),
            yes_or_no(r.matched),
            yes_or_no(r.saw_5014),
            yes_or_no(r.before),
            r.n3308,
            r.n3309
        );
    }
    let _ = writeln!(out);
    let _ = writeln!(out, "EXPERIMENT 2: {} ({} titles)", if all_ok { "yes" } else { "no" }, runs.len());
    Ok(all_ok)
}

/// `lazymkv-dev exp02 <dir>`. Py: exp02_check's `sys.exit(0 if main(sys.argv[1]) else 1)`.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    let Some(dir) = args.first() else {
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, REQUIRED);
    };
    if dir == "-h" || dir == "--help" {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "usage: lazymkv-dev {USAGE}");
        return 0;
    }
    let tree = match DiskTree::open(&ctx.abs(dir), dir) {
        Ok(tree) => tree,
        Err(error) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {NAME}: error: {dir}: {error}");
            return 2;
        }
    };
    match report(&tree, &PathKey::root(), out) {
        Ok(true) => 0,
        Ok(false) => 1,
        Err(message) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {NAME}: error: {message}");
            2
        }
    }
}

Python spellings: `bytes.splitlines()` is `py_bytes_splitlines` (`\n`, `\r`, `\r\n` only; 02-interfaces.md open point 7); `data.decode("utf-8")` and its `UnicodeDecodeError` text are `decode_text(.., Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Strict)`; `decode("utf-8", errors="replace")` is `Errors::Replace`; `decode("cp1252", errors="replace")` is the table below; `[:160]` counts characters.

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev encoding <file>`: experiment 8, which encoding does makemkvcon use for robot output?
//! Py: check_encoding, its lines verbatim. Exit 0; 2 where the Python crashed (no argument, the file unreadable).

use crate::evidence::Ctx;
use crate::usage_error;
use lazymkv_core::recording::{decode_text, py_bytes_splitlines, Encoding, Errors};
use std::io::Write;

/// The command's name as typed.
const NAME: &str = "encoding";
/// Its usage after "usage: lazymkv-dev ". The Python read sys.argv[1] and ignored any further word; so does this.
const USAGE: &str = "encoding <file>";
/// A missing file argument (the Python crashed with an IndexError).
const REQUIRED: &str = "the following arguments are required: file";
/// How many lines with a byte above 127 are shown, and how many characters of each shown line.
const SHOW_NON_ASCII: usize = 5;
const SHOW_CHARS: usize = 160;
/// How many lines with a backslash-escaped quote are shown.
const SHOW_QUOTED: usize = 3;

/// Windows-1252 for the bytes 0x80 to 0x9F, and U+FFFD for the five it leaves undefined (0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90,
/// 0x9D), as Python's decode("cp1252", errors="replace") gives them. Every other byte is Latin-1 (U+0000 to U+007F,
/// U+00A0 to U+00FF).
const CP1252_80_9F: [char; 32] = [
    '\u{20ac}', '\u{fffd}', '\u{201a}', '\u{0192}', '\u{201e}', '\u{2026}', '\u{2020}', '\u{2021}',
    '\u{02c6}', '\u{2030}', '\u{0160}', '\u{2039}', '\u{0152}', '\u{fffd}', '\u{017d}', '\u{fffd}',
    '\u{fffd}', '\u{2018}', '\u{2019}', '\u{201c}', '\u{201d}', '\u{2022}', '\u{2013}', '\u{2014}',
    '\u{02dc}', '\u{2122}', '\u{0161}', '\u{203a}', '\u{0153}', '\u{fffd}', '\u{017e}', '\u{0178}',
];

/// The lines check_encoding.main prints for the bytes of a robot log. Py: check_encoding.main.
pub fn report_lines(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    match decode_text(data, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Strict) {
        Ok(_) => lines.push("valid UTF-8: yes".to_string()),
        Err(error) => lines.push(format!("valid UTF-8: NO ({error})")),
    }
    let mut shown = 0;
    for raw in py_bytes_splitlines(data) {
        if raw.iter().any(|byte| *byte > 127) {
            lines.push(format!("utf-8 : {}", first_chars(&utf8_replaced(raw), SHOW_CHARS)));
            lines.push(format!("cp1252: {}", first_chars(&cp1252(raw), SHOW_CHARS)));
            shown += 1;
            if shown == SHOW_NON_ASCII {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    lines.push(format!("lines with non-ASCII bytes shown: {shown}"));
    let quoted: Vec<&[u8]> = py_bytes_splitlines(data)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|raw| raw.windows(2).any(|pair| pair == b"\\\""))
        .collect();
    lines.push(format!("lines with a backslash-escaped quote: {}", quoted.len()));
    for raw in quoted.iter().take(SHOW_QUOTED) {
        lines.push(format!("   {}", first_chars(&utf8_replaced(raw), SHOW_CHARS)));
    }
    lines
}

/// bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").
fn utf8_replaced(raw: &[u8]) -> String {
    decode_text(raw, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace).unwrap_or_default()
}

/// bytes.decode("cp1252", errors="replace").
fn cp1252(raw: &[u8]) -> String {
    raw.iter()
        .map(|&byte| if (0x80..=0x9f).contains(&byte) { CP1252_80_9F[usize::from(byte - 0x80)] } else { char::from(byte) })
        .collect()
}

/// text[:n]: the first `n` characters.
fn first_chars(text: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    text.chars().take(n).collect()
}

/// `lazymkv-dev encoding <file>`. Py: check_encoding's `main(sys.argv[1])`.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    let Some(file) = args.first() else {
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, REQUIRED);
    };
    if file == "-h" || file == "--help" {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "usage: lazymkv-dev {USAGE}");
        return 0;
    }
    match std::fs::read(ctx.abs(file)) {
        Ok(data) => {
            for line in report_lines(&data) {
                let _ = writeln!(out, "{line}");
            }
            0
        }
        Err(error) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {NAME}: error: {file}: {error}");
            2
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::run;
    use crate::evidence::Ctx;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

    /// A folder under the system's temporary folder, removed when dropped. Py: TempDir.
    struct TempDir(PathBuf);

    impl TempDir {
        fn new(name: &str) -> TempDir {
            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lazymkv-test-hit-rate-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
            TempDir(dir)
        }

        /// Py: TempDir.write (UTF-8, parent folders made).
        fn write(&self, name: &str, text: &str) -> PathBuf {
            let path = self.0.join(name);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
            path
        }
    }

    impl Drop for TempDir {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
        }
    }

    /// A recording with meta.json, lookup-status.txt and the answers given. Py: HitRate.disc.
    fn disc(tmp: &TempDir, name: &str, status: &str, hash_body: Option<&str>, id_body: Option<&str>) {
        tmp.write(&format!("{name}/meta.json"), r#"{"format": "UHD"}"#);
        tmp.write(&format!("{name}/lookup-status.txt"), status);
        if let Some(body) = hash_body {
            tmp.write(&format!("{name}/thediscdb-hash.json"), body);
        }
        if let Some(body) = id_body {
            tmp.write(&format!("{name}/thediscdb-discid.json"), body);
        }
    }

    /// The command over `dir`: (exit code, stdout, stderr). Py: quiet(hit_rate.main, dir).
    fn quiet(dir: &Path) -> (i32, String, String) {
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(dir);
        let args = vec![dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned()];
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = run(&ctx, &args, &mut out, &mut err);
        (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
    }

    /// The lines as print() writes them.
    fn printed(lines: &[&str]) -> String {
        lines.iter().map(|line| format!("{line}\n")).collect()
    }

    /// Two recordings whose every lookup answered: a hit by both, a miss by both.
    fn answered(tmp: &TempDir) {
        disc(tmp, "a", "dischash 200\ndiscid 200\n", Some(r#"{"titles": [{"index": 0}]}"#), Some(r#"[{"titles": []}]"#));
        disc(tmp, "b", "dischash 404\ndiscid 200\n", Some(r#"{"title": "Not Found"}"#), Some("[]"));
    }

        assert_eq!(code, 0, "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("TheDiscDB knows 1 of 2 discs by fingerprint"), "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("by fingerprint or disc ID: 1 of 2 discs"), "{out}");
    }

    #[test]

        let tmp = TempDir::new("failed");
        disc(&tmp, "a", "dischash 500\n", Some(r#"{"errors": "x"}"#), None);
        disc(&tmp, "b", "dischash 200\n", Some("not json"), None);
        disc(&tmp, "c", "", None, None);
        let (code, out, _) = quiet(&tmp.0);
        assert_eq!(code, 1, "{out}");
        assert!(!out.contains("hash=miss"), "{out}");

Insert at the top of `crates/dev/src/cmd/hit_rate.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]`. Python spellings: `sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if ...)` is `Tree::list` (`PathKey` order); `read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").splitlines()` and `line.split()` are Task 1's `lookup_statuses`; `json.loads(... "utf-8-sig")` is `read_json`; the answer's shape is Task 1's `thediscdb_answer`; `{x:<40}` pads by characters, as Rust's `{:<40}` does.

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev hit-rate <dir>`: experiment 10, how many recorded discs does TheDiscDB know?
//! Py: hit_rate, its lines verbatim. Exit 0 when there is a recording and every lookup answered; 1 otherwise; 2
//! where the Python crashed (no argument; the folder or a meta.json unreadable; a lookup-status.txt not UTF-8).

use crate::evidence::{Ctx, DiskTree};
use crate::usage_error;
use lazymkv_core::recording::files::{lookup_statuses, thediscdb_answer, DiscDbAnswer, Meta};
use lazymkv_core::recording::{decode_text, read_json, Encoding, Errors, Ordered, PathKey, Tree};
use std::io::Write;

/// The command's name as typed.
const NAME: &str = "hit-rate";
/// Its usage after "usage: lazymkv-dev ". The Python read sys.argv[1] and ignored any further word; so does this.
const USAGE: &str = "hit-rate <dir>";
/// A missing folder argument (the Python crashed with an IndexError).
const REQUIRED: &str = "the following arguments are required: dir";

/// How a lookup ended. Py: lookup's strings.
const HIT: &str = "hit";
const MISS: &str = "miss";
const FAILED: &str = "failed";
const NOT_MADE: &str = "n/a";

/// HTTP status per lookup, from the recorder's lookup-status.txt ({"dischash": "200"}); empty when the file cannot be
/// read (the Python's OSError); Err when it is not UTF-8 (the Python crashed). Py: hit_rate.statuses.
pub fn statuses(tree: &dyn Tree, disc: &PathKey) -> Result<Ordered<String>, String> {
    let bytes = match tree.read(&disc.join("lookup-status.txt")) {
        Ok(bytes) => bytes,
        Err(_) => return Ok(Ordered::new()),
    };
    let text = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8Sig, Errors::Strict)?;
    Ok(lookup_statuses(&text))
}

/// "hit", "miss", "failed" or "n/a" for the answer file `path` given the lookup's HTTP status. Only an answer from
/// TheDiscDB counts as a miss. Py: hit_rate.lookup.
pub fn lookup(tree: &dyn Tree, path: &PathKey, status: Option<&str>) -> &'static str {
    match status {
        // the lookup was not made, for example the disc has no disc ID
        None => NOT_MADE,
        Some("404") => MISS,
        // network error, rate limit or server error
        Some(status) if status != "200" => FAILED,
        Some(_) => match read_json::<serde_json::Value>(tree, path) {
            Err(_) => FAILED,
            Ok(value) => match thediscdb_answer(&value) {
                DiscDbAnswer::Hit => HIT,
                DiscDbAnswer::Miss => MISS,
                // a 200 answer that is not a disc record
                DiscDbAnswer::NotADisc => FAILED,
            },
        },
    }
}

/// Writes hit_rate.main's lines for the recordings directly in `root` as it goes, and returns the exit code; Err
/// where the Python crashed, after the lines written so far. Py: hit_rate.main.
pub fn report(tree: &dyn Tree, root: &PathKey, out: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<i32, String> {
    let mut rows: Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
    for disc in tree.list(root) {
        if !tree.exists(&disc.join("meta.json")) {
            continue;
        }
        let meta: Meta = read_json(tree, &disc.join("meta.json"))?;
        let status = statuses(tree, &disc)?;
        let by_hash = lookup(tree, &disc.join("thediscdb-hash.json"), status.get("dischash").map(String::as_str));
        let by_id = lookup(tree, &disc.join("thediscdb-discid.json"), status.get("discid").map(String::as_str));
        rows.push((by_hash, by_id));
        // str(meta.get('format')): the format, or "None" without one.
        let format = meta.format.as_deref().unwrap_or("None");
        let _ = writeln!(out, "{:<40} {:<7} hash={:<6} discid={}", disc.name(), format, by_hash, by_id);
    }
    let answered: Vec<&str> = rows.iter().map(|(by_hash, _)| *by_hash).filter(|by_hash| *by_hash == HIT || *by_hash == MISS).collect();
    let hits = answered.iter().filter(|by_hash| **by_hash == HIT).count();
    let unanswered = rows.len() - answered.len();
    let id_failed = rows.iter().filter(|(_, by_id)| *by_id == FAILED).count();
    let either = rows.iter().filter(|(by_hash, by_id)| *by_hash == HIT || *by_id == HIT).count();
    let _ = writeln!(out);
    let _ = writeln!(out, "TheDiscDB knows {hits} of {} discs by fingerprint", answered.len());
    let _ = writeln!(out, "by fingerprint or disc ID: {either} of {} discs", rows.len());
    if unanswered > 0 {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "{unanswered} fingerprint lookups failed or were not made; they are not counted as misses");
    }
    if id_failed > 0 {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "{id_failed} disc ID lookups failed; the combined figure may be too low");
    }
    Ok(if !rows.is_empty() && unanswered == 0 && id_failed == 0 { 0 } else { 1 })
}

/// `lazymkv-dev hit-rate <dir>`. Py: hit_rate's `sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1]))`.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    let Some(dir) = args.first() else {
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, REQUIRED);
    };
    if dir == "-h" || dir == "--help" {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "usage: lazymkv-dev {USAGE}");
        return 0;
    }
    let tree = match DiskTree::open(&ctx.abs(dir), dir) {
        Ok(tree) => tree,
        Err(error) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {NAME}: error: {dir}: {error}");
            return 2;
        }
    };
    match report(&tree, &PathKey::root(), out) {
        Ok(code) => code,
        Err(message) => {
            let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {NAME}: error: {message}");
            2
        }
    }
}

- [ ] **Step 16: Write `compare-scans`**

Insert at the top of `crates/dev/src/cmd/compare_scans.rs`, above `#[cfg(test)]`. Python spellings: `Counter` arithmetic is `counts`/`surplus` over a `BTreeMap` (`count_a - count_b` keeps positive differences, `count_a & count_b` the minima); `sorted(str(key) ...)` sorts by `python_repr` (the tuple's repr, `py_repr_str` per part, `None` for an absent attribute; Rust's `String` order is code point order); each printed key is `shown`, `pyjson::dumps` with `Style::PY_DEFAULT` per part (the deliberate change of spec 3.4); `read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")` is `decode_text(.., Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace)` (a byte-order mark stays; `robot::parse` strips it) followed by `text_mode`.

```rust
//! `lazymkv-dev compare-scans <A> <B>`: experiments 3 and 5, the title lists of two recorded scans compared by source
//! file, segment map and duration. Py: compare_scans, its lines verbatim but for one deliberate change (spec 3.4): a
//! title key is printed as `(a, b, c)` with each part written by the JSON writer ("00800.mpls", null for an absent
//! attribute), not as Python's tuple repr; the lists keep the Python's order, sorted by that repr. Exit 0 when no
//! title is on one side only; 1 when one is, or when a scan has no title; 2 where the Python crashed (fewer than two
//! arguments, a scan unreadable).

use crate::evidence::Ctx;
use crate::pyjson::{dumps, Style};
use crate::usage_error;
use lazymkv_core::recording::{decode_text, py_repr_str, Encoding, Errors};
use lazymkv_core::robot::{parse, Scan};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::io::Write;

/// The command's name as typed.
const NAME: &str = "compare-scans";
/// Its usage after "usage: lazymkv-dev ". The Python read sys.argv[1] and [2] and ignored any further word.
const USAGE: &str = "compare-scans <A> <B>";
/// The two arguments, as the usage names them.
const POSITIONALS: [&str; 2] = ["A", "B"];
/// The line a scan without titles adds.
const EMPTY_SCAN: &str = "EMPTY SCAN: a scan with no titles cannot be compared";

/// A title's key: its attributes 16 (source file), 26 (segment map) and 9 (duration), None when absent.
pub type Key = [Option<String>; 3];

/// One (key, comment) pair per title, the comment being attribute 49 ("" when absent). Py: compare_scans.titles.
pub fn titles(scan: &Scan) -> Vec<(Key, String)> {
    scan.titles
        .values()
        .map(|a| ([a.get(&16).cloned(), a.get(&26).cloned(), a.get(&9).cloned()], a.get(&49).cloned().unwrap_or_default()))
        .collect()
}

/// What compare found. Py: compare's dict.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Comparison {
    /// Keys more often in A than in B, once per surplus title, in the Python's order.
    pub only_a: Vec<Key>,
    /// Keys more often in B than in A.
    pub only_b: Vec<Key>,
    /// Keys on both sides whose sorted comment lists differ.
    pub comment_differs: Vec<Key>,
    /// Titles on both sides, each key counted as often as its smaller side has it.
    pub common: usize,
}

/// How often each key occurs. Py: Counter(key for key, _ in side).
fn counts(side: &[(Key, String)]) -> BTreeMap<Key, usize> {
    let mut counts = BTreeMap::new();
    for (key, _) in side {
        *counts.entry(key.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
    }
    counts
}

/// Each key's comments in order. Py: comments.setdefault(key, []).append(comment).
fn comments(side: &[(Key, String)]) -> BTreeMap<Key, Vec<String>> {
    let mut comments: BTreeMap<Key, Vec<String>> = BTreeMap::new();
    for (key, comment) in side {
        comments.entry(key.clone()).or_default().push(comment.clone());
    }
    comments
}

/// Every key as often as `mine` has it more than `theirs`. Py: (count_a - count_b).elements().
fn surplus(mine: &BTreeMap<Key, usize>, theirs: &BTreeMap<Key, usize>) -> Vec<Key> {
    let mut keys = Vec::new();
    for (key, n) in mine {
        let m = theirs.get(key).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        for _ in m..*n {
            keys.push(key.clone());
        }
    }
    keys
}

/// Titles are compared as multisets, so a title listed twice on one side is a difference. Py: compare_scans.compare.
pub fn compare(a: &[(Key, String)], b: &[(Key, String)]) -> Comparison {
    let (count_a, count_b) = (counts(a), counts(b));
    let (comments_a, comments_b) = (comments(a), comments(b));
    let mut only_a = surplus(&count_a, &count_b);
    let mut only_b = surplus(&count_b, &count_a);
    let mut comment_differs = Vec::new();
    for (key, mine) in &comments_a {
        if let Some(theirs) = comments_b.get(key) {
            let (mut mine, mut theirs) = (mine.clone(), theirs.clone());
            mine.sort();
            theirs.sort();
            if mine != theirs {
                comment_differs.push(key.clone());
            }
        }
    }
    let common: usize = count_a.iter().map(|(key, n)| (*n).min(count_b.get(key).copied().unwrap_or(0))).sum();
    for keys in [&mut only_a, &mut only_b, &mut comment_differs] {
        keys.sort_by_cached_key(python_repr);
    }
    Comparison { only_a, only_b, comment_differs, common }
}

/// str(key) in Python: "('00800.mpls', '1,2', '1:59:10')", None for an absent part. The order of the lists.
pub fn python_repr(key: &Key) -> String {
    let parts: Vec<String> = key.iter().map(|part| part.as_deref().map_or_else(|| "None".to_string(), py_repr_str)).collect();
    format!("({})", parts.join(", "))
}

/// A key as compare-scans prints it: "(\"00800.mpls\", \"1,2\", \"1:59:10\")", null for an absent part (spec 3.4).
pub fn shown(key: &Key) -> String {
    let parts: Vec<String> = key
        .iter()
        .map(|part| match part {
            Some(text) => dumps(&Value::String(text.clone()), Style::PY_DEFAULT),
            None => "null".to_string(),
        })
        .collect();
    format!("({})", parts.join(", "))
}

/// compare_scans.main's lines for two scans' titles, and its exit code. Py: compare_scans.main.
pub fn report_lines(a: &[(Key, String)], b: &[(Key, String)]) -> (Vec<String>, i32) {
    let result = compare(a, b);
    let mut lines = vec![format!("titles: A={} B={} common={}", a.len(), b.len(), result.common)];
    for (name, keys) in [("only in A", &result.only_a), ("only in B", &result.only_b), ("comment differs", &result.comment_differs)] {
        lines.push(format!("{name}: {}", keys.len()));
        for key in keys.iter() {
            lines.push(format!("  {}", shown(key)));
        }
    }
    if a.is_empty() || b.is_empty() {
        lines.push(EMPTY_SCAN.to_string());
        return (lines, 1);
    }
    let code = if result.only_a.is_empty() && result.only_b.is_empty() { 0 } else { 1 };
    (lines, code)
}

/// The text as Python's text-mode read hands it to robot.parse: "\r\n" and a lone "\r" become "\n".
fn text_mode(text: &str) -> String {
    text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace('\r', "\n")
}

/// A scan's titles, read as Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"). Py: compare_scans.titles.
fn read_titles(ctx: &Ctx, arg: &str) -> Result<Vec<(Key, String)>, String> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(ctx.abs(arg)).map_err(|error| format!("{arg}: {error}"))?;
    let text = decode_text(&bytes, Encoding::Utf8, Errors::Replace)?;
    Ok(titles(&parse(&text_mode(&text))))
}

/// `lazymkv-dev compare-scans <A> <B>`. Py: compare_scans' `sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]))`.
pub fn run(ctx: &Ctx, args: &[String], out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32 {
    if args.first().is_some_and(|arg| arg == "-h" || arg == "--help") {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "usage: lazymkv-dev {USAGE}");
        return 0;
    }
    if args.len() < POSITIONALS.len() {
        let message = format!("the following arguments are required: {}", POSITIONALS[args.len()..].join(", "));
        return usage_error(err, NAME, USAGE, &message);
    }
    let mut sides = Vec::new();
    for arg in &args[..2] {
        match read_titles(ctx, arg) {
            Ok(titles) => sides.push(titles),
            Err(message) => {
                let _ = writeln!(err, "lazymkv-dev {NAME}: error: {message}");
                return 2;
            }
        }
    }
    let (lines, code) = report_lines(&sides[0], &sides[1]);
    for line in lines {
        let _ = writeln!(out, "{line}");
    }
    code
}

```

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{coverage, load_scan, match_tracks, run, Row};
    use crate::evidence::Ctx;
    use lazymkv_core::recording::files::MkvmergeIdent;
    use serde_json::json;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

    /// A pinned public scan under corpus/thediscdb/movie.
    fn movie(parts: &[&str]) -> PathBuf {
        let mut path = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../corpus/thediscdb/movie");
        for part in parts {
            path.push(part);
        }
        path
    }

    /// Py: JOHN_WICK.
    fn john_wick() -> PathBuf {
        movie(&["John Wick (2014)", "4k-ultra-hd--blu-ray", "disc01.txt"])
    }

    /// Py: KNOWING.
    fn knowing() -> PathBuf {
        movie(&["Knowing (2009)", "2010-dvd", "disc01.txt"])
    }

    /// A stand-in for `mkvmerge -J`: tracks are (type, language, audio channels or None). Py: ident.
    fn ident(tracks: &[(&str, &str, Option<i64>)]) -> MkvmergeIdent {
        let tracks: Vec<serde_json::Value> = tracks
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(id, (kind, lang, ch))| {
                let mut properties = serde_json::Map::new();
                properties.insert("language".to_string(), json!(lang));
                if let Some(ch) = ch {
                    properties.insert("audio_channels".to_string(), json!(ch));
                }
                json!({"id": id, "type": kind, "codec": "x", "properties": properties})
            })
            .collect();
        serde_json::from_value(json!({ "tracks": tracks })).unwrap()
    }

    /// (tag, scan stream) of every row. Py: tags.
    fn tags(rows: &[Row]) -> Vec<(&'static str, Option<u32>)> {
        rows.iter().map(|(tag, r, _)| (tag.as_str(), r.as_ref().map(|r| r.stream))).collect()
    }

    /// A folder under the system's temporary folder, removed when dropped.
    struct TempDir(PathBuf);

    impl TempDir {
        fn new(name: &str) -> TempDir {
            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lazymkv-test-exp11-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
            TempDir(dir)
        }

        fn write(&self, name: &str, text: &str) {
            let path = self.0.join(name);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
        }
    }

    impl Drop for TempDir {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
        }
    }

    /// The made-up recording folder `m`: title 0 (1:30:00) with video, two English audio streams (the second a core,
    /// flag 256) and English and French subtitles; title 1 (0:05:00) with no stream. eng-only kept video, the
    /// TrueHD stream and the French subtitles; all-tracks is a rip of title 0 with every stream.
    fn write_m(tmp: &TempDir) {
        tmp.write(
            "m/scan.txt",
            "TINFO:0,9,0,\"1:30:00\"\nTINFO:1,9,0,\"0:05:00\"\n\
             SINFO:0,0,1,6201,\"Video\"\nSINFO:0,0,6,0,\"MpegH\"\nSINFO:0,0,28,0,\"eng\"\n\
             SINFO:0,1,1,6202,\"Audio\"\nSINFO:0,1,3,0,\"eng\"\nSINFO:0,1,6,0,\"TrueHD\"\nSINFO:0,1,14,0,\"8\"\n\
             SINFO:0,2,1,6202,\"Audio\"\nSINFO:0,2,3,0,\"eng\"\nSINFO:0,2,6,0,\"DD\"\nSINFO:0,2,14,0,\"2\"\nSINFO:0,2,22,0,\"256\"\n\
             SINFO:0,3,1,6203,\"Subtitles\"\nSINFO:0,3,3,0,\"eng\"\nSINFO:0,3,6,0,\"PGS\"\n\
             SINFO:0,4,1,6203,\"Subtitles\"\nSINFO:0,4,3,0,\"fra\"\nSINFO:0,4,6,0,\"PGS\"\n",
        );
        tmp.write(
            "m/eng-only/mkvmerge.json",
            r#"{"tracks": [
 {"id": 0, "type": "video", "codec": "HEVC/H.265/MPEG-H", "properties": {"language": "und", "forced_track": false}},
 {"id": 1, "type": "audio", "codec": "TrueHD Atmos", "properties": {"language": "eng", "audio_channels": 8, "forced_track": false, "tag_number_of_bytes": "1234", "track_name": "Main mix"}},
 {"id": 2, "type": "subtitles", "codec": "HDMV PGS", "properties": {"language": "fra"}}
]}
"#,
        );
        tmp.write(
            "m/all-tracks/mkvmerge.json",
            r#"{"tracks": [
 {"id": 0, "type": "video", "codec": "HEVC/H.265/MPEG-H", "properties": {"language": "und"}},
 {"id": 1, "type": "audio", "codec": "TrueHD Atmos", "properties": {"language": "eng", "audio_channels": 8}},
 {"id": 2, "type": "audio", "codec": "AC-3", "properties": {"language": "eng", "audio_channels": 2}},
 {"id": 3, "type": "subtitles", "codec": "HDMV PGS", "properties": {"language": "eng"}},
 {"id": 4, "type": "subtitles", "codec": "HDMV PGS", "properties": {"language": "fre", "track_name": "it's"}}
]}
"#,
        );
        tmp.write("m/all-tracks/rip-summary.json", "{\"ok\": true, \"title\": 0}\n");
    }

    /// The command with `cwd` as the current directory: (exit code, stdout, stderr).
    fn run_in(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> (i32, String, String) {
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(cwd);
        let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect();
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = run(&ctx, &args, &mut out, &mut err);
        (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
    }

    /// The lines as print() writes them.
    fn printed(lines: &[&str]) -> String {
        lines.iter().map(|line| format!("{line}\n")).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn coverage_a_uhd_with_only_english_audio_tests_neither_special_nor_nolang() {
        let n = coverage(&load_scan(&john_wick()).unwrap(), 0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            n,
            vec![("audio-lang", 0), ("nolang", 0), ("sub-lang", 2), ("core", 1), ("special", 0), ("sub-flagged", 0), ("audio-512", 0)]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn coverage_a_dvd_with_a_flagged_commentary_tests_special() {
        let n = coverage(&load_scan(&knowing()).unwrap(), 0).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            n,
            vec![("audio-lang", 1), ("nolang", 0), ("sub-lang", 2), ("core", 0), ("special", 1), ("sub-flagged", 2), ("audio-512", 0)]
        );
    }

    // Knowing, title 0: 0 video; audio 1 eng 6ch, 2 spa 6ch, 3 eng 2ch flag 1; subtitles 4 eng, 5 spa, 6 eng flag 1,
    // 7 spa flag 1. The eng prediction keeps 0, 1, 4 and 6. Py: Match.

    #[test]
    fn match_a_file_as_predicted_has_no_difference() {
        let scan = load_scan(&knowing()).unwrap();
        let file = ident(&[("video", "und", None), ("audio", "eng", Some(6)), ("subtitles", "eng", None), ("subtitles", "eng", None)]);
        let rows = match_tracks(&scan, 0, &file).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(tags(&rows), vec![("predicted", Some(0)), ("predicted", Some(1)), ("predicted", Some(4)), ("predicted", Some(6))]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn match_a_kept_commentary_and_a_dropped_subtitle_are_named() {
        let scan = load_scan(&knowing()).unwrap();
        let file = ident(&[("video", "und", None), ("audio", "eng", Some(6)), ("audio", "eng", Some(2)), ("subtitles", "eng", None)]);
        let rows = match_tracks(&scan, 0, &file).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            tags(&rows),
            vec![("predicted", Some(0)), ("predicted", Some(1)), ("EXTRA", Some(3)), ("predicted", Some(4)), ("MISSING", Some(6))]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn match_a_track_out_of_scan_order_is_unmatched() {
        let scan = load_scan(&knowing()).unwrap();
        let file = ident(&[("video", "und", None), ("subtitles", "eng", None), ("audio", "eng", Some(6))]);
        let rows = match_tracks(&scan, 0, &file).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            tags(&rows),
            vec![("predicted", Some(0)), ("MISSING", Some(1)), ("predicted", Some(4)), ("UNMATCHED", None), ("MISSING", Some(6))]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn exp11_match_prints_the_pythons_lines() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("match");
        write_m(&tmp);
        let (code, out, err) = run_in(&tmp.0, &["match", "m", "0", "eng-only"]);

    #[test]
    fn exp11_a_title_the_scan_does_not_list_exits_1() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("unlisted");

        assert_eq!(run_in(&tmp.0, &["coverage", "m@7", "m"]), (1, String::new(), "m: the scan lists no title 7\n".to_string()));

        assert_eq!(run_in(&tmp.0, &["match", "./m/", "3", "eng-only"]), (1, String::new(), "m/scan.txt lists no title 3\n".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(run_in(&tmp.0, &["match", "m", "-1", "no-such-label"]), (1, String::new(), "m/scan.txt lists no title -1\n".to_string()));
        // Where the Python crashed: a title word that is not a number, a label without mkvmerge.json.
        assert_eq!(run_in(&tmp.0, &["coverage", "m@x"]).0, 2);

    #[test]
    fn exp11_reads_its_arguments_as_argparse_did() {
        let tmp = TempDir::new("args");
        let top = "usage: lazymkv-dev exp11 [-h] {coverage,match} ...\n";
        let cases: [(&[&str], String); 6] = [
            (&[], format!("{top}lazymkv-dev exp11: error: the following arguments are required: command\n")),
            (
                &["bogus"],
                format!("{top}lazymkv-dev exp11: error: argument command: invalid choice: 'bogus' (choose from 'coverage', 'match')\n"),
            ),
            (
                &["coverage"],
                "usage: lazymkv-dev exp11 coverage [-h] where [where ...]\n\
                 lazymkv-dev exp11 coverage: error: the following arguments are required: where\n"
                    .to_string(),
            ),
            (
                &["match", "a"],
                "usage: lazymkv-dev exp11 match [-h] folder title label\n\
                 lazymkv-dev exp11 match: error: the following arguments are required: title, label\n"
                    .to_string(),
            ),
            (
                &["match", "a", "x", "b"],
                "usage: lazymkv-dev exp11 match [-h] folder title label\n\
                 lazymkv-dev exp11 match: error: argument title: invalid int value: 'x'\n"
                    .to_string(),
            ),
            (&["match", "a", "1", "b", "c"], format!("{top}lazymkv-dev exp11: error: unrecognized arguments: c\n")),
        ];
        for (args, stderr) in cases {
            assert_eq!(run_in(&tmp.0, args), (2, String::new(), stderr), "{args:?}");
        }
        let (code, out, err) = run_in(&tmp.0, &["-h"]);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
        assert!(out.starts_with(&format!("{top}\nExperiment 11 (spec section 17, row 11)")), "{out}");
        let (code, out, _) = run_in(&tmp.0, &["match", "a", "-h"]);
        assert_eq!(code, 0);
        assert!(out.starts_with("usage: lazymkv-dev exp11 match [-h] folder title label\n"), "{out}");
    }
}
