````markdown
# Goldens of the Rust port

The files in this folder and in every `<slug>/golden/` folder are the acceptance tests of lazymkv's Rust port of the
phase 0 analysers (the port design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-rust-port-design.md` in the lazymkv
repository, section 5). `write_goldens.py`, beside this file, wrote them once from the phase 0 Python: the
`scripts/phase0/*.py` of the lazymkv commit the `written_by` block below names, run on the Mac with Python 3.9.6, with
this repository cloned at `corpus/owner/`, the level series of every `audio-levels-20ms-*` folder present (the
git-ignored side files), and the OCR text and one audio proxy copied from the tuning dataset into a temporary folder
that was deleted right after. `lazymkv-dev golden check` recomputes every golden with the Rust and compares;
`lazymkv-dev golden write` writes the same files from the Rust, for a re-recording only (see "Re-recording a golden").
The goldens hold numbers, verdicts, classes, roles and report lines: no subtitle text, no drive line, no scan message,
no machine user name, no token and no unit-key content.

## Checking

    lazymkv-dev golden check [--evidence DIR] [--text DIR]

`--text DIR` (or the environment variable `LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT`) names a folder laid out as `tuning-fetch.ps1` copies
from the tuning dataset: `DIR/<slug>/<label>/subs-ocr/sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl` (with `-Text`) and
`DIR/<slug>/<label>/audio-proxy.mka` with its `audio-proxy.json`. Every comparison prints one line, `<golden>: pass`,
`<golden>: fail: <the first differences>` or `<golden>: skipped: <reason>`, and the last line counts them:
`golden check: <p> pass, <f> fail, <s> skipped`. The exit status is 1 when one fails, 3 when none passed or failed
(nothing could run), else 0. A comparison is skipped, with its reason, when its input is absent: the evidence clone
(`no evidence clone at <dir>`), a recording's `golden/` folder (`no golden/ folder for <slug>`), a rip label's golden
folder or a golden file (`not covered: ...`), a level folder's level series (the Python's line `<slug>/<label>/<folder>:
its level files are not here (git keeps only streams.json): pull the recording or copy the folder from the dataset
share`), a title's OCR text (`no OCR text: <path> (give --text DIR or LAZYMKV_OCR_TEXT)`), `ffmpeg` or `ffprobe`
(`ffmpeg is not on PATH`), the golden's `ffmpeg` (`ffmpeg is <first line of ffmpeg -version>, the golden was written
by <that line then>`), or the golden's proxy (`the proxy is not fetched: <path>`, or `the proxy <path> has SHA-1 <x>,
the golden was written from <y>`). `cargo test -p lazymkv-dev --test golden` runs the same comparisons and prints
every skip as a `skipped: <reason>` line.

## How each file is compared

- A JSON golden is parsed and compared structurally with the Rust's value: objects as sets of keys, arrays in order,
  every float within 1e-9 of the golden's and the floats under an `smi` or `rev_smi` key within 1e-6 (port spec
  section 4), an int never equal to a float, strings, booleans and `null` exactly. The Python's `NaN` is written as
  `null`.
- A text golden (`.txt`) is compared line by line, byte for byte. Every line, the last too, ends with `LF`.
- `golden/retune-report.txt` is compared line by line, except three lines that state the measure cache and the
  baseline, not the rule: the line beginning `measures: `, the line beginning `snapshot: `, and the parenthesis of
  `Changes since the previous snapshot (...):`. The line count must match.
- `<slug>/golden/proxy-<folder>/`: every file but `golden.json` byte for byte against the folder
  `lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy` writes from the same proxy, with the same `ffmpeg`. `proxy.txt` (it names a path)
  and `ffmpeg.txt` (ffmpeg's own messages) are neither kept nor compared.
- `audio-dataset.json`, the harness baseline beside this folder, is not a golden but the other side of the round
  trip of port spec section 5: the snapshot the Rust harness makes from this repository is compared structurally with
  it, as a JSON golden is, ignoring `format`, `created`, `code`, `tracks[].key` and `tracks[].peer.key`, with
  `measures_cache` compared as a multiset of measures (the cache key's formula changed with the port, RP5).
- `golden/README.md`, this file: its `written_by` block must parse.

## The files

Every golden belongs to one recording, `<slug>/golden/`, except `golden/retune-report.txt`. A rip label is a folder
of the recording (not `golden/`) with a `rip-summary.json`, else an `extract-summary.json`, saying `"ok": true` and
naming an int title, and with an `mkvmerge.json`; its selection is `eng` when the summary's profile file name is
`eng-only.mmcp.xml`, else `all`. A level folder is a rip label's `audio-levels-20ms-*` folder (the first
measurement's `audio-levels-<main>-<cand>` folders are not). Paths printed inside a golden begin `corpus/owner/`.
JSON goldens are `json.dumps(value, indent=1)` and a newline, ASCII.

`<slug>/golden/scan.json`, for a recording with a `scan.txt`: the parsed scan without its `DRV` and `MSG` lines (Rust
`core::robot::ScanJson`). `scan.txt` is read as UTF-8, invalid bytes replaced.

```json
{"titles": {"<title>": {"<attribute>": "<value>"}},
 "streams": {"<title>,<stream>": {"<attribute>": "<value>"}},
 "disc": {"<attribute>": "<value>"},
 "duration_seconds": {"<title>": "<seconds of attribute 9 (int), or null when it is absent, not H:MM:SS or negative>"}}
```

`<slug>/golden/titles.txt`, for a recording with a `scan.txt`: the lines of `lazymkv-dev titles <slug>` (the Python's
`audio_similarity.py --titles`).

`<slug>/golden/labels.json`, for every recording: the lines `lazymkv-dev labels check corpus/owner/<slug>` prints, its
exit code, and for every labelled track of the recording's `audio-labels.json` (file order, when the file validates)
why its label does not count for experiment 13 (`""` when it counts), with the fitted set of spec section 17 row 13
and `audio-fitted.json` (Rust `core::audio::labels::LabelsJson`).

```json
{"check": ["<line>"], "exit_code": "<0 or 2>",
 "tracks": [{"label": "<label>", "stream": "<int>", "kind": "<kind>", "how": "<how>", "not_counted_because": "<text>"}]}
```

`<slug>/golden/<label>/reconcile.json`, for every rip label: everything `lazymkv-dev reconcile` computes for the rip
(the Python's `compare_tracks.py corpus/owner/<slug>/scan.txt <title> corpus/owner/<slug>/<label>/mkvmerge.json
--selection <selection>`, its rip log found beside `mkvmerge.json`), as data (Rust `core::reconcile::Report`).

```json
{"title": "<int>", "selection": "<all or eng>", "rip_log": "<corpus/owner/<slug>/<label>/rip.txt, or null>",
 "want": ["<row>"], "dropped": ["<row>"], "unknown_removed": ["<int>"],
 "got": [{"id": "<int>", "type": "<text>", "lang": "<text>", "lang_raw": "<text>", "codec": "<text>",
          "ch": "<int or empty text>", "tags": ["<text>"]}],
 "verdicts": {"count": "<bool>", "order": "<bool>", "video": "<bool>", "chapters": "<bool>", "duration": "<bool>"},
 "numbers": {"scan_chapters": "<int>", "file_chapters": "<int>", "scan_seconds": "<int>", "file_seconds": "<float>"},
 "video_tracks": "<int>", "statistics_tags": "<bool>", "exit_code": "<0 or 1>"}
```

A `want` or `dropped` row is `{"stream", "type", "lang", "lang_raw", "codec", "out", "ch", "flags"}` as the Python
builds it (`type` null when the stream has no attribute 1).

`<slug>/golden/<label>/audio-<folder>.json`, for every level folder of a rip label (`<folder>` is the level folder's
whole name, so the file is `audio-audio-levels-20ms-1-2.json`): the folder measured with the default rule and
constants and no cache (Rust `core::audio::report::FolderJson`).

```json
{"folder": "<level folder name>", "main": {"<manifest key>": "<value>"}, "frames": "<int>",
 "dialogue": "<fc or mix>", "veto": {"holds": "<true, false or null>", "why": "<text>"}, "veto_line": "<report line>",
 "candidates": [{"stream": "<text>", "duplicate_of": "<text or null>", "verdict": "<verdict>", "not_judged": "<text>",
                 "cross_language": "<text>", "before_veto": "<verdict or null>", "measures": "<measures or null>",
                 "reverse": "<measures or null>", "swapped": "<measures or null>", "swapped_verdict": "<verdict or null>",
                 "peer": "<null, or {stream, measures, verdict}>"}]}
```

Measures are the Python's dict: `frames`, `lag_ms`, `r_global`, `overlap`, `main_silent`, `dc`, `gain_db`, `gap_s`,
`ag`, `ag_s`, `adl`, `tenths`, `tenths_comm`, `tenths_ad`, `smi`, `smi_windows`, `ls_db`, `added_s`, then `rev_error`
and the 15 `rev_` keys; `{"frames", "error"}` for a pair too short to measure. `reverse` is the reverse run alone (the 15
keys without `rev_`), `swapped` the pair with the roles exchanged (the forward run as the `rev_` block), each `null`
when the measures carry none, `{"error"}` when the reverse run had one.

`<slug>/golden/<label>/audio-<folder>.txt`: the lines of `lazymkv-dev audio-report corpus/owner/<slug>/<label>/<folder>`
(the Python's `audio_similarity.py <folder>`) for the same measures. The `audio-content-20ms-*.txt` files beside the
level folders predate the veto line and the long reverse form; they are not compared.

`<slug>/golden/<label>/subs.json` and `subs.txt`, for every rip label with a `subs/index.json` and a `subs-ocr/` folder:
the run of `lazymkv-dev subs --rec corpus/owner/<slug>/<label> --text <the title's OCR text>` (the Python's
`subtitle_text.py`), the original language from the recording's `tmdb.json`. `subs.txt` holds its printed lines.
`subs.json` holds its numbers and decisions only, never an event's features, words or word pairs (Rust
`core::subtitle::text::SubsJson`):

```json
{"reading": "subs-ocr", "exit_code": 0, "orig_lang": "<code or null>",
 "streams": [{"n": "<int>", "tag": "<text>", "codec": "<text or null>", "forced": "<bool>", "events": "<int>",
              "status": "<read, set aside or not read>", "pairing": "<text or null>", "m": "<measures or null>",
              "decide": "<null, or {role, review, note}>", "spec87": "<text or null>", "before_yes": "<text or null>"}],
 "pairs": [{"a": "<int>", "b": "<int>", "aligned": ["<float>", "<float>"], "cb": ["<float or null>", "<float or null>"],
            "uc": ["<int>", "<int>"], "timing": "<same, diff or between>", "content": "<same, different, partial or unknown>",
            "subset": "<s<a> in s<b>, s<b> in s<a>, or no>"}],
 "text_sha1": {"sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl": "<SHA-1 of the text file read>"}}
```

`m` is the measure's dict of the Python (`events`, `text_events`, `lines`, `words`, `note_only`, `letter_events`,
`wordlike`, `readable`, `lang`, `shares`, `caps_share`, `caps_style`, `CUE`, `LABEL`, `CHEV`, `M`, `SO`, `CS`, `rate`,
`CAPS_CUE`, `NOTE`, `NOTE_LOOSE`, `ODD`, `corrections`, `class`, `why`) for a stream whose text was read; `before_yes`
is the outcome until experiment 14 answers yes, for a stream both `decide` and `spec87` give. The `subtitle-text.txt`
files beside the rips are older runs of the same script; they are not compared.

`<slug>/golden/<label>/align.json`, for every rip label with a `subs/` folder: the table of `lazymkv-dev align
--subs-dir corpus/owner/<slug>/<label>/subs` (the Python's `subtitle_alignment.py`) with its defaults, as numbers
(Rust `core::subtitle::align::AlignJson`).

```json
{"clear_max_bytes": 64, "tolerance_ms": 300, "exit_code": "<0 or 2>", "error": "<text or null>",
 "streams": [{"name": "<s<n>-<lang>-<text or image>[-forced]>", "codec": "<text or null>", "track_name": "<text or null>",
              "packets": "<int>", "buckets": ["<int>", "<int>", "<int>", "<int>"], "events": "<int>"}],
 "matrix": [["<aligned(row, column), unrounded>"]], "pairs": [{"a": "<name>", "b": "<name>", "larger": "<float>"}]}
```

`<slug>/golden/proxy-<folder>/`, for one level folder (`short-circuit-1986-dvd/all-tracks/audio-levels-20ms-1-2`):
`manifest.txt`, the level files and `streams.json` that `lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy` writes (the Python's
`proxy_levels.py`) from the title's `audio-proxy.mka` in the tuning dataset, for the folder's main stream and
candidates, and `golden.json` (Rust `ProxyGolden`):

```json
{"slug": "<slug>", "label": "<label>", "folder": "<level folder name>", "main": "<int>", "cands": ["<int>"],
 "ffmpeg_version": "<first line of ffmpeg -version>", "proxy_sha1": "<SHA-1 of audio-proxy.mka>"}
```

`golden/retune-report.txt`: the report of `lazymkv-dev retune` (the Python's `audio_dataset.py`) over this repository,
written without replacing the baseline. Its lines are the Python's, byte for byte, but for the snapshot line, whose
path is written `$TMPDIR/lazymkv-golden-retune.json`, and the lines of port spec 3.4 that name a script or a code hash,
which are written as lazymkv-dev prints them:

| The Python printed | The golden holds |
|---|---|
| `    python3 scripts/phase0/audio_labels.py set corpus/owner/...` (the To-label hint) | `    lazymkv-dev labels set corpus/owner/...` |
| ``... with the reference that `audio_dataset.py args` prints, ...`` (a wrong reference's FAIL line) | ``... with the reference that `lazymkv-dev levels-args` prints, ...`` |
| `... (proxy_levels.py writes streams.json from audio-proxy.json, ...` (a folder without streams.json) | `... (lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy writes streams.json from audio-proxy.json, ...` |
| `rule: audio_similarity.py <12 hex digits>, ...` | `rule: version 1, ...` |
| `Changes since the previous snapshot (<created>, code <12 hex digits>):` | the same: a v2 previous snapshot prints its code hash in the Rust too, and the parenthesis is not compared |

## Provenance

`write_goldens.py` fills the block below: the lazymkv pull request of the port, the branch commit whose
`scripts/phase0` it imported and that folder's tree hash, the commit of this repository the inputs are at, the
versions of Python and `ffmpeg`, and the SHA-1 of every input (a path below this repository; the OCR text and the
proxy by their path below the `--text` folder, whose layout is the same).

```json written_by
{"pull_request": 0, "branch_commit": "", "scripts_phase0_tree": "", "evidence_commit": "", "python": "", "ffmpeg": "", "inputs": {}}
```

## Re-recording a golden

A golden changes only in a commit of this repository that does nothing else and whose message names the goldens, the
reason and the lazymkv commit that makes the change. A port mistake is never re-recorded: the Rust is fixed. A
deliberate change of a measure, a threshold, a verdict or a report line (`RULE_VERSION` bumped where a measure or a
threshold changes) re-records the goldens it changes, and only those: `lazymkv-dev golden write --text <DIR>` writes
every golden from the Rust; keep the ones the change explains, restore every other (`git checkout -- <path>`), and
keep each replaced Python file beside its successor as `<file>.python` (a proxy folder as `proxy-<folder>.python/`),
which no check reads. Add a line to the list below for every re-recorded file. The `written_by` block stays the
Python's.

Re-recorded since the Python wrote them: none.

## Writing them again from the Python, and the checks before a commit here

The plan of the port (lazymkv `docs/superpowers/plans/`, Task 14) gives the steps: fetch the OCR text of every rip
label with a `subs-ocr/` folder (`tuning-fetch.ps1 -Text`) and the proxy of `short-circuit-1986-dvd/all-tracks`
(`tuning-fetch.ps1`) into a new temporary folder `TEXT`, re-run `audio_dataset.py` and commit the baseline here if it
changed, then, from the lazymkv checkout:

    python3 -B corpus/owner/golden/write_goldens.py --text "$TEXT" --pull-request <N>

Before the commit, each of these prints nothing (run from the lazymkv checkout, after
`git -C corpus/owner add -A -- golden ':(glob)*/golden/**'`; the user names come from `scripts/phase0/box.env` and
`id -un`, never typed; `echo "${#u}"` prints the length of the first, which must not be 0):

    u="$(. scripts/phase0/box.env && printf '%s' "${LAZYMKV_BOX%%@*}")"; echo "${#u}"
    git -C corpus/owner grep --cached -nia -F -e "$u"
    git -C corpus/owner grep --cached -nia -F -e "$(id -un)"
    git -C corpus/owner grep --cached -nIE '(BU40N 1\.03|BDR-XS07U 1\.01) [^"]' -- golden ':(glob)*/golden/**'
    git -C corpus/owner grep --cached -nE 'eyJhbGciOi[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|"(fs|bigrams|text)":|"(lines|words)": \[' -- golden ':(glob)*/golden/**'
    find corpus/owner -iname '*unit_key*'
    git -C corpus/owner ls-files --cached -- ':(glob)**/*.ocr.jsonl' ':(glob)**/ocrs-s*[0-9].jsonl'

Then `rm -rf "$TEXT"` once `lazymkv-dev golden check --text "$TEXT"` has run: subtitle text never stays on the Mac.
````

- [ ] **Step 11: Write `golden/write_goldens.py` in the evidence repository**

Create `corpus/owner/golden/write_goldens.py` with exactly this content (Python 3.9 standard library, ASCII only). It lives beside the goldens it writes, so their provenance does not depend on how the `lazymkv` pull request is merged, and it is never part of the `lazymkv` repository.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Writes the goldens of lazymkv's Rust port from the phase 0 Python (port spec section 5; README.md beside this file).

Run once, on the Mac, with Python 3.9:

    python3 -B corpus/owner/golden/write_goldens.py --text TEXT --pull-request N

corpus/owner/ is this evidence repository, cloned in a lazymkv checkout whose scripts/phase0/ still holds the Python
(the rust-port branch before the port deletes it). Every audio-levels-20ms-* folder must hold its level series (the
git-ignored side files: pull the recordings first). TEXT is a temporary folder holding what tuning-fetch.ps1 copied
from the tuning dataset: TEXT/<slug>/<label>/subs-ocr/sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl for every rip label that has a subs-ocr/
folder here (tuning-fetch.ps1 -Text), and TEXT/<slug>/<label>/audio-proxy.mka with its audio-proxy.json for the
--proxy title (tuning-fetch.ps1). This script fetches nothing and changes no input. It imports the phase 0 modules
from scripts/phase0 (never a copy), writes every file README.md lists into <slug>/golden/ and golden/, and fills
README.md's written_by block. It refuses to start when an input is missing, when scripts/phase0 has uncommitted
changes, or when this repository has changes outside the goldens; any other failure ends in a traceback, which is a
finding to report, not to work around. No golden holds subtitle text, a drive line, a scan message, a machine user
name, a token or unit-key content.
Python 3.9 standard library. ASCII only.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import io
import json
import math
import os
import pathlib
import platform
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from contextlib import redirect_stdout

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent  # corpus/owner/golden of a lazymkv checkout
ROOT = HERE.parents[2]                          # that checkout
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts" / "phase0"))
try:
    import audio_dataset as dataset
    import audio_labels as labels
    import audio_similarity as sim
    import compare_tracks
    import proxy_levels
    import robot
    import subtitle_alignment as align
    import subtitle_text as st
except ImportError as error:
    sys.exit("write_goldens.py: %s: scripts/phase0 of %s holds no phase 0 Python; check out the branch commit "
             "README.md names (the port deletes the Python after the goldens are written)" % (error, ROOT))

CORPUS = pathlib.Path("corpus") / "owner"  # relative to ROOT, the working folder: every path a golden prints begins so
OUT = CORPUS                               # where the goldens are written
GOLDEN = "golden"                          # the folder name reserved for goldens
READING = "subs-ocr"                       # the OCR reading tuning-fetch.ps1 -Text copies
RULE_VERSION = 1                           # core::audio::rule::RULE_VERSION when the goldens were written
PROXY = "short-circuit-1986-dvd/all-tracks/audio-levels-20ms-1-2"
SNAPSHOT_SHOWN = "$TMPDIR/lazymkv-golden-retune.json"
ALIGN_CLEAR_MAX_BYTES = 64                 # subtitle_alignment.py's --clear-max-bytes default
ALIGN_TOLERANCE_MS = 300                   # subtitle_alignment.py's --tolerance-ms default
LEVEL_INPUTS = ("manifest.txt", "main-mix.txt", "main-fc.txt", "streams.json", "audio-proxy.json")
# Port spec 3.4: the retune report's lines that name a command or a code hash, as lazymkv-dev prints them. The fifth,
# "Changes since the previous snapshot (<created>, code <sha>):", keeps its form: a v2 previous snapshot prints the
# code hash in the Rust too, and golden check does not compare its parenthesis.
REWRITES = (
    (re.compile(r"^    python3 scripts/phase0/audio_labels\.py set "), "    lazymkv-dev labels set "),
    (re.compile(r"`audio_dataset\.py args`"), "`lazymkv-dev levels-args`"),
    (re.compile(r"\(proxy_levels\.py writes streams\.json "), "(lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy writes streams.json "),
    (re.compile(r"^rule: audio_similarity\.py [0-9a-f]{12}, "), "rule: version %d, " % RULE_VERSION),
)
WRITTEN_BY = re.compile(r"(^```json written_by\n)(.*?)(^```$)", re.S | re.M)


def fail(message):
    sys.exit("write_goldens.py: " + message)


def run(args, cwd):
    """The standard output of a command that must succeed."""
    p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        fail("%s: exit %d: %s" % (" ".join(args), p.returncode, p.stderr.strip()[:300]))
    return p.stdout


def sha1(path):
    return hashlib.sha1(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def plain(value):
    """value as a golden holds it: NaN as null and tuples as lists, at every level."""
    if isinstance(value, float) and math.isnan(value):
        return None
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(k): plain(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [plain(v) for v in value]
    return value


def write_bytes(path, data):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(data)
    print("wrote %s (%d bytes)" % (path, len(data)))


def write_json(path, value):
    """json.dumps(value, indent=1) and a newline, ASCII: the form lazymkv-dev golden write writes too."""
    write_bytes(path, (json.dumps(plain(value), indent=1, allow_nan=False) + "\n").encode("ascii"))


def write_lines(path, lines):
    """Every line followed by a newline, UTF-8."""
    write_bytes(path, "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines).encode("utf-8"))


def golden_path(path):
    """True for a path (as git status prints it) that this script writes."""
    return path.startswith(GOLDEN + "/") or re.match(r"[^/]+/%s/" % GOLDEN, path) is not None


def recordings():
    """The recording folders, in name order: every slug folder but golden/."""
    return sorted(p.name for p in CORPUS.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and p.name != GOLDEN and labels.SLUG.match(p.name))


def rip_labels(slug):
    """[(label, title, selection)]: every folder (not golden/) with a rip-summary.json, else an extract-summary.json,
    saying "ok": true and naming an int title, and with an mkvmerge.json; the selection is eng when the profile's file
    name (after the last backslash: a Windows path) is eng-only.mmcp.xml, else all (port spec 3.3)."""
    out = []
    for d in sorted(p for p in (CORPUS / slug).iterdir() if p.is_dir() and p.name != GOLDEN):
        summary = None
        for name in ("rip-summary.json", "extract-summary.json"):
            try:
                data = json.loads((d / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
            except (OSError, ValueError):
                continue
            if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("ok") is True:
                summary = data
                break
        if summary is None or not (d / "mkvmerge.json").is_file():
            continue
        title = summary.get("title")
        if not isinstance(title, int) or isinstance(title, bool):
            continue
        profile = str(summary.get("profile") or "")
        out.append((d.name, title, "eng" if profile.rsplit("\\", 1)[-1] == "eng-only.mmcp.xml" else "all"))
    return out


def level_folders(slug, label):
    return sorted(f for f in (CORPUS / slug / label).glob("audio-levels-20ms-*") if f.is_dir())


def needs_text(slug, label):
    """Whether the rip label has subtitle goldens: a subs/index.json and an OCR reading folder here."""
    d = CORPUS / slug / label
    return (d / "subs" / "index.json").is_file() and (d / READING).is_dir()


def preflight(text_root, proxy):
    if sys.version_info[:2] != (3, 9):
        fail("Python %s: the goldens are written by Python 3.9, which the phase 0 analysers ran on"
             % platform.python_version())
    if run(["git", "status", "--porcelain", "--", "scripts/phase0"], ROOT).strip():
        fail("scripts/phase0 has uncommitted changes: the goldens must come from a committed tree")
    dirty = [line for line in run(["git", "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all"], CORPUS).splitlines()
             if not golden_path(line[3:])]
    if dirty:
        fail("this repository has changes outside the goldens; commit them first: " + "; ".join(dirty))
    for slug, label, folder in dataset.find_folders(CORPUS):
        if not (folder / "manifest.txt").is_file():
            fail("%s/%s/%s: its level files are not here (git keeps only streams.json): pull the recording or copy "
                 "the folder from the dataset share" % (slug, label, folder.name))
    for slug in recordings():
        for label, _, _ in rip_labels(slug):
            reading = text_root / slug / label / READING
            if needs_text(slug, label) and not sorted(reading.glob("sub-*.ocr.jsonl")):
                fail("%s holds no sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl: fetch the OCR text of %s/%s with tuning-fetch.ps1 -Text"
                     % (reading, slug, label))
    slug, label, name = proxy.split("/")
    if not (CORPUS / slug / label / name / "manifest.txt").is_file():
        fail("%s: no such level folder (--proxy)" % proxy)
    for file_name in ("audio-proxy.mka", "audio-proxy.json"):
        if not (text_root / slug / label / file_name).is_file():
            fail("%s is missing: fetch the proxy of %s/%s with tuning-fetch.ps1"
                 % (text_root / slug / label / file_name, slug, label))
    if shutil.which("ffprobe") is None:
        fail("ffprobe is not on PATH")


def ffmpeg_version():
    try:
        printed = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-version"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    except FileNotFoundError:
        fail("ffmpeg is not on PATH")
    return (printed.splitlines() or [""])[0]


def scan_golden(slug):
    """scan.json: robot.parse's titles, streams and disc and every title's duration; no drive line, no message."""
    scan = robot.parse((CORPUS / slug / "scan.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))

    def attrs(a):
        return {str(k): a[k] for k in sorted(a)}

    def seconds(a):
        if 9 not in a:
            return None
        try:
            total = robot.duration_seconds(a[9])
        except ValueError:
            return None
        return total if total >= 0 else None

    return {"titles": {str(t): attrs(scan.titles[t]) for t in sorted(scan.titles)},
            "streams": {"%d,%d" % key: attrs(scan.streams[key]) for key in sorted(scan.streams)},
            "disc": attrs(scan.disc),
            "duration_seconds": {str(t): seconds(scan.titles[t]) for t in sorted(scan.titles)}}


def labels_golden(slug, fitted):
    """labels.json: audio_labels.py check of the recording, and why each labelled track does not count ('' when it
    does), with the fitted set of spec row 13 and audio-fitted.json."""
    root = CORPUS / slug
    check, bad = [], 0
    own = root / "audio-labels.json"
    files = [own] if own.exists() else sorted(root.glob("*/audio-labels.json"))
    if not files:
        check.append("%s: no audio-labels.json" % root)
    for path in files:
        try:
            data = labels.load(path)
            check.append("ok %s (%d tracks, %d titles)" % (path, len(data["tracks"]), len(data["titles"])))
        except ValueError as error:
            check.append(str(error))
            bad += 1
    fitted_path = root / "audio-fitted.json"
    if fitted_path.exists():
        try:
            check.append("ok %s (%d entries)" % (fitted_path, len(labels.load_fitted(root))))
        except ValueError as error:
            check.append(str(error))
            bad += 1
    try:
        data = labels.load(own)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        data = None
    tracks = [{"label": t["label"], "stream": t["stream"], "kind": t["kind"], "how": t["how"],
               "not_counted_because": labels.not_counted_because(t, data["slug"], fitted)}
              for t in (data["tracks"] if data else [])]
    return {"check": check, "exit_code": 2 if bad else 0, "tracks": tracks}


def reconcile_golden(slug, label, title, selection):
    """reconcile.json: everything compare_tracks.main computes and prints for the rip, as data (port spec 3.3)."""
    scan = robot.parse((CORPUS / slug / "scan.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
    mkvmerge = CORPUS / slug / label / "mkvmerge.json"
    ident = json.loads(mkvmerge.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    rows = compare_tracks.expected_rows(scan, title, selection)
    got = compare_tracks.file_rows(ident)
    folder = mkvmerge.parent
    rip_log = next((folder / name for name in compare_tracks.RIP_LOG_NAMES if (folder / name).exists()), None)
    removed = set()
    if rip_log:
        removed = compare_tracks.removed_streams(robot.parse(rip_log.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")))
    want, dropped = compare_tracks.without_removed(rows, removed)
    if any(w["type"] is None for w in want):
        fail("%s/%s: a predicted stream has no type (attribute 1), on which compare_tracks.py crashes" % (slug, label))
    verdicts, numbers = compare_tracks.checks(want, got, scan.titles[title], ident)
    return {"title": title, "selection": selection, "rip_log": str(rip_log) if rip_log else None,
            "want": want, "dropped": dropped,
            "unknown_removed": sorted(i for i in removed if i >= len(want) + len(dropped)),
            "got": got, "verdicts": verdicts, "numbers": numbers,
            "video_tracks": sum(1 for g in got if g["type"] == "video"),
            "statistics_tags": any(g["tags"] for g in got),
            "exit_code": 0 if all(verdicts.values()) else 1}


def audio_goldens(folder):
    """(audio-<folder>.json, audio-<folder>.txt): audio_similarity.results with the default rule and no cache, every
    candidate's forward, reverse and swapped measures, the swapped pair's verdict, the peer run, the veto and its line;
    and audio_similarity.report's lines for the same results (measured once)."""
    res = sim.results(str(folder))
    keep = sim.results
    sim.results = lambda *args, **kwargs: res
    try:
        lines = sim.report(str(folder))
    finally:
        sim.results = keep
    if not lines[2].startswith("  veto: "):
        fail("%s: the report's third line is not its veto line" % folder)
    candidates = []
    for r in res["candidates"]:
        m = r["measures"]
        back = sim.swapped(m) if m is not None else None
        peer = r["peer"]
        candidates.append({"stream": r["stream"], "duplicate_of": r["duplicate_of"], "verdict": r["verdict"],
                           "not_judged": r["not_judged"], "cross_language": r["cross_language"],
                           "before_veto": r["before_veto"], "measures": m,
                           "reverse": sim.reverse_measures(m) if m is not None else None, "swapped": back,
                           "swapped_verdict": sim.verdict(back) if back is not None else None,
                           "peer": None if peer is None else {"stream": peer["stream"], "measures": peer["measures"],
                                                              "verdict": peer["verdict"]}})
    return ({"folder": folder.name, "main": res["main"], "frames": res["frames"], "dialogue": res["dialogue"],
             "veto": res["veto"], "veto_line": lines[2], "candidates": candidates}, lines)


def subs_goldens(slug, label, text_root):
    """(subs.json, subs.txt): subtitle_text.main's run over the title (the original language from tmdb.json) and
    its printed lines; per stream the measures, class, decide, spec87 and before_yes outcomes, built from the measures
    and decisions only (never the event features, the words or the bigrams), and a SHA-1 of each text file read."""
    rec = CORPUS / slug / label
    text = text_root / slug / label / READING
    tracks = st.load_title(rec, text, st.RULE["CLEAR_MAX_BYTES"])
    if not any(st.has_text(t) for t in tracks):
        fail("no sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl in %s for the streams of %s/subs/index.json" % (text, rec))
    missing = [t for t in tracks if t.get("text") is False and t["tag"] in ("eng", "en", "und")]
    if missing:
        fail("%s: no OCR text for %s: fetch it again with tuning-fetch.ps1 -Text"
             % (rec, ", ".join("s%d" % t["n"] for t in missing)))
    orig = None
    tmdb = rec.parent / "tmdb.json"
    if tmdb.exists():
        orig = st.read_json(tmdb).get("original_language")
    unread = sum(1 for t in tracks if t.get("text") is False)
    aside = sum(1 for t in tracks if t.get("set_aside"))
    extra = "".join([", %d not read (another language)" % unread if unread else "",
                     ", %d set aside (closed captions)" % aside if aside else ""])
    lines = ["%s: %d subtitle streams with OCR text%s; rule thresholds are provisional"
             % (rec, sum(1 for t in tracks if st.has_text(t)), extra)]
    verdict = st.analyse(tracks, orig, rec.name, out=lines.append)
    today = st.spec87(tracks)
    read = [t for t in tracks if st.has_text(t)]
    pairs = []
    for i, a in enumerate(read):
        for b in read[i + 1:]:
            p = st.pair(a, b)
            subset = ("s%d in s%d" % (a["n"], b["n"]) if st.subset_of(a, b, p) else
                      "s%d in s%d" % (b["n"], a["n"]) if st.subset_of(b, a, {"cb": p["cb"][::-1]}) else "no")
            pairs.append(dict({"a": a["n"], "b": b["n"]}, **p, subset=subset))
    streams = []
    for t in tracks:
        n, v = t["n"], verdict.get(t["n"])
        streams.append({"n": n, "tag": t["tag"], "codec": t.get("codec"), "forced": t["forced"],
                        "events": len(t["events"]),
                        "status": "read" if st.has_text(t) else "set aside" if t.get("set_aside") else "not read",
                        "pairing": t.get("pairing"), "m": t["m"] if st.has_text(t) else None, "decide": v,
                        "spec87": today.get(n),
                        "before_yes": st.before_yes(v, today[n]) if v is not None and n in today else None})
    shas = {}
    for t in tracks:
        path = text / ("sub-%d.ocr.jsonl" % t["n"])
        if path.exists():
            shas[path.name] = sha1(path)
    committed = rec / "subtitle-text.txt"
    if committed.is_file():
        old = committed.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        same = sum(1 for x, y in zip(old, lines) if x == y)
        print("%s: %d of its %d lines are the lines the Python prints now (%d lines now)"
              % (committed, same, len(old), len(lines)))
    return ({"reading": READING, "exit_code": 0, "orig_lang": orig, "streams": streams, "pairs": pairs,
             "text_sha1": shas}, lines)


def align_golden(slug, label):
    """align.json: subtitle_alignment.py --subs-dir over the rip's subs/ folder, with its defaults, as numbers."""
    subs = CORPUS / slug / label / "subs"
    out = {"clear_max_bytes": ALIGN_CLEAR_MAX_BYTES, "tolerance_ms": ALIGN_TOLERANCE_MS, "exit_code": 0, "error": None,
           "streams": [], "matrix": [], "pairs": []}
    if not (subs / "index.json").exists():
        return dict(out, exit_code=2,
                    error="no %s/index.json: the title has no subtitle track, or the recording was not pulled" % subs)
    streams = align.index_streams(subs)
    if not streams:
        return dict(out, exit_code=2, error="%s/index.json lists no English or no-language subtitle stream" % subs)
    info, tracks = {}, {}
    for name, path, text, entry in streams:
        packets = align.load_packets(path)
        starts = align.events(packets, 0 if text else ALIGN_CLEAR_MAX_BYTES)
        info[name] = {"name": name, "codec": entry.get("codec"), "track_name": entry.get("track_name"),
                      "packets": len(packets), "buckets": align.buckets(packets), "events": len(starts)}
        tracks[name] = starts
    tolerance = ALIGN_TOLERANCE_MS / 1000
    names = list(tracks)
    matrix = [[align.aligned(tracks[a], tracks[b], tolerance) for b in names] for a in names]
    pairs = [{"a": a, "b": b, "larger": max(align.aligned(tracks[a], tracks[b], tolerance),
                                            align.aligned(tracks[b], tracks[a], tolerance))}
             for i, a in enumerate(names) for b in names[i + 1:]]
    return dict(out, streams=list(info.values()), matrix=matrix, pairs=pairs)


def retune_golden():
    """retune-report.txt: audio_dataset.main's report, with the baseline left alone (--snapshot to a temporary file),
    the snapshot line's path normalised and the lines of port spec 3.4 that name a script or a code hash rewritten."""
    tmp = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="lazymkv-golden-"))
    snapshot = tmp / "snapshot.json"
    printed = io.StringIO()
    try:
        with redirect_stdout(printed):
            code = dataset.main([str(CORPUS), "--snapshot", str(snapshot)])
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp)
    text = printed.getvalue()
    if code == 2 or not text.endswith("\n"):
        fail("audio_dataset.py exited %d: %s" % (code, text.strip()[-300:]))
    shown = "snapshot: %s" % snapshot
    lines = []
    for line in text[:-1].split("\n"):
        if line.startswith(shown):
            line = "snapshot: " + SNAPSHOT_SHOWN + line[len(shown):]
        for pattern, replacement in REWRITES:
            line = pattern.sub(replacement, line)
        if re.search(r"python3|\.py\b", line):
            fail("a retune report line still names a Python script: %s" % line)
        lines.append(line)
    print("retune report: %s (audio_dataset.py exit %d)" % (lines[-1], code))
    return lines


def proxy_golden(text_root, proxy, ffmpeg):
    """proxy-<folder>/: the level folder proxy_levels.build rebuilds from the title's proxy, without proxy.txt (it
    names the proxy's absolute path) and ffmpeg.txt; golden.json says what was rebuilt, from which proxy, with which
    ffmpeg."""
    slug, label, name = proxy.split("/")
    man = sim.read_manifest(CORPUS / slug / label / name)
    main = int(man["main"]["main"])
    cands = [int(c["cand"]) for c in man["cands"]]
    mka = text_root / slug / label / "audio-proxy.mka"
    dest = OUT / slug / GOLDEN / ("proxy-" + name)
    tmp = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="lazymkv-golden-proxy-"))
    try:
        built = tmp / name
        proxy_levels.build(str(mka), str(built), main, cands)
        for f in sorted(built.iterdir()):
            if f.name not in ("proxy.txt", "ffmpeg.txt"):
                write_bytes(dest / f.name, f.read_bytes())
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp)
    write_json(dest / "golden.json", {"slug": slug, "label": label, "folder": name, "main": main, "cands": cands,
                                      "ffmpeg_version": ffmpeg, "proxy_sha1": sha1(mka)})


def inputs(text_root, proxy):
    """Every input a golden was computed from, by its path below this repository (the OCR text and the proxy by their
    path below TEXT, which has the same layout), with the SHA-1 of its bytes."""
    found = {}
    for name in ("audio-dataset.json", "audio-fitted.json"):
        if (CORPUS / name).is_file():
            found[name] = sha1(CORPUS / name)
    for slug in recordings():
        rec = CORPUS / slug
        files = [rec / name for name in ("scan.txt", "tmdb.json", "audio-labels.json")]
        for d in sorted(p for p in rec.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and p.name != GOLDEN):
            files += [d / name for name in ("rip-summary.json", "extract-summary.json", "mkvmerge.json", "rip.txt",
                                            "extract.txt", "ffprobe-streams.json")]
            for folder in level_folders(slug, d.name):
                files += sorted(f for f in folder.iterdir()
                                if f.name in LEVEL_INPUTS or re.fullmatch(r"cand-\d+\.txt", f.name))
            files += sorted(d.glob("subs/index.json")) + sorted(d.glob("subs/sub-*.packets.json"))
            files += sorted(d.glob(READING + "/sub-*.frames.json"))
        for f in files:
            if f.is_file():
                found[f.relative_to(CORPUS).as_posix()] = sha1(f)
    for f in sorted(text_root.glob("*/*/%s/sub-*.ocr.jsonl" % READING)):
        found[f.relative_to(text_root).as_posix()] = sha1(f)
    slug, label, _ = proxy.split("/")
    for name in ("audio-proxy.mka", "audio-proxy.json"):
        found["%s/%s/%s" % (slug, label, name)] = sha1(text_root / slug / label / name)
    return dict(sorted(found.items()))


def fill_readme(block):
    """README.md's ```json written_by block, replaced by `block`."""
    readme = OUT / GOLDEN / "README.md"
    text = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    new, count = WRITTEN_BY.subn(lambda m: m.group(1) + json.dumps(block, indent=1) + "\n" + m.group(3), text)
    if count != 1:
        fail("%s holds no single ```json written_by block" % readme)
    write_bytes(readme, new.encode("utf-8"))


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="write_goldens.py",
                                 description="Writes the Rust port's goldens from the phase 0 Python (README.md).")
    ap.add_argument("--text", required=True, metavar="TEXT",
                    help="the folder the tuning dataset's copies were fetched into: "
                         "TEXT/<slug>/<label>/subs-ocr/sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl and TEXT/<slug>/<label>/audio-proxy.mka")
    ap.add_argument("--pull-request", required=True, type=int, metavar="N",
                    help="the number of lazymkv's pull request of the Rust port")
    ap.add_argument("--proxy", default=PROXY, metavar="SLUG/LABEL/FOLDER",
                    help="the level folder rebuilt from its title's proxy (default: %(default)s)")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    text_root = pathlib.Path(a.text).resolve()
    os.chdir(ROOT)
    preflight(text_root, a.proxy)
    ffmpeg = ffmpeg_version()
    fitted = labels.load_fitted(CORPUS, labels.fitting_slug())
    for slug in recordings():
        gold = OUT / slug / GOLDEN
        if (CORPUS / slug / "scan.txt").is_file():
            write_json(gold / "scan.json", scan_golden(slug))
            write_lines(gold / "titles.txt", sim.titles_report(str(CORPUS / slug)))
        write_json(gold / "labels.json", labels_golden(slug, fitted))
        for label, title, selection in rip_labels(slug):
            write_json(gold / label / "reconcile.json", reconcile_golden(slug, label, title, selection))
            for folder in level_folders(slug, label):
                data, lines = audio_goldens(folder)
                write_json(gold / label / ("audio-%s.json" % folder.name), data)
                write_lines(gold / label / ("audio-%s.txt" % folder.name), lines)
            if needs_text(slug, label):
                data, lines = subs_goldens(slug, label, text_root)
                write_json(gold / label / "subs.json", data)
                write_lines(gold / label / "subs.txt", lines)
            if (CORPUS / slug / label / "subs").is_dir():
                write_json(gold / label / "align.json", align_golden(slug, label))
    write_lines(OUT / GOLDEN / "retune-report.txt", retune_golden())
    proxy_golden(text_root, a.proxy, ffmpeg)
    block = {"pull_request": a.pull_request,
             "branch_commit": run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], ROOT).strip(),
             "scripts_phase0_tree": run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD:scripts/phase0"], ROOT).strip(),
             "evidence_commit": run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], CORPUS).strip(),
             "python": platform.python_version(), "ffmpeg": ffmpeg, "inputs": inputs(text_root, a.proxy)}
    fill_readme(block)
    print("goldens written from evidence commit %s with Python %s and %s"
          % (block["evidence_commit"][:12], block["python"], ffmpeg))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

- [ ] **Step 15: Fetch the OCR text and the proxy from the tuning dataset**

The text lives only in the tuning dataset (decision D16). `tuning-fetch.ps1` copies one title's part to `C:\lazymkv\phase0\tmp\tuning-fetch\` on the mini PC, its log prints the `scp` line and the clean-up line, and the Mac runs both at once. Make a new folder for the copies and a function for one fetch (the ssh target comes from `box.env`, so no user name is typed):

```bash
TEXT="$(mktemp -d)/lazymkv-golden-text"
mkdir -p "$TEXT"
. scripts/phase0/box.env
fetch() {  # fetch <slug> <label> [-Text]
  slug="$1"; label="$2"; shift 2
  log="golden-fetch-$slug-$label${1:+-text}"
  scripts/phase0/job.sh tuning-fetch.ps1 "$log" -Slug "$slug" -Label "$label" "$@" || return 1
  while :; do scripts/phase0/wait.sh "$log"; rc=$?; [ "$rc" -eq 3 ] || break; done
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  src="C:/lazymkv/phase0/tmp/tuning-fetch/$slug/$label"; dest="$TEXT/$slug/$label"
  if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then src="$src/subs-ocr"; dest="$dest/subs-ocr"; fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
  scp -q -r -o BatchMode=yes "$LAZYMKV_BOX:$src" "$dest" || return 1
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$LAZYMKV_BOX" 'rmdir /s /q C:\lazymkv\phase0\tmp\tuning-fetch'
}
fetch short-circuit-1986-dvd all-tracks
fetch pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd all-tracks -Text
fetch pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd eng-only -Text
fetch short-circuit-2-1988-dvd all-tracks-2 -Text
fetch the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray e16-stereo -Text
fetch the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray rehearsal -Text
fetch the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray t3-all-tracks -Text
find "$TEXT" -name '*.ocr.jsonl' | wc -l
ls "$TEXT/short-circuit-1986-dvd/all-tracks"
```

Expected: each `fetch` prints the job's log, which ends `fetched: ... (<bytes> bytes)`, the `scp (on the Mac; ...)` line, the `clean-up (on the Mac, ...)` line and `RESULT ok`, then a `PHASE0-DONE status=ok` line; the `scp` and the clean-up print nothing (the `scp` is the line the log printed, with `DEST` the folder under `$TEXT`). The `find` prints `7` (one OCR text file per stream read: two for `pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd/all-tracks`, one for each of the other five titles); `ls` shows `audio-levels-20ms-1-2`, `audio-proxy.json` and `audio-proxy.mka`. A log ending `RESULT FAILED: ... holds no OCR text` means that title was never read: stop and report. `RESULT FAILED: ... already exists: an earlier fetch was not deleted`: run the clean-up line it prints, then that `fetch` again. Never leave a fetch on the mini PC: if a `fetch` stops after its job, run `ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$LAZYMKV_BOX" 'rmdir /s /q C:\lazymkv\phase0\tmp\tuning-fetch'` before anything else.

- [ ] **Step 4: Pin the two spellings of `audio-proxy.json`'s reader**

`audio-levels.ps1` writes into `audio-proxy.json` the line `read = "... then measure (proxy_levels.py)"`, which Step 13 changes to `(lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy)`; every proxy already in the tuning dataset and in the evidence keeps the old text, and spec section 6 says the Rust reader accepts both. Task 4's `parse_proxy` never looks at the field. This test pins that before the string changes; it passes at once (it guards the future, it does not drive code).

Create `crates/core/tests/proxy_read_spellings.rs`:

```rust
//! `audio-proxy.json` names, in `encoding.read`, the program that reads the proxy back: `audio-levels.ps1` wrote
//! "(proxy_levels.py)" until the Rust port and writes "(lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy)" since, while the files already
//! in the tuning dataset and in the evidence keep the old text. Port spec section 6: "the Rust reader accepts both".
//! The reader never checks the field; this test pins that, so a later check of it has to keep both spellings.

use lazymkv_core::audio::levels::{parse_proxy, PROXY_FORMAT};

/// The `read` text audio-levels.ps1 wrote before the port (its proxy headroom is 18 dB).
const READ_BEFORE: &str =
    "add 18 dB in float, convert to the source stream's sample_fmt, then measure (proxy_levels.py)";
/// The same text since the port.
const READ_SINCE: &str =
    "add 18 dB in float, convert to the source stream's sample_fmt, then measure (lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy)";

/// A made-up audio-proxy.json of one stereo AC-3 stream (its mixdown and its side signal), with the fields the reader
/// keeps.
fn proxy_json(read: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        concat!(
            "{{\"format\": \"{format}\", \"slug\": \"some-film\", \"label\": \"all-tracks\",\n",
            " \"source\": {{\"file\": \"title_t00.mkv\", \"bytes\": 1000, \"audio_streams\": 1}},\n",
            " \"encoding\": {{\"codec\": \"flac\", \"gain_db\": -18, \"read\": \"{read}\"}},\n",
            " \"tracks\": [{{\"track\": 0, \"source_stream\": 1, \"series\": \"mix\",\n",
            "   \"source\": {{\"codec\": \"ac3\", \"channels\": 2, \"language\": \"eng\"}}}},\n",
            "  {{\"track\": 1, \"source_stream\": 1, \"series\": \"side\",\n",
            "   \"source\": {{\"codec\": \"ac3\", \"channels\": 2, \"language\": \"eng\"}}}}]}}\n"
        ),
        format = PROXY_FORMAT,
        read = read
    )
}

#[test]
fn both_spellings_of_the_reader_parse_alike() {
    let before = parse_proxy(&proxy_json(READ_BEFORE)).expect("the spelling before the port parses");
    let since = parse_proxy(&proxy_json(READ_SINCE)).expect("the spelling since the port parses");
    assert_eq!(before.encoding.get("read").and_then(|v| v.as_str()), Some(READ_BEFORE));
    assert_eq!(since.encoding.get("read").and_then(|v| v.as_str()), Some(READ_SINCE));
    for proxy in [&before, &since] {
        assert_eq!(proxy.format.as_ref().and_then(|v| v.as_str()), Some(PROXY_FORMAT));
        assert_eq!(proxy.encoding.get("gain_db").and_then(|v| v.as_i64()), Some(-18));
        assert_eq!(proxy.source.get("audio_streams").and_then(|v| v.as_i64()), Some(1));
        let series: Vec<Option<&str>> = proxy.tracks.iter().map(|t| t.series.as_deref()).collect();
        assert_eq!(series, vec![Some("mix"), Some("side")]);
        assert_eq!(proxy.tracks[0].source_stream.as_i64(), Some(1));
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Write the failing test of the mapping table**

Create `crates/dev/tests/port_mapping.rs`:

```rust
//! `docs/phase1/rust-port-tests.md` maps the 213 Python tests of `scripts/phase0/test_*.py`, deleted by the Rust
//! port, to the Rust tests that port them one for one (port spec section 5, "Ported tests"). These tests check the
//! table so a reviewer can trust it: 213 rows numbered 1 to 213, exactly the Python tests in their files' order
//! (pinned by a SHA-1), the count per file of spec section 2, every Rust test named once and defined in the file its
//! row names, a task of the port that ports tests, and no placeholder left.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use lazymkv_dev::evidence::{repo_root, skip};
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};

/// The table, from the repository root.
const TABLE: &str = "docs/phase1/rust-port-tests.md";
/// SHA-1 (hex) of the 213 names "<file>::<class>::<method>", each followed by "\n", in the order of the files by name
/// and of their lines: the list Task 15 Step 7 printed from the Python of the last commit that had it.
const PYTHON_NAMES_SHA1: &str = "6f6bbb40160c0bce4002ba9ea5913e2d0cab2e00";
/// The number of Python tests.
const PYTHON_TESTS: usize = 213;
/// `def test_` per Python file (port spec section 2).
const PER_FILE: [(&str, usize); 7] = [
    ("test_analysis.py", 13),
    ("test_audio_dataset.py", 64),
    ("test_audio_similarity.py", 36),
    ("test_decisions.py", 26),
    ("test_exp11_tracks.py", 5),
    ("test_ocr_compare.py", 20),
    ("test_subtitle_text.py", 49),
];
/// The tasks of the port's plan that port Python tests.
const PORTING_TASKS: std::ops::RangeInclusive<u32> = 2..=12;
/// The placeholders Task 15 replaces before the table is committed.
const PLACEHOLDERS: [&str; 2] = ["PY_COMMIT", "PR_NUMBER"];

/// One row: "| n | `python` | `rust` | `file` | task |".
struct Row {
    number: usize,
    python: String,
    rust: String,
    file: String,
    task: String,
}

/// A table row, or None for any other line (the header row's "#" and the rule's "---" are not numbers).
fn row(line: &str) -> Option<Row> {
    let inner = line.trim().strip_prefix('|')?.strip_suffix('|')?;
    let cells: Vec<&str> = inner.split('|').map(str::trim).collect();
    if cells.len() != 5 {
        return None;
    }
    let number = cells[0].parse().ok()?;
    let code = |cell: &str| cell.trim_matches('`').to_string();
    Some(Row { number, python: code(cells[1]), rust: code(cells[2]), file: code(cells[3]), task: cells[4].to_string() })
}

/// The repository root and the table's text; None (after a skip line) when there is no repository around the crate.
fn table_text() -> Option<(PathBuf, String)> {
    let Some(root) = repo_root(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))) else {
        skip("no repository root (a Cargo.toml with [workspace]) above crates/dev");
        return None;
    };
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(root.join(TABLE)).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{TABLE}: {e}"));
    Some((root, text))
}

fn rows(text: &str) -> Vec<Row> {
    text.lines().filter_map(row).collect()
}

#[test]
fn the_table_lists_the_213_python_tests_in_their_files_order() {
    let Some((_, text)) = table_text() else { return };
    let rows = rows(&text);
    assert_eq!(rows.len(), PYTHON_TESTS, "{TABLE}: rows");
    for (i, r) in rows.iter().enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(r.number, i + 1, "{TABLE}: row {} is numbered {}", i + 1, r.number);
    }
    let names: String = rows.iter().map(|r| format!("{}\n", r.python)).collect();
    let digest: String = Sha1::digest(names.as_bytes()).iter().map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}")).collect();
    assert_eq!(digest, PYTHON_NAMES_SHA1, "{TABLE}: the Python column is not the list of the Python tests in order");
    for (file, count) in PER_FILE {
        let prefix = format!("{file}::");
        assert_eq!(rows.iter().filter(|r| r.python.starts_with(&prefix)).count(), count, "{TABLE}: {file}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn every_rust_test_is_named_once_and_defined_in_its_file() {
    let Some((root, text)) = table_text() else { return };
    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
    for r in rows(&text) {
        assert!(seen.insert(r.rust.clone()), "{TABLE}: row {}: {} is named twice", r.number, r.rust);
        let name = r.rust.rsplit("::").next().unwrap_or_default();
        assert!(!name.is_empty(), "{TABLE}: row {}: no Rust test", r.number);
        let source = std::fs::read_to_string(root.join(&r.file))
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{TABLE}: row {}: {}: {e}", r.number, r.file));
        assert!(source.contains(&format!("fn {name}(")), "{TABLE}: row {}: no `fn {name}(` in {}", r.number, r.file);
        let task: u32 = r.task.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("{TABLE}: row {}: task {:?}", r.number, r.task));
        assert!(PORTING_TASKS.contains(&task), "{TABLE}: row {}: task {task} ports no Python test", r.number);
    }
}

#[test]
fn no_placeholder_is_left() {
    let Some((_, text)) = table_text() else { return };
    for placeholder in PLACEHOLDERS {
        assert!(!text.contains(placeholder), "{TABLE} still holds {placeholder}");
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Pair each Python test with its Rust test**

Every task that ported tests names them in its own section of the port's plan (`PORT_PLAN`): Tasks 2 to 12, in tables headed "Python test | Rust test" or, for Task 11, in its Step 1's sentence. Most keep the Python method's name without `test_`, some keep it whole, and some add a prefix (Task 12's `exp02_...`). The rule: **the Rust test of a Python test is the test `cargo test --workspace -- --list` lists whose last `::` segment is the Python method's name or that name without `test_`, when exactly one test is such; else the one test whose last segment ends with `_` and that name without `test_`, when exactly one does; otherwise the one the porting task's table or sentence names for that method.** The task of a row is fixed by the Python class (it is the task index's assignment; `Counts` goes to Task 8, as Task 7 hands it over).

Build the pairing:

```bash
SCRATCH=<the scratch directory>
. "$SCRATCH/t15.env"
export LC_ALL=C
cargo test -q --workspace -- --list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/: test$//p' | sort -u > "$SCRATCH/rust-tests.txt"
wc -l < "$SCRATCH/rust-tests.txt"
touch "$SCRATCH/map-manual.tsv"
awk -F'\t' -v OFS='\t' '
  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { manual[$1] = $2; next }
  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { n = split($0, p, "::"); last = p[n]; path[last] = $0; count[last]++; all[++total] = last; next }
  {
    split($0, q, "::"); f = q[1]; c = q[2]; m = q[3]; s = substr(m, 6)
    key = f "::" c
    task = (key ~ /^test_analysis\.py::(SplitFields|Parse)$/ || key == "test_decisions.py::ParseLines") ? 2 \
         : (key == "test_decisions.py::CompareTracks") ? 3 \
         : (key ~ /^test_audio_similarity\.py::(Reading|Measures)$/) ? 4 \
         : (key ~ /^test_audio_similarity\.py::(Rule|ReverseRun|CrossLanguage|PositionVeto)$/ || key == "test_audio_dataset.py::Similarity") ? 5 \
         : (key ~ /^test_audio_similarity\.py::(Report|Titles)$/) ? 6 \
         : (key ~ /^test_audio_dataset\.py::(Spec|Labels)$/) ? 7 \
         : (key ~ /^test_audio_dataset\.py::(Counts|Dataset|NotChecked|Joins|Routine)$/) ? 8 \
         : (key ~ /^test_analysis\.py::(Alignment|SubsDir)$/) ? 9 \
         : (f == "test_subtitle_text.py") ? 10 \
         : (key == "test_audio_dataset.py::ProxyStreams") ? 11 \
         : (key ~ /^test_decisions\.py::(Exp02|CompareScans|HitRate)$/ || f == "test_exp11_tracks.py" || f == "test_ocr_compare.py") ? 12 \
         : "?"
    if (m in manual) { print $0, manual[m], task; next }
    k = count[m] + count[s]
    if (k == 1) { print $0, (count[m] ? path[m] : path[s]), task; next }
    if (k == 0) {
      hits = 0
      for (i = 1; i <= total; i++) {
        t = all[i]
        if (length(t) > length(s) + 1 && substr(t, length(t) - length(s)) == "_" s) { hits++; found = t }
      }
      if (hits == 1) { print $0, path[found], task; print "suffix rule: " m " -> " path[found] > "/dev/stderr"; next }
      k = hits
    }
    print $0, "UNRESOLVED (" k " candidates)", task
  }
' "$SCRATCH/map-manual.tsv" "$SCRATCH/rust-tests.txt" "$SCRATCH/py-tests.txt" > "$SCRATCH/map.tsv"
wc -l < "$SCRATCH/map.tsv"
awk -F'\t' '{ print $3 }' "$SCRATCH/map.tsv" | sort -n | uniq -c
grep 'UNRESOLVED' "$SCRATCH/map.tsv"
```

Expected: a number of Rust tests well above 213 (the port added its own); on standard error, one `suffix rule: <method> -> <Rust test>` line per Python test paired by the prefix rule (check each against its task's table: `grep -n '<method>' "$PORT_PLAN"` shows the row; a wrong pair goes into `$SCRATCH/map-manual.tsv` as below); `213`; the per-task counts `7 2`, `10 3`, `8 4`, `21 5`, `8 6`, `12 7`, `49 8`, `7 9`, `49 10`, `2 11`, `40 12` (no `?`); then the `UNRESOLVED` lines, if any.

For each `UNRESOLVED` line: find the method in the port's plan with `grep -n '<the Python method>' "$PORT_PLAN"`, read the Rust test its porting task names, find that test's full path in `$SCRATCH/rust-tests.txt` (`grep -E '(^|::)<the Rust fn>$' "$SCRATCH/rust-tests.txt"`, exactly one line), and append to `$SCRATCH/map-manual.tsv` the line `<the Python method><TAB><that full path>`. Then run the block again, until `grep 'UNRESOLVED'` prints nothing. `0 candidates` for a method that no task's text names means it was never ported: stop and report it (the review that wrote this plan found one such pair: `test_audio_dataset.py::Counts`, whose two tests Task 7 hands to Task 8 while Task 8's list of 47 does not include them; if Task 8 did not port them, Task 8 must, before this task goes on).

Then check the pairing against the test list and find each Rust test's file:

```bash
SCRATCH=<the scratch directory>
export LC_ALL=C
awk -F'\t' '{ print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/map.tsv" | sort | uniq -d
awk -F'\t' '{ print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/map.tsv" | sort | comm -23 - "$SCRATCH/rust-tests.txt"
: > "$SCRATCH/map-files.tsv"
while IFS="$(printf '\t')" read -r py rust task; do
  name="${rust##*::}"
  files="$(git grep -l -E "fn ${name}\(" -- crates)"
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$py" "$rust" "$(printf '%s' "$files" | tr '\n' ' ')" "$task" >> "$SCRATCH/map-files.tsv"
done < "$SCRATCH/map.tsv"
awk -F'\t' '$3 ~ / ./ || $3 == ""' "$SCRATCH/map-files.tsv"
```

When a name is defined in two files (two modules with a function of the same name), the last command prints the row with both files: keep the one whose module path matches the test's path (`crates/<crate>/src/<module path>.rs`, or `.../<module>/tests.rs`, or `crates/<crate>/tests/<binary>.rs` for an integration test) by editing that row of `$SCRATCH/map-files.tsv`, and run the last command again.

````diff
--- a/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-lazymkv-phase-0-evidence.md
+++ b/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-04-lazymkv-phase-0-evidence.md
@@ -42,9 +42,10 @@
 - Commit commands take the form `git commit -m "<message>"`.
 - The saving message is `MSG:5014`, or `MSG:5015` when a profile is in use. Found on 2026-10-05, on the first real rip: with `--profile`, MakeMKV 2.0.0 prints `MSG:5015` ("Saving %1 titles into directory %2 using profile '%3' from file '%4'") and no `MSG:5014`. Every rip in this plan uses a profile. Wherever a task says `MSG:5014`, read "`MSG:5014` or `MSG:5015`"; the scripts accept both, and their labels (`5014=`, `saw_5014`, `stopped-at-5014`, `added-before-5014`) keep their names and are true for either code. A `codes=` list then ends in 5015. The profile named in the `MSG:5015` line is the proof that MakeMKV used the job profile.
 - Decision D16 (owner, 2026-10-05): every MakeMKV call runs with `--debug` (`Get-MkFlags` adds it) and its debug log, which MakeMKV 2.0.0 always writes to `%USERPROFILE%\MakeMKV_log.txt`, is kept beside the call's output as `<output>.makemkv-debug.txt` by `Save-MkDebugLog`. With `--debug` the robot output also carries `MSG:1004` and `MSG:1003` lines. Every rip also keeps `system.csv` (CPU load, free RAM and bytes written every 5 s) and `system-events.json` (Windows warnings and errors about storage, USB and the network during the rip). A script that calls MakeMKV without `Get-MkFlags` adds `--debug` and calls `Save-MkDebugLog` itself. Exceptions: env.ps1's Get-DiscIndex drive listing runs without --debug (its log would be overwritten by the call that follows); scan-copy.ps1's nodebug/plain diagnosis modes leave it out on purpose; backup-disc.ps1 and extract-from-copy.ps1 keep the debug log and system events but not the free-RAM/CPU sampler.
-- Tuning dataset (decision D16): every rip that ends `RESULT ok` is added to the audio tuning dataset after its probe and pull, while the rip is still in staging, and at the latest before its task's commit. `python3 scripts/phase0/audio_dataset.py args corpus/owner/<slug> <label>` prints one job line and its `wait.sh` line for the title's programme reference against every other stream in a wanted language (or the reference alone), then one per language that is not wanted and has two or more streams (dataset only). Run each pair, then `scripts/phase0/pull-recording.sh <slug>`, `python3 scripts/phase0/audio_labels.py auto corpus/owner/<slug>` and `python3 scripts/phase0/audio_dataset.py`. audio-levels.ps1 writes, besides its level folder, a compact copy of every audio stream (`audio-proxy.mka`: FLAC, 8 kHz, mono, 24 bit) and a copy of the level folder to `$TuningData\<slug>\<label>\` (`\\unas-pro\media\lazymkv-tuning`); it writes `audio-proxy.json` into the level folder last, so a level folder without it is from a run that did not finish. Nothing under `$TuningData` is deleted without the owner's say. The one exception to writing large files only to the share (never to `C:`): a proxy may be copied to C:\lazymkv\phase0\tmp\tuning-fetch for the minutes an scp takes, at most 2 GB, deleted right after. `scripts/phase0/tuning-fetch.ps1 -Slug <slug> -Label <label>` (a job) makes that copy of one title's dataset folder, refuses more than 2 GB or a second copy while one is still there, and prints the size, the `scp` command and the clean-up command; the Mac runs the clean-up command immediately after the `scp`. It is needed only when a future measure needs the proxies on the Mac, never in this routine. The owner's label for each measured track is asked for without showing any verdict and is recorded only with `audio_labels.py set` or `unset` (never by editing the JSON); whether a label counts for experiment 13 is worked out by the harness, never stored. `audio_dataset.py` exits 1 when a track the owner labelled as programme audio gets a drop verdict, when a level folder is measured against the wrong reference, when a reference is labelled as unwanted audio, when a labelled programme track gets `commentary-cross-language`, or when a labelled candidate, taken as the reference, would give the programme the commentary verdict (`swapped reference`) (stop and report); 2 when a labels file does not validate; 3 when something could not be checked (level files missing, a label with no measurement, a measured track gone).

Spec section 5: `cargo test --workspace` passes on the Mac "with the clone, the series and the text" before the pull request is marked ready. Task 14 deleted its copy of the text (its Step 20); fetch it again the same way (Task 14 Step 15's function; the ssh target comes from `box.env`, so no user name is typed), and keep the folder's path in `t15.env`:

```bash
SCRATCH=<the scratch directory>
TEXT="$(mktemp -d)/lazymkv-golden-text"
mkdir -p "$TEXT"
printf 'TEXT=%s\n' "$TEXT" >> "$SCRATCH/t15.env"
. scripts/phase0/box.env
fetch() {  # fetch <slug> <label> [-Text]
  slug="$1"; label="$2"; shift 2
  log="t15-fetch-$slug-$label${1:+-text}"
  scripts/phase0/job.sh tuning-fetch.ps1 "$log" -Slug "$slug" -Label "$label" "$@" || return 1
  while :; do scripts/phase0/wait.sh "$log"; rc=$?; [ "$rc" -eq 3 ] || break; done
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  src="C:/lazymkv/phase0/tmp/tuning-fetch/$slug/$label"; dest="$TEXT/$slug/$label"
  if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then src="$src/subs-ocr"; dest="$dest/subs-ocr"; fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
  scp -q -r -o BatchMode=yes "$LAZYMKV_BOX:$src" "$dest" || return 1
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$LAZYMKV_BOX" 'rmdir /s /q C:\lazymkv\phase0\tmp\tuning-fetch'
}
fetch short-circuit-1986-dvd all-tracks
fetch pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd all-tracks -Text
fetch pans-labyrinth-2006-uhd eng-only -Text
fetch short-circuit-2-1988-dvd all-tracks-2 -Text
fetch the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray e16-stereo -Text
fetch the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray rehearsal -Text
fetch the-office-2005-s3d3-bluray t3-all-tracks -Text
find "$TEXT" -name '*.ocr.jsonl' | wc -l
ls "$TEXT/short-circuit-1986-dvd/all-tracks"
```

```markdown
## Rust port of the phase 0 analysers

The fifteen Python analysers of `scripts/phase0/` are now Rust, and the Python is deleted, as `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-rust-port-design.md` designs it (decisions RP1 to RP6; the implementation plan is `PORT_PLAN`).

- `crates/core` gains `lang`, `recording`, `robot`, `reconcile`, `audio::{levels, measures, rule, reference, titles, report, labels, dataset}` and `subtitle::{align, text}`: the robot-output parser (spec 9.4), the reconciler as phase 0 ran it (6.2 step 7; RP6), the audio content rule of 8.6 with the D21 veto, the D16 labels and D23 counting, the tuning harness, and the subtitle text and alignment rules of 8.7. `core` does no I/O: every function takes text, parsed values or an in-memory tree.
- `crates/dev` builds `lazymkv-dev`: one command per Python entry point with the Python's flags, lines and exit codes (spec 3.4), plus `decide` (the first form of phase 1's command) and `golden`.
- The 22 Python files are deleted; the last commit with them is PY_COMMIT_FULL. `fetch-thediscdb-fixtures.sh` reads JSON with `jq`; the PowerShell comments and the string `audio-levels.ps1` writes into `audio-proxy.json` name the `lazymkv-dev` commands (the reader accepts both spellings); the phase 0 plan's still-run steps call `lazymkv-dev` (their inline Python became `jq` and `awk` that print the same lines) and its other Python steps are marked historical; the READMEs, the phase report, the experiment documents and spec sections 4.2, 15 and 16 say where each tool now lives.

### Acceptance

- Goldens written once by the Python (`golden/write_goldens.py` in lazymkv-evidence, at evidence commit GOLDEN_COMMIT): `lazymkv-dev golden check` with the OCR text gives `GOLDEN_SUMMARY`, the harness round trip included.
- `lazymkv-dev retune` on the evidence clone ends `RESULT ok`; the v3 baseline it wrote is lazymkv-evidence commit BASELINE_COMMIT.
- Ported tests: 213 of 213 Python tests, one Rust test each, listed in `docs/phase1/rust-port-tests.md` and checked by `crates/dev/tests/port_mapping.rs`.
- `cargo test --workspace` on the Mac with the evidence clone, the level series and the OCR text: MAC_SUMMARY. On the mini PC through `scripts/box.sh`, without the clone: BOX_SUMMARY.
- `scripts/phase0/check-names.sh`, the token grep and the unit-key find print nothing; the drive-serial grep finds only the two drive lines whose serial was scrubbed to the placeholder `SERIAL` in phase 0, and no serial; `git ls-files '*.py'` is empty.

### Deliberate differences from the Python (port spec 3.4 and 4)

- exit 3 when the evidence directory is missing; exit 2 where the Python crashed with a traceback;
- `-h` or `--help` as the first word of `exp02`, `encoding`, `hit-rate` or `compare-scans` prints `usage: lazymkv-dev <cmd> <args>` and exits 0, where the Python took the word as a path and crashed;
- the recorder's files (`meta.json`, `rip-summary.json`, the frame index, the OCR records and summaries) are read through typed views: a field of an unexpected type makes the file unreadable, exit 2, where the Python skipped that field and read on (the port plan's open point 10); every recorded file has the expected types;
- stream numbers, crop numbers and `exp02`'s run numbers take ASCII digits only, where Python's `str.isdigit` also took other Unicode digits (the port plan's open point 9); no recorded or pinned scan holds a non-ASCII digit;
- `compare-scans` writes its tuples as `(a, b, c)`;
- `proxy.txt` names the proxy's path as given, not resolved;
- the harness snapshot is v3: `code` is `{"rule_version": 1}`, and the cache key hashes the rule version, not the script;
- the five report lines that named a script or a code hash name the `lazymkv-dev` command and the rule version.

### Kept on purpose

- Row 13 of the design spec's section 17 still says "its harness `audio_dataset.py`": `retune` reads that row, so it is unchanged byte for byte.
- `labels check`'s two sentences that named the script are rewritten to name the Rust (Task 7): `... (audio_labels.py kinds)` becomes `... (lazymkv-dev labels kinds)` and `...; update audio_labels.py` becomes `...; update core::audio::labels`. This goes beyond the five report lines that spec 3.4 rewrites; neither sentence reaches a golden. No `labels` string keeps a `.py` name: the only ones left in `crates/` outside comments are those the bullets after this one name, each kept on purpose.
- `retune` refuses a file that is no snapshot with `not a snapshot written by lazymkv-dev retune (...) or by audio_dataset.py (lazymkv audio dataset snapshot v2)` (`crates/dev/src/cmd/retune.rs` and its test): `audio_dataset.py` is the program that wrote every v2 snapshot, the committed baseline before this pull request among them.
- `crates/dev/tests/golden.rs` says `write_goldens.py writes them`: the program that wrote the goldens, which lives beside them in lazymkv-evidence (`golden/write_goldens.py`), not here.
- `crates/dev/tests/port_mapping.rs` names the seven `test_*.py` files whose tests its table counts, and `crates/core/tests/proxy_read_spellings.rs` holds the old `(proxy_levels.py)` spelling of `audio-proxy.json`'s `read` line, which every proxy already written carries and the reader still accepts.
- The subtitle thresholds are not under `retune` yet: that is phase 1 work after this pull request (spec section 15, EXP-14-design.md).
EXTRA_LINES
